Where to go: Admin center > Settings > Reports > Call Status

Calculate how many calls were not recorded due to participants who didn't give their consent via the consent page.

1. In the Call Status report page, select the team and timeframe for the report, and then click EMAIL REPORT.
2. Download the report that is sent to your email.
3. Filter the report for calls where "Consent Page Used" is "TRUE", and make a note of the number of calls.
4. Next, filter the report again for calls where: Make a note of the number of calls in this filter.
  - "Status" is "ABORTED", and
  - "Skip Reason" is "COMPLIANCE_USER_REQUEST"
5. Divide the number of calls where consent wasn't given (i.e. that matched the filter in step 5) by the number of calls where the consent page was used (i.e. that matched the filter in step 4). The result is the consent opt out rate. Monitor this rate over time to understand regular levels for your business.

chunks.text:
Understanding call recording consent:
Call recording consent determines whether participants are informed that a call is being recorded and whether permission is required before recording begins.

Some regions require consent from one participant on the call, while others require consent from all participants. Dual consent, also known as all-party consent or two-party consent, means that every participant must be informed before the call is recorded and choose whether to continue.

Gong provides consent settings that allow you to configure how recording notifications and consent are handled based on your organization’s policy and applicable regulations. For background on consent models and recording laws, see Sales call recording laws and compliance.

chunks.text:
Get consent to record calls:
Your Tech admin may have set Gong up to display a consent page before a participant joins a meeting. This lets participants give consent to being recorded before they join your meeting, helping you to comply with privacy regulations.
chunks.body: Your Tech admin may have set Gong up to display a consent page before a participant joins a meeting. This lets participants give consent to being recorded before they join your meeting, helping you to comply with privacy regulations.
chunks.title: Call recording and consent settings

chunks.text:
Get consent to record calls > How recording consent works:
Your Tech admin may have configured a consent profile which manages how meeting participants give consent to being recorded. The consent profile determines which methods Gong uses to inform participants and get recording consent. The consent profile includes the following:

- Pre-call email: Sends an email 10 minutes prior to the meeting reminding the participant that the meeting is due to start and that it will be recorded
- Consent page: Displays a consent page before the participant joins the meeting where they can give explicit consent to being recorded
- Audio prompt: Plays an audio message when a participant joins the meeting announcing that the call is being recorded

The settings in the consent profile are set by your Tech admin and apply to all calls. You can’t disable the settings for an individual call.

chunks.text:
Get consent to record calls > Multiple web-conferencing providers:
Your consent profile may include more than one web-conferencing provider.

If you use Microsoft Outlook and you schedule meetings using the Gong calendar add-on, you can set up different meetings with different providers. As long as the provider is included in your consent profile, you will be able to get consent to record the meeting.

If you use Google Calendar, you can schedule meetings with the default provider defined in the consent profile.

The web conference providers supported in Gong are:

- Zoom
- Google Meet
- WebEx
- Microsoft Teams
- GoToMeeting
- Amazon Chime
- RingCentral Meetings
- RingCentral Video
- join.me
- Uber Conference
- Appointlet

If you use a non supported provider or a provider not selected in your consent profile, Gong won’t be able to display the consent page. If your call is not going to be recorded (for example, if you set the call as private), then the consent page will not appear before the call.

Get consent to record calls > Meeting link types:
There are two types of links that you can use to create meetings that display the consent page.

- Dynamic meeting links: Every meeting has a unique link.

In some cases, when you make calls using Gong Connect, your call may appear to the recipient as spam or unknown. This may be due to either the recipient or caller carrier, and is the result of STIR/SHAKEN* protocols, which aim to prevent companies from caller ID spoofing on public telephone networks.

As a Gong verified customer, your company calls should go through, and will most likely be classified as Unknown, but this ultimately depends on the carriers.

If you’re experiencing issues, or want to increase the chance that your Gong Connect call goes through and is verified, we suggest that you register your number in the Free Caller Registry.

Once your number is registered here, there is a greater chance that it will be identified as “Verified” by major US cellular providers. This process must be done separately for each number that you use to make calls via Gong Connect. The process can take a few weeks to complete.

If you’re experiencing issues with blocked calls or call identification, contact Gong Support.

*STIR/SHAKEN is a suite of protocols and procedures that have been implemented in the United States and Canada to combat robocalls.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

chunks.text:
Set up CallRail:
You (or the CallRail admin) need to set up the initial connection between CalllRail and Gong.

1. Request an account number and API key from CallRail. These are input when adding CallRail and used to authenticate the access to CallRail.
2. Go to the CallRail website and define each person using Gong as a User.
3. For each user, provide their email address and all their phone numbers. This enables Gong to link the calls to the correct user.
4. Set up a call flow for inbound calls for the total number of users.
5. Go to Manage Account > Manage > Details, and under General Settings select Allow my team to record outbound calls.

Trackers are tools that identify when words, phrases or concepts are mentioned in calls, allowing you to know what your reps and customers are talking about. In addition to out-of-the-box trackers that come with Gong, you can set up your own trackers, according to your company’s business priorities, and what you want to capture insights around. See Trackers: Overview for more details.

The TRACKERS table includes both smart trackers and keyword trackers. A new row is added to the table for each tracker in the system.

| WORKSPACE_ID | Snowflake: varcharBigQuery: stringDatabricks: stringRedshift: varchar(MAX)S3: Byte_array, UTF8 | NULL | The workspace the tracker is associated with |

| ROW_ID | Snowflake: varcharBigQuery: stringDatabricks: stringRedshift: varchar(MAX)S3: Byte_array, UTF8 | Unchanged | The ID to identify the row in the table. |

In the Snowflake database, a record is inserted for the tracker with all the keywords defined and in addition for each keyword in the keyword tracker. For example, if you have a tracker which is named pricing which includes the keywords, budget, price and discount, the tracker is entered to the database as follows:

| tracker_id | name | keywords | type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| t_1 | Pricing | [budget, price, discount] | keyword_tracker |
| t_2 | Pricing / budget | [budget] | keyword_tracker |
| t_3 | Pricing / price | [price] | keyword_tracker |
| t_4 | Pricing / discount | [discount] | keyword_tracker |

Smart trackers are added to the table as follows:

| tracker_id | name | keywords | type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| t_6 | My Smart Tracker | NULL | smart_tracker |

If a meeting is scheduled in Gong and you’re using pre-call emails, prospects receive an email notification before the call starts. If the meeting is canceled, you want to make sure prospects don’t receive that email notification. To ensure this, you need to make sure the scheduled recording is canceled in Gong, not just in the calendar. To do this, you first need to understand how the meeting was originally scheduled, since canceling the email, and the recording, may occur automatically or it may need to be done manually.

chunks.text:
Canceling calls scheduled in the calendar:
Calls scheduled in your calendar are updated or deleted automatically as long as you are set up to integrate with your email provider and your Gong settings are set to record calls. Gong scans your calendar every 15 to 30 minutes and any changes are updated in Gong. This includes recurring meetings.

1. Make sure when you cancel a recurring meeting to cancel all events in the calendar.
2. Send cancellation emails to all the event guests. This ensures that everyone receives the cancellation request, and that the meeting doesn’t end up still being scheduled in Gong because another Gong user was invited to the meeting.

chunks.text:
Canceling calls scheduled manually:
If you scheduled the meeting manually, either by adding the Gong assistant or in Gong in the Schedule new recording page, to cancel the meeting you must:

- For meetings scheduled in your calendar. When deleting/canceling the calendar event, you will receive a confirmation via email. Forward the cancelation email to the Gong assistant
- For meetings scheduled in Gong. In Gong, go to Home > View upcoming calls. Clickbeside the call name and then click Cancel recording. You’ll be given the option to cancel this recording only, or cancel this recording and any future meetings in the series.

chunks.text:
Canceling calls scheduled manually > Shadow calendar events:
In some cases, a rep may have created a completely separate calendar event in their own calendar with the exact same name and details as the original meeting. In these cases, prospects could still receive the pre-call notification email, even if the original meeting is canceled, and it will be related to the shadow event.

chunks.text:
Canceling calls scheduled manually > Users who no longer have permission to manually schedule calls:
It’s possible that when a meeting was manually scheduled, a user had permission to manually record calls and at a later stage, they don’t have this permission. In such cases, the user won’t be able to cancel a manual meeting by sending the cancellation email to the assistant email, so they must check the Gong homepage for remaining meetings and cancel the recording there instead.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

Gong’s AI revenue platform automatically records, transcribes, and analyzes your calls. This intelligent call-capture understands context, such as business relevant topics, and can identify patterns across calls to create actionable insights in the form of briefs.

Gong highlights key topics, objections, and commitments, so that customer-facing roles stay fully engaged during meetings. Searchable transcripts and AI-powered briefs allow for fast knowledge sharing across the organization, while trends and successful approaches are easily identifiable to implement team improvements.

This quick start guide helps you capture the right calls and shows you how to stop, review, and share recordings.

chunks.text:
Record a call:
Automatic call recording according to your organization’s criteria is set up by your company’s tech admin, although you can customize certain settings.

To ensure your call is recorded:

1. The Gong calendar add-on lets you add Gong meeting links to Google or Outlook events. Your tech admin may have installed it company-wide, but if not, you’ll need to install it yourself:
  1. Google Workspace: Go to Gong for Google Workspace and click Install, then follow the prompts.
  2. Outlook: Go to Gong for Outlook and click Get it now, then follow the prompts. Then add it through Outlook’s Get add-ins menu.
2. Set up a meeting in your calendar at least 30 minutes in advance.
3. Add the web conference link using the Gong calendar add-on:
  1. Google Calendar: In Add video conferencing, select Gong meeting.
  2. Outlook: Click the Gong button in the actions bar, then click Add a Gong Meeting.

There are several ways to troubleshoot when your calls aren’t automatically recording.

chunks.text:
Record calls manually:
There are several reasons that a call isn’t automatically set to record, for example, last-minute meetings, internal calls (check with admin), or company settings.

You have two options to manually record:

1. Schedule from your Gong homepage
  1. Under Conversations, click followed by Schedule new recording.
  2. Enter the meeting details, including: Web conference URL, the workspace, description or title, participant emails if you want to link the call to an account or opportunity, whether it's an external or internal call.
  3. Set the recording to start Now or Later.
  4. Click SCHEDULE CALL.

Note:If you're scheduling a last minute call, it may take up to 10 minutes for Gong to start recording.

1. Invite the Gong assistant
  1. Click your profile icon and select My settings.
  2. In Web conference recording, click Copy to copy your company's unique Gong assistant email address and add to your calendar event's participant list.
  3. You'll receive an email either confirming whether Gong can or can’t record the call.

Best practices for successful recording:
- Schedule meetings at least 30 minutes in advance.
- Don't mark meetings as Private in your calendar.
- Check your company’s consent settings: If your consent profile requires written consent, participants must accept via the consent page or the call won’t be recorded.
- Allow all participants to enter meetings via web browser in your web conference provider settings.
- If you’re using a waiting room, allow Gong to enter.

Stop a call recording > After a call has taken place:
If you didn't prevent or stop a recording, you can delete it, which permanently removes the recording and its data from Gong. This is available based on your permissions. To delete, open the call page, click and select Delete recording.

If you want to keep the recording but control access to it, you can make the call private. In the call page, click in the top right corner and select Set call as private.

Gong Connect, Gong’s mobile dialer, is a VoIP service built into the Gong mobile app. It works over both Wi-Fi and cellular networks, automatically recording calls and incorporating them into Gong for analysis and visibility.

With Gong Connect, you can make and receive calls directly from the mobile app, ensuring key conversations with prospects and customers are captured, even when you’re away from your desk.

Users with an Engage seat have access to both the web and mobile dialer, including full inbound and outbound calling capabilities. Users without an Engage seat can use the mobile dialer with limited functionality (outbound calls are available only from a verified personal number).

Note: This feature must be enabled by your Tech admin before it appears in the Gong mobile app. If you don’t see Gong Connect, it means it hasn’t been enabled for your account yet.

Before making or receiving calls, complete a short verification process in the Gong mobile app.

Make outbound calls:
Outbound calls made through the Gong mobile app are automatically recorded, analyzed, and tracked in Gong, giving you full visibility into conversations even when you’re on the go.

To make an outbound call:

1. Tap the Gong Connect call button .
2. Choose one of the following:
  - Select a contact from your contact list or recent calls.
  - Use Free dial to manually enter a phone number.

Note: Only calls placed through the Gong app are recorded.Contacts synced from your connected CRM, as well as contacts you’ve emailed, are available in Gong Connect.Free-dial calls are recorded but aren’t automatically linked to a specific account or opportunity.Gong Connect supports multiple phone number formats, but you must always include the country and area code (for example: +1 (555) 555-1234).

Calls are placed from your personal number by default. If you’re an Engage user with a business number configured, you can place calls from that number instead.

During the call, you can mute yourself, use speaker mode, access the dial pad, or cancel the recording. If you cancel the recording, it’s permanently deleted.

After the call ends, you can set a call outcome.

Receive inbound calls on mobile:
Engage users can receive inbound calls directly in the Gong mobile app. When a prospect or customer calls your business number, the call rings on both your desktop web dialer and your mobile device, so you can answer from wherever you are.

Why inbound calls on mobile matter:

- Never miss important callbacks: Answer calls while away from your desk or between meetings.
- Full caller context: See the caller’s name, title, company, and phone number (when available).
- Automatic recording: Inbound calls are recorded and logged in Gong just like outbound calls.
- No personal number required: Keep your personal number private while staying connected.

chunks.text:
Receive inbound calls on mobile > Setting up inbound calls:
When you install the Gong mobile app, you’ll be prompted to grant the permissions required for inbound calling:

- Notifications (for incoming call alerts)
- Microphone (for recording audio)
- Phone call management
- Bluetooth connectivity (when applicable)

Once these permissions are granted, inbound calls are activated automatically in the app. Any personal forwarding number is deactivated to prevent calls from ringing in multiple places.

Important:If notifications are deactivated, you’ll be prompted to enable them so you don’t miss incoming calls.

Receive inbound calls on mobile > App behavior and special scenarios:
Inbound calling behaves consistently across different states:

- Device locked: You can answer the call, but in-call actions are limited until the device is unlocked.
- Session expired: Calls are still received and recorded based on company settings, but you must sign in again to use in-call controls.
- Signed out: Inbound calls aren’t received.
- Already on a call: You’ll see an End call & Answer option to switch to the new caller.

Call trust protocols and recording regulations:
In the US and Canada, call trust protocols help protect against illegal robocalls and spoofing. These protocols may sometimes cause unidentified numbers to be flagged as spam. Here’s how to improve the likelihood that the calls you make via Gong Connect go through.

Important:Call recording regulations vary by country and region. It’s your responsibility to comply with local consent laws.

Some US states require consent from more than one party. Gong plays a reminder before calls connect, prompting you to inform participants that the call is being recorded. You can always pause or delete the recording during the call.

Your company may also use different recording methods based on region or state.

FAQs:
How much does the Gong Connect service cost?

Gong Connect is free of charge.

Is CRM integration required to use Gong Connect?

No, it’s not. You can free dial with Gong Connect without a CRM integration. To search for contacts on mobile, and for automatic call association you do need a CRM integration.

Can I call contacts stored on my phone via the Gong mobile app?

At the moment, you can only call CRM contacts that are in Gong via the Gong mobile (there is no connection between your phone contacts and the Gong mobile app.)

Can I free dial via the Gong mobile app?

Yes, you can free dial from Gong Connect, in the Gong mobile app, and this call can be recorded by Gong.

What’s my caller ID when I call someone?

During the open beta, the caller ID will be your current mobile phone number. Anyone you call can recognize your phone number, and won’t be able to see that you called via another dialing app.

Are international calls supported?

Yes, international calls are supported.

Do I need to do anything as an admin to enable inbound calls on mobile?

No additional setup is required. If inbound calls are already enabled on the desktop dialer, they will automatically work on mobile once users install the app and grant the necessary permissions.

Which inbound calls are routed to the Gong mobile app?

Only calls made to your assigned business number or company business numbers you’ve recently used are routed to the Gong mobile app. Calls made directly to your personal (private) number are not supported and will not ring in the mobile app.

  - Completed
  - Removed Response

  - Completed
  - Removed Response

- In progress

- Finished (no reply)
- Finished (meeting booked)
- Finished (removed manually)
- Bounced
- Removed (other)
- To-do expired
- No license
- Person deleted
- Flow deleted

Gong synchronizes data with Salesforce to keep tasks up to date. Tasks are updated for a variety of reasons, following both changes initiated by the user, for example, changing the time of a meeting, and changes following system driven updates, such as adding the call summary to a task.
chunks.title: Changes that cause task and event updates

chunks.text:
Activity updates:
Updates occur when new context or information becomes available about an activity.

- The timestamp of a task or event for all types of Gong activities may be updated even when the data that changed in Gong isn’t exported to Salesforce.
- New data is exported. For example, if a new account is added to the CRM, and there is an existing call with that account.
- Changes to meeting invites including:
  - Schedule modifications

What’s a changes widget:
The changes widget visualizes how the total amount in each forecast category changed over a selected period for a selected line of business. The chart shows the reason for the change, such as deals pushed out to future periods, amount decrease/increase, and deals that ended up being closed-lost.

Learn more about changes reports here.

chunks.text:
Building a changes widget:
Note:Your profile must include the relevant permission to create and manage widgets to dashboards

To build a new changes widget:

1. Select your dashboard, click +New widget and select Changes from the gallery.
2. In the dashboard header, click the edit icon to rename your widget and, optionally, + Add description.
3. Under Line of business, select the line of business for the widget.
4. Under Forecast, select the default forecast category to include in the widget. If you want viewers to not be able to change this selection, uncheck Add dropdown to widget.
5. Under Changes tracked, select the time interval for the tracked changes.
6. Under Select team and period, you’ll notice the team member and date fields are set to be dynamic and respond to whatever is selected in your dashboard. You can change them to fixed values. Note:If you select fixed values for the team member and period, the widget would no longer respond to selections made on the dashboard level.
7. Play with the preview option on the right. You can click the Pre-changes and Post-changes bars to drill into the deals behind the changes, giving you a deeper understanding of how and why your pipeline moved.
8. When you’re happy with the preview result on the right, click Save.

chunks.text:
Start from a call:
Start from a call when you want to work with one conversation. On a call page, Gong Assistant uses information from that call and related Gong data, including account, deal, and participant information.

This is the best place to start when you want to:

- Understand what happened in a specific call and related interactions with the same account or participants
- Ask follow-up questions in the same thread
- Request different response formats, such as bullet points, summaries, or drafted follow-up content
- Review citations and jump back to the source in the call or related data

Choose this starting point when the question is really about this call.

chunks.text:
Start from Search:
Start from Search when you want to analyze multiple conversations instead of reviewing calls one by one. On Search, Gong Assistant uses the conversations included in the current search results.

This is the best place to start when you want to:

- identify themes, patterns, or feedback across a group of calls
- ask broad questions about a set of matching conversations
- work from a scope defined by search filters

Each answer is tied to the search results that were active when you asked the question. If you change the filters, new questions use the updated results, while earlier answers stay tied to the earlier search state.

Choose this starting point when the question is about a set of calls, not a single conversation.

Both Gong's API and Data Cloud allow you to access your Gong data for analytics purposes. Each solution has different attributes making them suitable for different use-case scenarios.

While the API includes additional functionality beyond analytics, it is possible to extract data via various API endpoints as well as from the Gong data cloud. This table describes the different points to consider if you are choosing between setting up the Gong data cloud and setting up an integration with the Calls and Stats APIs.
chunks.body:
Both Gong's API and Data Cloud allow you to access your Gong data for analytics purposes. Each solution has different attributes making them suitable for different use-case scenarios.

While the API includes additional functionality beyond analytics, it is possible to extract data via various API endpoints as well as from the Gong data cloud. This table describes the different points to consider if you are choosing between setting up the Gong data cloud and setting up an integration with the Calls and Stats APIs.
chunks.title: Choosing between Gong's API and Data Cloud for analytics

chunks.text:
| Attribute | Gong data cloud | Gong API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data structure and analytics | Designed specifically for analytics with normalized tablesBuilt-in soft delete mechanism to track deleted recordsIncludes pre-built query templates ("cookbooks") for common use casesData is immediately ready for analysis | Returns nested JSON data that typically requires transformationRequires additional ETL processing to prepare data for analysisMore complex data structure that may need flattening for analytics use |
| Data freshness | Daily updatesAppropriate for most analytical use cases where daily refreshes suffice | Near real-time data accessSuitable for use cases requiring up-to-the-minute information |
| Implementation effort | Simple connection process Minimal technical expertise requiredNo coding necessaryReady-to-use analytics-friendly format | Requires technical resources to implementDevelopment time needed to write and maintain codeData must be adapted for analytics purposes |
| Storage and costs | Provides access to the complete data schemaFor reference, large enterprises with 5,000+ users and 6+ years of history typically use around 200GB of storage totalDaily updates are typically a few hundred megabytesSnowflake integration is based on data sharing and there aren’t any storage costs. The other integrations are based on data copying and a small cost is included | Allows more granular control over what data is retrievedStorage requirements depend on implementation and retention choices |
| Data breadth or depth | Includes all data required to perform analytics in a BI toolIncludes emails, meetings and more extensive usage dataAnalytics friendly data model | Provides extensive data on calls |
| Supported systems | SnowflakeBigQueryDatabricks |  |

chunks.text:
When to choose each solution:
Use the Gong data cloud if:

- Daily data updates meet your needs
- You have limited technical resources or want to minimize technical implementation effort
- You need comprehensive analytics capabilities out of the box for example:
  - Activity reporting: Gong data cloud includes calls, emails and unrecorded meetings, which make activity reporting more accurate
  - Gong usage: Gong data cloud includes a very detailed dataset for Gong usage. The API doesn’t expose the equivalent data.
  - Productivity reports
  - Competitor analysis, using a pre-built Gong cookbook.
- You're starting fresh with Gong analytics integration

Use the API if:

- You need more frequent than daily updates, for example Engage users who report on their team’s activities multiple times a day
- You are an Engage user and you want reports on Engage flows, such as which prospects are assigned to which flows
- You use an unsupported data warehouse platform
- You're already integrated with the API and the information available is sufficient for your needs
- You need specific data points not yet available in the Gong data cloud
- You have use cases, such as audit logs, importing data to Gong, which can only be done via the API

chunks.text:
Build out your coaching habits > Check out your call stats:
Reviewing a call can be much more than just listening to how it went. Review your interaction stats for each call to see what your talk times and call dynamics are like, figure out whether you're talking too much or too little, and learn from that to course correct.

This is measured data, so besides leveraging it to become more aware of yourself, you can also follow how your performance improves over time.

- To see interaction stats, clickon the right side of the call.

The stats you see include:

- Talk Ratio: The percentage of the call in which you spoke. The recommendation is for no more than 65% of the time.
- Longest Monologue: The duration, in minutes, of the longest speech you made. The recommended length is no more than 2m 30s.
- Longest Customer’s Story: The duration, in minutes, of the longest customer-talking segment. This can include short interruptions by you. The recommended length is between 1 and 2 minutes.
- Interactivity: This shows how often the conversation switched back and forth between you and your customer, and is on a 0–10 scale. The recommended grade is 5 or more.
- Patience: This shows how long you waited after the customer completed talking before you took over the conversation. The recommended wait time is between 0.6 and 1 second.

If your org has enabled Whisper for call interaction, on each stat you'll see a green or yellow dot next to the stats icon. Green indicates that you are within the recommended range, and yellow indicates that you are outside the recommended range.

Configurable forecast boards let you control how forecast data is structured, displayed, and calculated, so you can match your board setup to how your team actually forecasts. This setup works for any forecasting motion, including new business, renewals, and hybrid models.

This article details the process of building and managing configurable forecast boards.
chunks.title: Create and edit forecast boards

chunks.text:
Before you start:
Before you start building a forecast board, make sure the metrics and targets required for your board are configured. You can go back and build new ones and make changes as needed.

chunks.text:
Before you start > Build a forecast board:
To build a new configurable forecast board:

Go to Revenue > Forecast, click > Add board

Note: Until legacy forecast boards are fully retired, both configurable boards and legacy boards are available.

The sidebar has all the sections listed and you can use this to go straight to the right place.

General settings:

- Details
- Board columns
- Period
- Cadence
- Company snapshot

Deal-related settings:

- Drill-down view
- Briefs
- Update CRM
- Warnings
- Deal analytics

When you’ve completed setting up your forecast board, click Save. Once it's saved you can share it with others, duplicate it and make tweaks, edit or delete it.

Before you start > Briefs:
Define which briefs appear in the Briefs and Score tabs of the deal panel that opens when team members inspect a deal.

Deal review: Select a default brief type that highlights key deal updates and insights, and define the time period the brief covers when generated. Team members can adjust these settings when inspecting a deal.

chunks.text:
Before you start > Deal analytics:
In Deal analytics, turn on analytics to generate out-of-the-box trends, changes, accuracy and pacing reports.

Note:Deal analytics give you insight into pipeline trends, including forecasting accuracy and reasons behind changes in forecast amounts. Analytics isn’t supported for boards with multiple fields, opportunity teams, opportunity splits, and multi-currency.

1. Turn on analytics: Turn on if this board tracks open vs. closed-won pipeline based on consistent user, date, and amount CRM fields.
2. Set deal attributes: Set the CRM fields associated with deals included in the reports.
3. Define deal status indicators: Define the conditions for open and closed-won deals.
4. Set target: Set the target to measure your bookings against, and track performance and attainment in trends and pacing reports.
5. Define forecast categories: Define the conditions for deals in each forecast category.
6. Show projection in board columns: Select which column to display projection in, and set reference periods. Turn on projection to help team members see where they are likely to land by the end of the period. Projection is based on deal attributes (2) and status indicators (3).

Note:Projection is based on deals that were expected to close in the reference period, and whether they were won or lost by the end of the period. They are based on deal attributes (a) and status indicators (c).

Once your forecast board settings are complete, click Save. Once saved, the board can be edited, duplicated or hidden.

Note:To align your reports with changes made to your data, reach out to your Revenue Architect (RA) after your board is set up. Learn about historical data backfill

Inactive team members are hidden by default and only appear on the board if they have relevant data for the selected forecast period (such as a target, submission, or deal inventory). No action is required. When shown, inactive users appear with an Inactive badge.

Example: Brian left the company in Q3 FY26

- Historical view (Q2 FY26): If Brian contributed to the forecast during this period, he appears on the board with an Inactive badge, preserving visibility into historical submissions and attainment.
- Current view (Q3 FY26): If Brian has no relevant data for this period, he’s hidden from the board.

chunks.title: Configurable forecast FAQs

chunks.text:
There are two ways to keep old deals rolled up to their original team:

- Create a placeholder user and assign the historical deals to that user.
- Create a placeholder user and assign the new deals to that user.

In both methods, historical deals stay rolled up to the original team, while new ones are rolled up to the new one.

Can I delete a forecast column?

You can’t delete a forecast column, but you can hide it from the board. This means that the column is removed from the board, and nobody is reminded to update a number for it. Historical data is retained and is available if you unhide the column in the future.

A renewal forecast board is used by revenue teams to track and predict upcoming contract renewals for existing customers. It typically includes customer accounts with contracts nearing expiration, forecasted renewal amounts, probability or confidence levels of renewal, and status indicators.

The goal of a renewal forecast board is to help teams proactively manage retention, forecast recurring revenue, and identify churn risks.

This article provides a basic recipe for a renewal forecast board. You can use it as is or adjust it to your specific forecast needs.

TipHead over to our Academy to see the Renewal Forecast Board Starter recipe

chunks.text:
Step 1: Build your metrics:
1. Build the following basic metrics:

- Up for renewal:
  - Base object: Deals
  - Aggregation: Sum of UFR Amount
  - Filtered by: Record Type = Renewal
  - Team member: Owner/CSM
  - Period: Close/Renewal date
- Won renewals:
  - Base object: Deals
  - Aggregation: Sum of ARR Impact Account
  - Filtered by: Record Type = Renewal, Status = Closed won
  - Team member: Owner/CSM
  - Period: Close Date/Renewal Date
- Open renewals:
  - Base object: Deals
  - Aggregation: Sum of ARR Impact Account
  - Filtered by: Record Type = Renewal, Status = Open
  - Team member: Owner/CSM
  - Period: Close/Renewal date
- Lost renewals:
  - Base object: Deals
  - Aggregation: Sum of ARR Impact Account
  - Filtered by: Record Type = Renewal, Status = Closed lost
  - Team member: Owner/CSM
  - Period: Close/Renewal date
- Forecasted renewals:
  - Base object: Deals
  - Aggregation: Sum of ARR Impact Account
  - Filtered by: Record Type = Renewal, Forecast = Commit, Most likely
  - Team member: Owner/CSM
  - Period: Close/Renewal date

1. Build the following formula metrics:

- Total Retention:
  - Formula: Won Renewals/Up for renewal
  - Format: Percent (%)
- Forecasted Retention:
  - Formula: (Forecasted renewals + Won renewals)/ Up for renewal
  - Format: Percent (%)
- Forecasted Churn:
  - Formula: Up for renewal - (Won renewals + Forecasted renewals)
  - Format: Currency
- Total Churn:
  - Formula: Closed renewals - Won renewals
  - Format: Currency

Call outcomes allow team members to record the result of each call. Team members use call outcomes to track conversations and manage follow-up activities. Managers use call outcomes in Engage analytics to analyze calling performance.

Gong provides a default set of call outcomes. You can create custom call outcomes to support your organization's sales process and reporting requirements.

Custom call outcomes allow you to classify call results in a way that reflects your team's workflow. Because each call outcome is assigned a Connect status, custom call outcomes can improve the accuracy of metrics such as connect rate.

Call outcomes are configured at the company level. All teams use the same set of call outcomes.

Note:The available call outcome settings depend on your CRM integration.If Gong is connected to Salesforce, you can create, edit, and delete custom call outcomes.If Gong is connected to a CRM other than Salesforce, you can set call outcomes as required, but you can’t manage existing call outcomes or create new ones.

chunks.title: About call outcomes

chunks.text:
Default call outcomes:
Gong includes a set of default call outcomes which you can as-is or create custom call outcomes to support your team's workflow. The call outcomes are organized into two groups:

No answer outcomes:

- No voicemail: Rep does not leave a voicemail.
- Left voicemail: Rep leaves a voicemail.
- Not in service: The number is not in service.
- Busy: The line is busy.

Answered outcomes:

- Follow up: The prospect asked for more information, asked to call back, or has not decided yet.
- Meeting booked: The prospect agreed to meet, or the rep sent a calendar invite.
- Bad timing: The prospect said they are not interested right now or in the near future.
- Has a solution: The prospect said they have a solution with a competitor.
- Bad persona: The prospect said they are not the right person and did not provide a referral.
- Wrong number: The number is incorrect.
- Gave referral: The prospect directed the rep to someone else.
- Bad fit: Either side determined it is not a good fit.
- Opt out: The prospect asked not to be contacted again.
- Hung up: The prospect hung up.
- Gatekeeper: A gatekeeper answered and the rep could not reach the intended person.
- Not interested (other): The prospect said they are not interested.

As an admin, you can manage how Gong Engage respects your organization's compliance requirements and your prospects' communication preferences for emails and calls. Tech admin, Business admin Gong Engage*

As an admin, you can manage how Gong Engage respects your organization's compliance requirements and your prospects' communication preferences for emails and calls. By aligning with global privacy regulations (like GDPR and CCPA), you can ensure reps only engage with contacts who have the appropriate consent.

Compliance policies apply to contacts and leads, not team members at your company. Policies are applied based on who the contact or lead is, not which team member is communicating with them.
chunks.title: Configure compliance settings

chunks.text:
Map your opt out fields:
Admin center > Engage > Compliance settings > Opt-out controls

Before creating policies, you need to define how Gong syncs opt-out data with your CRM. This is managed in the Opt-out controls tab. Mapping the fields in the Opt-out controls tab ensures that if a user opts out via a Gong unsubscribe link, the corresponding field in your CRM is updated.

The mapping of opt-out fields has moved from the Engage CRM setup page to this centralized Compliance settings area for a more streamlined configuration experience.

NoteMapping these fields is mandatory. If you do not map your CRM fields in the Opt-out controls tab, Gong won’t be able to identify which contacts have opted out, and your compliance policies will not be enforced.

1. Choose your mapping strategy based on your company's needs:
  - Global (single opt-out): Map one CRM field (ex: "Do Not Contact") that applies to all communication channels simultaneously.
  - Granular (channel-specific): Map separate CRM fields for Emails and Calls for both Contacts and Leads.
2. Select the specific CRM fields to ensure two-way syncing between Gong and your CRM.
chunks.body:
Admin center > Engage > Compliance settings > Opt-out controls

Before creating policies, you need to define how Gong syncs opt-out data with your CRM. This is managed in the Opt-out controls tab. Mapping the fields in the Opt-out controls tab ensures that if a user opts out via a Gong unsubscribe link, the corresponding field in your CRM is updated.

The mapping of opt-out fields has moved from the Engage CRM setup page to this centralized Compliance settings area for a more streamlined configuration experience.

NoteMapping these fields is mandatory. If you do not map your CRM fields in the Opt-out controls tab, Gong won’t be able to identify which contacts have opted out, and your compliance policies will not be enforced.

1. Choose your mapping strategy based on your company's needs:
  - Global (single opt-out): Map one CRM field (ex: "Do Not Contact") that applies to all communication channels simultaneously.
  - Granular (channel-specific): Map separate CRM fields for Emails and Calls for both Contacts and Leads.
2. Select the specific CRM fields to ensure two-way syncing between Gong and your CRM.

chunks.text:
Configure compliance policies:
Once your mandatory fields are mapped, use the Compliance policies tab to define how Gong handles outreach based on different regional or business requirements. A compliance policy is a centralized set of rules that defines how and when your team can interact with contacts and leads. It combines three elements:

- People: Which contacts and leads does this apply to (ex: all contacts in the UK)?
- Opt-out controls: What communication is allowed for emails and calls?
- Email tracking: Can we track opens and clicks for these individuals?

chunks.text:
Configure compliance policies > Default compliance policy:
Your Engage setup comes with a global default policy. This policy acts as a "safety net" to ensure any contact not specifically covered by a custom policy is still governed by your baseline company rules. You should edit its restriction levels to align with your standard global business needs.

You cannot delete this policy, and its targeting (People) cannot be modified because it applies to everyone by default.

chunks.text:
Configure compliance policies > Creating and customizing compliance policies:
1. Click Add compliance policy
2. Define policy targeting (people) to choose which contacts and leads the policy apples to. Custom policies use CRM-based filters to identify their audience. For example, you can create a policy that only triggers if:
  1. Contact country = Germany
  2. Lead source = Inbound
3. For each channel, define the level of restriction applied when a contact/channel is marked as "opted out" in your CRM:
  1. For emails:
    - Allow reps to send emails and add to flows: Reps can send one-off emails and add to flows.
    - Allow reps to send emails and skip email flow steps: Reps maintain the ability to send one-off emails and add to flows, but email steps are skipped.
    - Prevent sending emails and skip email flow steps: All email communication is blocked, and reps can’t send one-off emails. If using granular opt-out mapping, reps can still add to flows, but email steps are skipped. If using global opt-out mapping, reps can’t add to flows.
  2. For calls:
    - Allow reps to call and add to flows: Reps can make one-off calls and add to call flow steps.
    - Allow reps to call and skip call flow steps: Reps maintain the ability to make one-off calls and add to flows, but call steps are skipped.
    - Prevent calling and skip call flow steps: All call communication is blocked, and reps can’t make one-off calls. If using granular opt-out mapping, reps can still add to flows, but call steps are skipped. If using global opt-out mapping, reps can’t add to flows.
4. Define email tracking settings. Manage privacy by controlling how reps monitor engagement for people under this policy:
  - Track email opens: Set this to Allowed or Not allowed to control whether email open tracking is available for these contacts and leads.
  - Track email link clicks: Set this to Allowed or Not allowed to control whether email link click tracking is available for these contacts and leads.

Managing multiple policies:
Create as many policies as your business needs. When a person matches multiple criteria, Gong uses the following logic:

- Gong checks the contact against your policies starting from the top of the list.
- The first policy on the list that matches the contact’s CRM data is the one that is applied.
- Drag and drop policies to change their priority at any time.

*The features available to you depend on your company’s plan and your assigned seats.

Who can use this: Tech adminAvailable on: Gong Foundation

Where to go: Admin center > Agent studio

Associating activities such as calls and emails to your CRM entities provides proper context for your Gong activities. Once a Gong activity is properly associated, you will know who a call was made to, the company they work with and the deal the activity is for. As there can be several accounts or deals that a conversation can be associated with, you can customize and control the association logic so that the association is tailored to your specific CRM implementation.

To get the most accurate associations, make sure the configurations reflect how data is stored in your CRM. For example, if you don’t store the deal owner details in the CRM, set the deal owner to off.

Before updating your settings, test how those changes affect associations. For more details see Simulate activity association.

When you click Update settings:

- The settings are applied to new activities in Gong.
- Select Reassociate activities from the last 30 days. This may take up to 24 hours to update activities occurring in the last 30 days. When activities that were exported to the CRM are reassociated, they may be re-exported and associated with the new account or deal.

You can also apply new settings to a single call. In the Call page menu, select Apply association rules to this call.

chunks.title: Configure CRM entity association

chunks.text:
Stages in CRM entity association:
The stages of CRM entity association are:

1. Generating a list contacts and leads that could be associated with the activity: A list of CRM contacts and leads is generated for each activity attendee. Attendees are identified by comparing their phone number to all phone number fields in the CRM or to the standard email field. You can set additional email fields for Gong to identify contacts and leads by. A maximum of five contacts or leads per attendee are chosen. If there are more than five duplicate contacts or leads in the CRM, the five with the most recent last modified date are selected. Contacts are given preference over leads.
2. Generating a list of accounts that could be associated with the activity: The account list includes:
  1. Accounts that a Gong activity participant, who is also a contact in the CRM, activity belongs to.
  2. Optional. Accounts of deals where the participant is defined as a contact role. This account may be different to the account the participant belongs to.
  3. Optional: Accounts with the same website domain as the participant’s email domain. This is selected by default and it recommended for cases where sales activities include participants that are still not contacts in the CRM
  4. Optional: Accounts that are related to the participant’s account, such as a parent account.
3. Identifying the account most likely to be associated with the activity: If more than one account is found, set how Gong should choose the correct account to associate with the activity.
4. Identifying the deals most likely to be associated with the activity: Once we have associated an account, set the parameters for how Gong should choose the correct deal to associate with the activity.

Stage 1: Contact and lead association:
Gong identifies activity participants and checks whether they appear in your CRM as contacts or leads. These settings control which CRM fields are checked and how to handle participants who match both record types.

To open contact and lead association settings:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. Click the Agent Studio tab.

4. In Contact and lead association, click Contact email fields, and select additional fields that contain contact email addresses.
5. Click Lead email fields, and select additional fields that contain lead email addresses.

Gong checks these fields when looking up contact and lead records for activity participants.

chunks.text:
Stage 2: Account association:
CRM contacts are always associated with an account. Therefore, participants who are also CRM contacts have an associated account. We start by generating a list of those accounts. However, it’s possible that the correct account is different to the account the participant is associated with and therefore we provide options for expanding the list of accounts.

Note:If you have multiple duplicate contacts in your CRM, we associate a maximum of five contacts to the activity.

chunks.text:
Stage 2: Account association > Narrow down the account list > Filter logic:
There is no limit to the number of filters you can set up. The logic for the filters is:

1. Is filters are grouped together in an OR function so that all values set are used to build a list of which accounts to include in the association
2. Is Not filters are grouped together in an OR function so that all values set are used to build a list of which accounts to exclude from the association
3. To include an account for association, the account must be in the include (Is list) and must not be in the exclude (Is Not list).

2. If you toggle On, you must provide the name of the CRM field you store the account owner in.

Stage 2: Account association > If multiple accounts are still options:
If multiple accounts can still be associated with the activity, for example, there is a call with two account owners participating, we provide two options for selecting a single account:

- Number of CRM contacts: Associates the account with more contacts participating in the activity. If out of two possible accounts, one account has 2 participants and the other has 4, select the account with 4 participants. If this is activated and there is a single account, we associate the activity to that account.
- Most recent CRM entry: Associates the account with the most recent entry in the CRM, such as the newer account, or the account with the most recent update. For this option select:
  - Date field for the most recent CRM entry: The date field in the CRM which you want to use to determine the most recent entry. For example, if you want to choose the newer account, select the date field which holds the account creation date.
  - Number of accounts to associate: At this stage if a single account can’t be chosen, you might prefer to associate the activity to all the accounts found, maximum of 10, or limit association to 1 account.

Stage 3: Deal association:
Once we know which account the activity is associated with, we can identify deals which the activity may be related to. If you don’t want your activities associated with deals, click Disable to disable deal association.
chunks.body: Once we know which account the activity is associated with, we can identify deals which the activity may be related to. If you don’t want your activities associated with deals, click Disable to disable deal association.

chunks.text:
Stage 3: Deal association > Create a list of potential deals:
The list of deals includes those that were open around the time the conversation took place. Identifying open deals is based on the value of two fields:

- Deal status: set by the rep, indicates whether the deal is open or closed.
- Deal close date: a rough estimate of when the rep expects the deal to close

If these fields aren’t maintained, there may be deals where the status is open and the close date was several weeks or months previous. In addition, conversations just before or after a deal is opened or closed may still be related to that deal.

Therefore, the list of potential deals to associate is made up of:

- Deals opened up to 14 days after the conversation took place
- Deals closed up to 14 days before the conversation took place
- Deals with a deal status of open but the close date field was up to 100 days before the conversation took place

This timeline shows when conversations might be associated with an opportunity based on the opportunity’s status and close date.

Example

Stage 3: Deal association > By deal filters:
Set up filters to automatically include or exclude specific deals from being associated with activities as follows:

chunks.text:
Stage 3: Deal association > Filter logic:
There is no limit to the number of filters you can set up. The logic for the filters is:

1. Is filters are grouped together in an OR function so that all values set are used to build a list of which deals to include in the association
2. Is Not filters are grouped together in an OR function so that all values set are used to build a list of which deals to exclude from the association
3. To include a deal for association, the deal must be in the include (Is list) and must not be in the exclude (Is Not list).

Examples

In the CRM:

| Deal name | Deal type | Forecast category | Deal stage | Industry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deal1 | New business | Most likely | Finance review | Airlines |
| Deal2 | Upsell | Best case | Proposal | Software |
| Deal3 | Adjustment | Closed | Closed won | Airlines |

Filters:

- Forecast category is Most likely, Best case
- Industry is Airlines
- Deal type is not Churn, Adjustment
- Deal stage is not Inquiry, Proposal

The filter logic is as follows:

Include deals:

- Forecast category is most likely, best case OR where the Industry is airlines: Deal1 and Deal2

AND exclude deals:

- Deal type is churn or adjustment OR deal stage is inquiry or proposal: Deal2 and Deal3

The filters result in associating the activity with Deal1.

Stage 3: Deal association > Filter logic > By deal contact:
Deal contacts (known as contact roles in Salesforce) are contacts with roles who are defined and the primary contact for the deal. If you do not use contact roles in your CRM, set this to Off. If there are participants from several deals, we assume that if a deal contact is on the call, the call is predominantly related to that deal.

1. If you toggle Associate if deal contact is an activity participant to on, select:
  1. Optional: If no deal contact is a participant, other deals can be associated with the activity.
  2. Mandatory: If no deal contact is a participant, the activity won’t be associated with an account. Select this option if you maintain strong CRM hygiene and your deal contacts are always listed for the account.
2. If you toggle On, you must provide the CRM object you save your deal contact in.

Examples

chunks.text:
Stage 3: Deal association > If multiple deals are still options:
- By number of CRM contacts: Associates the deal that has more contacts participating in the activity. If out of two possible deals, one deal has 2 participants and the other has 4, select the deal with 4 participants. If this is activated and there is a single deal, we associate the activity to that deal.
- By relevant date: Choose how to associate deals based on a selected date field. If a single deal still isn’t identified, associate all possible deals, up to 20. For this option select:
  - Most recent date: Associates the deal with the most recent date in the selected field. For example, if two deals have close dates of June 1 and July 15, the deal with the July 15 close date is selected.
  - Date closest to activity: Associates the deal with the date in the selected field that is closest to the activity date. For example, if a call took place on June 10 and two deals have close dates of June 1 and June 20, the deal with the June 1 close date is selected as it is closer to the activity date.
- Deal date field: The date field in the CRM which you want to use to determine the most recent entry. For example, if you want to choose the newer deal, select the date field which holds the deal creation date.
- Maximum number of deals to associate: Set the maximum number of deals to associate, up to 20.

chunks.title: Configure data import

chunks.text:
1. Go to Admin center > Settings > CRM > CRM settings
2. In the Salesforce integration page, go to the Data import tab.
3. Select the fields in the Account, Contact, Lead, and Opportunity entities you want to import.
4. Mark Create placeholder next to any CRM field you want to use as a field placeholder to personalize activities such as Engage emails.
5. Mark Track changes for any CRM field you want to follow over time. Gong keeps a history of the field so you can see what changed and when. In playbooks, users can see when fields were last updated. The different values are shown in the account timeline and account page. Note:This step requires field history tracking to be configured in Salesforce. For details, see Field History Tracking and Track Field History for Custom Objects in Salesforce. For formula fields, refer to Unable to track Field History of Formula Fields. Ensure that you select Set history tracking and then select Track old and new values for each field.
6. Click Save.

Once you have set up the fields to import, the Import status section is displayed in the Connection tab. This shows when the last update was made in the CRM and when the Salesforce data was last imported to Gong. If there are problems in importing data, you may see this here.

Gong Dialer call recording settings determine whether calls are recorded automatically, recorded manually by the rep, recorded only on the rep side, or not recorded at all. chunks.title: Configure dialer recording settings

chunks.text:
Recording methods:
Gong supports four recording methods. You set a default for your company, and can override it for specific countries or area codes:

- Manual: The rep can start recording at any point during the call by pressing Record. Recording does not begin automatically.
- Automatic: Calls are recorded automatically from the start.
- Rep-side only: Calls are recorded automatically, but only the rep's side of the conversation is captured.
- Don't allow recording: The Record button is not shown and recording is not possible for calls matching this rule.

- Don't allow recording: The Record button is not shown and recording is not possible for calls matching this rule.

chunks.text:
Assign recording methods for specific regions:
Use regional recording rules when your team calls into countries or US states with specific consent requirements. When a rule is set for a region, it overrides the default recording method for calls to numbers in that region.

To add a recording rule for a country or region:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click Dialer setup under Gong Engage.
3. Click the Recording tab.
4. Click + Add customization.
5. Select the country from the dropdown.
6. Select the recording method to apply for that country.

For the United States, you can set recording rules at the area code level rather than for the whole country:

1. In the Country dropdown, select United States (specific area codes).
2. Choose the recording method for those area codes.
3. Enter each 3-digit area code, separated by commas.

It is your company’s responsibility to understand and comply with call recording regulations in each country your team calls. Different countries have different regulations about recording consent.

chunks.text:
Export historical call data:
You may need to re-export your call data if Gong has already exported your call data to Salesforce, for example, in a sandbox environment.

Keep in mind your Salesforce data storage consumption when choosing how far back to export calls. Gong for Salesforce uses a single API call to create a new Gong Conversation record, which creates between 25-40 additional child records.

1. Go to Admin center > Settings > CRM > CRM settings and go to the Gong for Salesforce tab.
2. Uncheck Export data from calls that occurred up to and click Update. This prevents Gong from exporting any calls to Salesforce while exporting historical call data.
3. In Salesforce, delete any Gong conversations.
4. In Gong, in the Gong for Salesforce tab, select Re-export historical call data to Salesforce. The Export data from calls that occurred up to checkbox is automatically checked.
5. Select the number of months to update calls for (for example, if you've been working with Gong in your sandbox instance for the past month, select one month ago).
6. Click Update. Typically, it takes an overnight sync to export historical calls.
7. Once the historical calls have been exported to Salesforce, Gong will continue to export your current calls to Salesforce.

chunks.title: Configure Salesforce tasks or events

chunks.text:
Default task status:
Most tasks are created with a status of Completed as Gong activities are exported after they have already occurred. This includes emails, telephony calls, conference calls and Engage activities depending on what you choose to export to Salesforce.

Salesforce events don’t have a status field.

chunks.title: Configure Salesforce tasks or events

chunks.text:
Default task status > Meeting invite status:
Salesforce tasks for meeting invites have a status of In Progress as they are exported before the meeting takes place. If past meeting invites are exported, they are also assigned the In Progress status.

After the meeting takes place, the task is updated as follows:

- Recorded meetings: The recording of the meeting is added to the corresponding meeting invite task, and the task status is changed to Completed.
- Non recorded meetings: The status remains In Progress and is not closed automatically. No additional details of the meeting are exported.
- Canceled meetings: The title of the task is updated with Meeting Canceled. The task status remains In Progress.
- Deleted meetings: Call and task are deleted from the CRM.

See Values assigned to task fields for more details.

chunks.title: Configure Salesforce tasks or events

chunks.text:
Task/event configurations:
Gong activities can be associated with multiple CRM entities, for example in activities where there are multiple participants who could be from different accounts. When exporting, choose between:

- Creating a single Salesforce task/event: Details of all CRM entities involved in the activity displayed in one task. For example, if there are 5 contacts, those contacts are listed in the participants field. Here is an example of a single task created for an email with three contacts. The primary contact is in the Name field and the other contacts are added to the Gong participants custom field.
- Create several Salesforce tasks/events: A task/event is created for each entity in the activity. For example, if there are 4 contacts on a call, 4 tasks/events will be created for the call. In addition, more tasks will be created for the accounts and opportunities the call is associated with. Here is an example of two tasks created for the same email, one for the contact and one for the opportunity.

The decision of whether to create single or multiple Salesforce activities depends on how you use data in Salesforce. For example, if you want to see which reps are on which emails or calls, this will be easier if you create multiple activities in Salesforce. If you want data on how many activities are occurring, you will need to create single Salesforce activities.

chunks.text:
Task/event configurations > Creating one task per activity:
Each Salesforce activity can hold only one value per field. When a Gong activity includes multiple values, Gong selects one to display and adds the rest to a custom field.

- Contacts: The Name field holds one contact. If there are several contacts, Gong selects the one with the most recent activity date in Salesforce. Other contacts are displayed in the Gong_Participants__c custom field.
- Opportunities: If an activity is linked to several opportunities, Gong selects one opportunity. Other opportunities are listed in the Gong_Associated_Opportunities__c custom field.
- Duplicate contacts or leads: When multiple CRM contacts or leads could match a single Gong participant, Gong selects the one with the most recent due date from closed tasks or events. If no due dates exist, Gong randomly assigns one contact to the activity.

chunks.title: Configure Salesforce tasks or events

chunks.text:
Task/event configurations > Creating one task per activity > Populating the task/event fields:
Fields for single tasks/events are populated as follows:

- Name: We select the participant based on the following:
  1. CRM contact: we look for the CRM contact that corresponds to each participant in the Gong activity.
  2. CRM lead: if there are no contacts, we look for CRM leads. As leads aren’t associated with accounts in the CRM, we will not be able to associate the task/event with an account or opportunity and the Related to field will be empty.
  3. Domain: if there are no CRM leads we look to see if there is an account with the same domain as any of the participants, and we associate the Salesforce activity with that account. In this case, the Name field is empty.
- Related to: This is either an opportunity or an account based on the following criteria:
  1. Opportunity: if we identify one opportunity associated with the Gong activity, the Related to field is populated with the opportunity.
  2. Account: If there are no opportunities, or there are multiple opportunities that can be associated with the activity, the Related to field is populated with the account of the participant in the Name field.

Additional participants, accounts, and opportunity details are displayed in custom fields that should be defined in the task/event:

- Gong_Participants__c: to display the list of participants Note:The maximum length of this field is 255 characters. If the list of participants exceeds this, see the activity in Gong for the full participant list
- Gong_Associated_Accounts__c: to display the list of associated accounts
- Gong_Associated_Opportunities__c: to display the list of associated opportunities

See Setting up Salesforce custom fields for more details.

chunks.title: Configure Salesforce tasks or events

chunks.text:
Task/event configurations > Creating several Salesforce activities for calls:
A separate task/event is created for each of the relevant contacts, leads, accounts and opportunities identified by Gong.

For example, if a meeting was held for Acme Robotics about a Renewal opportunity with Marcus Rashford and Jack Grealish from Acme Robotics, then separate Salesforce activities will be created for the Acme Robotics Account, Renewal Opportunity, and Marcus and Jack's Contacts records.

In the Acme Robotics record, you’ll see 2 tasks; one for Marcus, and one for Jack. In the Renewal Opportunity, you will also see 2 tasks, one for each contact.

chunks.title: Configure Salesforce tasks or events

chunks.text:
Task/event configurations > Creating several tasks for emails:
Multiple tasks for emails are created as follows:

1. The email sender and receiver are either Salesforce users or contacts
2. For outbound emails: the Salesforce contact or user are in the To field and not in the CC field of the email For inbound emails: the Salesforce contact or user are in either the To or the CC field of the email
3. Separate tasks are created for each Salesforce user and contact and for each opportunity the email is associated with
4. A separate task may be created for up to five email recipients. If an email has more than five recipients, the recipient names are added to the task comments but no task is generated for them.
5. For inbound emails, tasks are created for Salesforce users that are either the opportunity owner if the status of the opportunity is open, or the account manager.

Task/event configurations > Configuring the type for a Salesforce activity:
Salesforce activities include a type field which you can customize. This lets you create reports in Salesforce based on the different types of Gong activities. The default types set by Salesforce are:

- Call
- Meeting
- Other

In order to be able to set a task type for emails, Engage to-dos and LinkedIn messages, we recommend creating the following types for Salesforce tasks:

- Email: mapped automatically if the task type is already defined in Salesforce. You can change this if needed.
- To-Do
- LinkedIn message

Once you have configured the types, set the relevant task type for each activity in the Salesforce task settings section. Existing tasks are not updated with the relevant task type. To update your existing tasks with the new task type, see Updating existing tasks with a task type.

The following table shows the default values for the task type and task subtype if you do not set a task type for the activity:

| Activity | Task type | Task subtype |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Email | Other | Email |
| To-do | Other |  |
| LinkedIn message | Other |  |

Task/event configurations > Ensure exported data is displayed in the task:
In order to display all relevant data in the task, you need to define additional fields in the task object and add them to the task layout in Salesforce. This can be done automatically by Gong if you install the Gong for Salesforce app, or you can set the fields up manually in Salesforce.

In the Custom fields section of the page, select whether you want automatic or manual setup for the custom fields. You can also install Gong for Salesforce if you have not done so.

A list of features and the custom fields for those features are listed with a status of whether they are defined in Salesforce or not. See Setting up Salesforce custom fields for details of how to define the fields in Salesforce.

chunks.text:
Step 1: Verify who has already connected Gong to Zoom:
By knowing which Zoom admins have already connected Gong to Zoom, you can find a different or create a new Zoom admin to connect the new instance.

1. Log in to the Zoom App Marketplace as a user with an owner role, and then click Manage.
2. Go to ADMIN APP MANAGEMENT > Apps on Account. The list of installed apps on this account.
3. Find the Gong (Gong for Zoom Meetings) app and click on it.
4. Navigate to Current Subscribers. A list of Zoom users that are currently subscribed to the Gong app appears.

Step 2: Connect a new Gong instance to Zoom:
Before you begin: Make sure that the Zoom admin does not appear in the Gong for Zoom Meetings app current subscribers list (step 1), and that they have the necessary Zoom role permissions.

1. Sign into the new Gong instance that you want to connect to the Zoom account as a technical admin.
2. Go to Admin center > Settings tab > Data capture > Web conferencing.
3. In the Zoom row, click SETTINGS.
4. Click Connect. Follow the instructions: sign in to the Zoom account using the different or new user, and authorize access to Zoom.

When you connect to Zoom, we install a Gong for Zoom Meetings app instance in your Zoom account, and ask for the following permissions:

- View and manage all user meetings
- View and manage all user recordings
- View all users' Zoom Rooms information
- View and manage all users

TipGo here for more information on required scopes.

(Note the Gong for Zoom Meetings app is not the same as the Gong app for Zoom which enables your Gong users to take notes in Zoom).

chunks.text:
Connect Gong to Microsoft Copilot:
Setting up the Gong integration with Copilot requires creating a connection with Gong in the Microsoft admin center and providing a Gong generated API key.

1. Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center
2. Go to Copilot > Connectors.
3. Select + Add Connection, search for Gong and click Add to open the setup page.
4. Enter the the following:
  1. Display name: Enter the name you want to be displayed to users. Use a meaningful name so users know answers are coming from Gong.
  2. Gong URL: Provide the base URL listed in the Gong API settings page. Click Gong API Authentication Settings in the Copilot help panel to open the API settings page in Gong. Note:You must open the page from this link in order to get an API key for Copilot
5. In the Gong API page:
  1. Copy the base URL for API calls and paste it in Gong URL in Copilot.
  2. In Gong, click Get Copilot API key (only available if you opened the page from the link in the Copilot admin center) and copy the Access key.
6. In the Copilot setup page:
  1. In Authentication type, select Basic.
  2. Paste the access key into Access key.
  3. In Gong, click Show secret. Copy and paste the secret into the Access key secret in the Microsoft admin center.
7. Turn on Rollout to limited audience and select the people or groups you want the integration to be available for. Leave the toggle off to make the integration available to everyone.
8. Check the Notice checkbox and click Create to finish.

chunks.body:
Setting up the Gong integration with Copilot requires creating a connection with Gong in the Microsoft admin center and providing a Gong generated API key.

1. Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center
2. Go to Copilot > Connectors.
3. Select + Add Connection, search for Gong and click Add to open the setup page.
4. Enter the the following:
  1. Display name: Enter the name you want to be displayed to users. Use a meaningful name so users know answers are coming from Gong.
  2. Gong URL: Provide the base URL listed in the Gong API settings page. Click Gong API Authentication Settings in the Copilot help panel to open the API settings page in Gong. Note:You must open the page from this link in order to get an API key for Copilot
5. In the Gong API page:
  1. Copy the base URL for API calls and paste it in Gong URL in Copilot.
  2. In Gong, click Get Copilot API key (only available if you opened the page from the link in the Copilot admin center) and copy the Access key.
6. In the Copilot setup page:
  1. In Authentication type, select Basic.
  2. Paste the access key into Access key.
  3. In Gong, click Show secret. Copy and paste the secret into the Access key secret in the Microsoft admin center.
7. Turn on Rollout to limited audience and select the people or groups you want the integration to be available for. Leave the toggle off to make the integration available to everyone.
8. Check the Notice checkbox and click Create to finish.

After setup, the Gong connector is available to Copilot users according to your access settings. See more about the integration Gong integration with Microsoft Copilot.

chunks.text:
Connect Gong to Salesforce:
Set up the Salesforce integration to enable data sharing between Gong and Salesforce.

To connect Gong to Salesforce:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click CRM settings, under CRM.
3. In the CRM page, select Salesforce. You can only connect one CRM to Gong.
4. In the Salesforce integration settings page, click Connect and log into your Salesforce account using the credentials of the integration user you set up.
5. When prompted, click Allow to authorize Gong to access Salesforce. Gong asks for access to read data (Lead, Contact, Account, Opportunity, Opportunity History, Field History tables, Task, Organization table and so on) using REST API. Provide write access to these objects if you want to export Gong activities to Salesforce. Note:Ensure the integration user is set up with the correct permissions in Salesforce. Providing read/write access when setting up the integration does not guarantee that entities will be imported and exported.

4. Click Install for each app.

  - Account locator: the identifier for the Snowflake account you want Gong data to be available from.
  - Account region: available from your Snowflake admin. If the account region is not included in the list, the region is not currently supported. You can ask us to add the region and we will let you know when your region is supported. Supported regions are:

    - AZURE_NORTHEUROPE

chunks.text:
Give Gong access to Google Workspace:
1. In the Google Workspace page, in Provide access to, select whether to:
  1. import calendar meetings and emails
  2. import calendar meetings
2. Click Connect or if you’re not a Google super admin, click Send link to a Google Workspace Admin to send instructions of how to install the Gong app in Google Workspace.
3. In the Google Workspace marketplace, click Domain Install to install the Gong.io app. Note:Changes to permissions when updating other Google Workspace configurations may cause the Google Workspace integration with Gong to become unstable.
4. Click Allow to grant Gong.io the right to access your domain data. This permission is static, and ensures that Gong can import emails and calendar events for your company. For more details on the elements Gong can access, click i in the grant screen.
5. Optional: In the Turn ON for area, select the organizational unit (OU) you want to turn the Gong app on for. Gong will only be able to access data for people in that unit. Note that if you need to set up recording for a group of people, we recommend that you use OUs and not groups.
6. Click Accept. When the set up is complete and Gong has access permissions, the set up screen closes, and a success message is displayed in the Google Workspace integration page. This can take up to 24 hours to fully complete.
