chunks.text:
Create a stream from the search page:
1. Go to Conversations > Search.
2. In the filter panel on the left, search for calls using at least one filter.
3. Click Create stream at the top of the page. This button only appears after you’ve filtered for calls.
4. In the General section: Give the stream a name and choose where to save it. By default, streams created from the search page will be saved in your library, but you can choose a different folder if you want, or save it in the company library (depending on your permissions).
5. In the Filters section, you’ll see the filters you used in your search. After the stream is saved, you’ll be able to edit them by editing the stream. Note:If you filter the stream by AI trackers and the tracker isn’t activated or there aren’t enough credits, calls won’t be added to the stream.
6. In the Brief section, choose the brief type you want displayed in stream results and immediate notifications. The Highlights brief type is selected by default, but you can choose from any of your company’s call brief types. Tip:If the Highlights brief type is selected, you’ll be able to choose which sections you want to display. For all other brief types, all sections are displayed.
7. In Microsoft Teams notifications, select the team and channel that will be notified when a call is added to the stream. Only available if your company set up the Gong notifications app for Microsoft Teams.
  1. Select which AI summaries you want to display in the Microsoft Teams notification:
    - Recap: A short summary of the call
    - Key points: A bullet list of the call’s main points
    - Next steps: Action items form both sides of the conversation
8. In the Slack notifications section, select a Slack channel. If it’s a private Slack channel, make sure Gong is invited to the channel. Note: For Slack notifications to be possible, your company must be connected to Slack, and the stream must be set to standard, not personalized. Choose which AI summaries you want to display in the Slack notification.
  - Call brief: 1-paragraph summary of the call
  - Key points: 10-bullet list of main call points
  - Next steps: Action items from both sides of the conversation
  - Smart trackers: If the stream has smart tracker filters, choose whether you want to see a summary of the smart tracker mentions, or a transcript of the relevant snippets. If the stream already has calls in it, you’ll be able to test how these summaries look in the Slack notification by clicking Test on Slack.
9. In the Share and set email notifications section, share the stream with other people at your company, subscriber them to email notifications, and set the notification cadence.
10. In the Stream type section, set whether the stream is standard or personalized.
  - Standard All calls are shown to everyone viewing the stream. This is required if you want to enable Slack notifications for the stream, and preferred when building a stream in the company library, so that everyone visiting the library can see all of its calls.
  - Personalized Each person who is subscribed to the stream only sees the calls owned by them or their team.
11. Save the stream.

1. In Gong, in Admin center > Settings > People > Team Member Provisioning.

3. In the new assignment, give the assignment a meaningful name so that you can know who should be included in the assignment.
4. In the <IdP> groups area, select the group you want to define the settings for.
5. Select the Gong seats you want users in this group to have assigned to them. Note: Ensure you assign the Gong seats required for the permissions and other settings included in the assignment.
6. In the Workspaces and permissions area, set the permissions profile for each workspace in your organization.
7. In the Data capture area, select which data should be captured and imported to Gong. For details see Add or edit a team member.
8. In Email export to CRM, select whether you want emails of team members with this assignment to be exported to the CRM or not. See Edit email settings for existing assignments for details on setting this.
9. In the Update settings area, define how settings can be managed for this assignment: For more details, see Automatic vs manual updates
  - Manual editing: edit team member settings manually in Gong. Changes to the group settings in your IdP will not be updated in Gong.
  - Automatic updates: edit team member settings in your IdP. Data capture and permission settings are defined in Gong only when creating the assignment. Once the assignment has been set up, changes are made in your IdP and then updated in Gong.
10. Click ADD ASSIGNMENT.

As a sales manager, making coaching a regular practice can be challenging when you're pressed for time or lack visibility into which reps need coaching on specific skills. Gong removes these barriers by automatically capturing calls, providing AI-assisted scorecards to speed up feedback, and highlighting exactly where coaching is needed.

This quick start guide walks you through the core practices that make coaching a regular part of your team's process.

chunks.text:
Provide your team with feedback:
There are several ways to give feedback directly from the call page, making it easy to coach your team in the context of real customer conversations.

chunks.text:
Add a comment:
Adding comments on a call is a valuable way for teams to collaborate, and it's also a simple way for managers to leave positive or corrective feedback while reviewing conversations.

To add a comment:

1. Open the call page and click the comment icon in the right sidebar.
2. Click anywhere in the transcript or timeline to add a timestamped comment. Tip:Actionable comments tied to exact call moments help reps understand what to improve.
3. Tag your direct report to notify them of your feedback.
4. Choose whether to make the comment public, private or visible to specific people.
5. Click Post and the comment will appear in the Comments tab.

chunks.text:
Score a call:
Scoring calls gives reps quick, structured feedback they can track over time. Scorecards help distinguish strong calls from those that need improvement by focusing on key elements like setting an agenda, handling objections, and addressing pain points.

To score a call:

1. Open the call you want to score and click the star icon in the right panel.
2. Select the participant, choose a scorecard, and click Score this call.
3. If scorecards already exist, click +Add scorecard to add another.
4. Answer each question.
5. If Scoring guide appears below a question, click it to see instructions from the scorecard creator on how to answer it.
6. Use Add more feedback to add context to your answers.
7. Choose the visibility of the completed scorecard.
8. Click Submit.

Start by scoring one call per rep each week, then increase frequency as coaching becomes a routine habit.

chunks.text:
Set the consent page options:
In the Consent page section, if you want to get consent to record before starting/joining the meeting, set the following:

1. Consent page. Turn On and click Show settings. This enables but does not enforce displaying the consent page before opening the meeting. Without enforcing the consent page, Gong may record meetings where where the meeting link is not a consent-enabled link.
2. Enforce use of consent page: Check to ensure Gong only records meetings where consent was explicitly given via the consent page to record the call. If additional meeting links are included in the invitation, the call may not be recorded.
3. Send reminder email to use the consent-enabled meeting link: Check to send an email reminder that meeting links should be set up with the Gong add on.
4. Allow participants to join without giving consent (recording will be canceled): Adds an option to the Gong consent page that lets participants join the meeting without recording it.

Note:These compliance settings are applied to all web conference providers you add to the consent profile.

chunks.text:
Set the consent page options > Add web conference providers:
1. In the Web conferencing providers section, click Add provider. People who set meetings using Microsoft Outlook are able to choose any of these web conference providers. Providers defined in your default consent profile are automatically added to new profiles, and you may see them defined here. Different settings are available for different providers.
2. Link settings. If your web conferencing provider is Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or Webex select the meeting link type for the consent profile. See Understanding recording consent for considerations of which link to choose.
  1. Dynamic link: the meeting link is dynamically generated for each meeting
  2. Static link: the meeting link is the same for each meeting Note:If the web conference provider app doesn’t include a personal meeting room, team members can create meetings with static links by setting up a recurring meeting with no end date and using the team member’s Personal meeting room link defined in their profile.
  3. Let host decide. allows the person setting up the meeting to decide which type of link to use
3. Link personalization: Customize the meeting link to include your company name if relevant. Each time you change this link, the previous link is disabled. To share the updated link with team members associated with the consent profile, go to the Recording consent page, hover over the consent profile, open the Options menu (⋮), and select Send consent instructions.

  2. Mark Use a different company name, and enter the alternative company name if relevant..
  3. Provide a link to the Privacy policy.
  4. Review the preview of the email and click Send me a sample email if necessary.

Set the audio prompt:
The audio prompt makes a verbal announcement that the call is being recorded. If using JoinMe, the audio prompt is only available if the call host has signed in to the web conference call using their computer. If you disable the audio prompt, ensure you have another notification in place.

1. Switch the Audio prompt on and click Show Settings.
2. Select when the audio prompt should be played:
  1. Play the prompt once, shortly after the first guest with their audio on
  2. Play the prompt shortly after each guest joins the call with their audio on. Each participant hears the audio prompt. Gong identifies participants belonging to your company and doesn't play the audio prompt when they join the call.
3. (Optional) In the Language area, click Change language to select the language for the audio prompt.
4. (Optional) Don't play the audio prompt if the consent page is used: Set this so that the audio prompt doesn’t play if consent was explicitly given to record the call.
5. Select the voice and text of the audio prompt. Click to listen to the audio prompt. The default voice and text is Female: “We’re recording this call for better-note taking, following up and training purposes”

chunks.text:
Add a custom call outcome:
Create custom call outcomes when the default call outcomes don't accurately reflect your team's calling activities or reporting requirements.

To add a custom call outcome

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click Dialer setup under Gong Engage.
3. Click the Call outcomes tab.
4. Click + Add new outcome.
5. Enter a name for the call outcome. The name is displayed in the dialer, search, timeline, and Engage analytics.
6. Select a Connect status:
  - Connected: Calls are counted as connected in analytics.
  - Not Connected: Calls are counted as not connected in analytics.
7. Select a sentiment: Each sentiment has a default color and is used in analytics reporting.
  - Positive
  - Neutral
  - Negative
8. Select a default to-do action: For flow to-dos, both options are available. For to-dos that aren't associated with a flow, Complete is the only available option.
  - Complete: Completes the to-do.
  - Complete and remove: Completes the to-do and removes the person from the flow.
9. Select Mark as opt-out if you want the person to automatically be marked as do not contact when a team member selects this call outcome.
10. Click Update.

Note:Rulesets override call outcome automations for matching outcomes. For calls in a flow, the matching ruleset action runs instead of the automation configured for the call outcome.

A team member who manages and configures the Gong platform and handles CRM integrations, user provisioning, permissions, and system settings. Find my Tech admin.

Create a custom smart tracker:
Create a new custom smart tracker:

1. Go to Admin center > Agent Studio.
2. Hover over AI Tracker and click Settings.
3. In the AI Tracker settings page, click +New tracker, and select Smart tracker.

Customize your smart tracker:

The screenshot below shows you the steps you need to take to build your smart tracker:
chunks.body:
Create a new custom smart tracker:

1. Go to Admin center > Agent Studio.
2. Hover over AI Tracker and click Settings.
3. In the AI Tracker settings page, click +New tracker, and select Smart tracker.

Customize your smart tracker:

The screenshot below shows you the steps you need to take to build your smart tracker:
chunks.title: Create smart trackers

chunks.text:
Create a custom smart tracker:
1. Choose how to build your question:
  1. Use question builder (default): Construct a question by selecting from predefined phrases for three individual sections.
  2. Write a free-text question: Write your own question about what happened in the conversation, using natural language.
2. Ask a question about something that happened in the conversation.
  1. Question builder: Select from the fixed word choices, then add your own topic if needed.
  2. Free-text: Type your question directly.
3. Provide extra information to improve tracking accuracy.
  1. Question builder: Gong autofills this section. Review it and edit, add, or replace details. (Some elements will always need replacing, such as Competitor, Solution, or Integration names).
  2. Free-text: Enter any additional details. Note: Switching from the question builder to free-text carries over any pre-filled details (see step 3). Switching back to the question builder restores your original selections.
4. Choose which side of the conversation you want to track: Our rep (your side); Customer; Any party.
5. Refine your question with in-app AI suggestions.
6. Choose where to track it. The estimated credit usage shown here is based on your selected settings.
  1. Type of conversation: Calls or Calls and emails.
  2. Filters: Click Edit filters to refine your results, for example, by participants, account name, call title, emails, or internal vs. external calls. Click + Add filters to add other filters.
  3. Part of call: Default is Anytime, which includes the entire call. Change to the First or Last X Minutes or Percent, if needed.
7. Click Preview results to test your tracker. Gong samples 100 random calls and shows results in the right pane. Each includes meeting details, such as account, and a summary of the tracked concept.
  1. Click Based on X mentions to view the relevant conversation snippets.
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the list to search beyond the initial 100 calls.
  3. If you’re not satisfied with the results, adjust the question, details, or filters, and preview again.
8. When you’re satisfied with the results, you have two options:
  - Click Save: Name the tracker and save it. You’ll find the tracker in your AI Tracker settings page, with the label Draft, until you publish it. Click Edit when you’re ready to publish it.
  - Click Publish:
  - Name the tracker and choose settings:
    - Apply only to upcoming calls, or include calls from the past 1,3,6 months or 1 year. The estimated credit usage shown here is based on your selected settings.
    - Decide whether to collect the calls in a stream and set up when to be notified.

chunks.body:
Who can use this: Tech admin, Business adminAvailable on: Gong Engage

Rulesets are groups of rules applied to flows that allow you to manage flow behavior. Instead of configuring individual flow settings, set the behavior once and apply it across multiple flows at scale.
chunks.title: Creating and managing rulesets

chunks.text:
How to create a ruleset:
Where to go: Assets > Flow rulesets
chunks.body: Where to go: Assets > Flow rulesets
chunks.title: Creating and managing rulesets

chunks.text:
How to create a ruleset:
1. Click Create ruleset
2. Give your ruleset a name and description
3. Configure each rule within the ruleset. There are several categories of rules available within rulesets:
  - Flow properties: Set the following:
    - If the flow is exclusive, meaning a person can’t be added to other flows at the same time. This rule is only configurable if Allow contacts and leads to be in more than one active flow is turned on in your company’s Flow settings.
    - Whether to apply or ignore the cool-off period. The cool-off period is set in your company’s Flow settings. The cool-off period is applied when a person either finishes or is removed from a flow.
  - Outbound emails: Set opt-out settings. Choose whether or not to display an opt-out footer for all emails in the flow. Whether or not this rule is configurable depends on your company’s Email settings for displaying opt-out footers.
  - Response handling: Controls what happens when someone replies, books a meeting, calls back, or their email bounces. When someone replies with an out of office message, the current to-do for all flows the person is in will be snoozed until the person’s return date (the flows are not paused). This ensures that follow-ups resume only after the contact is expected to return. If Gong can't detect a date of return, the flow will not be paused. It will continue as originally scheduled, even if the only replies are repeated automated OOO messages.Customizable response handling triggers and actions include:
    - Replies via email → Pause the flow, stop the flow, continue the flow, or remove all account contacts from all flows and optionally create a response to-do
    - Meeting booked → Pause the flow, stop the flow, continue the flow, or remove all account contacts from all flows and optionally create a meeting booked to-do
  - CRM change. Automate how people are handled in a flow when key information changes in your CRM to ensure that your flows always reflect the most current information.
    - For example:
      - When a lead is disqualified, remove them from all active flows.
      - When an opportunity is marked as Closed Lost, remove all associated contacts from their flows.
      - When an account churns, remove all contacts associated with that account from all flows.
  - Flow status change. Automatically keep lead status in your CRM in sync with what’s happening in the flow. Every time a flow status is updated in Gong, the corresponding lead status in your CRM updates automatically. Supported for Salesforce, HubSpot, and Dynamics365.
    - For example:
      - When flow status changes to In progress, update lead status to Working. When flow status changes to Finished, update lead status to Closed-not converted.
    - Learn more about flow statuses in your CRM
4. Click Save. Your ruleset is now ready to be applied to flows.

chunks.text:
Remove all account contacts from all flows:
For CRM change or Response handling rules, you have the option to remove all contacts associated with an account from all flows. For teams executing multi-threaded, account-based outreach where you’re contacting multiple people at the same company simultaneously, this action stops outreach once one contact engages. It ensures that once someone in an account replies, all other contacts at that same account are removed from every active flow automatically. This action is best for prospecting or account-based outreach, not internal or existing customer flows where multiple people might legitimately need to be messaged in parallel.

By selecting the action Remove all account contacts from all flows, Gong finds all other contacts associated with the same account and removes them from any flows, even if those flows are different or owned by different team members.

This action only applies to contacts, not leads, because leads don’t have an account entity. If a lead triggers the rule, it won’t remove other contacts.

Since this impacts all flows for an account, ensure your team is aware of the behavior so no outreach gets removed unexpectedly. You must have permission to create and manage flow rulesets to enable this action.

chunks.text:
How to create a CRM change rule:
Create rules that define flow behavior when key information changes in your CRM. For example, stop a flow when an account churns.

Where to go: Assets > Flow rulesets

1. Select a ruleset or create a new one.
2. In the CRM change section, click + Add rule.
3. Define the trigger that will start the rule. You can create triggers based on updates to a Lead, Contact, Account, or Opportunity. Note:When you use an opportunity trigger, it only applies to people in flows that are linked to that opportunity. Gong can’t determine whether a flow is relevant to an opportunity unless it’s explicitly linked.
4. Set the conditions for the trigger. You can define which specific values will trigger the action. For example, for the Status field, you might select the values Closed-Converted and Working-Contacted. You can select multiple values.
5. Choose the action to take when the conditions are met. The available action is Remove contact/lead from the flow.
6. Click Apply.

chunks.text:
How to configure the email bounce rule:
Where to go: Assets > Flow rulesets

Configure the email bounce rule to define what happens when an email sent from a flow bounces. This helps your teams keep sales tasks moving without adding manual work for reps.

When a bounce is detected by Gong, you can control:

- What happens to the person in the flow
- Whether or not a to-do is created for the rep assigned to the flow

To create an email bounce rule:

1. Select a ruleset or create a new one.
2. In the Response handling section, go to the rule that begins with When an email bounces
3. In the first dropdown, choose one option:
  - Pause the flow: The person is paused in the current flow. This is the default behavior.
  - Remove them from the flow: The person is removed from the current flow.
  - Move to an email-free flow: The person is removed from the current flow and starts another flow that has no email steps. When you choose this option, select a destination flow. Only email-free flows are available to select.
4. In the second dropdown, choose whether to create a to-do:
  - Create an email bounced to-do: A to-do is created for the flow assignee. This is the default behavior.
  - Don’t create an email bounced to-do: No to-do is created.

Things to note:

How to configure the email bounce rule:
- Email bounce rules are not retroactive. If you edit the rule, the new configuration only applies to bounces that occur after the change has been saved. It will not apply to people who have already been paused or had a to-do created under the old rule.
- All bounce types (hard and soft bounce) trigger the rule.
- If the destination flow is deleted or the person cannot start the flow for any reason, the person’s current flow will be paused and an email bounced to-do is created for the flow assignee.

chunks.text:
Who can update CRM data directly from the deal board?:
Anyone who has the permissions to update a CRM field will be able to do so directly from a column cell in the deal board. Additionally, with Forecast Essentials or Gong Forecast you can use the Update CRM section to define available CRM fields that won’t show up as a column, but can be found in deal activity.*

Make sure that the CRM field values you need are mapped and synced with Gong (Salesforce/ HubSpot/ Dynamics 365). Specifically, rollup forecast categories and CRM values, filters, and deal board columns.

Note:Salesforce field name differences worth noting:The Last activity field from the Account object shows in the Deals board as Account Last Activity date.The Last activity field from the Opportunity object shows in the Deals board as Deal Last Activity date.The Record Type ID field from the Opportunity object shows in the Deals board as Opportunity Record Type.

What CRM fields can I use as filters or columns?:
When your Gong admin sets up the CRM integration, they can import any CRM fields to Gong. You can use these fields as filters or columns when creating your board.

The most crucial field to import is the amount field, as that is used as the deal value in the boards.

Are there any CRM fields that aren’t supported?:
The following CRM fields are unsupported for displaying columns, filtering and grouping in deal boards:

1. Multi-picklist fields (fields of the type “multi-picklist”)
2. Reference fields (fields that reference other objects)
3. Fields from standard objects other than Opportunity or Account
4. Fields from custom objects

Additional unsupported field for filtering in deal boards:

- Date fields

Additional unsupported field for grouping in deal boards:

- Number fields and currency fields

chunks.text:
Why is the total at the top of the tab wrong?:
If the total deal value shown at the top of the tab is different to what you'd expect, check with your tech admin that the CRM field you're using as the deal value in the deal board matches the field set as the currency amount field in your Salesforce integration settings.

Settings > [CRM] > Import from [CRM] area > Set the [CRM] currency amount field you want to appear as the deal value in Gong.

chunks.text:
Why can I edit fields in Gong that are restricted in Salesforce by validation rules?:
Gong allows you to edit fields in the deal board and then checks your user permissions and company validation rules in Salesforce to make sure we can update the record.

If the edit is valid, you'll see a green success message. If your edit isn't allowed, you'll see a red error message, and the deal board field will return to the previous value.

If you have dependent fields, we suggest also adding the dependent fields to the deal board.

New calls are processed in Gong and updated immediately in the CRM. For calls where there are changes to its associated data (for example – trackers, associations in the CRM data, editing), changes usually appear within 24 hours.

The fields included in the report are:

Who can use this: Tech adminAvailable on: Any Gong plan

Where to go: Admin center > Settings > CRM

Gong’s CRM integration brings customer conversations and activities together with your CRM data. Syncing data between the CRM and Gong adds business context to each conversation, enabling advanced analysis and understanding of how to impact your pipeline.

Integrate Gong with your CRM to:

- Import CRM data to Gong: Import CRM data like accounts, contacts, and opportunities to add context to customer interactions and enable features like Engage, Deal boards, Forecast, and advanced insights into team and deal performance.
- Engage with prospects: Engage users can configure accounts and contacts in the CRM, and then continue outreach directly from Gong.
- Search by CRM fields: Search or filter Gong conversations using CRM fields such as opportunity stage, region, or owner.
- Export Gong data to your CRM: Keep customer communication managed in one place. Calls, emails, and other activities captured in Gong are exported to your CRM as objects (for example, tasks in Salesforce or meetings in HubSpot). Use CRM reports to combine Gong data with CRM data for complete activity metrics.
- Update CRM data directly in Gong: Imported CRM fields can be edited in Gong, and instantly synced back to the CRM. This keeps processes streamlined and data accurate without switching between systems.
- Create variables from CRM fields: Configure CRM fields as variables in Gong to personalize Engage emails or AI briefs with live data.

Dedicated integration user:
Set up a dedicated integration user in the CRM to authorize the integration. If a regular user sets up the connection and their account is deactivated, the integration will disconnect. A dedicated integration user avoids this risk because it is not tied to an individual and is not deactivated. See how to set up an integration user with the relevant permissions for Salesforce, Dynamics 365, and HubSpot.

Supported CRMs:

chunks.text:
CRM association settings:
Gong provides a default algorithm for identifying the accounts and opportunities that should be associated with each Gong activity. The activity participants are first identified in the CRM, and if the participant is also a contact in the CRM, the contact’s account is associated with the activity.

To find relevant open deals, the algorithm checks if one of the participants is also a deal owner. If the deal owner is an activity participant, the deal is associated with the activity. If not, up to 5 deals are associated.

The association settings can be configured to reflect how data is stored in the CRM so that associating CRM objects with Gong activities will be more accurate. It is possible to test the associations before activating them in the production environment.

3rd parties:
CRM settings include settings that indicate when a deal is managed by a third party. When set up, Gong displays a label showing that the account is a 3rd party account and any deals are managed by the third party. Gong can import and display communication between you, the partner, and the customer. However, conversations between the partner and customer cannot be imported to Gong and therefore, these deals may not have complete data. For more details, see Set up 3rd party association.

chunks.text:
What’s a custom chart:
Custom charts are visual representations of data tailored to meet your company’s business needs. You can use them to create unique visualizations filtered and broken down by any predefined criteria. Custom chart widgets support all dashboard date picker types and updates the widget results based on the date selection made in the dashboard.

You can use them to create unique visualizations filtered and broken down by any predefined criteria. Custom chart widgets support all dashboard date picker types and updates the widget results based on the date selection made in the dashboard.
chunks.title: Custom chart

chunks.text:
Building a custom chart:
Note:Your profile must include the relevant permission to create and manage widgets to dashboards

To build a new custom chart:

1. Select your dashboard, click +New widget and select Custom chart from the gallery.
2. In the dashboard header, click the edit iconto rename your widget and, optionally, + Add description.
3. By default, you are required to select a metric; however, you can base the chart on a custom analysis made on the fly (and not saved to your metric list). If your metric list includes the analysis type you need, select the metric and proceed to the next step.

How to find the right metric

Hovering over any of the metrics displays a card detailing the metrics calculation, the fields it’s based on, and the conditions applied to it.

If you can’t find the metric you need for this widget, you can:

- From the metric selection dropdown, click + New metric to create a new metric, and then pull it to your custom chart. Click to edit an existing metric and click Save. You can rename a metric by clicking and then Rename metric.
- Click Custom analysis and then select your base object (deals/accounts), the aggregation type and field (ex: Count deals, Count accounts). This analysis is used locally by your widget and isn’t saved to your company’s metric repository.

chunks.title: Custom chart

chunks.text:
Building a custom chart:
1. After selecting the analysis type, you’ll notice two filters are added to the chart, and the team member and date fields are set to be dynamic and respond to whatever is selected in your dashboard. You can change them to fixed values. Note:If you select fixed values for the team member and period, the widget would no longer respond to selections made on the dashboard level.
2. In addition to the two filters, you may add any filter (+Add filter) that defines which deals/accounts qualify for the analysis. For example: deals in which Sales qualified is true and Deal stage is neither Closed-won nor Closed-lost.
3. Select how to break down the data. You can add up to two breakdown levels. A two-level breakdown allows a wider display variety, like stacked vertical/stacked horizontal bars. You can break it down by:

- Team member fields (ex: Owner, Created by). In this case, you should select the level of granularity (teams/individuals).
- Date fields (ex: Close date, Created date). In this case, you should select the level of granularity (days, weeks, etc.).
- Any lookup/text field (excluding rich text).
- You cannot break the data by a numerical or rich text fields.

chunks.title: Custom chart

chunks.text:
Building a custom chart:
1. Select your drilldown view:
  - If your analysis is deal-based, select the deal board that opens up when viewers click to inspect the deals included in the widget. The selected drilldown view inherits the column selection and their order from the selected deal board, as well as the warning configuration, but not the deal board filters.
  - If your analysis is account-based, a predefined hardcoded drilldown view is automatically selected.
2. Validate your setting by selecting different options on the preview pane.
3. Select the visualization type: vertical bars, stacked vertical bars, horizontal bars, stacked horizontal bars, pie, or table.
  - For tables: color code the table so you can easily see which metrics have high values, which have medium values, and which are low.
4. When you’re happy with the Preview results on the right, click Save.

chunks.text:
Configure the Account details widget:
The Account details widget helps teams focus on the account information most relevant to their workflow. You can add Gong fields, imported CRM fields, and extractors configured for your organization.

To customize the Account details widget:

1. Open an account page.
2. Click the More actions icon , and select Edit account view.
3. In Account console view, select Account details.
4. Click Add field.
5. Select the fields you want to display.
6. Drag fields using the Reorder icon .
7. Click the Remove icon next to a field to remove it.
8. Review the Preview panel on the right, to verify the field selections with real account data. The preview updates automatically as you make changes.
9. Click Save to keep the changes as a draft, or Publish to make the changes live across that workspace.

Set the default AI brief:

NoteOnly published account-level briefs are available to select as the default brief.

To set the default AI brief:

1. Open an account page.
2. Click the More actions icon , and select Edit account view.
3. In Account console view, select Brief.
4. Brief: Select the published account-level brief you want to use as the default.
5. Period: Select a preset time period or create a custom date range.
6. Review the Preview panel on the right to confirm the correct brief appears.
7. Click Save to keep the changes as a draft, or click Publish to make the changes live across that workspace.

AI Deal Monitor generates warnings when it detects unusual patterns that could put a deal at risk. Learn how to customize which warnings appear, based on the risks most relevant to your business.

Tips before you start:

- Configure warnings based on expected engagement at that stage of the deal. Prospective businesses may have significantly different deal cycles, e.g. SMBs vs. enterprise accounts. To fully benefit from warnings, it’s worthwhile to create separate deal boards for early and late stage deals.
- Refer to the default warning settings when you create a new board. Also, wherever available, consider the typical settings below that are based on the cadence of your sales cycle.
- Choose the warnings that commonly affect your deals, and look at past successful deals to get an idea of where your threshold is between healthy and risky deals.

Note:If you edit the warning settings, it can take up to a few hours to update in the board while the data is recalculated.

Here’s how to set your warnings:

Where to go: Revenue > Deals

- Select your deal board and click Edit board or click followed by + Create board.
- Toggle on the warnings you want to include in your board.
- Adjust the warning settings as required.

Note:The number of days in warning settings refers to calendar days.

Not enough contacts:
X (1/2/3/4/5 active contacts) or fewer for X days indicates deals where no one on the prospect side had involvement in any of the detected activities.

chunks.text:
No power:
No active X (Director/ Vice president/ C level) or higher and deal is closing in X days or less.

This warning indicates deals where nobody of the specified power level is active on the deal, and the expected deal close date is during that time.

Gong tracks email signature and CRM titles on contacts associated with the deal over the last 90 days. If we can verify at least 75% of the participants' titles are below the rank you defined for the warning, we’ll warn you that there's not enough power on the deal.

These are the titles we attribute to the 3 levels:

| Level | Mapped title |
| --- | --- |
| C-level | CEO, Chief, Founder, President |
| VP | Senior Vice President, Executive Vice President, Regional Vice President, Associate Vice President, Head of, General manager |
| Director | Senior Director, Director |

Pricing not mentioned:
No mention and deal is closing in X days or less indicates deals where nobody has discussed pricing yet, and the expected deal close date is within that time.

This warning shows when we haven't found any references to pricing in recent call topics or email labels e.g. “that’s too expensive” or ”we need a discount.”

Note:Emails in foreign languages aren’t yet considered for this warning.

chunks.text:
Red flag:
Email labeled “Red flag” received in the last X days indicates deals where a prospect has sent an email that presents a potential risk to the deal. This warning leverages Gong's AI-powered email labelling. We alert you to this potential risk so that you can address it quickly, and the warning will disappear when you reply to the flagged email, or when the sender joins a call.

How does Gong AI determine that an email contains a red flag?

Gong’s AI model was trained to recognize red flags using real sales emails across different industries. The model analyzes the full context of an email and determines intent, even if the exact phrasing differs. For example, words like "unsure" or "priority" alone aren’t red flags – it’s the complete sentence that matters.

Examples of phrases that trigger a red flag include:

- Although the team feels strongly about your product, they are unsure about the funding.
- The decision-makers haven’t shown interest at this time.
- We are cutting budgets and can't commit to additional costs.
- This project has dropped in priority.

Note:Red flag warnings are currently only available in English.

chunks.text:
Stalled in stage:
No change for X days or more indicates deals that have been stuck in a particular stage for a defined amount of time.

The momentum of a deal, and specifically the time it spends in each stage, is a strong indicator of the deal’s ultimate outcome. This warning alerts you when deal momentum is slowing, so that you can address it promptly.

You can customize it by adding all available stages, and setting the length for each one.

Note:This warning relies on the information in your CRM being up to date, so that Gong is updated when a deal moves stages. You'll need to reconfigure the warning if you rename or remove a stage in your CRM.

Gong scorecards analysis:
Get details of how scorecards are being used in your company, who fills in the most cards, who fills in the least, which reps score highest and which reps need coaching. Use the dashboard to identify the reps who need more feedback, and the managers who should be giving more feedback. The reports included in the dashboard are:

- Top users to score a call: shows the people who filled in the most scorecards over the last 30 days
- Scoring done per month by manager: shows how many scorecards managers filled in each month in the last two fiscal quarters
- Top users to get scored: shows the people who scored the highest in scorecards filled in for their calls in the last 30 days
- Bottom users to score a call: shows the people who filled in the least scorecards over the last 30 days

Economic pulse:
This dashboard shows data on how current economic considerations are affecting your sales. The reports give details such as how often this comes up in calls, the potential amount in your pipeline affected by this, and whether there has been a change in the win rate over time.

Note:This dashboard displays data only when the Economic Pulse tracker is enabled and configured to be used in the CRM call object.

The dashboard includes the following reports:

- Economic pulse rate in conversations over time: Shows the percentage of conversations economic pulse tracker terms came up in conversations in the current and previous fiscal quarter.
- $ pipeline impacted by Economic Pulse: Shows the total amount of all opportunities where economic pulse tracker terms were mentioned so that you can evaluate risk to your pipeline.
- Economic Pulse - Impacted Opportunities by Stage: Shows a breakdown of the stage different opportunities were in when economic pulse terms were mentioned, together with the total amount of the opportunities.
- Economic Pulse - Impacted Industries: Shows the number of opportunities per industry where the economic pulse tracker terms were mentioned together with the month the opportunity started.
- Economic Pulse - Impacted Account Types: Shows the number of times the economic pulse tracker terms were mentioned by different types of accounts, such as customers or prospects.
- Overall win rate per Q: Shows the percentage of deals won in the current and previous fiscal quarter.
- Win Rate - Economic pulse impacted opps per Q: Shows the percentage of opportunities won where economic pulse terms were mentioned.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Who can use this: Tech admin, Salesforce admins, Sales enablement teams

This article will give you the principles for troubleshooting dashboards and reports, rather than a guide to troubleshoot specific reports.

Note:This article refers to troubleshooting issues with the Gong for Salesforce app.

Issue: Gong Reports or Gong Dashboards folders not showing

Make sure people can see the Gong reports and dashboards folders when they navigate to their available reports or dashboards.

If they can't see the Gong Dashboards or Gong Reports folders, then check the sharing permissions for both folders:

Add anyone who doesn't have access to the dashboards and reports, and define the manage, edit, and view settings for the folders.

If the user still can’t see dashboards and reports, ensure they have the Gong Users permission set.

Issue: No data in the report

There can be a few reasons that data isn't showing in the reports. Check the following:

Check the Show Me filter

The Show Me filter defines the scope of records that users are exposed to. It can be set to be org-wide, or restricted based on roles and hierarchies.

Check the Show Me filter gives access to data you need.

Check the Opportunities Stages filter

In some reports, additional filters include opportunity stage values. If your org has tailored the names of the opportunity stages, check that the names of the stages in the filter are the ones used by your org.

Check the Contact Titles filter

The following reports use contact titles:

- Closing Opps w/o their VP participation
- Closing Opps with your VP participation

The reports are designed to show late stage opportunities with or without power on the deal. Consider adjusting the titles that represent power in your specific space.

Issue: I can't see my standard objects custom fields

Your reports and dashboards are up and running, and you want to view some of your custom fields, or use them as filters, yet they are unavailable for selection in the reports builder - what's going on?

- Trackers appearing in opportunities
- Topics appearing in opportunities
- Opportunities with Gong Conversations and Contacts

As custom report types are part of a managed package, they can't be updated. Likewise, the fields available for these custom report types can't be updated.

Likewise, the fields available for these custom report types can't be updated.

To work around this limitation, do the following:

1. Clone the managed Custom Report Type.
2. Save the cloned custom report type.
3. In the clone, click Edit Layout to add additional custom fields.

5. Click Save.
6. In the Reports page, click New Report and select your newly created custom report type in the report builder.

Issue: No data in the dashboard

1. In the Gong for Salesforce setup, make sure the push call data option is checked.
2. Check for trackers - make sure all phrases are there.
3. Click Edit > .
4. In the Properties window, set View Dashboard As to Let dashboard viewers choose whom they view the dashboard as. to ensure they can see the data in the dashboard.

It takes approximately 24 hours for all the Gong data to be accessible from the Dashboard.

The Gong for Dynamics app contains custom objects with data needed to display a Gong call in MS Dynamics. The Gong Conversation object is the main parent object. It contains unique call details, such as the conversation title, the date of the call, duration, scope.

The child objects represent elements that have a one-to-many relationship with the call, for example, trackers, topics, notes, invitees, structure, participants, interaction stats, related accounts, related contacts, related leads, and related opportunities.

When a new call is exported to MS Dynamics, a trigger creates the records for the child objects from JSON structured data contained in the conversation custom fields. The result is your reps get a full perspective for each call, including information such as who your main competitors are, how often they are mentioned during the sales journey, and how successful your company is compared to your competitors.

Where to go: Admin center > Settings > Data protection & privacy

Gong's standard data retention period for existing customers is the lesser of three years and the period you are a customer. If a non-standard retention period is required due to regulatory or other mandatory business reasons, we recommend consulting with your Revenue Architect (RA) on what the likely usage impacts to your teams will be. If you cease being a Gong customer, your data will be irreversibly deleted in 30 days.

Warning: If a retention period is shortened and calls are purged, Gong will not be able to restore those calls. Significantly shortening the retention period may impact Gong insights, and reduce the overall value you get from Gong.

Data retained includes emails, calls, and transcripts that are stored in Gong.

This policy does not include calls that are in the company library. Calls in the company library are not automatically deleted after three years, and are available until they are deleted from the library manually.

chunks.text:
Calls in the Gong library:
Company library folders: Calls here are not automatically deleted after three years, and are available until they are deleted from the library manually. This applies to both public and private folders.

Your library folders: Calls here are automatically deleted once they have reached the limit of your company retention policy. This applies to your folders and folders that have been shared with you.

Streams: Calls collected in streams are automatically deleted once they have reached the limit of your company’s data retention policy.

To apply the retention policy to calls in the company library too, click Admin center > Settings tab> Data capture > Data protection & privacy and toggle on Apply retention policy to calls stored in library. This automatically removes calls in the company library once they have reached the limit of the company retention policy.

chunks.title: Database design

chunks.text:
Conversations table:
The CONVERSATIONS table is a supertype used to store details common to all conversations in Gong. A record is generated for each call, email, and meeting. Shared attributes such as workspace, conversation type (call, email, meeting), and start time are stored here.

The CONVERSATIONS table includes two identifiers:

- CONVERSATION_KEY: The primary key. A unique identifier for the record in the CONVERSATIONS table.
- CONVERATION_ID : A foreign key to the table for the conversation type (CALLS, EMAILS, or MEETINGS)

The CONVERSATIONS table includes two identifiers:

- CONVERSATION_KEY: The primary key. A unique identifier for the record in the CONVERSATIONS table.
- CONVERATION_ID : A foreign key to the table for the conversation type (CALLS, EMAILS, or MEETINGS)
chunks.title: Database design

chunks.text:
Identifiers for calls, emails, and meetings:
Each conversation type has its own table that stores attributes relevant to that type. For example, the CALLS table stores call-specific details such as recording URL or duration. Each conversation is saved once in their dedicated table and contains the following identifiers:

- CONVERSATION_KEY: A foreign key to the CONVERSATIONS.CONVERSATION_KEY
- CONVERATION_ID: The unique identifier for the conversation in the table for the call

The MEETINGS table includes additional identifiers:

- CALL_CONVERSATION_ID: A foreign key to the CALLS table so that the meeting can be associated with a call. As not all meetings have an associated call this can be NULL.
- CALL_ID: A foreign key to the CALL_RECORDINGS table. This is the Id of the call recording

chunks.title: Database design

chunks.text:
Call, email, and meeting data:
The CALLS table includes call attributes including the call spotlight.

Once the call has been recorded it is added to the CALL_RECORDINGS table, with details such as the language the call took place in and the duration of the call. Any activities done on the call, such as feedback or comments are stored in the USER_CONVERSATION_GONG_ACTIVITIES table. The USER_CONVERSATION_GONG_ACTIVITIES table holds the ID of the user who did the activity, as well as the date and time and the activity type.

The CALL_TRANSCRIPT table contains a JSON of the transcript. The call is split up according to who spoke when during the conversation. The JSON includes a speaker ID which represents the person speaking at that time. Comments made on calls are available in the COMMENTS table.

Email and meeting details are stored in the EMAILS and MEETINGS tables respectively. Call, email, and meeting participants are found in the CONVERSATION_PARTICIPANTS table.

chunks.title: Database design

chunks.text:
Gong users:
All users are stored in the USERS table which includes user details such as their first name, last name and email address. This table maintains history for the user so you can see details such as who was a manager when a specific call took place. In addition, to support the situation where a Gong user has multiple CRM IDs, the USER_CRM_IDS table contains the CRM IDs for each user.

chunks.title: Database design

chunks.text:
Trackers, scorecard, and insights data:
Trackers are tools that identify when words, phrases or concepts are mentioned in calls and emails, allowing you to know what your reps and customers are talking about. Smart trackers and keyword trackers are stored in the TRACKERS table and each tracker identified in a conversation is added to the CONVERSATIONS_TRACKERS table.

You can see data on who has filled out scorecards and their assessment of the call. The SCORECARD_QUESTIONS table contains a row for each question in the scorecard together with the scorecard details, such as the scorecard name and when it was created. The SCORECARD_ANSWERS table contains a row for each question and answer given and includes the Id of the call the scorecard was given for.

You can associate your CRM objects, such as opportunities, deals, or leads, with your Gong conversations using the CONVERSATION_CONTEXTS table. A conversation can be associated with multiple CRM objects. For example, a conversation can be associated with a deal or opportunity and an account.

You can get statistics on your reps activities and how they manage calls in the USER_CONVERSATION_GONG_ACTIVITIES and INTERACTION_STATS. These tables give you details on what kind of actions a user did on a call, such as asking for feedback and statistics on metrics such as how long they speak on a call or how many questions they ask.

chunks.text:
Getting Forecast data:
The following diagram displays the relationships between the tables containing forecast data:

Forecast data includes forecast submissions and targets.

In the FORECAST_SUBMISSIONS and FORECAST_TARGETS tables, you can see each user's forecast and targets for a specific period. These can be for an individual sales rep, or for a team. When the value is the team forecast or target, the IS_TEAM field is set to true. The period the forecast or target is for is set according to the PERIOD_TYPE, PERIOD_YEAR and PERIOD_NUMBER. The period type designates whether the forecast is for a month or a quarter, the period year sets the year and the period number sets which quarter or month in the year the forecast and target are for.
chunks.body:
The following diagram displays the relationships between the tables containing forecast data:

Forecast data includes forecast submissions and targets.

In the FORECAST_SUBMISSIONS and FORECAST_TARGETS tables, you can see each user's forecast and targets for a specific period. These can be for an individual sales rep, or for a team. When the value is the team forecast or target, the IS_TEAM field is set to true. The period the forecast or target is for is set according to the PERIOD_TYPE, PERIOD_YEAR and PERIOD_NUMBER. The period type designates whether the forecast is for a month or a quarter, the period year sets the year and the period number sets which quarter or month in the year the forecast and target are for.

chunks.text:
Getting Forecast data > Deal likelihood scores:
Gong assesses each deal and gives it a score indicating how likely the deal will be closed-won in its expected quarter compared to other deals in the pipeline. The DEAL_LIKELIHOOD_SCORES table contains each deal’s score, score category (Low, Fair, or High) and the last time the score was updated. The details of a deal can be retrieved from the CRM using the CRM_DEAL_ID.

📘 Using a Service Principal & Token instead of your Personal Access Token You may prefer to create a Service Principal to use for authentication instead of using a Personal Access Token. To do so, use the following steps to create a Service Principal and generate an access token. In your Databricks workspace, click your username in the top right, click Admin Settings, Identity and access, and next to the Service Principals options, click Manage. Click the Add service principal button, click Add new in the modal, enter a display name and click Add. Click on the newly created Service Principal, and under Entitlements select Databricks SQL Access and Workspace Access. Click Update, and make a note of the Application ID of your newly created Service Principal. Back in the Admin Settings menu, click the Advanced section (under the Workspace admin menu). In the Access Control section, next to the Personal Access Tokens row, click Permission Settings. Search for and select the Service Principal you created, select the Can use permission, click Add, and then Save. Navigate back to the SQL Warehouses section of your Workspace, click the SQL Warehouses tab, and select the SQL Warehouse you created in Step 1. Click Permissions in the top right, search for and select the Service Principal you created, select the Can use permission, and click Add. Use your terminal to generate a Service Principal Access Token using your Personal Access Token generated above. Record the token value. This token can now be used as the access token for the connection.

Step 2: Configure Access:
Record the token value. This token can now be used as the access token for the connection.

curl --request POST "https://<databricks-account-id>. cloud. databricks. com/api/2. 0/token-management/on-behalf-of/tokens" \ --header "Authorization: Bearer <personal-access-token>" \ --data '{ "application_id": "<application-id-of-service-principal>", "lifetime_seconds": <token-lifetime-in-seconds-eg-31536000>, "comment": "<some-discription-of-this-token>" }'

1. In the Databricks UI, select the Catalog tab, and select the target Catalog . Within the catalog Permissions tab, click Grant . In the following modal, select the principal for which you generated the access token, select USE CATALOG , and click Grant .
2. Under the target Catalog , select the target schema (e.g., main.default , or create a new target schema). Within the schema Permissions tab, click Grant . In the following modal, select the principal for which you generated the access token, and select either ALL PRIVILEGES or the following 9 privileges and then click Grant :

- USE SCHEMA
- APPLY TAG
- MODIFY
- READ VOLUME
- SELECT
- WRITE VOLUME
- CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW
- CREATE TABLE
- CREATE VOLUME

What’s changed?:
1. Deals is now Revenue. The Deals section in the sidebar has been renamed to Revenue. This update reflects that the section now centralizes accounts, deals, forecasts, analytics, and dashboards in a unified space.
2. Pipeline is now Deals. Under Revenue, what was previously called Pipeline is now labeled Deals. There’s no functional change, this is a naming update only. You’ll continue to see your deal boards, to help you visually track and manage your sales pipeline.
3. New: Account boards. Under Revenue, you’ll now see Accounts. Account boards provide a dedicated space to manage and prioritize accounts, giving teams a more complete view of performance across both deals and accounts.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

chunks.title: Deals widget

chunks.text:
Building a deals widget:
Note:Your profile must include the relevant permission to create and manage widgets to dashboards

To build a new deals widget:

1. Select your dashboard, click +New widget and select Deals from the gallery.
2. In the dashboard header, click the edit icon to rename your widget and, optionally, + Add description.
3. Under Deal board, select the deal board from which the deals displayed in the widget are derived.
4. Under Pipeline, select the Default deal board tab from which deals are derived. If you want viewers to not be able to change this selection, uncheck Add dropdown to widget.
5. Under Columns, we import the initial 10 fixed deal board columns, and the amount columns configured in the board. These are all included in the widget by default and are ordered as in the original deal board. You can customize the list by removing some of them (except for Deal name, which can't be removed). Viewers can later sort the list by any of the selected columns.
6. Under Filters, set the criteria to include a deal in the widget. For example: deal amount is greater than 30,000
7. Under Select team and period, you’ll notice the team member and date fields are set to be dynamic and respond to whatever is selected in your dashboard. You can change them to fixed values. Note:If you select fixed values for the team member and period, the widget would no longer respond to selections made on the dashboard level.
8. Play with the Preview options on the right to validate your settings. When you’re happy with the results, click Save.

chunks.text: Associating activities such as calls and emails to your CRM entities provides proper context for your Gong activities. Once a Gong activity is properly associated, you will know who a call was made to, the company they work with and the deal the activity is for. Gong provides a default association algorithm for identifying the accounts and opportunities that should be associated with each Gong activity. To get more accurate results, you can customize the settings.
chunks.body: Associating activities such as calls and emails to your CRM entities provides proper context for your Gong activities. Once a Gong activity is properly associated, you will know who a call was made to, the company they work with and the deal the activity is for. Gong provides a default association algorithm for identifying the accounts and opportunities that should be associated with each Gong activity. To get more accurate results, you can customize the settings.
chunks.title: Default CRM entity association

chunks.text:
Account association:
1. Find the CRM contacts that correspond to the activity participants. CRM contacts are identified by their email address or phone number. In addition to the standard CRM email address field, we also check for matches in any fields listed in Contact email addresses and Lead email adddresses in the Engage CRM setup page. For details of how to set this up, see Set up Gong Engage. Association works as follows:
  1. For participants that have a CRM contact:
    1. Associate the activity to that account
  2. For participants that don’t have a CRM contact:
    1. If there is an account with the same website domain as the participant email domain, associate the activity to that account.
    2. If there isn’t an account with the same website domain as the participant email domain, do nothing.

In this scenario, an activity could be associated with multiple accounts or with no accounts. If you customize your settings, the list of accounts that can be associated with the activity is expanded and other accounts may be found to be relevant to association.

chunks.title: Default CRM entity association

chunks.text:
Deal association:
1. Identify open deals for the accounts associated in the account association stage. See How we identify open deals.
2. If there are open deals:
  1. Associate with deals where the deal owner is an activity participant.
  2. If there are no deal owners, associate with all deals.
3. If there are no open deals, no deals are associated with the activity.

chunks.title: Default CRM entity association

chunks.text:
Deal association > How we identify open deals:
The list of deals includes those that were open around the time the conversation took place. Identifying open deals is based on the value of two fields:

- deal status: set by the rep, indicates whether the deal is open or closed.
- deal close date: a rough estimate of when the rep expects the deal to close

If these fields aren’t maintained, there may be deals where the status is open and the close date was several weeks or months previous. In addition, conversations just before or after a deal is opened or closed may still be related to that deal.

Therefore, the list of potential deals to associate is made up of:

- Deals opened up to 14 days after the conversation took place
- Deals closed up to 14 days before the conversation took place
- Deals with a deal status of open but the close date field was up to 100 days before the conversation took place

This timeline shows when conversations might be associated with an opportunity based on the opportunity’s status and close date.

chunks.text:
CRM entity reassociation:
As data is added to the CRM it can be necessary to reassess the association assigned when the activity occurred. For example, if a new account is generated, we may be able to associate an activity to an account that we had previously not found a relevant association for.

Creating, updating or deleting the following CRM fields triggers reassociating activities to CRM entities:

- CRM contact: email, phone, mobilephone, accountId
- CRM account: website
- CRM deals or opportunities: parentid, contact reference fields depending on configuration, user reference fields depending on configuration
- Contact roles in a deal: (reassociation happens when the deal contacts association settings are set to On: Optional or On: Mandatory) contactId, opportunityId

Reassociation could result in activities which were originally associated to a specific deal is now reassociated with a different deal, or activities that weren’t associated to any deal may now be associated to a deal.

We update relevant activities that occurred up to one year prior to the current day.

chunks.title: Define the recording settings

chunks.text:
1. Click Admin center > Settings tab > Data capture > Recording settings.
2. In the Web conferencing calls area, answer the following questions:
  1. Which meetings should be recorded? Choose between:
    - Web conference calls organized by a recorded team member
    - Web conference calls organized by anyone in your company, with a recorded team member invited Note:If you use the Gong bot for Zoom to record calls, you must give your Zoom users permissions to record to computer files. See Set up Zoom recording with the Gong bot
  2. Should Gong record internal web conference calls? All calls with participants who are external to the company are recorded. In this setting, you can choose whether to record: To record external calls only, ensure your internal domains are defined so that Gong will be able to identify which calls include external participants.
    - Yes, record internal web conference calls
    - No, only record web conference calls with at least one invitee outside your company
  3. Should Gong record video? Choose between recording audio and video, or audio only.
  4. Select the name of the recording bot. Choose the name you want displayed for the Gong bot:
    - Gong Recorder
    - [Your Company] Recorder by Gong
    - Gong AI Notetaker
    - Gong Notetaker
3. In the All calls area, define the minimum duration a call must be to be imported and analyzed. This setting is applied to web conference and telephony system calls. Note:Default is 30 seconds for web conference and telephony callsDefault is 3 seconds for calls made with the Gong Dialer or a dialer associated with Gong Engage (even if the call isn’t made through Engage). This cannot be configured manually.
  - Default is 30 seconds for web conference and telephony calls
  - Default is 3 seconds for calls made with the Gong Dialer or a dialer associated with Gong Engage (even if the call isn’t made through Engage). This cannot be configured manually.
4. Click UPDATE to save your changes.

Follow these steps to delete a workspace. You can also use this flow to merge two workspaces together.

To delete a workspace:

1. Move team members whose emails are imported to the new workspace.
2. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
3. In the Settings tab, click Workspaces under Company.
4. Click the trash icon in the Last updated column.
5. Select the workspace that you want to transfer any calls and home workspaces to, and then click Delete.

Calls and the home workspaces are transferred. The following items will be deleted:

- Permission profiles
- Trackers
- Topics
- Scorecards
- Custom vocabulary
- Automation rules
- Library folders, streams, saved searches, and notifications

When you're set up for native Zoom recording, there are 2 settings in Gong that can help you both reduce the amount of storage used in your Zoom account, and help you uphold your data retention policy.

Both settings are in the Zoom settings page, accessible via the Web Conferencing settings.
chunks.body:
When you're set up for native Zoom recording, there are 2 settings in Gong that can help you both reduce the amount of storage used in your Zoom account, and help you uphold your data retention policy.

Both settings are in the Zoom settings page, accessible via the Web Conferencing settings.
chunks.title: Deleting recordings in Zoom

chunks.text:
Delete recordings from Zoom once they are retrieved by Gong:
Turn this setting on for 2 important benefits:

- It minimizes the effect of Gong recordings on your Zoom storage, particularly if your Zoom plan has a limited amount of cloud recording storage capacity. (See the Zoom Dashboard to view the amount of storage in your account.) After Gong retrieves a recording, it is deleted from Zoom, thus ensuring the recordings don't affect your storage capacity.
- It gives you more control over the recording because once a call is in Gong, it becomes subject to Gong's data retention policy, and other access controls and permissions. IMPORTANT: Be mindful of upholding personal rights under international privacy regulations. For example, under European law, people have the right to request their personal data be deleted from your system. With Gong, you're able to easily delete personal data. If the "delete recordings from Zoom" setting is not turned on, a copy of the call will remain in Zoom, meaning you are not compliant with this regulation.

NoteZoom will send an email alert to the account owner when usage is at 80% of the subscribed storage limit. If the storage limit is reached during a recording, Zoom will continue to record until the meeting ends.

chunks.text:
Delete recordings initiated by Gong but not retrieved:
Turn this setting on to delete recordings (in Zoom) that we initiated but decided not to bring into Gong (i.e. short recordings).

For example, short calls where:

- Someone stopped recording at the beginning of the call
- Someone joined the call via the consent page, but did not give their consent to be recorded

If you do not turn on this setting, short recordings will remain in your Zoom account.

chunks.title: Zoom settings for native Zoom recording

chunks.text:
Required Zoom settings:
These required settings are prerequisites to enabling native Zoom recording.

1. Make sure Cloud recording is switched ON and unlocked for any group that contains users recorded by Gong.
2. Automatic recording can be switched ON or OFF, but it must be unlocked for any group that contains users recorded by Gong.
3. Make sure the Embed passcode in invite link for one-click join is enabled. This must be set in order to display the consent page before a meeting.
4. If you have a Zoom pro license, in the Cloud recording settings section, make sure the following are checked:
  - Record active speaker with shared screen
  - Record active speaker, gallery view and shared screen separately
    - Active speaker

Note:Recording consent disclaimerZoom will always notify meeting participants that a meeting is being recorded. It is not possible to disable this notification. For participants joining by desktop client or mobile app, the screen will display a recording consent disclaimer. Participants who dial in on the phone will hear an audio prompt when they first join the meeting if it is already being recorded or at the time the recording is started.

Download a call snippet:
To download a call snippet:

1. Open the call page under the call screen.
2. Yellow bars will appear on the timeline below the call screen. Move them to the part of the call you want to select. This part is highlighted in the transcript also, where it’s anchored by pointers, and the selection is synchronized as you drag either the yellow bars or the pointers.
3. In the action menu that opens, choose Download snippet. The file will be downloaded as a video.

Downloading may take a few moments, since we need to prepare the snippet before it is downloaded. Before this happnes, you'll be warned that the file may contain personal information subject to various data protection regulations. Please make sure that any personal information in the file is kept confidential.

chunks.text:
Editing flows with active contacts and leads:
You can edit a flow at any time. What you can change depends on whether the flow has contacts. Locking the structure of flows with active contacts and leads helps keep reporting clear and prevents version confusion.

Open the flow you want to work on by going to Engage from the main menu on the left-hand side, then Flows, then select the flow you want to work on.

If a flow has no active or past contacts, you can:

- Add, delete, or reorder steps
- Change step types
- Edit step content and timing

If a flow already includes contacts, structural changes are locked to keep reporting accurate. You can’t:

- Add new steps
- Delete steps
- Reorder steps
- Change step types

You can still:

- Edit step content (email subject and body)
- Update timing and delays
- Modify assets within steps

To make structural changes, duplicate the flow and edit the new version.

chunks.text:
Editing flows with active contacts and leads > How edits affect contacts already in a flow:
Edits apply only to steps that haven’t been generated yet.

Edits applied to existing to-dos

- Message updates reflect in scheduled or upcoming steps
- Timing changes apply if the to-do hasn’t been created yet
- New steps at the end of a duplicated flow apply as contacts reach them

Auto emails use the latest content as long as the email hasn’t been drafted yet. The draft is created right before send time. If you update the subject or body before the draft is created, the scheduled email will use the updated content. Changes to timing won’t affect auto emails that are already scheduled for contacts who have reached that step.

Edits not applied

- Changes won’t affect steps where a to-do has already been generated

For example, if a contact is already on step 3 and that to-do exists, updating step 3 won’t affect them. If they haven’t reached step 3 yet, the update will apply.

When a flow has active contacts or leads, you’ll see a banner at the top of the flow editor explaining these restrictions. If you have permission, the banner also includes a Duplicate flow option so you can quickly create a copy and make structural changes there. This helps ensure that contacts already in a flow continue through the same structure and that reporting remains consistent and accurate.

FAQs:
What happens to contacts and leads in the original flow if I duplicate it?

Contacts and leads in the original flow remain there. There is no connection between the original flow and the duplicated flow.

The new flow has no active contacts and leads upon duplication, so you can modify its structure.

Do I need to pause contacts and leads in the original flow and add them to the duplicated flow?

This is up to you. Gong does not automatically move contacts between flows.

What if contacts and leads are at different steps when I duplicate the flow?

Contacts remain in the original flow at their current step. Gong does not automatically move contacts to the duplicated flow. If you want contacts to move to the new flow, you need to manage that transition manually.

Sending a large number of emails all at once may raise red flags for Internet service providers. To help your company maintain a healthy sender reputation and avoid getting marked as spam, your admin can set up email limits for the following categories:

- Number of flow emails from the same sender per day/per week
- Number of flow emails sent from the same domain (company) per day
- Number of flow emails sent from your company to the same recipient per day
- Number of flow emails sent from your company to recipients within the same domain (company) per day. Generic domains, such as Gmail, Yahoo, and Outlook, are excluded from this limit

While all types of emails count towards reaching the limit, once it is reached, only flow emails will be limited. Email limits refresh in a rolling 24-hour window, except for Emails from the same sender, which resets at midnight (12 AM) each day according to the user’s time zone, and weekly flow email limits for individual reps which reset at midnight on Saturday. Auto emails snoozed by a sending limit will be sent at 8:00 AM user local time.

How will I know when I’ve reached an email limit?

When you’re close to reaching a flow email limit or have reached a limit, we’ll let you know on the To-dos page and inside the email composer.

When you’re close to reaching a flow email limit, you might see one of the following notifications:

The following table describes Gong's onboarding emails and which emails can be controlled, and by whom.

| Topic | Description | Sent when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Welcome | An optional email that admins can send to welcome new users in Gong | Tech admins can decide whether the welcome mail is sent at the time a user is provisioned, or later. |
| Complete setup | An email sent to prompt people to complete a manual step required to finish setting up their Gong account, for example to connect their calendar or email. | Gong identifies that the step needs to be completed |
| First call is due to be recorded | An email sent to help people understand what to expect when their web conference is recorded by Gong. | Gong is scheduled to record a web conference call for the first time. |
| Gong product tips | A short series of emails intended to help onboarding to Gong that includes tips on various features. The first email is sent after a new user signs in to Gong for the first time. | Individuals: manage your emails on your My Notifications page.Tech admins: manage the default settings for your company in the Notification Settings page. |

Where to go: Open the relevant call.

Add your calls to third-party applications such as a learning management system (LMS) for a seamless, more secure, experience. For example, share best demos, great sales pitches, and more so that other people can learn from them.

For security reasons, people must be Gong users with permission to access the embedded call, and they need to be signed in to Gong to play it. There are three ways you can embed a call or snippet: manually, by copying the URL, or using API.
chunks.title: Embed a call in third-party software

chunks.text:
Manually embed a call or snippet:
1. Go to the call page of the call you want to share:
  - In the top right corner of the call, click Share call > Embed call. This opens a dialog with a code and a URL. You can also share part of the call from here. Click Share snippet and select the part you want to share.
  - To embed a call snippet, select a snippet in the transcript, or from the action bar under the call video, and click Embed call.
2. Copy the code or URL:
  - If the third-party where you’re pasting the call/snippet supports adding HTML code, click COPY CODE to copy the embed code, which is the iframe tag containing the relevant embedded call URL ( recommended).
  - If your system supports adding URLs and embeds them in an iframe, click COPY URL to copy the call’s embeddable URL, which you can then put inside the third-party application.
3. Follow the instructions of your third-party application to insert the code/URL where you want. The call displays inline where you placed the code.
  - For the copied URL, use an iframe element as follows: <iframe width="[width]" height="[height]" src="[embeddable-url]" frameborder="0"/> Where the embeddable-url is the URL you got in step 2. Note that the iFrame width must have a width of at least 280px.
