This section explains the conventions used when building the Snowflake database and functionality for implementing various features such as history tracking and support for ETL.
chunks.title: Integration functionality

chunks.text:
Data update methodology:
Gong data is made available in data warehouses using different methodologies:

- Snowflake: Get your data via a data share
- Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift: Changed data is transferred daily
- S3: Data is appended, so the last occurance of an Id is the correct value. Data is updated daily.

Note:If you create databases, schemas, tables, or views that consume Gong data, those objects are not automatically updated when the Gong Data Cloud schema changes.

Note:If you create databases, schemas, tables, or views that consume Gong data, those objects are not automatically updated when the Gong Data Cloud schema changes.
chunks.title: Integration functionality

chunks.text:
ETL support:
Each table includes ETL_MODIFIED_DATETIME column which records the date and time the entity was last updated.
chunks.body: Each table includes ETL_MODIFIED_DATETIME column which records the date and time the entity was last updated.
chunks.title: Integration functionality

chunks.text:
History tracking:
History is tracked in the USERS table using Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) type 2.0 with the VALID_FROM_DATETIME and VALID_TO_DATETIME columns. The VALID_TO_DATETIME is NULL for data that is currently valid. Historical data is available from August 2022. Contact us if you need earlier data.
chunks.body: History is tracked in the USERS table using Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) type 2.0 with the VALID_FROM_DATETIME and VALID_TO_DATETIME columns. The VALID_TO_DATETIME is NULL for data that is currently valid. Historical data is available from August 2022. Contact us if you need earlier data.
chunks.title: Integration functionality

chunks.text:
Update frequency:
The Gong database is updated a maximum of 24 hours after the data is available in Gong. Forecast submissions are updated once an hour.
chunks.body: The Gong database is updated a maximum of 24 hours after the data is available in Gong. Forecast submissions are updated once an hour.
chunks.title: Integration functionality

chunks.text:
Soft delete:
Certain tables contain the is_deleted field to support soft delete of data. The is_deleted field by default is false, and is changed to true for records that were deleted in Gong. When a record is deleted in Gong, some of the data for that record is deleted from Snowflake as well. The record's primary keys are retained.

When a record is deleted in Gong, some of the data for that record is deleted from Snowflake as well. The record's primary keys are retained.
chunks.title: Integration functionality

chunks.text:
Schema and naming conventions:
This is a list of conventions used when designing the database:

- The schema is in 3rd normal form. Some data may be denormalized for query ergonomics.
- Table names are plural and snake_case.
- Column names are SNAKE_CASE.
- Id columns are suffixed with _id and are of varchar type and should be treated as such regardless of their content.
- Date and time column names are suffixed with _datetime and are of type TIMESTAMP_TZ which includes UTC offset.

Use your existing calls in third-party applications such as a learning management system (LMS) for a seamless, more secure, experience. For example, share best demos, great sales pitches, and more so that other people can learn from them.

For security reasons, people must be Gong users with permission to access the embedded call, and they need to be signed in to Gong to play it.

There are three ways you can embed a call or snippet: manually, by copying the URL, or using API. These three methods are described below.
chunks.title: Embed a call in third-party software

chunks.text:
Manually embed a call or snippet:
This is the easiest way to embed a call or snippet.

1. Start by picking what you want to share:
  - To embed an entire call, go to the call page and click Share Call > Embed call.
  - To embed a call snippet, go to the call page, select a snippet in the transcript view, and click Share > Embed call.
2. Copy the code or URL:
  - If the third-party where you’re pasting the call/snippet supports adding HTML code, click COPY CODE to copy the embed code, which is the iframe tag containing the relevant embedded call URL (recommended).
  - If your system supports adding URLs and embeds them in an iframe, click COPY URL to copy the call’s embeddable URL, which you can then put inside the third-party application.
3. Follow the instructions of your third-party application to insert the code/URL where you want. The call displays inline where you placed the code.
  - For the copied URL, use an iframe element as follows: Where the embeddable-url is the URL you got in step 2. Note that the iFrame width must have a width of at least 280px.

chunks.title: Embed a call in third-party software

chunks.text:
Copy the URL (oEmbed):
Use this method if the target third-party application supports the oEmbed protocol.

1. Start by picking what you want to share:
  - To embed the entire call, copy the call URL from the browser address of the call page in Gong.
  - To embed a call snippet, select a snippet of the call in the transcript view, and click Share > Share internally, and click Get shareable link.
2. Paste the URL that you got in step 1 to the third-party application embed area.
3. In the target, invoke the following request: https://[your subdomain].app.gong.io/oembed?url=[call page url] Where the call page url is the URL you got in step 1. The call displays inline where you placed the code. Tip:Ask your Gong admin if you're not sure what your company subdomain is.

chunks.title: Embed a call in third-party software

chunks.text:
Use API to embed a call or snippet:
Use this method when you have obtained the call ID or URL via the API.

1. Use the Gong API to get the call ID via the API. Refer to the Gong API documentation if you don't know how to do this.
2. Prepare the following URL formats for embedding: Tip:Ask your Gong admin if you're not sure what your company subdomain is.
  - Full call: https://[your subdomain].app.gong.io/embedded-call?call-id=[call-id] Where the call-id is the one obtained via the API.
  - Call snippet (based on data obtained from the API like topics, trackers or keywords): https://[your subdomain].app.gong.io/embedded-call?call-id= [call-id]&from=[from]&to=[to] Where the call-id is the one obtained via the API, and the from and to are the number of seconds since the beginning of the call for the start and end of the snippet.
3. Add the prepared URL to an iFrame in the target: <iframe width="[width]" height="[height]" src="[embeddable-url]" frameborder="0"/> Where embeddable-url is the URL you prepared in step 2.

These metrics support common workflows such as 1:1s, coaching conversations, onboarding, and enablement planning.

Call screen: Before the video begins to play, you'll see basic info about who was on the call. While the call is playing, you'll see the person who is talking, or whatever was shared during the call at that time.

chunks.text:
- Send data via Zapier to supported applications Zapier enables you to pick and choose which data to forward and to who via, for example, Slack or HubSpot. Include data such as user name, media type, user ID, opportunity name, account name, snippet, call URL, opportunity amount, scope, and snippet speaker. For more information, see Zapier.
- Send data using webhooks* Webhooks are often used to send data to other apps to automate tasks and workflows and combine the call data with other company data to see a fuller picture. The data includes topics, trackers, team member stats, and more. For more information, see Create a webhook rule.
- Automatically delete calls Delete calls based on the rule’s filters. For example, if you set a filter in which specific terms were said (or not said), calls in which those terms were detected (or not detected) will be deleted. Once a call is deleted, it can’t be retrieved. Note that speech-to-text conversions can be inaccurate, so calls that shouldn’t be deleted may be deleted, and vice versa. For more information, see Create a rule to delete calls.
- Automatically set call as private Set calls to private based on the rule’s filters. For example, if you set a filter in which specific terms were said (or not said), calls in which those terms were detected (or not detected) will be set to private. Once a call is set as private, the call host can make it public. For more information, see Create a rule to set calls as private.

chunks.text:
Who can use this: Any team memberRequired permissions: Manage AI Trackers

What are keyword trackers?

Keyword trackers detect words, terms or phrases that are mentioned in calls, and flags them, so that team members can easily spot them. The calls that trackers identify are also used for data analysis.

Where can I see keyword trackers?

Keyword trackers can be seen in many places, including call pages, in emails, in the Gong API, and in the CRM export. You control where trackers are displayed. You can also rearrange the trackers to determine the order in which they appear.

What can I track with keyword trackers?

A keyword tracker can track several words or terms, each separated by a comma. If you want to track a large number (10,000, for example), put the number in quotation marks (“10,000”) so that the digits are not split when tracking. Use filters to narrow down whether words are tracked only when said by a customer, only by people at your company, or by anyone.

How many keyword trackers can I have?

You can have as many keyword trackers as you want.

How long does it take for keyword trackers to start working?

Keyword trackers start tracking right away.

Can I search for words in past calls using keyword trackers?

Yes, you can. Go to Conversations > Search and use the trackers filter.

How do I view each phrase as a separate tracker?

Similar phrases may appear in one column when displayed in a CSV report, CRM Call object, or API request result. To include a separate column/tracker for each phrase, select the Separate phrases option.

chunks.title: Keyword tracker FAQs

chunks.text:
To include a separate column/tracker for each phrase, select the Separate phrases option.

Why aren’t my keyword tracker metrics showing up?

When you create a new keyword tracker, or save an update to an existing tracker, Gong reprocesses all of your company’s calls to look for that tracker. While we're processing, the tracker doesn't appear in metrics on the Stats page or in the Gong API. However, you can search for the tracker on the Search page.

Processing time is determined by the number of calls that are processed by Gong at the same time, and in extreme cases, this may take a couple of days.

How does Gong match words and terms?

Gong matches words and terms with the words said on the call verbatim. To track related words and phrase forms, click Include related word forms.

For example, for “renew” Gong will surface “renewal” and “renewing” too.

How can I use keyword trackers to bulk analyze my calls?

When exporting calls in CSV format, Gong includes the keyword tracker you select and indicates how many times the words or terms appear in each call. For deeper analysis, you can set up each word or term to appear in a separate column. This way, you can compare competitors, technologies or other words across your calls. Similarly, the data is available using the Gong API and when pushing the data into the CRM.

How many calls does a keyword tracker need to surface in order for it to appear in 'Stats for trackers'?

A keyword tracker must appear in at least four calls to be shown in Stats. If a tracker appears less than four calls, it shows N/A.

For deeper analysis, you can set up each word or term to appear in a separate column. This way, you can compare competitors, technologies or other words across your calls. Similarly, the data is available using the Gong API and when pushing the data into the CRM.

How many calls does a keyword tracker need to surface in order for it to appear in 'Stats for trackers'?

A keyword tracker must appear in at least four calls to be shown in Stats. If a tracker appears less than four calls, it shows N/A.
chunks.title: Keyword tracker FAQs

chunks.text:
If a tracker appears less than four calls, it shows N/A.

Why should I download and upload keyword trackers?

A typical use is a team of business admins using on the same tracker, with the need to collaborate in an external tool, such as Google Sheets. A list of trackers can be exported in CSV format, edited, and then imported again to add new or update existing trackers.

Another common use is copying trackers from one workspace to another.

Is there a best practice for uploading trackers?

We recommend you always export a fresh copy of the keyword tracker CSV, make the required changes, and then import the updated file. This ensures that any manual updates to keyword trackers made in Gong are included in the latest version.

Also, it's important not to change the format of the keyword tracker list. If you're copying trackers to another workspace, follow the instructions for deleting the tracker fingerprints in this article.

How can I copy keyword trackers between workspaces?

Glad you asked. Follow this guide to maintain the same trackers across different workspaces.

Do new keyword trackers retroactively update in the conversation record in the Gong for Salesforce app?

You bet they do! However, this magic only works when a tracker is updated; and the option to push to Salesforce is selected (in the tracker settings). Gong will then automatically go back and re-push calls with that tracker to reflect whatever changes were made.

Gong will then automatically go back and re-push calls with that tracker to reflect whatever changes were made. I’ve set a word in a keyword tracker but it’s not getting tracked. Why not?

In some cases, what we transcribe in a call is different from what was actually said. For example, if someone says "Ryan" very slowly or with a bad audio connection, we might transcribe it as "Rye" "and." So, if you've set "Ryan" as a word to be tracked in a keyword tracker, it may not be picked up.

If this seems to be what’s happening, add the term “Ryan” to your custom vocabulary, and have it set as the term to replace what’s being transcribed as “Rye” “and”. Learn more about using the custom vocabulary

What’s a KPI widget:

chunks.text:
Building a KPI widget:
Note:Your profile must include the relevant permission to create and manage widgets to dashboards

To build a KPI widget:
chunks.body:
Note:Your profile must include the relevant permission to create and manage widgets to dashboards

To build a KPI widget:
chunks.title: KPI widget

chunks.text:
Building a KPI widget:
1. Select your dashboard, click +New widget and select KPI from the gallery.
2. In the dashboard header, click the edit icon to rename your widget and, optionally, + Add description.
3. By default, the widget is set to display a single metric. To display two metrics, click + Add metric. To display a forecast submission number, rather than a metric’s value, click the Metric dropdown and select Forecast submission.
4. If you chose to display a metric, from the Select metric dropdown, select your metric or click + New metric to create a new metric, and then pull it to your KPI widget. Click to edit an existing metric and click Save. You can rename it by clicking and then Rename metric.
5. If you chose to display a forecast submission, select the forecast board (line of business), the submission category, and whether to include individual submissions or a team rollup.
  1. Individual submissions reflect the latest submission provided by the selected manager or individual seller: When the manager is selected, their submission for the entire team is reflected, and when an individual seller is selected, their personal submission is reflected.
  2. Team rollups reflect the total of the latest submissions of all team members reporting to the selected manager: When the manager is selected, the latest submissions of their direct reports are rolled up and displayed as a single number.
6. For each metric and forecast submission, check Measure it against a target to track its target attainment (for example, measure booking $ against the booking target).
7. After selecting the metrics/forecast submissions, you’ll notice two filters are added to the widget, and the team member and date fields are set to be dynamic and respond to whatever is selected in your dashboard. You can change them to fixed values. Note:If you select fixed values for the team member and period, the widget would no longer respond to selections made on the dashboard level.
8. In addition to the two filters, you may add any filter (+Add filter) that defines which deals qualify to be included in the widget. For example, deals in which Sales qualified is true and Deal stage is neither Closed-won nor Closed-lost.
9. Select your Drilldown view: the deal board that opens up when viewers click to inspect the deals included in the widget. The selected drilldown view inherits the column selection and their order from the selected deal board, as well as the warning configuration, but not the deal board filters.
10. When you’re happy with the Preview results on the right, click Save.

chunks.title: Leadership forecast dashboard recipe

chunks.text:
How to build it:
1. Build 4 KPI widgets:
  1. Booking attainment:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Bookings ($) and set it to be measured against the bookings target.
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Gap to target:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Gap to target.
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  3. Coverage:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Coverage ($) and measure it against the open pipeline target.
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  4. Total pipeline created
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Pipeline created ($).
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
2. Build 1 forecast rollup widget:
  1. Period forecast rollup
    1. Base the widget on a line of business and select the column “team members” to include in the widget.
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
3. Build 1 changes widget:
  1. Pipeline changes in the last week:
    1. Base the widget on a line of business.
    2. Select the forecast category and the range date to reflect the last 7 days.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
4. Build 1 custom chart:
  1. Open pipeline ($) by stage and forecast category:
    1. Base the widget on Open pipeline ($).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by stage and forecast category.
5. Build 1 trends widgets:
  1. How’s this quarter’s pipeline trending?
    1. Base the widget on your line of business.
    2. Break down the data by forecast category and select the default forecast category.
    3. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the current fiscal quarter.
6. Build 2 deals widgets:
  1. Highest value deals
    1. Base the widget on a deal board, select the board’s default tab, and select the columns to include in the widget.
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Open deals with low scores
    1. Base the widget on a deal board, select the board’s default tab, and select the columns to include in the widget.
    2. Filter the deals by low score.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
7. Build 5 custom charts:
  1. Pipeline created ($) this quarter by source and current stage:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created ($).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by source and stage.
  2. Pipeline created (#) this quarter by source and current stage:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created (#).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by source and stage.
  3. Pipeline created ($) in the last 13 weeks by source:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the last 13 weeks.
    3. Break down the data by weeks and source.
  4. Pipeline created (#) in the last 13 weeks by source:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created (#).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by weeks and source.
  5. Open pipeline ($) lookout by month and stage:
    1. Base the widget on Open pipeline ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the date as 3 fiscal quarter + current.
    3. Break down the data by month and stage.

chunks.text:
Building a list widget:
Note:Your profile must include the relevant permission to create and manage widgets to dashboards

To build a list widget:

1. Select your dashboard, click +New widget and select List from the gallery.
2. In the dashboard header, click the edit icon to rename your widget and, optionally, + Add description.
3. Under List, select a predefined account list view. If you can’t find the view you’re looking for, click Manage list views and create one.
4. After selecting a view, you’ll notice a default filter is applied to the widget, and the account’s owner ID is set to be dynamic and respond to whatever is selected in your dashboard. You can change it to fixed values: Note:If you select fixed values for the team member, the widget would no longer respond to selections made on the dashboard level.
5. In addition to the Owner ID filter, you may add any filter (+Add filter) that defines which accounts qualify to be included in the widget.
6. When you’re happy with the Preview results on the right, click Save.

chunks.text:
Overview of the call page:
Click on a call to open the call page.

At the top of the page, you'll see the following:

1. Call title: Hover the title to edit it.
2. Call date, duration, and account: Click on the account name to open the account panel on the right, where you see recent meetings and emails, changes to the CRM, digital interactions and more.
3. Add to:
  1. Add to library: Click here to add the call, or part of it, to a folder
  2. Add to Listen later: Click to make the call accessible via the Listen later list on the homepage and the Gong mobile app
4. Share call: Click here to share the call with customers or people at your company, or to embed the call.
5. Generate follow-up email: Click here to generate a follow-up email that includes a summary of the meeting.
6. Action menu: Clickto choose from actions you can take on the call, including download, set as private, manual association, and more. For more details about the actions here, see Manage a call recording.

chunks.text:
Listen to a recorded call:
Below the video is a playback bar with the following controls:

1. Choose to listen to specific speakers.
2. Select parts of the call to share, save, trim, or download.
3. Speed up or slow down the call as you listen.
4. Jump 15 seconds backwards.
5. Play the call, or pause it while it's playing.
6. Jump 15 seconds forwards.
7. Move to the next speaker.
8. Adjust the volume.
9. Turn subtitles on or off.
10. Expand the video to full screen, or exit full screen if expanded.
11. Move the purple point to any place you want in the call. If the call comes with an AI-generated outline, hovering here shows a preview of what was covered at that moment in the call.
12. See who spoke during the call and when. Hover their name on the left side of the screen. Turn the toggle off if you don't want to hear their part in the conversation.
13. Screen share: See when the screen was shared.
14. Topics: See which topics were covered in the call.

If you're viewing the call in full screen, click Scroll for more details to see this info about the call.

Once you've listened to a call, it's marked along the top. Hover the icon and see when you listened, and for how long.

If you want to listen to specific speakers on a call, click in the action bar, and select the person or people you want to listen to.

You can also select which speakers to listen (or not) listen to by hovering the speaker names to reveal a toggle. Turn on the toggle to hear only that speaker. Turn it off so you don't hear that speaker.

Listen to a live call:
You can join a live call as a participant, or just listen in.

Join a live call

- From the homepage, click on a call that's marked ON AIR and then click Join.
- From the Activity page: click the call and then click JOIN.

Listen in to a live call

- From the homepage, click on a call that's marked ON AIR and then click just listen in.
- From the Activity page: click the call and then click LISTEN IN.

The call opens in a new tab. You can listen to it, but not join. You won't be registered as a participant during the call or in the call data presented afterward. Up to 2 people can listen in at once.

Note: Listening in is not available for orgs using native Zoom recording.

chunks.text:
Troubleshooting the call playback:
Having trouble playing back a call? Is the playback slow, or maybe you can't skip forward or move backwards. If so, check the following and if necessary, contact your IT department:

1. Check your certificate provider: In your browser, navigate to the certificate for Gong. Check the certificate is valid. This is an example of an invalid certificate:
2. Play the call back in an incognito or private window.
3. Clear the browsing history.
4. Connect to a different network, for example through a hotspot, or turn of the VPN.
5. Play the call using a duplicate tab.
6. Play the call using an external share link.
7. Check whether other people in your organization are experiencing the same problem.
8. Check to see if any web security applications are installed on your computer. If so, ensure that *.gong.io is excluded.
9. Contact Gong Support.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

Who can use this: Tech adminAvailable on: Any Gong plan

Where to go: Admin center > Settings > People > Team members

Save time and keep user data up-to-date and accurate with bulk user update which enables you to update several users at one time by uploading a CSV file. This is especially useful when changes at your company affect a large number of Gong users, for example new company email addresses or additional hierarchies.
chunks.title: Make bulk changes via a CSV file

chunks.text:
Updating multiple team members at once:
1. Click Admin center > Settings > Team members.
2. Click in the top right corner and select Bulk update team members.
3. From the popup that opens, click Download the CSV template. This CSV contains all of the fields you can edit via bulk upload.
4. The first column in the file is the primary email address. This field must be filled in for all users that you want to update.
5. Fill in the values for users who you want to update. Values you fill in will replace any existing values in Gong. So, for example, if you enter a mobile number, the new number will replace the one that’s currently in Gong. If you want to allow for multiple values in a field (for example, in the additional email address field, separate each value with a comma.
6. In fields that can have multiple values (for example, additional email addresses), the value you provide in the new CSV will override existing values. If you want to keep the existing value and add additional ones, include both the existing value and new values in the CSV and separate the values with commas.
7. Regarding empty fields: When you go to upload the updated CSV, you'll be able to choose whether or not we ignore empty fields in the new file.
  1. By default, we'll ignore cells that are empty in the CSV. If there are current attributes for these cells in Gong, we'll leave them as they are.
  2. If you select the mark the checkbox beside Delete existing values for empty cells that's what we'll do. Attributes in Gong for fields that are left empty in the CSV file will be deleted.
8. Once you’ve entered the info you want to update in the CSV, you’re ready to upload the file.
9. Repeat steps 1 and 2 to open the Bulk update team member popup.
10. Upload the updated CSV and we’ll validate the file. This may take a few moments, since we check that the values are provided in the required format. For example, that email addresses are phrased correctly, phone numbers contain only numbers, and more.
11. If validation fails for any of the fields, you’ll see an error message citing which column and row couldn’t be validated, and why. Update the file accordingly and upload again.
12. Once all changes in the file are validated, you’ll see a summary of the changes. If everything looks good, click Apply.
13. A message appears indicating that the changes are underway. When they’re complete, you’ll receive an email confirming the changes.

chunks.text:
Columns in the CSV template:
The CSV you download includes the following columns. We recommend deleting the ones you don’t want to update. If you keep columns that you don’t want updated, we’ll ignore those columns, unless you mark “Delete empty columns” in which case we’ll delete existing content for those columns.
chunks.body: The CSV you download includes the following columns. We recommend deleting the ones you don’t want to update. If you keep columns that you don’t want updated, we’ll ignore those columns, unless you mark “Delete empty columns” in which case we’ll delete existing content for those columns.
chunks.title: Make bulk changes via a CSV file

chunks.text:
Columns in the CSV template:
- Email address (Required and can’t be left empty): This is the unique identifier for each user. Fill in the email addresses of the team members you want to edit, exactly as they appear in Gong.
- First name: If you’ve selected “Delete existing values for empty cells” and you keep this column in the file, it must be filled. If you haven’t selected to delete existing values for empty cells the field can be left empty, and we’ll ignore it.
- Last name: If you’ve selected “Delete existing values for empty cells” and you keep this column in the file, it must be filled. If you haven’t selected to delete existing values for empty cells the field can be left empty, and we’ll ignore it.
- New email address: Only keep this column if you’re replacing the user’s primary email address. If you’re adding email addresses, use the “Additional email addresses” column. (Can’t be empty if Delete empty columns is selected.)
- Additional email addresses: Enter additional email addresses, separated by a comma.
- Trusted email address: This column appears if there’s a trusted authentication account. For more info, see this. To enable this user to access this account through their other Gong user (their trusted account), enter the trusted account email.
- Phone number
- Extension
- Mobile number
- Time zone: If you’ve selected “Delete existing values for empty cells” and you keep this column in the file, it must be filled. If you haven’t selected to delete existing values for empty cells the field can be left empty, and we’ll ignore it.
- Locale: Use the following format: en-US
- Job Title
- Manager email address
- Languages spoken during calls: Enter languages, separated by a comma
- Custom hierarchies: Columns will be created for each custom hierarchy, with the field name as the column name. For example, Hierarchy 'City office' manager email address, Hierarchy 'Divisions' manager email address.

- Trusted email address: This column appears if there’s a trusted authentication account. For more info, see this. To enable this user to access this account through their other Gong user (their trusted account), enter the trusted account email.
- Phone number
- Extension
- Mobile number
- Time zone: If you’ve selected “Delete existing values for empty cells” and you keep this column in the file, it must be filled. If you haven’t selected to delete existing values for empty cells the field can be left empty, and we’ll ignore it.
- Locale: Use the following format: en-US
- Job Title
- Manager email address
- Languages spoken during calls: Enter languages, separated by a comma
- Custom hierarchies: Columns will be created for each custom hierarchy, with the field name as the column name. For example, Hierarchy 'City office' manager email address, Hierarchy 'Divisions' manager email address.
chunks.title: Make bulk changes via a CSV file

chunks.text:
FAQs:
Can I bulk update users if my company uses automatic provisioning?

Bulk update users is a manual update. If it conflicts with automatically provisioned users, it will fail.

Can I update custom fields with automatic provisioning?

Yes

Can I bulk update data capture settings this way?

No, not at the moment. But some settings (for example, email import and web conference recording settings) can be updated for teams via Team settings. For more, see Change settings for a team.

Can I add or remove users this way?

No, not at the moment.

Are there any mandatory columns for the updated CSV?

Yes, the email address column is required, as that's the way we identify the team member.

chunks.text:
Free-dialing:
If you have an Engage license, you can access the dialer from anywhere in Gong by clickingfrom the quick access menu in the top right corner, or using the keyboard shortcut Shift + D. Use the Keypad tab to dial and the Search tab to search for contacts and leads by name.

Enter a number manually or paste it in. If you type in a number linked to an existing contact or lead in Gong, their name will be displayed.

Suppose you call a number that isn’t already linked to a contact or lead in Gong and doesn’t exist in your CRM yet. In that case, Gong uses default CRM entity association to ensure the call activity is properly associated. If you manually link the number to a contact or lead in Gong or create a new contact with this number later on, the call is automatically associated with that person.

If a call is recorded, you can find it in Conversations, even if it isn’t linked to a specific contact or lead. If a call is not recorded, you can find it on your home page or the contact or lead’s activity timeline.

chunks.text:
Numbers you can call from:
At the top, you’ll see the number you’re calling from. You may be able to choose from several numbers. These may include:

- Assigned number: Numbers assigned to you specifically by your manager or admin
- Personal number: A number that you or your admin has entered, that you verify personally from your own mobile device. It's not recommended to use your personal number for outbound calls as personal numbers are often labeled as spam when used with the dialer. We recommend using virtual numbers for outbound calls and personal numbers for inbound calls, as the forwarding number
- Unassigned numbers: Numbers available to everyone in your company. When you make calls from an unassigned number, the person cannot call you back directly, but they can call back to a forwarding number, if your admin has set one.

Gong's dialer, whether you're using it from web or mobile, will not sync with another phone such as a desk phone for outbound calls.

chunks.text:
Numbers you can call from > Maximize call efficiency with local dialing:
When you make calls using a number that matches the locale of the person you’re dialing, they’re more likely to answer the call. Once your admin has enabled local dialing, Gong selects local numbers for you to call from automatically. The number is displayed to the person you’re calling as an ordinary number, just like any other business number in Gong.

When using local dialing, we follow a specific order to select a local number with a matching area code:

1. Check the company’s local dialing inventory. We first search for a number with the desired area code in your company’s local dialing inventory.
2. Check company and user-assigned numbers. If no match is found, we look through the company’s owned numbers and any numbers assigned to the user making the call.
3. Attempt to purchase a matching number. If there’s still no available number with the desired area code, we attempt to purchase one and add it to your local dialing inventory automatically.

This final step may occasionally fail if Twilio doesn't have any available numbers in that area code at the time.

chunks.text:
Numbers you can call to:
If we already have a number for the person you're calling, it will appear in the drop-down menu below their name. If there are multiple numbers for the contact, you'll see them all here. You can also free dial a number and click Call.

Can I make international calls?

You can make calls to/from anywhere you want, minus a few exceptions. However, we recommend buying a local number from the regions where you operate to improve answer rates.

For example, if you're located in the US but you want to dial UK numbers, your admin can provision a UK number for you. This helps with conversion rates as call recipients are more likely to pick up calls from numbers within their locale.

Gong understands what country a phone number in the CRM belongs to using the following logic:

- If the number starts with +, we try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.
- If not, see if the contact has an address. If we know the country, try adding that country's prefix and see if the result is a valid number.
- If not, try adding the US prefix and see if the result is a valid number.
- If not, add + at the beginning, try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.
- If not, leave it as is.

Will I incur charges for making international calls?

When you dial out of Engage or the mobile app, the call recipient will see your personal number, but the call is relayed from Gong/Twilio and your company will not incur any charges.

chunks.text:
Recording a call:
Your company can set up recording methods per region so that you can easily comply with regulations in different states or countries. The recording options are:

- Manual: you can start recording manually at any point in the call.
- Automatic: calls are automatically recorded
- Rep-side only: calls are recorded automatically, but only the rep is recorded
- Don't allow recording: the record button isn't displayed and you can't record the call

You cannot change or override the default call recording setting for a region, but you can stop the recording.

If manual recording is selected, initiate recording by pressing Record as soon as the call connects to the receiver.

Define your audio settings:
Enable microphone access and set the microphone and speaker you want to use when making a call:

1. Start by permitting Google Chrome to access the microphone. You may need to do one or more of the following:
  - Open the Gong dialer and when prompted, choose Allow.
  - Open the Gong dialer and click the site information icon next to the URL address. Make sure the microphone is enabled in site settings.
  - Go to your browser settings and navigate to microphone settings. Adjust your default settings or add Gong to your list of allowed sites.
2. To set the microphone and speaker when making a call, click to the right of the Calling from phone number.
3. Select the speaker and microphone you want to use. Test the sound as needed.
4. Select whether you want the following:
  - Echo cancellation: reduces background noise and echo for improved call clarity
  - Noise suppression: minimizes background noise interference during calls
  - Automatic gain control: adjusts audio levels and ensures consistent audio quality throughout the call
5. Click Done.

chunks.text:
Choose a call outcome:
You can set the outcome during the call or after it. Whether call outcomes are optional or required depends on your company’s setup.

You have the following outcomes to choose from:

Call result: No answer

- No voicemail: Rep doesn’t leave a voicemail
- Left voicemail: Rep leaves a voicemail
- Not in service: Number is not in service
- Busy: Line is busy

Call result: Answered

- Follow up: Person asks for more information, asks to call back, or hasn't decided yet
- Meeting booked: Person agrees to meet, or seller sends an invite
- Bad timing: Person says they're not interested right now or in the near future
- Has a solution: Person says they have a solution with a competitor
- Bad persona: Person says they are not the right person, and doesn’t provide a referral
- Wrong number: Number is wrong
- Gave referral: Person directs to someone else
- Bad fit: One of the sides says it's a bad fit
- Opt out: Person asks not to be contacted again
- Hung up: Person hangs up
- Gatekeeper: Gatekeeper answers and user can't reach targeted person
- Not interested (other): Person says they're not interested

chunks.text:
Set a forwarding number for inbound calls:
If you have at least 1 business number assigned to you, you can set your own forwarding number so people can call you back. As long as the business number is assigned to you in Engage, if someone calls back, the call will be routed to you via inbound calls on your web browser. If you’re not available on the web, you can also take the call from your personal forwarding number.

To do this:

1. Go to My Settings and scroll to Gong Connect.
2. Here, you’ll see whether Gong Connect is enabled by your admin, how many business numbers are assigned to you directly, and whether your company has set a default forwarding number.
3. To set your own forwarding number, click Set personal forwarding number, then enter your mobile number and click Call me to verify it. If you’ve made calls from your personal number, or from a number that your admin assigned to you, this is the number to which calls will be directed if people call you back. If you’ve called people using a number that is available to your whole team, return calls will not be directed to this number. If your admin has not set up a company forwarding number and you haven’t verified your personal forwarding number, we’ll attempt to call back the web browser—but this will only work if you’re currently in Gong and able to receive it.

Inbound calls made to a company forwarding number are routed to the last team member who dialed the prospect or customer from that company number.

chunks.text:
Gong dialer FAQs:
Does the Gong dialer support voicemail drop?

Yes. See Record and drop voicemail messages for details on how to set it up.

I left a voicemail message on a call, but the call was registered in Gong as having dropped. How come?

If the voicemail message is longer than 60 seconds, the call is terminated and registered as dropped.

Can the Gong dialer receive inbound calls?

Inbound calls are currently supported by routing them to the web and the rep's personal forwarding number or company forwarding number, depending on what has been set up.

For example: let’s say a contact called John makes an inbound call to a business number at Acme, and that business number has been assigned to all users by the Acme admin. John’s inbound call will be routed to the rep at Acme who last dialed John from that business number, if that rep has set a personal forwarding number. If the rep has not set a personal forwarding number, John’s call will be routed to the Acme company forwarding number (if a company forwarding number was set by the Acme admin).

Does the Gong dialer support power dialing?

The Gong dialer doesn't currently support power dialing.

Are all calls made via the Gong dialer automatically recorded?

Calls within the USA and Canada aren't automatically recorded by the Gong dialer by default. You can set your system up to automatically record calls and you can exclude specific area codes as necessary.

Gong dialer FAQs:
We do not offer the porting of numbers from existing tools out of the box. This may be done with a custom SOW via our professional services team. Please contact your Revenue Architect (RA) for assistance.

If I dial using a local presence phone number, what happens if the person doesn't answer and then calls back later?

The person can call back the number you called from, but the call will be routed to your personal forwarding number.

Does the Gong dialer localize the caller's number automatically?

For example, if I dial an Ireland number from a UK number, will the recipient see an Ireland number (+353)?

The rep can manually select the origin number, as long as that origin number is available to the rep to use.

Can I import calls from another dialer?

Gong captures calls of other supported dialers. These calls won't appear as part of flow steps or reporting. Your tech admin can set up your org to capture calls from other dialers via company settings.

chunks.text:
Change speaker name:
If a speaker is misidentified or not identified, call participants or a business admin can edit the speaker name.

1. Open the call page and hover the speaker name until appears.
2. Click to open the Change name dialog, search for the correct name, and click Apply.

It takes a few moments for the speaker name to update. When it does, it’s updated in the call info tab, Spotlight, search, and call stats. Manually editing the speaker name does not affect the activity association, so it doesn’t update in the activity feed.

Can’t find the person you’re looking for?

If you can’t find the person you’re looking for, it’s possible that they aren’t a contact in your CRM yet. Add them as a contact to your CRM, then come back to the call page and you’ll be able to find them here.

chunks.text:
Trim a call:
Remove parts of your own calls that aren’t important or suitable for everyone. For example, trim out small talk at the beginning of a call, or sensitive information mentioned during the call. Only the call owner or tech admin can trim a call.

1. Open the call page and click under the call screen.

1. Yellow bars appear on the timeline below the call screen. Move the bars to select the part of the call you want to trim out.
2. Select Trim out this part.

Trimming the call takes some time, during which the call won’t be accessible.

chunks.title: Manage a call recording

chunks.text:
Trim a call > Restore trimmed parts of a call:
From the moment the call was recorded, you have 6 months to restore parts that have been trimmed out. After this time, the original recording is discarded and only the trimmed recording is kept. Only the call owner or tech admin can restore trimmed parts of a call.

1. Open the call page and click on the part of the call that is trimmed.
2. Click Restore entire call. This opens a dialog that prompts you to confirm the restoration.

Restoration of the trimmed parts includes analyzing the call again. This process usually takes less than an hour.

chunks.text:
Delete a call > What's removed when you delete a call?:
When you delete a call recording, you permanently remove it from Gong, along with any associated data. This includes:

- Call-related data like transcripts and media
- Notes, comments, and scores
- Call stats
- SFDC tasks that were created in relation to the call

If the call is in Gong Conversations in Salesforce, it's deleted there too.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

  - Created by
  - Last updated by
  - Status
  - Trigger
4. Use More actions icon to:

  - Duplicate the automation
  - Delete the automation (deletion requires confirmation).

Open Engage from your Gong sidebar to access all tools for prospect and customer outreach. The sidebar includes quick links to the main pages you’ll use to manage your daily sales activities.

Below is a closer look at the core Engage pages, and the key actions available on each.

chunks.text:
To-dos:
Your To-dos list shows tasks with a description, assignee, due date, and required action. This helps you stay on top of follow-ups and ensures nothing gets missed.
chunks.body: Your To-dos list shows tasks with a description, assignee, due date, and required action. This helps you stay on top of follow-ups and ensures nothing gets missed.
chunks.title: Manage customer and prospect outreach with Engage

chunks.text:
To-dos > Types of to-dos:
One-off to-dos: These are individual tasks you create for yourself. These can be email, call, or task types and can be linked to contacts, leads, accounts, or deals.

Flow to-dos: These are automatically generated by flow steps and appear when an outreach step requires your action.

chunks.text:
To-dos > Completing your to-do’s:
Here are some ways to manage your to-dos efficiently:

1. Sort your to-do list: By default, your list shows overdue and today’s to-dos sorted by recent engagement, so you can prioritize active prospects. You can also sort by flow name, step number, or other fields.
2. Bulk actions: Save time by selecting multiple to-dos to:
  - Start a queue of tasks
  - Update due dates
  - Mark items as complete
  - Dismiss or skip
  - Click to Remove from flow or Pause flow
3. Filtering: Filter to-do’s by due date, flow name, type, linked to accounts or deals, and CRM fields.
4. Work sequentially: Click the first to-do and use Next to move through them one after another.

To-dos > Create a one-off to-do:
Any Gong user with an Engage seat can create a one-off to-do. Here’s how:

1. Click Add a to-do.
2. You’re set as the default assignee, though you can switch it if needed.
3. Select the type: Email, call, or task.
4. Choose the contact or lead (required for email/call types, optional for tasks).

Flows > Add a contact or lead to a flow > Use an existing flow:
Any Engage user can add a contact to an existing flow.

From Accounts or People:

1. Click Add to flow next to a contact.
2. Hover over chosen flow and click Flow options.
3. Set the start step (if not beginning from step 1).

Flows > Add a contact or lead to a flow > Create a personal flow:
If you have flow creation permissions, you can create a personal flow.

1. Go to Engage > Flows
2. Click New and select + New flow.
3. Name your flow and choose a personal or company folder to add it to.
4. Click Create.
5. Add steps by clicking Add step, choosing from:
  1. Manual email
  2. Auto email
  3. Call
  4. LinkedIn connect
  5. LinkedIn message
  6. Task: Any other action items
6. Add the text for your email, call script or task description. Select from Templates, Blocks or AI Generate an email to help you.
7. Add delays between steps using Delay from flow start.
8. Click Save.

Once the flow is saved, you can add a contact to it using the steps above.

chunks.text:
Remove an email from a deal:
Where to go: Revenue > Deals > Deal panel

Required permissions:Delete emails

Here’s how you can remove an email from a deal, but not from the account:

1. From the Activity tab, select the email you want to remove.
2. Click and select Remove from deal.
3. You’ll be asked to confirm by clicking REMOVE.

chunks.title: Manage emails in deals and accounts

chunks.text:
Remove an email from an account:
Where to go: Account console

You can remove the email from the account, which will delete it completely from Gong. Here’s how:

Note:You can only delete an email from an account that you’re associated with.

1. Click Review account to open the account page.
2. Find the email you want to remove.
3. Click and select Delete this email.
4. If you have permission to delete the email, you’ll be asked to confirm. The email is removed from the account. This action can't be undone.

Once deleted, the email message ID is listed on an exclude list and is removed from all places in Gong and never reimported. For example, if two users received the email, it’s deleted from both instances.

Add an email to your Do-not-import list:
Where to go: Revenue > Deals > Deal panel

In some cases, emails between a specific team member and a CRM contact or lead shouldn’t be imported to Gong. To prevent these emails being in Gong, each team member has their own Do-not-import list.

Existing emails between the team member and someone in their Do-not-import list are removed from Gong and new emails aren’t imported to Gong. Emails with multiple participants from your company may still be imported to Gong from their mailbox.

You can add someone to your Do-not-import list from two places:

1. Either:
  1. Go to the Activity tab.
  2. Or click Review account to open the account console.
2. Select the email with the participant you want to add to the list.
3. Click and select Add to Do-not-import list. From Activity tab: From Account console:
4. You’ll be asked to confirm by clicking Add to Do-not-import list.
5. If there is more than one person on the email, choose whether to add everyone to the Do-not-import list or only specific participants. Note:For details on how to manage your Do-not-import list, see My Settings.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

Some countries require compliance documentation before you can provision phone numbers. Once submitted, you can track the status of your requests, edit drafts, and delete submissions you no longer need from the Regulatory compliance tab in Dialer setup.

If a rep needs a local number in a country where your business doesn't have a registered physical presence, you can submit individual compliance documentation on their behalf. This allows internationally distributed teams to use local numbers without requiring a local office entity.

Drafts are saved for 30 days. The page shows a running count of your submitted and approved requests.

chunks.title: Manage regulatory compliance documentation

chunks.text:
Submit documentation for individual numbers:
Required documents vary by country but typically include a government-issued ID (such as a passport) and proof of address for the individual rep.

To submit documentation for an individual number:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click Dialer setup under Gong Engage.
3. Click the Regulatory compliance tab.
4. Click the in Submit business documentation and hover over Submit individual documentation.
5. Scroll to the relevant country and select whether you want a Local or Mobile number.
6. Add the required individual information
7. Upload the required documents, such as passport, proof of address.
8. Submit for review.

Once approved, the number is added to your pooled numbers and must be assigned to the rep it was submitted for.

Workspace settings:
Settings at the workspace level control the default translation language for a specific workspace, including AI content like briefs, suggested playbook notes, and the language for AI-generated summaries that are exported to the CRM. To set a workspace language:

1. Go to Admin center > Agent Studio > AI Translator > Settings. This brings you to the languages section of your company’s general settings page.
2. Under Languages, select the preferred translation language for each workspace.
3. Click Update to save settings.

Team members can choose a different language on-demand for specific transcripts, briefs and AI-suggested playbook notes.

Note:The language of AI-generated summaries exported to the CRM is controlled at the workspace level.

chunks.text:
Pause a smart tracker:
Pausing is the recommended way to stop a smart tracker analyzing new conversations, and consuming credits. Paused trackers remain fully configured so you can republish it at any time.

Unlike unpublishing, pausing doesn't require you to remove the tracker from deal boards, scorecards, playbooks, streams, or other assets.

Smart trackers can be paused in one of the following ways:

- Manually paused: You pause the tracker from the AI Tracker setting page or the Edit Smart tracker page.
- Paused due to insufficient credits: Gong automatically pauses published trackers when your company runs out of credits.

To pause a smart tracker:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center, and select Agent Studio.
2. Hover over AI Tracker, and click Settings.
3. Locate the tracker you want to pause.
4. Click the More actions icon and select Pause. Note: You can also pause a tracker from the Edit Smart tracker page.
5. Review the confirmation message, and click Pause.

The tracker's status changes to Paused. The tracker remains visible throughout Gong and can be republished at any time.

chunks.text:
Republish a paused smart tracker:
Republish a paused tracker when you're ready for it to resume analyzing conversations. Republished trackers keep the same configuration they had before they were paused.

When your company's credit balance reaches zero, published question-based smart trackers are automatically paused. After additional credits are purchased, paused trackers must be republished before they resume analyzing conversations. If the tracker was paused because your company ran out of credits, make sure additional credits are available before republishing.

To republish a smart tracker:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center, and select Agent Studio.
2. Hover over AI Tracker and click Settings.
3. Locate the tracker you want to republish. Paused trackers are marked with the status Paused, but will have a different icon depending on why it was paused:
  - Pause icon: Tracker was manually paused
  - Credit icon: Tracker was paused due to insufficient credit.
4. Click the More actions icon and select Republish.
5. Choose how far back you want to apply the tracker. Tip;Select the date the tracker was paused if you want Gong to analyze conversations that were missed while the tracker was paused.
6. Review the estimated credit consumption and click Republish.

Unpublish or delete a smart tracker:
Unpublish a smart tracker when you no longer want the tracker to be available, but may want to use it again later. Existing results are preserved and remain available if you republish the tracker in the future. If your goal is to stop a tracker from consuming credits while keeping it configured, we recommend pausing the tracker instead of unpublishing it.

Delete a smart tracker only when you're sure you no longer need the tracker. Deleting a tracker permanently removes it and its data.

To unpublish or delete a smart tracker:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center, and select Agent Studio.
2. Hover over AI Tracker and click Settings.
3. Locate the tracker you want to unpublish or delete.
4. Click More actions icon, and choose one of the following:
  1. Unpublish: Review the confirmation dialog and click Unpublish.
  2. Delete: Review the confirmation dialog and click Delete. If you delete the tracker, the action can't be undone.

Frequently asked questions:
Can I assign the same number to more than one team member?

No. Each number can be assigned to one team member at a time. To make a number available to everyone again, reassign it or remove the current assignment.

Can I reassign a number that is already assigned to someone?

Yes. First unassign the number and then click Assign and select a different team member. The previous assignment is replaced immediately.

Can I recover a number after removing it?

No. Removing a number releases it back to Twilio and it cannot be recovered. If you need the number again, you would need to provision a new one, and the same number is not guaranteed to be available.

What happens to a number assigned to a team member who leaves the company?

The number remains in your account but stays assigned to the deprovisioned user. We recommend reassigning or reviewing assigned numbers when a team member is removed.

Why doesn't a team member appear in the assign list?

Only team members with dialer access appear in the list. If someone is missing, check that the Gong Dialer has been enabled for them in Admin center > Settings > Team members.

Each time you visit Messages, you'll land on the Delivered tab first by default. Your emails are categorized into different tabs so you can easily find what you need:

To see when an email is scheduled to be sent, hover over the Scheduled status label.

Note that some emails that are part of a flow can't be deleted, including auto email flow steps and manual email flow steps that have been manually scheduled.
chunks.title: Manage your emails from Gong

chunks.text:
Start managing your emails:
- Delivered: This tab contains any emails you sent out of Engage that were successfully delivered. It does not include emails sent by your teammates or anyone else at your company. To track email opens and link clicks that occurred since the date the email was sent, hover over the blue lightning icon next to a delivered email. If the person you sent the email to is linked to an account, you'll see an account name in the Account column. To delete a delivered email, click and click Delete. Deleting an email from here removes it from Emails, but it's still visible from other areas in Gong, such as the activity timeline. To see when an email was delivered, hover over the Delivered status label. Learn about how Engage helps you comply with spam regulations and set up for successful email delivery.
- Drafts: See any draft you started working on in the AI Composer and have not yet sent or scheduled to be sent. Any time you click Write email in Engage, an email draft is created for you. To send an email draft now, schedule it to be sent, or delete it, click . Note that some emails that are part of a flow can't be deleted, including auto email flow steps and manual email flow steps that have been manually scheduled. To see when a draft was created and last modified, hover over the Draft status label.
- Scheduled: Here, you can find any email drafts you created and scheduled to be sent later. Auto email steps do not appear in the Scheduled tab. To see scheduled auto emails, open contact view by clicking on the name of a contact or lead from anywhere in Engage and go to the To-dos tab. You may also see emails with the status label Pending in the Scheduled tab, meaning we've delayed your email as a part of our email throttling system to prevent you from getting marked as spam. If you see the Pending status, there is no action needed from your end. We'll send out your email as soon as possible.
- Failed: This tab shows any emails that bounced or couldn't be sent because of an error. Hover over the Failed status label to find out why the email failed and whether there are any steps you can take to send it successfully, depending on what went wrong.
- All: See all emails here.

chunks.text:
Gong email FAQs:
I sent an email. Why don't I see it in the Delivered tab?

The page doesn't currently update automatically, so once you've sent something, refresh the page to see an updated list.

Are there any size limits on emails I send from Gong?

Email draft body size can be up to 3 MB. Draft body size does not include attachments, but it does include in-line images and GIFs.

Total size of an email, including attachments, can be up to 20 MB.

Can I I resend a failed email?

You can resend a failed email, as long as you've addressed the reason it failed. For example, if an email fails to send because it has missing variables, replace or remove the missing variables and then try resending the email.

Can I see my team's emails?

Currently, you can only see your emails and email drafts.

My organization's G Suite is connected to Gong, but I still can't connect my email. Why not?

Your organization's G Suite admin may need to set Gong as a trusted 3rd party app via the Google Admin console.

Are emails I send logged in my CRM?

Yes, emails are logged in your CRM. Learn more about exporting emails as Salesforce tasks or syncing emails to HubSpot.

What is the data retention policy for emails in Gong?

Every email you send from Gong is retained according to the retention policy your admin has set up for your company. You can learn more about Gong's standard data retention policies.

What happens if I delete an email?

chunks.text:
Publish, share, and give access:
Note:Until published, dashboards are in draft mode and are only accessible to you and other team members with permission to manage dashboards.

To publish, share, and give access to the dashboard:

1. Click Publish and share.
2. Under Invite, select the people you want to share the dashboard with.
3. Choose whether to Notify people or not, and then, optionally, include your own message in the notification. Note:Invited people would only see the dashboard if they have an active Forecast seat and permission to view dashboards. If they don’t have these and are invited, they’ll be notified but won’t be able to view the dashboard.
4. Set the dashboard’s access: You can either give access only to invited people or to the entire company.
5. Click Share. People you invited will be notified and see the dashboard under Shared with you. Others will see it under Company dashboards.
6. Published dashboards appear on the left navigation under Restricted or Public, depending on the access you provided.
7. To unpublish a dashboard, click the more actions icon and select Switch to draft.

How Gong handles email domains:
Gong does not support sending and ingesting emails from multiple domains per user.

chunks.title: Managing email domains in Gong

chunks.text:
How Gong handles email domains > Company-wide email import (Google Workspace integration):
When a company integrates Google Workspace using a company-wide access model for importing emails, all emails are imported from a single domain. However, sending emails, which requires write permissions, is always authenticated per user. We do not support company-wide write permissions. The authenticated domain for write permissions should be the same as the company wide domain.

The authenticated domain for write permissions should be the same as the company wide domain.

chunks.title: Managing email domains in Gong

chunks.text:
How Gong handles email domains > Company-wide email import (Google Workspace integration) > Non-recommended approach:
While emails may be imported from domain X, an individual user could still send emails from domain Y. However, if a user sends emails from a different domain than the one used for email import, replies may not be properly ingested, leading to the system failing to detect responses and import emails, and flows not pausing correctly when a reply is received. To prevent these issues, it’s recommended to ensure the sending domain matches the domain used for email import.

Learn how to connect company-wide.

chunks.title: Managing list views

chunks.text:
Create a list view:
1. Go to Admin center > List views. The page lists all existing list views, including their names, descriptions, who last modified them, and the count of metrics and widgets using each of them. Note:The list includes a preset Generic account view with commonly used fields. The view is automatically assigned to account-based metrics unless a custom view is assigned.
2. Click + New view, give your list view a name and a description, and click Next. Tip:Use descriptive names like "Prospect account info" or "Accounts with ARR info" so other dashbaord admins can easily find them.
3. Choose which fields are included in the view by adding/removing columns. You can also select a related object field (so for deal based metrics you can select an account field). Scroll to the bottom of the list to find the Related objects fields.
  - Drag and drop columns to rearrange them.
  - Click column headers to sort the table.
  - Choose a sort field and direction to control the default order in which accounts will be shown.
4. Click Save. The view is now available to be used as a drilldown view, by assigning it to account-based metrics and optionally by overriding the default in widgets.

Adding a new target:
Note:This procedure requires permissions to manage dashboards.

1. Go to Admin Center > Data studio > Targets and click +New target. Tip:Sort the list by clicking any of the column headers.
2. Give your target a Name (for example, “Retention”) and a Description to help others understand it.
3. Select the target type - Currency for measuring amounts and Units for measuring a quantity of items (for example, the number of sales accepted opportunities).
4. Click Download Template. A template CSV file is downloaded to your computer.
5. Edit the CSV file and populate it with team members and team target values. You can add up to 10,000 records to the file.
6. Upload the file. The target is added to your target list, along with its general information and number of records. When the target is used anywhere in Gong it will be indicated under Used in, so you and others understand the implications of modifying it:

Note:If you’re experiencing any issue with uploading the file, check out this troubleshooting article.

chunks.text:
Best practices:
To make the most out of your targets, we recommend:

Coupling targets and metrics/Forecast boards

Ideally, you should have a metric per target or forecast board column.

Team vs. individual records

Each record in the CSV file represents a team or an individual.

Under the column “is team”, individual quota-carriers should be assigned the value “false”, while teams should be assigned the value “true”.

If a team member is both an individual contributor and a manager, the team target value will be measured against their team rollups, while the individual value will be measured against their own numbers (deals in which they are the user associated with the deal).

For example, John Smith has two entries in “Bookings $”:

- As an individual quota-carrier, where they’re the owner of deals (is team=”false”), their target is 30K USD for Q2, FY2025.
- As a sales manager, where their direct reports are the owners of deals (is team=”true”), their target is 150K USD for Q2, FY2025.

Multiple records

Each individual or team can be assigned a designated value per period per target type.

For example, John Smith can have:

- A currency target value for Q2, FY2025
- A currency target value for Q3, FY2025
- A unit target value for Q2, FY2025
- A unit target value for Q3, FY2025

Gong associates conversations (emails, calls) with contacts, accounts, and deals in your CRM based on your association settings. However, in some cases, your reps may want to manually associate a conversation with a different account or deal.

chunks.text:
Add the Gong Assistant to the meeting invite:
1. Add your company’s Gong Assistant email address (e.g., companyname@assistant.gong.io) as a participant to the meeting invite.
2. This can be done by the meeting host or any team member with the right permissions.

If the meeting is hosted by someone outside of your organization or if the calendar system doesn’t allow you to add participants:

1. Forward the meeting invite manually to the Assistant's email address
2. If the meeting time or date changes, you will need to forward each email with a meeting invite update to the Assistant. Gong cannot detect updates from previously forwarded invites.

chunks.text:
Recording consent settings still apply:
If the recording consent profile of the call owner has Enforce consent enabled, Gong will record the meeting only if:

1. The meeting uses a Gong consent-enabled meeting link
2. The link type (static or dynamic) matches the configuration of the web conference provider in the consent profile
3. The meeting description does not contain a different web conference URL that allows participants to bypass consent
4. The consent-enabled link does not belong to an external company (e.g., another Gong customer who also uses Gong consent)
5. Before joining the meeting, none of the participants click Join but don’t record on the Gong recording consent page.

Note:The Gong assistant records according to your company’s consent settings. Calls are only recorded if the meeting meets those requirements.

chunks.text:
What’s not required for manual recording:
When you manually invite the Gong assistant, these automatic recording conditions don’t apply:

- Gong doesn’t need calendar access for the user.
- Team members don’t need to have email or calendar capture enabled in their data capture settings.
- Exclusion rules don’t apply when the assistant is manually invited. This means meetings are still recorded even if they are private, or if participants, domains, or keywords appear on your organization’s exclusion lists.

chunks.title: Market

chunks.text:
Trends:
Use Market to identify and be notified when economic trends are discussed in customer conversations; and analyze how these trends are impacting your deals over time.

For example if you're viewing the trends using the Economic Pulse Tracker, and the words recession or layoffs are being mentioned more frequently in conversations, it suggests more people are concerned about the future of the economy.

- A trend line in an upward trajectory indicates more concern about the future of the economy
- A trend line in a downward trajectory indicates less concern about the future of the economy

Trends enable you to make proactive decisions rather than reactive ones.

- Prepare and coach sales reps to better handle calls
- Adopt your marketing strategy for a predicted bear market
- Tweak the Trends to suit your requirements

To use Trends:

This example uses the Economic Pulse Tracker to describe how to use Trends.

Go to Insights > Market, and do the following:

1. Select the team you’d like to track.
2. View the trends or mention rates for all Calls or Deals.
3. Select the activity time frame.
4. Select the Economic Pulse tracker.
5. Narrow down the data based on your CRM preferences; for example use the CRM Account Type filter to view data originating from prospects.
6. Analyze the info:
  1. Hover over the trend line markers to view trend statistics and compare changes over time.
  2. Click win rate to open the Win/Loss window and view the following:
    - A visual display of how the trend affects your win rate

Use Market to identify and be notified when economic trends are discussed in customer conversations; and analyze how these trends are impacting your deals over time.

For example if you're viewing the trends using the Economic Pulse Tracker, and the words recession or layoffs are being mentioned more frequently in conversations, it suggests more people are concerned about the future of the economy.

- A trend line in an upward trajectory indicates more concern about the future of the economy
- A trend line in a downward trajectory indicates less concern about the future of the economy

Trends enable you to make proactive decisions rather than reactive ones.

- Prepare and coach sales reps to better handle calls
- Adopt your marketing strategy for a predicted bear market
- Tweak the Trends to suit your requirements

To use Trends:

This example uses the Economic Pulse Tracker to describe how to use Trends.

Go to Insights > Market, and do the following:

1. Select the team you’d like to track.
2. View the trends or mention rates for all Calls or Deals.
3. Select the activity time frame.
4. Select the Economic Pulse tracker.
5. Narrow down the data based on your CRM preferences; for example use the CRM Account Type filter to view data originating from prospects.
6. Analyze the info:
  1. Hover over the trend line markers to view trend statistics and compare changes over time.
  2. Click win rate to open the Win/Loss window and view the following:
    - A visual display of how the trend affects your win rate
    - How many deals were closed when Economic Pulse Tracker terms were not mentioned in calls

For more information see How to add a tracker.

Gong uses AI to give you deeper insights into what's going on in your business. We use a variety of AI models, and measure performance per model and in different ways to make sure the AI is accurate and optimized. How we measure performance depends on the type of model we're using. Smart trackers, for example, are based on in-house models, and we measure hit rate (how many snippets were correctly detected) and precision (how many of the snippets that we detected as positive were actually positive). Learn more about how we estimate performance for smart trackers see this.

Features like Call spotlight and Ask anything use generative AI based on large language models (LLMs). Multiple elements that go into these models, including different LLMs, the type of data they receive, and the types of prompts used to generate responses. We evaluate all of these elements on an ongoing basis using the Elo rating system to make sure that the model we're using is optimized.

chunks.title: Measuring AI performance at Gong

chunks.text:
Making sure we are always improving:
The Elo rating system was originally developed for calculating the relative skill level of chess players. Today, this system is used to rank a variety of competitive games, as well as LLM performance. At Gong, we've adopted the Elo system to compare and measure the performance of AI models on a per feature level. This includes measuring the systems that support the models, what data is brought into the models, and how that data is handled.

The Elo ranking system has a variety of benefits that make it particularly suited to measuring AI performance:

- Objectivity: It provides a clear, numerical value, making it easy for everyone to understand the advancements we're making.
- Simple comparison: It enables us to directly compare new model versions with older ones, so that when we update a model we know that the new one is an improvement.
- Widely recognized: It's a universally accepted rating method.

chunks.title: Measuring AI performance at Gong

chunks.text:
How we implement the Elo rating system:
We use the Elo system to determine if we should adopt a new model in a number of situations. These include:

- When we upgrade the underlying LLMs
- When we update prompts
- When we improve the input or data we give to the prompt
- When we migrate from off-the-shelf models to fine-tuned proprietary models

In all of these situations, we follow a structured process to assess performance and see whether the new model outperforms the old one:

1. Setup comparison: We create a comparison scenario in which each AI model is tested under similar conditions. Outcomes are categorized as 'old win', 'new win' or 'tie'.
2. Calculate win rate: Each 'new win' scores a point; each 'tie' scores half a point. The total points are then divided by the total number of possible points to get the win rate.
3. Calculate the Elo difference: Using the win rate, we calculate the Elo difference between the old and new models. This number indicates the level of improvement.
