chunks.text:
Search conversations:
Filter calls to get a deeper understanding of how much interest has been generated by your brand campaign. Here’s how:

1. Go to Conversations > Search > Words or phrases. Note:Words or phrases is a default filter on the sidebar. If it isn’t there, go to +Add filters, search for Words and phrases and check the box. Click APPLY.
2. Now you can search for calls based on the campaign you’re looking for. Use quotation marks to find exact matches, for example “Super bowl commercial” or “Michael Lewis podcast.”
3. To search for several words or phrases, click + next to this field to add additional fields. Enter a phrase to search for calls that contain the term added in the first field, as well as the term’s in the additional fields.
4. Narrow your search further by choosing results that:
  1. Don’t contain the term.
  2. Contain related forms of the term.
  3. Were said by a specific party (your team, the customer, or anyone).
  4. Were said during specific parts of a call (as part of a question, during specific parts of the call, in specific topics).

You’ll see a list of calls where the phrase was mentioned. You have the following options:

- Click on a time segment in a specific call to play it from the exact point where the phrase is mentioned.
- Select a call to open the full transcript, with all instances of the phrase highlighted.
- View the chart at the top of the page to analyze trends.
- Create a stream to automatically collect relevant calls matching your search terms, and receive notifications when new calls are added.

chunks.text:
Create keyword trackers:
Keyword trackers are simple to set up, and provide a valuable way to monitor calls related to your brand campaign. They not only allow you to track specific mentions, but also offer deeper insights, such as win/loss analytics and trends over time. This enables you to see how many deals were converted where your campaign was referenced in at least one customer call.

Here’s how to create your own keyword tracker:

1. Go to Admin center > Agent studio.
2. Click Settings on the AI Tracker card.
3. Click + Create tracker and select Keyword tracker.
4. Choose a name and language.
5. Add phrases relating to your brand campaign, separated by commas. Check the box if you want related word forms included.
6. Under Tracker filters, select to have the term tracked when said by people not at your company (prospects or customers).
7. Click on Call filters to narrow your search further by choosing results that were said during specific parts of a call (as part of a question, during specific parts of the call, in specific topics).
8. Under Track in, choose whether you want the tracker to be applied to calls only, or calls and emails.
9. Finally, under Where do you want to use this tracker? select where you want to see tracker results. See this article for more guidance on creating keyword trackers.

You can now use your keyword tracker to filter for relevant conversations faster, and set up a stream – in order to receive notifications when it comes up during a call or email.

chunks.text:
Set up Entra ID to provision to Gong:
1. Follow step 3 of Microsoft's tutorial on configuring Gong for automatic user provisioning: Step 3: Add Gong from the Entra ID application galleryTo add the Gong app:
  1. Log in to your account
  2. Go to Enterprise Applications and choose New Application.
  3. Search for Gong. When you click the app, Microsoft starts adding it.
2. The following fields are mandatory when provisioning with Gong:
  - Given name: mapped to the First name for the team member
  - Last name: mapped to the Last name for the team member
  - Primary email: mapped to the Email address for the team member. The email domain must match your company primary domain, otherwise the user won't be imported.
3. The following fields are optional, but it’s highly recommended to configure them for your users before provisioning in order to avoid the need for manual updates: Note:Provisioned fields cannot be edited manually in Gong. If you leave a field empty, it can be manually set one time in Gong. After this, the field can’t be modified.
  - Phone number: mapped to the team member’s Phone number. Following formats are supported:
    - (865) 365-1900
    - (212) 575-1994 ext 3437
    - (317) 251-0700 ext. 468
    - (202) 903-2585 x2991
    - (206) 324-1800 x 229
    - 540.946.4600 Ext. 143
  - Primary Phone Ext: mapped to the team member’s Extension
  - Secondary Email: mapped to team member’s Additional email addresses. Used for additional ways to identify the user. Includes both additional email addresses and email aliases. See Primary and additional email address.
  - Private Email: If users have a private email, configure this field.
  - Title: mapped to the team member’s Job title
  - Manager Email: (Recommended) Enter the manager's email address. This is required for building the company hierarchy.
  - Manager Full Name: In the format firstname lastname, e.g. John Doe. The manager’s full name should be provided if you can’t provide the manager’s email. If neither this field or the Manager ID field are defined, Gong cannot automatically build your org hierarchy. Note that, if there's more than one manager with the same name, Gong can't set the manager for the user and you'll have to set this manually in Gong. This method is not recommended for building the company hierarchy.
  - Time zone: Use any value from the list of time zones in List of tz database time zones. Note:Updating the user’s time zone after they have been provisioned can only be done by updating their time zone in Entra ID. Changing their country won’t change their time zone.
  - Country: Enter the country’s full name or 2 or 3 letter country code, according to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes
  - State or Province: Enter the full state or province name, or two letter code according to the following ISO codes:
    - US: ISO 3166-2:US
    - Canada: ISO 3166-2:CA
    - Australia: ISO 3166-2:AU (for Australia the state code can be 2 or 3 letters)
  - Locale: Use the following format: en-US. If you don’t define a locale for a user, they are assigned en-US by default. This field is used in Gong to identify the user weekend in order to avoid sending notifications when the user is not working.
4. Locate the group/s you want to use in Gong, and push them to Gong.

chunks.text:
Set up Entra ID to provision to Gong > How is the timezone calculated?:
Note:Timezone offsets (e.g. -05:00) are not supported.Updating the user’s time zone after they have been provisioned can only be done by updating their time zone in Entra ID. Changing their country won’t change their time zone.

Gong calculates the user timezone according to the following hierarchy:

1. Time zone attribute from Entra ID, if provided.
2. Country attribute from Entra ID, if provided.
3. State-or-Province attribute from Entra ID, in a country where timezones are different between states or provinces.
4. Default timezone, as set for the company in Gong.

chunks.text:
Authenticate the bot to join Teams meetings:
By default, the Gong bot joins Teams meetings as an anonymous guest. Some companies prevent guests from automatically joining meetings with:

- CAPTCHAs: Guests must complete a captcha before joining, which blocks Gong’s bot
- Waiting rooms: Guests are placed in a lobby and must be admitted manually

If anonymous access is not possible in your company, you can authenticate the bot as a verified Teams user. This bypasses captchas and allows the bot to join calls.

To enable the authenticated bot, your Teams admin must allow Gong as an external domain and then configure the authenticated bot in Gong:

1. Go to Microsoft Teams admin center > Users > External access.
2. Either allow all external domains or click + Add a domain and enter: meetings.gong.io. For more details, see Configure external meetings and chat.
3. In Gong, go to Admin center > Settings > Data capture > Web conferencing.
4. In the Microsoft Teams row, click Settings.
5. Turn on Allow Gong bot to log in as a Teams user.
6. In the dialog, mark Got it. I’ll complete the Teams admin configuration and click Continue.

Note:The authenticated bot requires meetings.gong.io to be allowed in Microsoft Teams. This lets it join meetings hosted in your company’s Teams environment. It also means authenticated Gong bots from other companies can be admitted to your meetings. Meetings hosted by another company that require captchas may still block the bot.

chunks.text:
Set up the integration:
Setting up the Gong integration with Microsoft Teams phone involves creating an application instance, and a compliance recording policy. The compliance recording policy is then associated with users or groups in your Active Directory.

The integration is configured by default in strict mode by Microsoft so that users can only make, receive, and record calls from Microsoft Teams to a phone number. Users can stop a recording from Gong if necessary. You must disable strict mode if you want to record other types of calls such as web conferencing calls or voice calls via Microsoft Teams. In order to record web conference calls via the Gong bot, you must configure the Microsoft Teams integration for web conference calls.

Note:In strict mode, calls made by users set up to use the Gong bot are recorded automatically. Depending on your use case and jurisdiction laws, you may be required to get consent to record the call. You are responsible for ensuring your compliance with applicable laws when using this feature.

chunks.headingPath: Configure Microsoft Teams phone to export calls to Gong > Create a Compliance Recording policy in Microsoft
chunks.title: Microsoft Teams Phone

chunks.text:
Configure Microsoft Teams phone to export calls to Gong > Create a Compliance Recording policy in Microsoft:
1. Get your TenantID. In PowerShell, connect to your Teams Tenant: Connect-MicrosoftTeams
2. Create an application instance using the Gong Compliance Bot application ID. This script creates an application instance together with a user in Entra ID’s Active Directory. This user is the user that used to record calls. Define the following parameters for the script: New-CsOnlineApplicationInstance -UserPrincipalName <userPrincipalName> -DisplayName <Recording assistant name> ` -ApplicationID <AppId>
  - appID: the appId you got after connecting to Microsoft Teams phone to Gong.
  - UserPrincipalName: an email to be associated with the Numonix bot. This email address will be added to Active Directory after running the script.
  - DisplayName: the display name for the user created in Active Directory. This name is displayed if the user is added to a call. Use a descriptive name such as 'Recording Assistant'.
3. The script returns the application ID, display name, and the object ID for the Gong Compliance bot generated. Keep a copy of the object id. Tip:Add the resource account (UserPrincipalName) to an allowlist in your security scanning or risk mitigation software. Do not disable or mark the resource account (UserPrincipalName) as inactive in your Active Directory; this will affect and/or disable your service.
4. Sync your application instance from Microsoft into the Agent Provisioning Service, using the object and application ID returned when you created the application instance. Sync-CsOnlineApplicationInstance -ObjectId <object ID> -ApplicationId <appId>
5. Create a Compliance Recording Policy with the following parameter: New-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy -Identity <policyidentity> -Enabled $true ` -Description "Teams Compliance Recording" ` -DisableComplianceRecordingAudioNotificationForCalls $true
  - policyIdentity: the policy identifier which is then associated with users you want to record.
6. Associate the compliance recording policy with the Gong Compliance Bot application with the following parameters: New-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingApplication -Id <object ID> -Parent <policyidentity>
  - policyIdentity: the policy identifier which is then associated with the users you want to record
  - objectId: the ID of the object generated when creating the application instance
chunks.body:
1. Get your TenantID. In PowerShell, connect to your Teams Tenant: Connect-MicrosoftTeams
2. Create an application instance using the Gong Compliance Bot application ID. This script creates an application instance together with a user in Entra ID’s Active Directory. This user is the user that used to record calls. Define the following parameters for the script: New-CsOnlineApplicationInstance -UserPrincipalName <userPrincipalName> -DisplayName <Recording assistant name> ` -ApplicationID <AppId>
  - appID: the appId you got after connecting to Microsoft Teams phone to Gong.
  - UserPrincipalName: an email to be associated with the Numonix bot. This email address will be added to Active Directory after running the script.
  - DisplayName: the display name for the user created in Active Directory. This name is displayed if the user is added to a call. Use a descriptive name such as 'Recording Assistant'.
3. The script returns the application ID, display name, and the object ID for the Gong Compliance bot generated. Keep a copy of the object id. Tip:Add the resource account (UserPrincipalName) to an allowlist in your security scanning or risk mitigation software. Do not disable or mark the resource account (UserPrincipalName) as inactive in your Active Directory; this will affect and/or disable your service.
4. Sync your application instance from Microsoft into the Agent Provisioning Service, using the object and application ID returned when you created the application instance. Sync-CsOnlineApplicationInstance -ObjectId <object ID> -ApplicationId <appId>
5. Create a Compliance Recording Policy with the following parameter: New-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy -Identity <policyidentity> -Enabled $true ` -Description "Teams Compliance Recording" ` -DisableComplianceRecordingAudioNotificationForCalls $true
  - policyIdentity: the policy identifier which is then associated with users you want to record.
6. Associate the compliance recording policy with the Gong Compliance Bot application with the following parameters: New-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingApplication -Id <object ID> -Parent <policyidentity>
  - policyIdentity: the policy identifier which is then associated with the users you want to record
  - objectId: the ID of the object generated when creating the application instance
chunks.headingPath: Configure Microsoft Teams phone to export calls to Gong > Create a Compliance Recording policy in Microsoft
chunks.title: Microsoft Teams Phone

chunks.text:
Disable “Strict” mode in the compliance recording profile:
When strict mode is enabled, all calls are recorded. The Numonix bot records PTSN calls.

To enable your users to make other types of calls, disable strict mode in the Teams compliance recording profile.

1. Connect to MSTeams using Powershell.
2. Identify the application that needs to be changed: Get-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingApplication The script returns the following: Identity:Tag:Priority:0ComplianceRecordingPairedApplications:{}Id:RequiredBeforeMeetingJoinTrueRequiredBeforeCallEstablishmentTrueRequiredDuringMeetingTrueRequiredDuringCall:TrueConcurrentInvitationCount:1
3. Set the parameters in bold to False. The object Id is the ID of the object generated when creating the application instance: Set-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingApplication –Identity Tag:<object Id> -RequiredBeforeMeetingJoin ` $false -RequiredDuringMeeting $false -RequiredBeforeCallEstablishment $false -RequiredDuringCall $false
4. Confirm the settings were updated: get-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingApplication The script returns the following: Identity:Tag:Priority:0ComplianceRecordingPairedApplications:{}Id:RequiredBeforeMeetingJoinFalseRequiredBeforeCallEstablishmentFalseRequiredDuringMeetingFalseRequiredDuringCall:FalseConcurrentInvitationCount:1
5. In Gong: Make sure to enable importing telephony system calls for users whose calls you want to record. Check that the list of users in Microsoft Teams and the list of users in Gong are aligned.

Assign policy to users:
1. Assign the compliance recording policy to a user or group:
  - Assign to User: Grant-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy -Identity -PolicyName
  - To remove a policy from a user: Grant-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy -Identity recordeduser@acme.com -PolicyName $null
  - Assign to group: New-CsGroupPolicyAssignment -GroupId -PolicyType TeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy ` -PolicyName -Rank 1
  - Remove a policy from a group: Remove-CsGroupPolicyAssignment -GroupId -PolicyType TeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy
2. Verify the policy was applied to a user or to the Entra ID Active Directory Security Group:
  - Verify user: Get-CsOnlineUser -Identity '' | Select-Object ` -ExpandProperty 'TeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy'
  - Verify group: Get-CsGroupPolicyAssignment -PolicyType TeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy

chunks.text:
Permissions required by Gong to install the app:
| Scope | Microsoft description | Gong explanation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read all users' basic profiles | Allows the app to read a basic set of profile properties of other users in your organization on behalf of the signed-in user. This includes display name, first and last name, email address and photo. | Required by Gong to retrieve relevant call metadata for the recorded user. |
| Sign in and read user profile | Allows users to sign-in to the app, and allows the app to read the profile of signed-in users. It also allows the app to read basic company information of signed-in users.This is a permission requested to access your data in the account. | Required by Gong to retrieve the relevant user email for a recorded user, to match the Microsoft user to the Gong user. |
| Access media streams in a call as an app | Allows the app to get direct access to media streams in a call, without a signed-in user.This is a permission requested to access your data in the account. | In order to record calls, Numonix needs access to the call’s audio stream.This is part of Microsoft’s minimum requirements to enable the compliance recording feature. |
| Join group calls and meetings as an app | Allows the app to join group calls and scheduled meetings in your organization, without a signed-in user. The app will be joined with the privileges of a directory user to meetings in your organization. This is a permission requested to access your data in the account. | In order to record, the Numonix Bot will silently join calls in order to access the audio stream. The bot user will not be visible to users.This is part of Microsoft’s minimum requirements to enable the compliance recording feature. |
| Join group calls and meetings as a guest | Allows the app to anonymously join group calls and scheduled meetings in your organization, without a signed-in user. The app will be joined as a guest to meetings in your organization. This is a permission requested to access your data in the account. | In order to record, the Numonix Bot will silently join calls in order to access the audio stream. The bot user will not be visible to users.Join group meetings as a guest is for covering the scenario when the recorded user joins a meeting hosted by another Teams org. The bot needs to be able to join said meeting even though they don’t have admin consent into the Organizers tenant.This is part of Microsoft’s minimum requirements to enable the compliance recording feature. |

chunks.title: Migrating from Outreach

chunks.text:
How migration works:
There are 2 main parts of the migration process:

- Connecting Outreach to Engage: We need the API keys to connect the 2 platforms. You can provide us with temporary admin access, or provide us with the API keys
- Choosing what to migrate: You can use migration to clean out old templates and Outreach sequences. Gong distinguishes between 'personal' flows - available for their owner to see and use, and 'company' flows, available for all users to see and use. Gong will migrate all active personal templates and sequences from Outreach, and assign them to their owners in Gong as personal flows. For company templates and sequences that are available to all users, Gong only migrates templates and sequences that are tagged. To do this, you’ll need to create a tag called "migrate for company availability" in Outreach and tag all of the templates and sequences you want to migrate and have available for all users in Gong.

chunks.title: Migrating from Outreach

chunks.text:
About the migration process:
- For company flows and templates, you’ll need to tag the ones you want to bring over, and then provide us with the tag you’re using so we can import them
- For personal flows, we only import them if the owner in Outreach has a matching user in Gong. This is detected based on email matching
- Flows and templates can be marked as active/inactive in Outreach. We only import active objects
- In Outreach, there are interval-based and date-based sequences. We only import the ones that are interval-based
- When importing templates from Outreach, we cannot import images
- You can migrate your Outreach snippets into Gong blocks
- Not all Outreach variables can translate to Gong, such as conditional variables, so it's important to review content once you've imported it

Gong supports one CRM connection per Gong instance. If your company uses multiple Gong instances, each with separate domains and logins, each instance can connect to a different CRM.

Before disconnecting your CRM, you must contact Gong Support to plan the migration with Gong. The CRM integration affects which data is available in Gong and migrating can have implications for duplicate CRM data in Gong, field mappings, Engage workflows, and other CRM-dependent features.

As disconnecting your CRM doesn’t automatically result in CRM data being deleted in Gong, it is important to work with Gong when migrating to a new CRM.

chunks.text:
When to disconnect your CRM integration:
You'll need to disconnect your current CRM integration from Gong in the following scenarios:

- Your organization is switching to a new CRM platform.
- You're moving to a different instance of the same CRM platform, for example when transitioning from a CRM sandbox to a production environment, or multiple organizations within your CRM.

Regardless of your specific migration scenario, you must always disconnect your current CRM integration before establishing a new one. This ensures a clean transition and prevents any data synchronization issues during the migration process.

chunks.title: Migrate your CRM

chunks.text:
CRM migration process:
To migrate your CRM:

1. Contact Gong Support before disconnecting your current CRM to coordinate the removal of existing CRM data and references. The data cleanup process takes up to 24 hours to complete.
2. Provide the support team with the following:
  - Your current CRM
  - Your new CRM
  - The date you want to disconnect Gong from your current CRM
  - The day you plan to connect your new CRM to Gong

Following this process ensures minimal disruption and maintains data integrity throughout your CRM migration.

chunks.title: Migrate your CRM

chunks.text:
CRM migration process > How changing your CRM affects Gong:
Changing your CRM has the following impact:

- CRM data: Old CRM data is not automatically removed when the old CRM is disconnected, and connecting the new CRM can temporarily create duplicate CRM records until cleanup is completed. Initial data population in the new CRM connection may also take time depending on your CRM data volume.
- Engage flows: All contacts and leads are automatically removed from existing Engage flows during migration. This action cannot be reversed. Prepare your sales team for this change and plan to rebuild relevant flows after migration is complete.
- Engage CRM setup: All field mappings must be reconfigured to your new CRM. This includes Engage CRM setup and any related functionality that depends on those mappings. Learn how to Set up Gong Engage.
- Do Not Contact / Invalid contact handling: This setting isn’t automatically copied to the new CRM.
- Engage To-dos: These are deleted during migration.
- Engage template variables: Variables must be remapped after the new CRM is in place.
- Playbook data: Data stored in Gong may require export or backfill in some cases.
- Deal boards, lines of business, and CRM-field-based filters: These may need to be reconfigured after the new mapping is established.

How to disconnect from your CRM:
Perform this together with your Gong team.

To disconnect your CRM:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click CRM settings under CRM.
3. In the CRM settings page, click Disconnect.

Gong is disconnected from your CRM.

Note:After you connect the new CRM, you may temporarily see duplicate CRM objects such as Accounts, Deals, Contacts, and Leads until the migration cleanup process is completed.

If you already migrated:
If you already disconnected your old CRM or connected your new one, contact Gong as soon as possible. While it is best to coordinate before the cutover, Gong can still help assess duplicate data, migration impact, and required cleanup after the migration has already happened.

Before cleanup begins, ensure that:

- The old CRM is disconnected from Gong.
- The new CRM is connected to Gong.
- New CRM data is actively populating in Gong.

Emails:
Emails are exported to a Salesforce task or event depending on your configuration. If tasks aren’t generated for emails check:

- The email exists in Gong. If the email isn’t in Gong, contact Gong support and include the EML file.
- The correct workspaces are checked for export.

- New team members have been added to each workspace manually. Adding a new team member either manually or with automatic provisioning doesn’t control email export.
- When the team member was configured to export emails from the workspace. Only emails sent after this date are exported. To export existing emails, contact Gong support.

Emails > Example:
With this configuration:

- Emails from 150 team members in Workspace1 will be exported to the CRM
- No emails will be exported from Workspace2 as no team members are configured for this workspace
- No emails will be exported from Workspace3 as the workspace isn’t checked for exporting to the CRM

To set which team members should export emails to the CRM:

1. In the CRM configuration page, scroll down to Gong captured emails.
2. Click the Edit button. On the left is a list of team members. On the right is the team members who are already configured for email export.
3. Ensure the team member is included in the list of team members whose emails are exported.

Make sure you have set:

- The workspaces you want emails to be exported for
- Whether you want all emails or only emails written in Gong
- The team members you want emails exported for.

For more details see, Create Salesforce tasks for Gong activities or Sync emails to HubSpot.

Troubleshooting tasks > Task status for meeting invites:
Meeting invites exported as tasks with a status of In Progress. Once the meeting has taken place the status is updated as follows:

- If recorded: Completed
- If not recorded: In Progress
- If canceled: Task title updates to Meeting Canceled, and the status remains In Progress
- If deleted: Task is removed from Salesforce.

Troubleshooting tasks > Multiple tasks for single activity:
The CRM configuration settings allow you to choose between generating multiple tasks for each Gong activity, or one single task.

For the Several tasks options, Gong generates a separate task/event for each of the associated contacts, accounts, opportunities, or leads.

To generate one task per activity, select the One task option. For more details, see Creating one task per activity.

May 2024

Maximize your productivity with new features from Gong Engage

Gong Extension

The Gong extension integrates Gong Engage into reps’ Gmail inboxes and Salesforce, eliminating the need to switch between multiple tabs to complete critical tasks across Gmail, Salesforce, and other tools. Use Gong’s AI to ask open-ended questions, receive insights about contacts, update CRM information, add to-dos, and add people to Gong Engage flows. Learn more

Advanced filtering in Accounts and People

With advanced filtering for all CRM field types, you can easily find the list of accounts or people you need, including filtering by CRM campaign object. Jump between saved filters to find the accounts or people you need faster. Learn more in Accounts, learn more in People

More from Engage

Export Engage notes to your CRM

Notes that you write for accounts, contacts and leads in Engage are now exported to Salesforce or HubSpot and are added to the relevant entity. You can set if and how notes should be exported in the Engage CRM setup page. Learn more

Submit regulatory documentation for UK numbers

As of July 29, 2024, regulatory documentation is required to get new UK business phone numbers. To keep existing UK numbers active, submit documentation by September 30, 2024. You can submit your documentation directly through Gong. Learn more

Simplified process of phone number provisioning

Improvements to Gong Connect settings make it easier for admins to view, search for, and assign phone numbers to team members. Learn more

Improvements in Engage Analytics

Use the new flow activity filter in the Activity and Performance tabs to see metrics for only flow-related activities. In Performance, click on the bounced deliveries metric to view the bounce reasons per rep and the bounced emails. Learn more

chunks.text:
Changes to Gong dialer recording options:
Recording rep side of conversation only

We’ve added a new recording method so that you can record the rep side of the call only.

Learn more

Default recording methods per region

To enable you to easily comply with regulations in different countries and states, you can now set dialer recording methods per region. This includes setting different recording methods for different area codes in the USA. If you have already configured recording calls in specific area codes, those settings will be migrated and do not have to be set up again.

Engage

Manage your email from Engage

The new Email page in Engage gives you a complete view of any emails and drafts you create and send through the Gong email composer. Edit, schedule, and send emails, find out why an email failed, and see what was successfully delivered. Learn more

Get more flexibility with Engage flows

Now you can fine-tune your flows, even while they're active. Re-order, add, and delete steps while there are people in a flow and the changes will apply to future contacts and leads added to the flow. You can also send automatic emails according to a recipient’s local time, set automatic emails to send immediately, organize flow steps by days, and predefine email recipients. Learn more

See all to-dos related to a specific contact or lead

Get a quick overview of any to-dos related to a contact or lead, including to-dos owned by other reps. Hover over the person's name from anywhere in Engage, click View contact or View lead, and go to the To-dos tab to see what's open. You can also mark to-dos as complete from here. Learn more

- Customize date range for initiative adoption tracking: Set any date range you want for analyzing initiative adoption rates, so you get exactly the data you need for supporting and optimizing your team. Learn more
- Track initiatives across multiple teams and individuals: Get a fuller picture of how your strategic initiatives are being adopting by tracking initiatives across several teams and team members. Learn more
- New search filter: Call Outcome (AI): Search for calls using the new Call Outcome (AI) filter, which enables you to find calls for coaching according to AI-based automatic dispositions. Learn more
- Hide forecast boards: Forecast admins can now hide unneeded forecast boards when business needs change. No reminders are sent for hidden boards. Read more
- Gong data cloud updates: Call transcripts and the call spotlight are now exported to Snowflake. Learn more

September 2023

Introducing Gong Engage

Say goodbye to ineffective spray-and-pray prospecting tactics, overwhelming manual tasks, and the burden of navigating multiple tools. Engage drives quality sales engagement at scale from the first touch to closed-won, all in one place.

Changes to Gong dialer recording options:
- Accurate rollups when the org user hierarchy changes: When users leave the company or become inactive, they are labeled ‘inactive’ while keeping attained revenues to prevent skewing company rollups. More
- Accurate rollups for inactive users in historical periods: We’ve improved the logic behind showing people who move teams or leave the company to ensure accurate numbers in historical periods. More
- New, customizable ‘Update CRM’ tab: Review and update critical CRM fields when inspecting a deal or calling your number. Find the tab when drilling into a deal from your deal or forecast boards. More
- Forecasts for multiple business motions in one view: Get clarity on how different parts of your business are performing at a glance, in an aggregated forecast board. Review and update numbers quickly or drill into each business line to get more context when needed. More
- Update your numbers automatically based on the underlying pipeline: Set the forecast category numbers to be filled automatically by the sum of all deals matching the filters. More
- Support for more revenue roles: We now support forecasting by alternative opportunity owners, such as SEs or CSMs. More
- Greater filtering flexibility with logic filters: Slice and dice your deals to accurately define your business motions. Use AND/OR/NOT logic conditions to filter deals in your deal & forecast boards. More
- Improved Canadian French, Japanese and Hebrew transcripts: Thanks to our new, in-house speech-to-text models, teams who speak Canadian French, Japanese and Hebrew now have a smoother, more accurate reading and searching experience that's above industry standards. Learn more
- Easier search: Find calls according to customer participants: Quickly find the calls you’re looking for using the Participants filter, which now includes customers who were on a call, as well as team members. Search for customer participants in the main navigation search, too. More about search
- Call categories: New look and feel: We’ve updated the call category management area, so it's easier to use. Learn more
- Showpad integration: See your Showpad engagement events in Gong to get a full picture of deal activity using Gong’s integration with Showpad. Showpad integration
- Trumpet Integration: Add your Gong recordings to pods in Trumpet and get your pod analytics in Gong with Gong’s integration with Trumpet. Trumpet integration
- Loxo Integration: Embed your Gong recordings in a Loxo minisite to share with prospects. Get Loxo analytics on when prospects visit your minisite with Gong’s integration with Loxo. Loxo integration
- Initiatives widget available from homepage: The initiatives widget on your homepage shows talk track adoption from the latest initiative board you visited, so you can keep track on who's adopting your sales initiatives and who is still catching up.

  - Ability to connect conversation participants with the relevant CRM contact.
  - Scorecard data now available.
  - Additional data in the CALLS table.

- Create one task per activity in Salesforce: In order to prevent data inflation in tasks, you can now choose to create one task for activities exported to Salesforce. Previously, a separate task was created for each participant in an activity. For more details, see Create Salesforce tasks for calls and emails

June 2023 Gong Engage is coming

Our newest product is the only sales engagement solution powered by customer interactions and the industry’s most accurate AI models. Engage will help you personalize engagement with account-based outreach from lead to close, increase rep productivity with AI-driven automation and guidance, and streamline team workflows in one place. Contact your account team to find out how to get started with Engage.

Save time with AI-generated call summaries for outbound telephony calls

See everything you need to know about prospecting calls at a glance with AI-generated call summaries. Get call outcome, next steps, a short summary, and prospect highlights, all without listening to a moment of the call. Learn more

Work in multiple currencies and roll up to a single currency

View deals, roll up your pipeline, and forecast in a single corporate currency, with the ability to edit deal amounts in the native currency.

Learn how to set up and work with multiple currencies here

Get CRM data in Snowflake as it was when the conversation occurred

n Snowflake, you can now get an accurate picture of your CRM data as it was when a call took place. You can use this data to understand how different behaviors help move a deal to the next stage, the time it takes close a deal, and the deal size. The fields_snapshot and mapped_fields_snapshot columns were added to the conversation_contexts table and contain the CRM fields and values that are imported to Gong. Currently, these fields contain call data only.

You may need to reach out to more contacts in order to move your deal forward. Gong now provides recommendations for contacts who may be missing from the deal. Gong has partnered with Apollo, Cognism, and LeadIQ to provide email and phone details for the recommended contacts. Learn more

The summarized report gives you an overall picture of how your company benefits from its Gong seats, while the detailed report shows how your employees are using all different areas of Gong. Learn more

- Choose the HubSpot object to export calls to: If you sync your calendar meetings to HubSpot you may get duplicate meeting objects when you export your Gong calls as meetings. To avoid this duplication, you can now choose to export your calls as a note or a call in HubSpot. Learn more
- Choose which CRM fields you see when you filter calls: When searching for specific calls, you can now customize which CRM fields you see in the results. Learn more about filtering for calls
- More ways to get smart tracker data: Using smart trackers to identify when concepts are discussed in your calls? You can now view results via the Calls API, and download them in the call CSV. More about smart trackers

- Fabius integration: You can now analyze your Gong recordings to identify cases where your reps conversations don't align with your sales methodology, by using Gong's integration with Fabius. Learn more

- Stalled in stage warning - Get alerted of risk in deal momentum so that you can eliminate it quickly. Define a time limit (in days) for any opportunity stage from your CRM when creating or editing your deal board.
- Deal drivers - Our new coaching tool gives you insights on total deal performance. Frontline managers can now track KPIs on how their team members behave on and manage deals in the TEAM > DEAL DRIVERS tab. Learn more.

- Improved team member provisioning - We simplified the set up flow for automatic provisioning, reducing the risk of importing the entire company (!). We also added support for automatic provisioning with Rippling.

chunks.text:
Changes to Gong dialer recording options:
- New warning: pricing wasn't discussed - Get a heads-up when a deal is due to close, but pricing wasn't discussed yet.
- Company primary currency - Set your company’s primary currency for use across Gong.
- Scheduler for deal digest subscriptions - You can now change the time and day(s) you receive your deal digests.
- My recent boards - Your recently-used boards now appear at the top of the find board drop-down list.
- productboard integration - Create feature requests for your product team using the exact words your customers are saying. Select a snippet from the call transcript and use it to create a note in productboard.
- Private scorecards - Score calls and decide whether the score should be public (visible to all), visible to just you and the call host, or visible only to yourself.
- New scoring types - You can now add questions that can be answered with scores of 1-3 stars, have a YES/NO answer, or that are open-ended, which gives you the ability to offer more structured coaching. Note that for now, the overall scorecard is still 1-5.
- New location for creating scorecards - Business admins can now create scorecards directly from within the TEAM tab > SCORECARDS.
- Coaching metrics - drill down into calls - Now senior managers can see what makes up the data behind the coaching stats, and understand where they're focussing their coaching efforts.
- Highlights in live call transcript - When playing a call, the transcript highlights the text for speech. When accessing a snippet shared with you, call page opens on the highlighted part of the transcript. Select & share snippets internally, to the library, and to productboard.
- Tracker info in calls page - Now when you search for calls using a tracker, you can see what words and phrases make up the tracker.
- Customize data privacy link name on consent page - Admins can now edit the name of the privacy policy link for the consent page. Available in all supported languages.
- Delete calls automation rule - Create a rule to automatically delete calls based on certain phrases.
- Mobile - new call screen on iOS - Jump to next speaker, listen to 1 speaker, see call topics, make hands-free voice comments, and easy access to common actions: see comments, show video, see call info, & share the call.

Moving calls to another workspace is useful if you've separated your Gong instance into different workspaces and want to keep calls with their associated teams.
chunks.title: Move calls to another workspace

chunks.text:
The impact of moving calls:
Here's a quick list of everything that’s affected by moving calls from one workspace to another.

- Links to calls: links to calls shared both internally and externally remain the same.
- Call access: following the move, access to calls is determined by a person’s permission profile in the destination workspace. Regardless of the permission, people can access calls that were shared with them, even if they were shared before the call was moved.
- Comments on the call: all comments, mentions, and feedback on a call moves with the call to the destination.
- Scorecards: Scorecards are part of the workspace they are created in, and do not move together with calls. Any scores given before the move will be removed from the source workspace statistics (Team > Stats > Coaching). In the destination workspace, the score history cannot be seen.
- Library folders: calls are removed from any library folders they belonged to in the source workspace.
- Topics and trackers: calls are rescanned for topics and trackers in the destination workspace, according to the topics and trackers that are defined there. In other words, topics and trackers picked up in the calls when in the source workspace will not show up in the destination workspace, unless someone set up the same topics and trackers.
- Statistics: the move will impact statistics that are calculated in the source workspace because the moved calls will no longer be used to calculate those statistics. In the destination workspace, new statistics will be calculated using the moved calls.

chunks.title: Move calls to another workspace

chunks.text:
How to move calls:
Note:You must be a tech admin to move calls to a different workspaceIf moving many calls at once, the move can take up to a few hours to complete

You can move a single call or multiple calls at once. Here's how:

- To move a single call:
  1. Search for the call you want to move.
  2. Click and select Move from workspace.
  3. Select the destination workspace and click Move call.
- To move multiple calls:
  1. Go to Conversations > Search and filter for the calls that you want to move.
  2. Hover over a call and check the checkbox that appears. Repeat for all calls you want to move or click Select all to check all the filtered calls.
  3. In the floating bar that appears at the bottom of the screen, click and select Move from workspace.
  4. Select the destination workspace and click Move calls.

A team member who manages and configures the Gong platform and handles CRM integrations, user provisioning, permissions, and system settings. Find my Tech admin.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

Manage your language settings > Set your AI Translator preference:
Your AI Translator preference sets the default language for transcripts and AI-generated content, including briefs and AI-suggested playbook notes.

To set your AI Translator preference:

1. Click Languages on the left side of the page.
2. Click the AI Translator dropdown, and select your preferred translation language.
3. Click Save changes.

Admins can also set this preference for you. The most recent change always applies. If your admin updates it after you do, their setting takes effect until you change it again.

To learn more about workspace and team-level translation settings, see How to manage settings for AI Translator.

chunks.body:
To enable Zoom Native recording feature you must have one of the following Zoom licenses:

- Zoom Pro

- Zoom Enterprise
chunks.title: Native Zoom recording

chunks.text:
Benefits to recording with native Zoom:
Gong governs native recording with Zoom in a similar fashion as recording with the Gong bot, meaning that the same business logic and privacy settings in Gong apply. Gong will start Zoom recording and retrieve the recordings from Zoom based on these rules.

Recording with Zoom (native recording) has clear benefits:

- Highest-possible video and audio recording
- On-screen recording notification
- Host can stop, start, and pause the recording as needed (for example, this is useful when screen-sharing or discussing sensitive information)
- No phantom meeting participant (i.e. the Gong bot)
- Ability to leverage Zoom's customizable consent options
- Zoom's recording prompt plays privately so participants only hear it once
- Bring call Zoom chats into Gong
- Leverage Gong app for Zoom to take notes during meetings that are timestamped and shown in the call page

A few limitations compared to recording with the Gong bot:

- No live listening
- No audio-only recording
- No breakout rooms - where the Gong bot can get assigned to a room and record there, with native recording, we can't do that.

Note that it can take a little longer for the call to appear in Gong. This is due to Gong waiting for the call to be ready in Zoom for retrieval.

What to do next: enable Zoom recording!

chunks.text:
Some numeric fields in the Gong data cloud are currently defined as decimal types even though they contain integer values.

To correct this, we have begun a process to update these fields to use the integer type for BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and Amazon S3 destinations.

To avoid breaking existing queries, duplicate fields with the suffix __NEXT have been added with the correct integer type. The __NEXT fields contain the same values as the existing fields.

In May 2026, the migration will be completed. The original fields will use the integer type and the __NEXT fields will be removed.

Who can use this: Tech adminAvailable on: Gong Engage

When a team member leaves your company, moves to a different role, or loses their Engage seat, their personal flows, templates, and blocks don't carry over to the rest of the team. In addition, open flow to-dos stay with them, not with the contacts they were working with. Completing these steps before deactivating their account helps make sure nothing gets lost and no contact falls through the cracks.

Note:If you have already deactivated the team member, temporarily reactivate their account, complete these steps, then deactivate them again.

chunks.title: Offboard a team member from Engage

chunks.text:
Before you begin:
- Personal assets: Personal flows, templates, blocks, are only visible to the team member who created them. If any are actively used or relied on by the team, plan to preserve them before deactivation. Check with the team member who's leaving or their manager if you're unsure what's worth keeping.
- Permissions: Non-managers need the Assign flows and to-dos to others permission to reassign flow to-dos. Managers can reassign without it. See Available permission settings for details.
- Timing: Reassignment is easier while the team member is still active. You'll still have full visibility into their assets and can confirm what needs moving. Check whether they have contacts in flows before you start.

chunks.text:
Offboard the team member:
Complete these steps in order. Deactivating the team member before finishing the earlier steps can mean lost assets, contacts with no one to follow up on them, and failed outreach. When a seat is deactivated, active flows are paused and scheduled auto-emails fail because they require an active seat and authenticated email connection.

chunks.text:
Offboard the team member > Step 1: Review and preserve important personal assets:
Personal assets such as flows, templates, blocks are only visible to the team member who created them, and they're permanently deleted when their account is deactivated. As an admin, you can see all personal assets shared by any team member. Review what the team member who's leaving has built and duplicate anything worth keeping before it's gone.

To review and duplicate personal assets (flows, templates or blocks):

1. From the left sidebar, click Assets, and select one of the following:
  - Flows
  - Content templates
  - Content blocks
2. Open the Shared with you section. As an admin, you can see flows, templates and blocks shared by any team member here, including personal ones from the team member who's leaving.
3. For each flow, template or block worth keeping, duplicate it and choose where you want to save it:
  1. Hover over the relevant flow, block or template.
  2. Click the More actions icon and select Duplicate.
  3. Choose where to save the flow, template or block based on who you want to have access to it:
    - Company: Anyone in the organization can use the flow.
    - Personal: Duplicate to your own flows, then share with specific teammates.
  4. Click Duplicate.
4. Review the duplicated flow, template or block for field placeholders, email accounts, or personal references that need to be updated for the new owner.

chunks.title: Offboard a team member from Engage

chunks.text:
Offboard the team member > Step 2: Reassign open flow to-dos:
When a team member is deactivated, their open flow to-dos don't move to anyone else automatically, and the contacts or leads they were working with simply stop receiving outreach. Reassigning from the To-dos page transfers the flow instance and all future to-dos in one action, so nothing goes cold. Learn more about flow to-dos.

Note:One-off to-dos and Gong-recommended to-dos cannot be reassigned. These will need to be closed or left to expire.

To reassign open flow to-dos:

1. From the left sidebar, click To-dos.
2. Use the filters at the top of the page to show only the to-dos belonging to the team member who's leaving.
3. Click the To-do assignee is filter and search for the team member who’s leaving.
4. At the top right, click the More actions icon , and select Reassign flow to-dos.
5. Choose how you want to reassign the open flow to-dos:
  - Reassign all of Team member's flow to-dos
  - Reassign only the flow to-dos matching the current filters: Check that the filters are correct.
6. Click New to-do assignee dropdown, and select the new assignee.
7. Click Reassign.

The flow instances and all future flow to-dos are transferred to the new assignee.

Note:This process applies to contacts. Leads in flows need different handling. If the lead’s next step doesn’t appear on the To-dos page, note the step they’re on, remove them from the flow, then re-add them to the same flow, start them from the correct step, and assign the new owner.

chunks.text:
Offboard the team member > Step 3: Reassign flows with scheduled emails:
Some flow work needs to be handled separately during offboarding. Before you deactivate the team member, check for scheduled email-related work that isn’t covered by the Reassign flow to-dos, then transfer the related flows to the new owner.

To check for manually scheduled emails:

1. From the left sidebar, click Engagement, and select Messages.
2. Click the Scheduled tab to see all emails the team member who's leaving has queued to send.

Note:Scheduled auto emails don’t appear on the Scheduled tab. If you know which flow they belong to, reassign the flow to transfer the upcoming auto emails to the new owner. If an auto email later fails to send, Gong converts it into a manual email instead of dropping it. To reduce unexpected manual email work during offboarding, reassign active flows before disconnecting the team member’s email account.

Once you’ve identified the email contacts whose flows need to be reassigned, you can reassign them from the People page.

To reassign a flow from the People page:

1. From the left sidebar, click Engagement, and select People.
2. Find the contact whose flow needs to be reassigned and click the status in the Flow status column.
3. In the Flows in progress section, find the flow you want to reassign and click the Manage flow icon .
4. Click the Assign owner dropdown, and select the new owner.
5. Click Save.

The flow and all its to-dos are transferred to the new assignee.

chunks.text:
FAQs:
Can I move a contact or lead if they’re already in an exclusive flow?

If a contact or lead is already in an exclusive flow, they may need to be removed from that flow before they can be added to a new one. A new rep may not be able to add them to another flow right away. You can remove them from their current flow as part of adding them to the new one. When bulk adding contacts, use Remove from current flows to move them in one action. Learn more about managing people in flows.

Does reassigning a flow update the CRM flow status fields?

No. Reassigning a flow changes ownership in Gong, but it doesn’t automatically refresh the flow status data already synced to your CRM. The CRM fields continue to reflect the flow state from the time of sync.

Can I transfer attachments when offboarding a team member?

Attachments are preserved as part of the flow or template they belong to, rather than through a separate transfer workflow. If a team member has attachments your team still needs, keep them by duplicating or sharing the relevant flow or template before deactivation.

chunks.text:
Set up provisioning in Okta > Set up the Gong profile in Okta:
1. In Okta, go to Directory > Profile Editor, and locate the Gong profile.
2. Click the Edit icon to edit the profile. In the Attributes > All tab, you can see all the attributes in the Gong profile.
3. The following fields are mandatory when provisioning with Gong:
  - Given name
  - Last name
  - Primary email: the email domain must match your company primary domain, otherwise the user won't be imported
4. The following fields are optional, but it’s highly recommended to configure them for your users before provisioning to avoid the need for manual updates: Note: Provisioned fields cannot be edited manually. If you leave a field empty, it can be manually set one time in Gong. After this, the field can’t be modified.
  - Phone number: Enter the phone number in any of the following formats:
    - (865) 365-1900
    - (212) 575-1994 ext 3437
    - (317) 251-0700 ext. 468
    - (202) 903-2585 x2991
    - (206) 324-1800 x 229
    - 540.946.4600 Ext. 143
  - Primary Phone Ext: Enter the extension number
  - Secondary Email: Mapped to team members Additional email addresses. Used as additional ways to identify the user. Includes both additional email addresses and email aliases. See Primary and additional email address.
  - Private Email: If users have a private email, configure this field.
  - Title: Enter the user's job title
  - Manager Email: (Recommended) Enter the manager's email address. Without this field, Gong cannot build your organization’s hierarchy. Note:The manager’s email is required for building the company hierarchy. If you set the assignment to automatic updates, this field must be provided.
  - Manager Full Name: In the format firstname lastname, e.g. John Doe. The manager’s full name should be provided if you can’t provide the manager’s email. If neither this field or the Manager ID field are defined, Gong cannot automatically build your organization hierarchy. Note that, if there's more than one manager with the same name, Gong can't set the manager for the user and you'll have to set this manually in Gong. This method is not recommended for building the company hierarchy.
  - Time zone: Use any value from the list of time zones in List of tz database time zones. Note:Updating the user’s time zone after they have been provisioned can only be done by updating their time zone in Okta. Changing their country won’t change their time zone.
  - Country: Enter the country’s full name or 2 or 3 letter country code, according to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes
  - State or Province: Enter the full state or province name, or two letter code according to the following ISO codes:
    - US: ISO 3166-2:US
    - Canada: ISO 3166-2:CA
    - Australia: ISO 3166-2:AU (for Australia the state code can be 2 or 3 letters)
  - Locale: Use the following format: en-US. If you don’t define a locale for a user, they are assigned en-US by default. This field is used in Gong to identify the user's weekend in order to avoid sending notifications when the user is not working.

Set up provisioning in Gong:
Once you have set Okta up to provision to Gong, configure the automatic provisioning settings in Gong.

1. Go to Admin center > Settings > People > Team Member Provisioning.
2. In the Manager's provisioning settings area:
  1. Select Notify direct managers with recorded teams when a new team member is imported to send a notification by email when new team members are automatically provisioned.
  2. Select Managers can turn data capture on or off for their team to allow direct managers to change the data capture settings for their team members. Note: This setting lets managers enable data capture despite not being a technical admin. If you only want appointed tech admins to have this capability, make sure this box is not checked.
3. Click SAVE.
4. Click Add assignments to create a new assignment or click an assignment you want to edit to assign seats, data capture settings, workspaces, and permissions to provisioned team members.

chunks.text:
Set up provisioning in Gong > Upgrade from one Gong app to a later version:
If you originally installed a version of the Gong for Okta app that is older than version 3, upgrade to version 3 to get the following fields: Manager Email, Manager Full Name, Private Email, Country, State or Province, and Primary Phone Ext.

Add a new instance of Gong in your Okta org. Follow these steps to migrate from to the latest instance of Gong:

1. Login to your Okta org as an Admin.
2. Open the Admin dashboard, and click Add Applications.
3. Add a new instance of Gong.
4. Configure the application including Provisioning. See step 3 above for more information. After SCIM Provisioning has been enabled, go to the Assignments tab of your new Gong app instance.
5. Click Assign and start assigning the same users/groups that are assigned to your old Gong instance. Note:Make sure you assign all the users to your new Gong instance to avoid any accidental de-provisioning/loss of access for your users.
6. Go back to your Admin dashboard, and open your old Gong app instance.
7. Go to the Provisioning tab, and in the SETTINGS section, click API.
8. Click Edit and clear the Enable API Integration checkbox.
9. Click Save. You can now deactivate or delete your old Gong app instance and start using the new instance. Important:If you were using SAML as the sign-on mode for your old Gong app instance, you will need to set up SAML on your new app instance in Okta (recommended) or maintain the old app instance to ensure that the SAML functionality continues to work. See this guide to set up SAML.

chunks.text:
Opportunity teams FAQs:
What if I use custom Salesforce objects for opportunity teams?

Support for custom objects may be available with additional configuration. For more details, Import Salesforce data from additional objects.

Does it matter which role the user has on the opportunity team? Do we need to choose which roles to show?

No, you don't need to select the relevant roles. We'll show all deals where someone is on the opportunity team, regardless of their role.

What is shown if two team members work on a deal? Do you count the deal amount twice?

No, we show the deal with the relevant attribution per person.

When looking at a team where two people worked on the same deal, we show the deal once.

For example:

Rep A and Rep B both worked on the Acme Industries deal.

When Rep A or B look at their deals, they see the deal and the deal value is included in the rollup.

When Rep A and Rep B's manager looks at the team deals, they see the deal once, with both Rep A and Rep B in the opportunity team column. The deal value is included once in the rollup.

Why can't I see opportunity teams in my forecast analytics?

We don't support opportunity teams in forecast analytics at this time.

chunks.title: FAQs: Opportunity teams and opportunity splits

chunks.text:
Opportunity splits FAQs:
What CRM fields are supported on the standard opportunity splits object?

Gong only supports Salesforce.

If you’re using the standard amount object – Opportunity splits, you’ll be able to easily set it up in Gong.

What if I use custom Salesforce objects for opportunity splits?

Support for custom objects may be available with additional configuration. Contact your Revenue Architect (RA) to learn more.

If two team members work on a deal, do you count the deal amount twice?

No, we show the deal with the relevant attribution per person.

When looking at a team where two people worked on the same deal, we show the deal once.

For example:

Rep A and Rep B split a deal 50:50.

When Rep A or B look at their deals, they see the deal with 50% of the deal value.

When Rep A and Rep B's manager looks at the team deals, they see the deal with 100% attribution, that is Rep A's 50% and Rep B's 50% combined.

Can a deal value exceed 100% (overlays)?

Yes - we show overlays if you set up overlay split types on the relevant amount field in your CRM.

We have splits on different amount fields in Salesforce. Which ones will Gong use?

We apply all active split types defined in Salesforce for the Amount field that's used to roll-up amounts in the Gong deal board.

Deactivated splits, or splits that apply to any other amount field won't be applied.

Why can't I see opportunity splits in my forecast analytics?

We don't support opportunity splits in forecast analytics at this time.

chunks.text:
Opportunity splits FAQs:
Troubleshooting: Not seeing split amounts

There are two key aspects to consider:

1. Opportunity splits are displayed for teams or individual members only when splits have been assigned to them.
2. Opportunity splits must be associated to the Amount field that's being used to roll up deals in the board.

Here’s what you can do in your CRM:

1. Verify that the deals you're looking at have assigned splits on them.
2. Check the Split types settings. Which split types are enabled? Which amount field are they applied to?

Here’s what you can do in your Gong deal board:

1. Make sure you're looking at deals and teams where splits are applied.
2. Check which Amount field is used in the board.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Who can use this: Any team memberAvailable on: Gong FoundationRequired permissions: Manage AI Trackers

Question-based AI Trackers consume Gong credits based on the amount of call and email data analyzed.

You can create and publish as many AI Trackers as needed.

Well-designed AI Trackers help reduce unnecessary processing and improve the quality of AI Tracker insights.

This guide explains how to create AI Trackers that:

- Analyze only relevant calls and emails
- Reduce unnecessary Gong credit consumption
- Focus AI Tracker analysis on high-value business workflows

Question-based AI Trackers consume Gong credits based on the amount of call and email data analyzed.

You can create and publish as many AI Trackers as needed.

Well-designed AI Trackers help reduce unnecessary processing and improve the quality of AI Tracker insights.

This guide explains how to create AI Trackers that:

- Analyze only relevant calls and emails
- Reduce unnecessary Gong credit consumption
- Focus AI Tracker analysis on high-value business workflows
chunks.title: Optimize AI Trackers for Gong credits

chunks.text:
Plan the AI Tracker before building it:
Clearly defining the AI Tracker purpose helps reduce unnecessary analysis and improve the relevance of AI Tracker results.

Define the following before creating the AI Tracker:

- What business concept, customer behavior, or conversational topic the AI Tracker should identify
- Whether the AI Tracker should analyze calls, emails, or both
- Which side of the conversation the AI Tracker should track:
  - Our rep
  - Customer
  - Any party
- Which conversations are relevant to the AI Tracker
- Whether filters are needed to narrow the analysis scope
- Whether the AI Tracker should analyze the entire conversation or only part of the call
- What additional details may help improve tracking accuracy

chunks.headingPath: Plan the AI Tracker before building it
chunks.title: Optimize AI Trackers for Gong credits

chunks.text:
Create focused AI Trackers:
AI Trackers work best when they focus on a specific business signal or workflow.

Examples of focused AI Trackers include:

- Pricing objections during proposal-stage calls
- Product feedback for a specific product line
- Customer churn risk during renewal discussions
- Competitor mentions during discovery calls

Focused AI Trackers are easier to validate and usually consume fewer credits than broad AI Trackers.

chunks.title: Optimize AI Trackers for Gong credits

chunks.text:
Avoid overly broad AI Trackers:
Broad AI Trackers may analyze large amounts of unrelated activity and consume credits unnecessarily.

Avoid AI Trackers that:

- Monitor too many unrelated concepts
- Analyze all company calls and emails without filters
- Combine multiple unrelated business goals into one AI Tracker

Example of an overly broad AI Tracker:

“Identify customer concerns, pricing objections, competitor mentions, and product feedback.”

Broad AI Trackers are harder to validate, may return less relevant results, and can consume large amounts of Gong credits.

chunks.text:
Decide when email analysis is necessary:
Selecting Calls and emails increases the amount of processed activity and may consume more credits.

Use Calls only when the relevant business signal mainly appears in spoken conversations. Examples include:

- Pricing objections discussed during sales calls
- Competitive discussions during discovery meetings
- Customer sentiment during live conversations
- Product feedback discussed during demos

Use Calls and emails only when the business signal commonly appears in both activity types. Examples include:

- Procurement discussions
- Legal approval processes
- Renewal communications
- Product requests discussed over email

chunks.title: Optimize AI Trackers for Gong credits

chunks.text:
Apply filters:
Filters help narrow AI Tracker analysis to relevant conversations.

Applying filters helps:

- Reduce Gong credit consumption
- Improve AI Tracker relevance
- Focus AI Tracker analysis on the correct audience or workflow

AI Trackers without filters may analyze large amounts of unrelated activity and consume credits unnecessarily.

chunks.text:
AI Tracker filter examples:
Available filters include:

- Call participants, including specific users, teams, or managers
- CRM filters for accounts, opportunities, contacts, or leads
- Deal stage, either during the call or the current deal stage
- Account type or account tier
- Account industry
- Opportunity type
- Close date
- Deal size
- Call duration
- Call type, including web conference, inbound, or outbound calls
- Conversation engagement metrics such as talk ratio or questions asked

Use multiple filters for more precise targeting:
Combining multiple filters helps narrow AI Tracker analysis to the most relevant conversations. Examples include:

- Enterprise accounts
- Proposal-stage opportunities
- AE team

This filter combination limits analysis to enterprise pricing conversations handled by account executives during proposal discussions.

Match filters to the AI Tracker purpose:
Identify which filters support the purpose of the AI Tracker. For example:

- If an AI Tracker supports a specific sales play, filter to the deal stage where that sales play is relevant
- If an AI Tracker is used for coaching a specific team, filter to that team’s calls
- If an AI Tracker monitors a specific product, filter to opportunities associated with that product

Understand how filters apply to emails:
Selecting both Calls and emails allows the AI Tracker to analyze email activity in addition to calls.

Most available filters also apply to emails, including:

- Participants
- Account name
- Date
- Scope

- Payments
- Scheduling
- Spam
- Legal

chunks.text:
Reduce unnecessary email analysis:
Users with captured email activity may send large volumes of outbound emails.

AI Trackers configured for both calls and emails may analyze irrelevant email activity if filters are too broad.

To narrow the analysis scope, consider using filters such as:

- Deal stage
- Associated with an opportunity

These filters help reduce analysis on irrelevant email activity.

Review AI Trackers regularly:
Business priorities and workflows change over time, and AI Trackers should be reviewed regularly. Review AI Trackers quarterly to:

- Remove outdated AI Trackers
- Refine filters
- Improve AI Tracker targeting
- Reduce unnecessary analysis

Regular maintenance helps improve AI Tracker quality and optimize Gong credit consumption.

chunks.text:
Who can use this: Tech adminAvailable on: Any Gong plan

Where to go: Admin center > Settings > Data capture > Telephony systems

Connect Gong to Outreach so that Gong can retrieve calls directly from Outreach. This is more reliable than going through a third party and makes troubleshooting easier.

To connect to Outreach:

1. Click Admin center > Settings > Data capture > Telephony systems.
2. Click + Add telephony system.
3. Select Outreach.
4. Set the speaker channel to the desired channel.
5. Click CONNECT.

To access account and prospect calls in Gong from Outreach, without having to connect to the Outreach telephony integration, see Gong for Outreach

Gong is committed to respecting the security of you and your customer's information, including electronic cardholder data. Gong Revenue AI Operating System is not intended to nor does it store any credit card information. Gong does have the ability to handle payment card information in transit that is compliant with PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) for accepting, processing, storing, or transmitting payment card information. By adhering to these standards, an organization enforces the security of credit, debit, and cash card transactions and protects cardholders against fraud or other misuses of their personal information.

chunks.title: Gong PCI DSS scope and responsibilities

chunks.text:
What is PCI DSS?:
PCI DSS is an information security standard for organizations that handle payment card information. Credit card payment brands require adherence to the PCI DSS standard for any entity that processes, transmits, or stores cardholder data. The standard was created to increase controls around cardholder data to reduce credit card fraud. Validation of compliance is performed annually.

Credit card payment brands require adherence to the PCI DSS standard for any entity that processes, transmits, or stores cardholder data. The standard was created to increase controls around cardholder data to reduce credit card fraud. Validation of compliance is performed annually.
chunks.title: Gong PCI DSS scope and responsibilities

chunks.text:
How has Gong's PCI DSS compliance been validated?:
Gong's PCI DSS compliance includes the completion of the SAQ-D questionnaire and external validation by a Qualified Security Assessor (QSA). Gong's PCI DSS environment is limited in scope and does not cover the entire Gong platform. Gong's current PCI DSS compliance only applies to the mechanisms that ingest calls from external telephony systems.

Gong's PCI DSS environment is limited in scope and does not cover the entire Gong platform. Gong's current PCI DSS compliance only applies to the mechanisms that ingest calls from external telephony systems.
chunks.headingPath: How has Gong's PCI DSS compliance been validated?
chunks.title: Gong PCI DSS scope and responsibilities

chunks.text:
What features are PCI DSS-compliant?:
The PCI DSS compliant environment includes Gong's application integrations with telephony systems only, initial storage of these calls, and processing intended to redact all payment card information from these calls in a non-recoverable manner. The QSA's scope consisted of Gong's API servers, call analyzer processors, the ability to identify and redact PCI-related data, and the temporary storage of calls before the sensitive data is redacted. What is not in scope of Gong's PCI DSS compliance are web recorders' calls or videos and other types of data (e.g. email). Gong Revenue AI Operating System is not intended to store payment card information.

chunks.title: Gong PCI DSS scope and responsibilities

chunks.text:
What are my responsibilities for using Gong in a PCI DSS-compliant manner?:
The customer's responsibility is to define the redaction rules for calls being uploaded from telephony systems to the Gong application. This can be done easily in the Data Protection & Privacy settings by defining the minimum sequence of digits that should be redacted. Once this is defined, all future calls will have these settings applied both on the audio files as well as on the call transcripts. Gong will only redact data based on the redaction settings the customer has defined. The customer still has the ability to delete recordings or telephony uploads. It is the customer's responsibility to adhere to Gong's stated PCI DSS scope.

chunks.text:
How to build it:
1. Build 4 KPI widgets:
  1. Booking attainment:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Bookings ($) - and set it to be measured against the bookings target.
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Overall win rate:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Win rate ($).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  3. Total pipeline created
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Pipeline created ($).
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  4. ASP
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Average sales price ($).
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
2. Build 1 performance widget:
  1. Team performance
    1. Include 4 metrics in the widget: Bookings ($), Win rate by amount ($), Win rate by deal count (#), and Average sales price ($).
    2. Set Bookings ($) to be measured against the bookings target and color code its values: green for when the value > 100, red for < 70
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
3. Build 1 trends widgets:
  1. How’s this quarter’s pipeline trending?
    1. Base the widget on your line of business.
    2. Break down the data by forecast category and select the default forecast category.
    3. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the current fiscal quarter.
4. Build 5 custom charts:
  1. Booking ($) performance over time by team:
    1. Base the widget on Bookings ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the last 4 fiscal quarters.
    3. Break down the data by quarter and team member (rolled up by team).
  2. Pipeline created ($) over time by type:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the last 4 fiscal quarters.
    3. Break down the data by quarter and opportunity type.
  3. Win rate performance ($) over time by type:
    1. Base the widget on Win rate ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the last 4 fiscal quarters.
    3. Break down the data by quarter and team member (rolled up by team).
  4. ASP ($) performance over time by team:
    1. Base the widget on Win rate ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the last 4 fiscal quarters.
    3. Break down the data by quarter and opportunity type.
  5. Loss reasons:
    1. Base the widget on Total lost ($).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by loss reason and opportunity type.
5. Build 2 deals widgets:
  1. Highest value won deals
    1. Base the widget on a deal board, select the board’s default tab, and select the columns to include in the widget.
    2. Filter the deals by status: Closed-won.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Highest value lost deals
    1. Base the widget on a deal board, select the board’s default tab, and select the columns to include in the widget.
    2. Filter the deals by status: Closed-lost.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
6. Build 1 funnel widgets:
  1. Last quarter’s funnel conversion:
    1. Base the widget on your amount, owner, and close date CRM fields.
7. Build 1 custom chart:
  1. Next quarter's pipeline by close date and stage:
    1. Base the widget on Open pipeline ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the current fiscal quarters.
    3. Break down the data by week and stage.

chunks.text:
What’s a performance widget:
With performance widgets, you can compare individual or team performance based on multiple metrics and targets. To simplify the view and allow viewers to see whether people are on the right track at a glance, you may assign different colors to value ranges. Viewers can also toggle between team and individual views. Performance widgets support all dashboard date picker types and updates the widget results based on the date selection made in the dashboard.

Building a performance widget:

To build a new performance widget:
