To build a new performance widget:
chunks.title: Performance widget

chunks.text:
Building a performance widget:
1. Select your dashboard, click +New widget and select Performance from the gallery.
2. In the dashboard header, click the edit icon to rename your widget and, optionally, + Add description.
3. Under Metric, select the first metric to include in the widget. The metric values will appear in the first column of the table, for each team/individual. Viewers can sort the table by the values in each column. You can rename it by clicking and then Rename metric. Click + New metric to create a new metric, and then pull it to your Performance widget. Click to edit an existing metric and click Save.
4. Check Measure against target to show the attainment value (metric/target percentage value) for each team or individual, in addition to the metric value, as a secondary number.
5. Check Assign display color to value ranges to color code the metric’s values, and apply green, yellow, and red indications to different ranges. Note:If Measure against target is selected, the ranges reflect the attainment value, rather than the metric’s value.
6. You may add any filter (+Add filter) that defines which deals/accounts qualify to be included in the column. For example, deals in which Sales qualified is true and Deal stage is neither Closed-won nor Closed-lost.
7. To add a metric to the widget, click Add metric and repeat the above steps. You can drag and drop the metrics to reorder the table columns.
8. Below your metrics, under Select team and period, you’ll notice the team member and date fields are set to be dynamic and respond to whatever is selected in your dashboard. You can change them to fixed values. Note:If you select fixed values for the team member and period, the widget would no longer respond to selections made on the dashboard level. The team selection will be applied to the selected metrics’ team member field, and the period selection will be applied to the selected metrics’ date field.
9. Select your Drilldown view: the view that opens up when viewers click to inspect the deals/accounts included in the widget.
10. Play with the Preview options on the right to validate your settings. When you’re happy with the results, click Save.

chunks.text:
Best practices:
To get the most out of performance widgets, we recommend:

Using color coding sensibly

The color coding should make sense for all teams/periods if the dashboard widget is set to work with dynamic teams and periods.

Therefore, use color coding only for metrics that have a standard definition of good across different teams and periods (such as win rate, ASP, attainment) and not metrics like Bookings or Pipeline created that can vary between teams and periods.

Using different ways to compare

To compare two periods’ performance, you can:

- Place two performance widgets side-by-side
- Place one performance widget at the top of the dashboard and a few KPI widgets, one for each metric included in the performance widget, underneath it.

Note:This procedure requires permission to manage revenue analytics

The easiest way to build this dashboard is by generating it from a template. If you prefer building it on your own, here’s how:

1. Build KPI widgets:
  1. Total pipe created:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Pipeline created ($), measured against its target - Pipeline created.
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Any number of pipe created by source widgets:
    1. Base each widget on a single metric - Pipe created - Source name.
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Optional: If your company has targets per source, you can measure each metric against its equivalent target.
2. Build a performance widgets - Pipeline creation by team and source:
  1. Add your metrics to your widget - Pipeline created ($), and all Pipe created by source metrics, and optionally measure them against their targets.
  2. Color code the value ranges. For metrics measured against targets, the colors apply to the attainment value.
3. Build 2 custom charts - Pipeline created ($) performance over time and Pipeline created (#) performance over time:
  1. Base one chart on Pipeline created ($) and the other on Pipeline created (#). In both widgets:
    1. Filter the data to show deals of the last six months.
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by month.

chunks.text:
How to build it:
1. Build 3 KPI widgets:
  1. Open pipeline ($):
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Open pipeline ($)
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Running win rate (%):
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Win rate (%).
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  3. ASP open deals ($):
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Average open deal size ($)
    2. Set the date (created date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
2. Build 7 custom charts:
  1. Open pipeline ($) by team and type:
    1. Base the widget on Open pipeline ($).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by team and opportunity type.
  2. Open pipeline ($) by tier:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created ($).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by tier.
  3. Open pipeline ($) by forecast category and stage:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created (#).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by forecast category and stage.
  4. Open pipeline ($) by month and stage:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created (#).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by month and stage.
  5. Open pipeline ($) by week and stage:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created (#).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by week and stage.
  6. Open pipeline ($) by next call date (week):
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created (#).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by week of the next call.
  7. Open pipeline ($) by last activity date (week):
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created (#).
    2. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Break down the data by week of the last activity.
3. Build 2 changes widgets:
  1. Pipeline changes in the last week:
    1. Base the widget on a line of business.
    2. Select the forecast category and the range date to reflect the last 7 days.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Pipeline changes since the beginning of the quarter:
    1. Base the widget on a line of business.
    2. Select the forecast category and the range date to reflect the time since the beginning of the quarter.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
4. Build 2 deals widgets:
  1. Highest value deals with warnings
    1. Base the widget on a deal board, select the board’s default tab, and select the columns to include in the widget.
    2. Filter the deals by the warnings and include all warnings.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  2. Open deals with low scores
    1. Base the widget on a deal board, select the board’s default tab, and select the columns to include in the widget.
    2. Filter the deals by low score.
    3. Set the date (closed date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
5. Build 2 trends widgets:
  1. How’s this quarter’s pipeline trending?
    1. Base the widget on your line of business.
    2. Break down the data by forecast category and select the default forecast category.
    3. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the current fiscal quarter.
  2. How’s next quarter’s pipeline shaping up?
    1. Base the widget on a line of business.
    2. Break down the data by forecast category and select the default forecast category.
    3. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the period as the next fiscal quarter.
6. Build 3 custom charts:
  1. Open pipeline ($) lookout by month and stage:
    1. Base the widget on Open pipeline ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the date as 3 fiscal quarter + current.
    3. Break down the data by month and stage.
  2. Open pipeline ($) lookout by team and tier:
    1. Base the widget on Open pipeline ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the date as 3 fiscal quarter + current/
    3. Break down the data by team member and tier.
  3. Overdue pipeline with past close date by owner:
    1. Base the widget on Open pipeline ($).
    2. Set the team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard and the date as last 30 months.
    3. Break down the data by team members (individuals).

chunks.title: Ask anything about a deal, account, or contact

chunks.text:
What interactions answers are based on:
When you ask a question about deals or accounts, Gong's AI analyzes your customer interactions in the selected period, and up to 60 calls and 500 emails, not including unrecorded meetings and automatic replies.

For questions about contacts, answers are based on conversations with the contact, drawing on up to 80 recent emails and 10 recent calls.

We filter out calls with a No Answer status, such as no voicemail, left voicemail, busy.

chunks.title: Ask anything about a deal, account, or contact

chunks.text:
How to write questions to get accurate answers:
The clearer the question is, the higher the accuracy of the answers. Here are some tips:

- Make sure you are asking a question. For example instead of writing:
  - Summarize the business pain points brought up by Acme.
  - Try: What were the business pain points brought up by Acme?
- Write specific instructions. For example instead of writing:
  - What was their main problem?
  - Try: What's their biggest pain point from a business perspective?
- Ask questions about past conversations. We search call transcripts and emails for answers to your questions using up to 10 calls and 80 emails.
- Use natural language. This helps AI to better understand your question. For example try using:
  - What's stopping Acme from moving ahead with the deal?
- Ask one question at a time. There's no limit to how many questions you can ask, and this way you'll get the most accurate answers.

Here are some examples which you can customize for your deals or accounts:

- What did the customer say about the price of our offer?
- What were Acme's main objections?
- Was specific pricing discussed?
- What does Acme prefer about our product over other products?
- What did Acme say about competitors?

Click inside the question field to see some suggested questions.

chunks.text:
FAQs:
Can I ask my question in any language?

Yes, you can ask your question in any language and the answer will be provided in the same language.

When answering a question about a deal or account, what's the answer based on?

Gong's AI analyzes your customer interactions in the selected period, and the answer is based on up to 60 calls and 500 emails, not including unrecorded meetings and automatic replies.

It doesn't take into account any information synced from CRM fields. For best results, frame your question around what's been discussed in conversations.

When answering a question about a contact, what's the answer based on?

The answer draws on up to 10 past calls and 80 past emails with that contact. For best results, frame your question around what's been discussed in those conversations.

Where can I see questions I've already asked?

Click in the question field to see a list of the 10 most recent questions you've asked about deals and accounts.

Ask anything is also available from our mobile app. Scan the QR code to download the app:

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

Gong’s AI-driven sales engagement solution that helps sales teams prioritize, personalize, and automate outreach activities to accelerate their pipelines. Access to features depends on your company’s plan and your assigned seat.

chunks.title: Placeholders FAQs

chunks.text:
What happens if I try to send an email with a missing field placeholder or manual placeholder?:
If you try to send an email with a missing placeholder, we'll warn you before sending. The same applies for auto-emails sent through flows. If there are values missing for field placeholders, the email will become a regular email step that appears on your list of to-dos for you to send manually.

Field placeholders that appear in purple are meant to populate automatically, meaning the person working on the email shouldn't have to do anything before sending. This is different from manual placeholders, which appear as text between curly brackets, intended for the person sending the email to replace before the email goes out.

If there's still text between curly brackets when you go to send an email, we'll warn you before sending.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Gong’s AI-driven sales engagement solution that helps sales teams prioritize, personalize, and automate outreach activities to accelerate their pipelines. Access to features depends on your company’s plan and your assigned seat.

A quota-carrying sales representative who manages client relationships. Reps can be Account executives (AEs) or Sales Development Representatives (SDRs).

A team member who manages a team of sales reps.

Assign seats:
Where to go: Admin center > Settings > People > Team members

The types of seats that can be assigned will depend on your organization’s plan.

- The banner at the top (1) displays the number of active team members and the Data capture capabilities that are enabled for them.
- The panel on the right (2) provides a summary of the number of seats in use per core license and application, out of the total number of seats available in your Gong contract.
- The Seats column (3) displays the application seats assigned to the team member. A purple icon indicates an active assigned seat.

2. Scroll down to Seats and switch on the required seats for the team member. You can also assign seats to multiple team members.

chunks.text:
Buy more seats > Adding seats after contract renewal:
When you renew your contract, your company will transition to Gong’s new plan model. Gong will provide as many seats as needed to maintain your current functionality for the renewal period. However, any seats added after the contract renewal must be paid for separately.

For example, suppose your previous contract included 20 Gong Pro seats, supporting 20 team members who were using Deals functionality. When you renew, Gong will provide 20 seats of the Gong Foundation core license as well as 20 seats of the Forecast Essentials application. This will ensure that you still have access to Deals features under the new model, at no additional cost. This remains the case even if you choose to increase your number of seats. For example, if you increase from 20 to 30 seats at renewal, Gong will provide the additional 10 seats for both Gong Foundation and Forecast Essentials to maintain your current functionality. However, any extra seats purchased after renewal must be paid for separately, as they were not included in the renewal transaction. So if you choose to add 10 more seats to your account one month after renewal, and you want those team members to also have full Deals functionality, you would need to purchase Gong Foundation as well as Forecast Essentials for those 10 new seats.

Which pre-built playbooks are available?:
The following playbooks are available: MEDDICC, BANT, SPIN, Challenger, SPICED, Solution Selling, and Sandler. Pick the playbook your company is already using.

How many active playbooks can I have?:
You can have as many active playbooks at a time as you want. You also can add unlimited playbooks to a deal board, although companies commonly use a single one.

You can have up to 20 elements in a playbook.

chunks.text:
What happens to data if I delete an element?:
If the element is synced with your CRM, data that’s already been synced isn’t affected. If the element hasn’t been synced, the data is removed from the playbook and can’t be restored.
chunks.body: If the element is synced with your CRM, data that’s already been synced isn’t affected. If the element hasn’t been synced, the data is removed from the playbook and can’t be restored.

What happens to the data in a playbook if I delete it?:
If you delete a playbook, data that was saved in the playbook can’t be restored. If elements were synced with your CRM, the synced data isn’t affected.

In what languages do AI notes work?:
Currently, AI notes are in English only. We’re working on support for other languages.

chunks.text:
Can I import existing data from the CRM?:
Yes. When you configure each element in a playbook, you can select a CRM field to provide synchronization for that element between Gong and your CRM.

the CRM fields that you’re already importing in Gong when creating your playbook. This is bi-directional sync where the latest updated one completes the other.

If you choose to start using your playbook without syncing any CRM field elements, data will be saved in the playbook in Gong. When you’re ready to sync with your CRM, add the CRM fields to the playbook and publish it:

- If there’s already data in Gong for these fields, it will override data in corresponding CRM fields.
- If there is no data in Gong for these fields, nothing will happen in corresponding CRM fields.

Gong will sync data from the playbook to your CRM, covering up to the past 3 months.

chunks.text:
What do the colors mean for each letter?:
White: There’s no manual note and no AI findings.

White with a star: There is no manual note but AI has suggested a note.

Light blue: A manual note was added by the rep, regardless of the AI state.

Dark blue: Either the rep or the manager (depending on your process) has confirmed that the note in the element is validated.

Light blue: A manual note was added by the rep, regardless of the AI state.

chunks.text:
How is the status of each element updated?:
The status updates according to actions that take place. For example, when Gong’s AI has suggested a note, it moves from white to white with a star.

When a manual note is added, it moves from white (or white with a star) to light blue. When a rep or manager confirms that an element is validated, it moves from light blue to dark blue.

Add Gong data to Salesforce objects > Account object:
1. Go to Setup > Object Manager > Account > Page Layouts and select Mobile & Lightning Actions in the page layout palette.
2. Drag the View Account in Gong button to the Lightning Experience Actions area.
3. Click Related Lists, select the Conversations related list, drag it to the Related Lists area in the lower pane, and click Save.
4. Click Related List properties and make sure the following fields are added in Selected Fields:
  - Conversation Title
  - Primary Account
  - Started
  - Duration (Min)
5. In the Buttons area, make sure the New and Change Owner checkboxes are not checked.

Activate new Engage flow status values - Version 2.30:
New values were added to the Gong_Current_Flow_Status__c to provide more details of the prospect status. When the new values for the flow status are first exported, they are set as inactive values for the field. This means you won’t be able to build reports or filter according to these values, although they are displayed in the object. For the list of values, see Flow statuses in your CRM.

To activate the values, go to the Lead, Contact, Task and Event objects and activate the inactive values. If some of the new values haven’t yet been added, you can add them manually. For details on how to add the picklist values, see Change Engage flow status picklist options.

chunks.text:
Display scorecards - Version 2.20:
Set up

Scorecard data, including for existing conversations is exported to Salesforce. Perform these steps to display scorecard data in Conversations records.

1. Navigate to the Salesforce Setup > Object Manager > Conversations > Page Layouts.
2. In the only available Layout add the Scorecards related list, and add the following columns: Scorecard Name, Question, Answer, Got Scored, Scored By, Note, Overall question, & Visibility.
3. Navigate to any Gong conversation record and click Edit Page in the top right corner.
4. In Page Setup, drag Related List - Single component to the Content tab and select the Scorecards related list:
5. Click Save and Activation to save this change.

Reports

You can see scorecard reports in the Conversation’s Content tab. The data includes the scorecard name, questions and all answers, and who was scored.

Drill down to see a detailed view of each scorecard, and further information such as scored by, notes, visibility (public or private), and more.

The scorecard analysis dashboard in Salesforce contains the following charts:

- Top scorers (by number of calls scored)
- Bottom scorers (by number of calls scored)
- Scorecards filled per month by manager
- Top-used scorecards
- Top people to get scored (by numbers of calls scored)
- Bottom people to get scored (by numbers of calls scored)
- People with the highest average score overall
- People with the lowest average score overall
- Average scores given over time (by manager)
- Average scores given over time (by rep)
- Scorecards used over time

You can repeat scenarios as many times as needed to refine your messaging, handle objections, and build confidence. Trainings may include lessons and practice modules–interactive simulations tailored to onboarding, new messaging, specific personas, or upcoming conversations.

Access your training:
Your enablement team or manager will assign your training, which can be accessed here:

1. Go to Coaching > My trainings.
2. You’ll see all your assigned, in progress, and completed training. You’ll be able to see the due date for your assignment.
3. Click Open training.

You’ll also receive an email as soon as a new training has been assigned, telling you that new training is ready for you. Click Lets go!

Once you open your training:

1. On the left, you’ll be able to see the number of modules you need to do before you complete your training. These include a mix of:
  1. Lesson: Text and image based learning.
  2. Practice: An AI scenario-based simulation.
2. If there is an overview of the training purpose, you'll see it first. You can then move through the modules using Next. While you can’t skip modules to get ahead, you’re able to click Back to repeat modules that you passed.

When you open a practice, you'll eventually engage in a realistic conversation with an AI customer.

Note: AI Trainer conversations can be conducted in any supported language.

chunks.text:
Complete a practice session:
1. On the right of your screen, you’ll see important areas of information.
  - Feedback. Includes:
    - Practice coach. Get immediate, conversational feedback from an AI coach, based on your completed practice session.
    - Scorecard (available only if a one was added during training setup.) Practice sessions are scored by an automatic review scorecard, and you can view all the questions here. These can be the same scorecards used for real calls, ensuring consistent and objective feedback.
  - Background. Background information provides key details about the company and contact, so you can dive straight into the scenario.
2. Before you begin, you can see how much time has been set for your practice call with the AI customer. The duration will be between 5 and 30 minutes.
3. Click Start once you're ready. The background information will show up again, click Start recording. Note:The background and scorecard is available at any time during training by clicking the side panel open with <.
4. Click Stop recording when you’re finished or want to start again.
5. If a scorecard was added, AI Trainer will now evaluate your practice session and give you both an overall score, as well as a breakdown of the main elements of the scorecard.
6. You can click Let's talk to discuss your practice session with the AI coach. Ask follow-up questions about the conversation, explore different approaches, and get guidance on how to improve future attempts. For example, you can ask: The AI coach can help you reflect on your practice and suggest ways to improve your skills for future conversations. Note:Practice coach is available after every practice session.If a scorecard is included in the scenario, both the scorecard and practice coach are available on the same results page.Feedback is private and only visible to the trainee.
  - How could I have handled an objection differently?
  - What questions could I have asked to learn more about the customer’s challenges?
  - What should I focus on in my next attempt?
7. You have the choice to Go again to complete the practice again.
8. Click Next to continue to the next module, or Finish if it’s the final module.

chunks.text:
Submit your training:
Once you’ve completed the entire training, Click Finish to see your score for all the practice elements.

You can now either:

- Click Back to training to try practice sessions again. You’ll be able to try them out as many times as you like before submitting your results to your manager.
- Click Submit training. The designated recipient will now be notified that you’ve completed the training. After you click Submit training, you can return to the completed course and re-enter the training page to redo any practice sessions. You can resubmit your score at any time — only the most recent score will appear on the assignment page, and resubmitting will trigger a new notification email to your manager.

Note: If you don’t click Submit training, your progress will be saved for up to 90 days so you can return and finish later. After 90 days of inactivity, the training will reset and any progress will be cleared.

chunks.text:
Tips for effective practice:
- Minimize background noise: Practice must be done in a quiet place. If there is background noise it will effect the AI experience.
- Practice sessions are private: Your practice attempts are only visible to you until you submit a final recording. This gives you the personal space to make mistakes and learn without pressure. Here are some tips to help you:
- Treat it like a real call: Engage authentically with the AI as if it were an actual customer The more realistic your practice, the more effective your learning.
- Practice multiple times: Your first attempt might not be your best. Use AI Trainer's unlimited practice to refine your approach, try different techniques, and build confidence.
- Focus on feedback: Review your scorecard results carefully after each session, and identify specific areas to improve before practicing again.
- Track your improvement: Compare your scores across multiple attempts to see your progress and celebrate your growth.

Who can use this: Any team memberAvailable on: Gong EngageIdeal for: Sales rep, Sales manager

Here are some ways you can use Engage to find the right people to reach out to, ensure you have the right contact details you need to engage with them, and update CRM information from directly within Gong.
chunks.title: Prepare contacts for engagement

chunks.text:
Explore the People page:
In People, you can view, manage, and reach out to all your contacts and leads directly from Gong. This page contains all contacts and leads your company works with. If they’re in your CRM, whether they're internal or external, they'll appear on the page. At the top, you can toggle between contacts and leads, and search for people based on their name, title, or company. Hover over someone's name to see details such as email address, phone number, and more.

Customize your view

Click Manage columns in the top right corner to add, remove, and reorganize columns to define what type of information you want to see here. You automatically have several columns defined by Gong, and can add any column based on fields in your CRM.

Filter the list of people

With advanced filtering for all CRM field types, you can use filters to see only the people that match certain criteria. You can filter by any account CRM fields that are imported to Gong, including filtering by CRM campaign object. If you don't see the CRM field you need, reach out to your admin to import it.

Contacts can be filtered by both contact fields and account fields, while leads can only be filtered by lead fields. For reps engaging with leads originating from a campaign, you can filter by the CRM campaign object filter. To do this, add the “Campaign name” filter, select a campaign name to filter by, and then you'll see all leads or contacts that are part of that campaign. If you don't see the CRM field you need, reach out to your admin to import it.

Explore the People page:
If you don't see the CRM field you need, reach out to your admin to import it.

To filter by Lead assignee or Account assignee, click Add filter and select Lead assignee or Account assignee, and then select the person whose contacts or leads you want to see. If you want to see only your contacts or leads, select your name as the field value.

The Account assignee filter shows contacts under accounts the team member is assigned to. When looking at leads, the Lead assignee filter shows leads the team member is assigned to. Both contacts and leads are sorted by last modified/created by default, so you'll see people who were newly added to the CRM first. You can also adjust the filter to see people assigned to another team member or members.

You can choose multiple fields to filter by. We'll keep them for you until you clear them, so that even if you leave this page, the filters you chose will still be there when you come back.

Filter contacts and leads by flow fields

Filter contacts and leads according to flow status. For example, filter by people actively in a flow, people not in a flow, people in a specific flow/step, and more.

To do this, click Add filter and search for a field, such as 'Current flow ID'.

For example, let's say you want to see leads that are not currently in flows. Select Leads at the top left and then click Add filter and select Currently in Engage flow.

chunks.headingPath: View and add contact details in person view
chunks.title: Prepare contacts for engagement

chunks.text:
View and add contact details in person view:
- View their LinkedIn Sales Navigator profile: Click on the compass icon to see their LinkedIn Sales Navigator profile directly in Gong.
- Ask anything about the contact: Get answers based on the content in the last 80 calls and 10 emails with the contact.
- View the person in your CRM: If they're not in your CRM, a message appears when hovering the cloud icon. Once added to a flow, the person will be added to your CRM automatically, and you can open their profile in your CRM directly by clicking on the cloud icon.
- See their address and time zone: Knowing where someone is located not only helps break the ice, but it also helps you avoid calling during someone's non-working hours. Engage calculates and displays local time zone based on the person's address in your CRM.
- Quick call or email: While gathering information about someone, you can send an email or make a call right away.
- See recent activity with the person: From the Overview tab, see whether you or your teammates have interacted with the person, including dialer calls. To see their full activity timeline, go to the Activity tab.
- See their flow status and flow history: If the person is currently in a flow or paused, they’ll have a badge next to their name. The badge shows how many flows they are in. Hover the badge to see the names of the flows. If the person is in multiple flows but some are paused, the number reflects the active flows. The badge is green if any flows are active, or yellow if all flows are paused. To see whether the person was ever in a flow and get a comprehensive, chronological view of their flow events, click and click View flow history. You can use flow history for key details such as the reason why an automatic email failed to send, why someone’s flow status changed, why a flow stopped or started, and more.
- Update contact information: As you get new information about people, you can edit, add, and remove phone numbers and email addresses to keep their contact information up to date. If you see numbers and emails that are in person view in Gong and are not pushed to your CRM, this may be because you've added more numbers and emails than your admin has defined in your company's settings. Additional phone numbers can also be added automatically from contacts' email signatures in emails that Gong ingests. If you don't have permission to edit contact information and you think you should, talk to your admin. Gong understands what country a phone number in the CRM belongs to using the following logic:If the number starts with +, we try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.If not, see if the contact has an address. If we know the country, try adding that country's prefix and see if the result is a valid number.If not, try adding the US prefix and see if the result is a valid number.If not, add + at the beginning, try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.If not, leave it as is.
  - If the number starts with +, we try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, see if the contact has an address. If we know the country, try adding that country's prefix and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, try adding the US prefix and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, add + at the beginning, try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, leave it as is.
- Mark phone numbers and email addresses as verified or invalid: Next time you or your teammates want to reach out to this person, you'll know right away which is the best number or email address to use. To mark as verified or invalid, go to the Contact details section under Overview, hover over the number or email and click . If you you mark the top email address on a contact or lead record as invalid, Gong moves that address to the bottom of that person’s saved email address list. This is not currently synced to your CRM.
- Mark someone as do not contact: Click on the far right of the top section and select Mark as do not contact. Learn more about what happens when you mark someone as do not contact
- Create and view notes about the person: In the Notes section, see notes your teammates have left about the contact or lead, or add and edit your own. Notes are not currently synced to your CRM
- See all to-dos related to them: See any to-dos owned by the current user and others that are related to the contact or lead, including auto emails, in the To-dos section. You can also mark to-dos as complete from here.
- View, update, and add/remove CRM fields: By default, you’ll see the CRM fields that your tech admin has configured for you and your team. The ability to create a personal configuration of CRM fields that overrides the default is based on your permissions. If you don't have it and think you should, contact your tech admin. Make sure you're logged in to your CRM to view and edit the values of CRM fields in Engage. Adding, and removing CRM fields only affects what you see, not what your teammates see. If you add or remove fields for a contact, that new list of fields will be shown for other contacts as well. If you work with leads and you add or remove fields for a lead, the new list of fields will be shown for other leads. If the CRM section is in read-only mode, you don't have the necessary permissions to update CRM fields. If you think you should, contact your admin.

- Ask anything about the contact: Get answers based on the content in the last 80 calls and 10 emails with the contact.
- View the person in your CRM: If they're not in your CRM, a message appears when hovering the cloud icon. Once added to a flow, the person will be added to your CRM automatically, and you can open their profile in your CRM directly by clicking on the cloud icon.
- See their address and time zone: Knowing where someone is located not only helps break the ice, but it also helps you avoid calling during someone's non-working hours. Engage calculates and displays local time zone based on the person's address in your CRM.
- Quick call or email: While gathering information about someone, you can send an email or make a call right away.
- See recent activity with the person: From the Overview tab, see whether you or your teammates have interacted with the person, including dialer calls. To see their full activity timeline, go to the Activity tab.
- See their flow status and flow history: If the person is currently in a flow or paused, they’ll have a badge next to their name. The badge shows how many flows they are in. Hover the badge to see the names of the flows. If the person is in multiple flows but some are paused, the number reflects the active flows. The badge is green if any flows are active, or yellow if all flows are paused. To see whether the person was ever in a flow and get a comprehensive, chronological view of their flow events, click and click View flow history. You can use flow history for key details such as the reason why an automatic email failed to send, why someone’s flow status changed, why a flow stopped or started, and more.
- Update contact information: As you get new information about people, you can edit, add, and remove phone numbers and email addresses to keep their contact information up to date. If you see numbers and emails that are in person view in Gong and are not pushed to your CRM, this may be because you've added more numbers and emails than your admin has defined in your company's settings. Additional phone numbers can also be added automatically from contacts' email signatures in emails that Gong ingests. If you don't have permission to edit contact information and you think you should, talk to your admin. Gong understands what country a phone number in the CRM belongs to using the following logic:If the number starts with +, we try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.If not, see if the contact has an address. If we know the country, try adding that country's prefix and see if the result is a valid number.If not, try adding the US prefix and see if the result is a valid number.If not, add + at the beginning, try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.If not, leave it as is.
  - If the number starts with +, we try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, see if the contact has an address. If we know the country, try adding that country's prefix and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, try adding the US prefix and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, add + at the beginning, try to parse it and see if the result is a valid number.
  - If not, leave it as is.
- Mark phone numbers and email addresses as verified or invalid: Next time you or your teammates want to reach out to this person, you'll know right away which is the best number or email address to use. To mark as verified or invalid, go to the Contact details section under Overview, hover over the number or email and click . If you you mark the top email address on a contact or lead record as invalid, Gong moves that address to the bottom of that person’s saved email address list. This is not currently synced to your CRM.
- Mark someone as do not contact: Click on the far right of the top section and select Mark as do not contact. Learn more about what happens when you mark someone as do not contact
- Create and view notes about the person: In the Notes section, see notes your teammates have left about the contact or lead, or add and edit your own. Notes are not currently synced to your CRM
- See all to-dos related to them: See any to-dos owned by the current user and others that are related to the contact or lead, including auto emails, in the To-dos section. You can also mark to-dos as complete from here.
- View, update, and add/remove CRM fields: By default, you’ll see the CRM fields that your tech admin has configured for you and your team. The ability to create a personal configuration of CRM fields that overrides the default is based on your permissions. If you don't have it and think you should, contact your tech admin. Make sure you're logged in to your CRM to view and edit the values of CRM fields in Engage. Adding, and removing CRM fields only affects what you see, not what your teammates see. If you add or remove fields for a contact, that new list of fields will be shown for other contacts as well. If you work with leads and you add or remove fields for a lead, the new list of fields will be shown for other leads. If the CRM section is in read-only mode, you don't have the necessary permissions to update CRM fields. If you think you should, contact your admin.

chunks.text:
Python:
```python
import SimpleHTTPServer
import SocketServer
import jwt
import hashlib

PORT = 7080

PUBLIC_KEY = "\n".join(['-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----', '', '-----END PUBLIC KEY-----'])

class MySimpleHTTPRequestHandler(SimpleHTTPServer.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):

        def do_POST(self):
            data_string = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length']))
            decoded_jwt = jwt.decode(str(self.headers['Authorization']), PUBLIC_KEY, algorithms=['RS256'])
            m = hashlib.sha256()
            m.update(data_string)
            assert m.hexdigest() == decoded_jwt['body_sha256'], "Request body sha256 isn't equal to sha256 from jwt payload"

            self.end_headers()

httpd = SocketServer.TCPServer(("", PORT), MySimpleHTTPRequestHandler)
httpd.serve_forever()
```

Who can use this: Any team memberAvailable on: Any Gong plan

In some cases, you may want to prevent Gong from recording a call, or stop a recording after it's already started. Your tech admins can set up lists of domains and terms that automatically exclude the call from being recorded. Here are ways you can prevent or stop a recording.
chunks.title: Prevent or stop a recording

chunks.text:
Prevent web conference recordings:
Gong records all calls that match your company's recording criteria by automatically joining as a participant. Unless your call is set up for native recording, the Gong bot appears in the call’s attendee list.

You can see upcoming calls scheduled for recording in the Conversations section on the homepage, and in the Activity calendar. Find the call you don't want to record and do one of the following:

- Set call as private in your calendar. This prevents Gong from having access to the call data. If you change a call's visibility to private after it's been scheduled, do so at least 2 hours in advance to make sure Gong doesn't record it.
- Deny entry to Gong recorder. Use the meeting waiting room feature to deny entry to the Gong recorder.
- Cancel the recording from inside Gong. In the homepage, in the Conversations section, click View upcoming calls to open a panel on the right. Hover the call you don’t want recorded, click, and choose Cancel recording. This must be done at least 1 hour in advance. If the meeting is part of a series, you can cancel recording for just one meeting, or for the entire series.

Prevent telephony recordings:
When you're set up with a telephony system integration, Gong imports all recorded calls. If you don't want to record a particular call, make the call using a telephony system that's not set up with Gong.

chunks.text:
Stop recording while the call is taking place:
Hosts, any team member invited to a call, as well as tech admins can stop live recordings from the Gong homepage or the call. This provides team members full control over meeting recordings, even if they're not the host. You can cancel the recording for a single call or recurring calls in a meeting series. If the call is recorded with native Zoom, the host can start recording again using native Zoom controls.

To stop recording from the homepage, select an on air call and select Stop recording.

To stop recording from a call, open an on air call, click , and select Stop recording.

Primary email address:
A primary email address generally shares the same domain as your company and is used to log into Gong. For example jennifer.juniper@acme.com is employed by company Acme with the same domain: www.acme.com.

When a user participates in a call using their primary email address, it helps Gong to:

- Identify the user
- Identify the user’s company
- Determine if a meeting is internal or external
- Determine whether to record a meeting

Additional email address:
In some cases, a team member may have more than one email address, or they may have set up an alias for their primary email. You can list any additional email addresses in the Additional email addresses field. When a user's profile contains additional email addresses, Gong maps those addresses to the user's primary email address. When the team member joins a meeting with one of their additional email addresses, Gong can identify the team member and determine if the meeting is external or internal.

Note:Gong imports emails, calendar meetings, and calls from one mailbox. This is the mailbox of the email address used to connect to the email provider. Emails sent to other mailboxes aren’t imported to Gong. Additional email addresses are used to identify the team member.Gong does not support sending emails from an email alias.

- User-by-user: connection is set up by the Tech admin but each team member has to connect to their mailbox individually

To send emails via Gong using the Gong email composer each user must set up the relevant connection in their company settings. This is regardless of whether emails are imported company wide or user-by-user.

chunks.text:
See the accounts that are relevant to you:
Accounts is your go-to place for viewing all information about the accounts you want to see, including contacts, activity, to-dos, and more. Click an account name from the panel on the left to open up its details.

To filter by Account assignee, click Show filters and click on the Account assignee filter, then select the person whose accounts you want to see. If you want to see only your accounts, select your name as the field value.

Since accounts are shown based on CRM assignment as set up by your admin, multiple teammates might see the same account. If you aren't seeing accounts and you think you should be, talk to your admin. Note that you may see accounts based on fields other than ownership, according to your admin setup. For example, you might have 100 accounts assigned to you, in 80 of which you’re the account owner and the other 20 you’re the Sales Development Representative.

You automatically have several columns defined by Gong, and can add any column based on fields in your CRM.
- Get more context on a contact: Click on a person's name to open a panel with information relating to that contact. You can enter a question that relates to interactions with that contact, and using Gong’s AI, we’ll give you an answer based on the past 80 calls and 10 emails.

Save time with AI summaries:
As a part of reviewing account activity, you might find it helpful to review calls quickly with AI summaries, visible when you open any outbound call. It includes:

- Basic call info: This includes date, length of call and participants.
- Outcome: Was a meeting booked? Should you follow up soon? Did you reach the wrong person? See this info right away, so you know how the call ended.
- Next step: Did the call end with an action item? Could be something like “Send an email with meeting details” or “Follow up in 4 months”. If there are no next steps, you'll see "No further action".
- Call brief: Click this tab to see a short summary of the call.
- Prospect highlights: This includes anything the prospect said that may be helpful for follow up. For example, if they mentioned that someone is on holiday or if there have been layoffs recently.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Where to go: Admin center > Settings > People > Team Member Provisioning

This article is a technical guide intended for people who want to develop their own provisioning source to use with Gong. Automatic provisioning is supported from these sources.

This article explains how to set up automatic provisioning by creating an integration with Gong and your IDP using standard OAuth and SCIM protocols.

This article is intended for tech admins with engineering capabilities who would like to automatically provision people from their identity provider.

Automatic provisioning with SCIM is also supported by connecting to identity providers that support SCIM, such as Okta and Rippling. For more info, see Provisioning team members.

When setting up provisioning, ensure team members have the necessary Gong seat. Features that require seats won't be available until seats are assigned.

Supported features:
- Provision new users: New users created in the custom source will also be provisioned in Gong. See Create a user, below.
- Provision user updates: Updates made to the user's profile in the custom source will be pushed to Gong. See Update a user, below.
- Provision user deactivation: Deactivating the user or disabling the user's access to Gong through the custom source will deactivate the user in Gong. See Deactivate a user, below.

chunks.text:
Configure the custom source in Gong:
Follow these steps to enable automatic provisioning from a generic SCIM source:

1. Go to Admin center > Settings > People > Team Member Provisioning.
2. Select Custom as the provisioning source.
3. A default assignment is set up where team members imported with this assignment are not assigned any seats, data capture capabilities or permissions. You can edit this or set up assignments for different teams.
4. Generate an OAuth bearer token to send with each SCIM provisioning request. See Generate the OAuth bearer token, below. When you have the bearer token, you can send SCIM provisioning requests.
5. Send the required SCIM provisioning requests. See Supported features, above, and the Sample requests, below.

chunks.text:
About SCIM:
SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) specification, is an open standard designed to manage user identity information.

SCIM defines a number of HTTP endpoints that handle requests containing data formatted in JSON.

Gong's base SCIM URL is provisioning.gong.io

For more guidance, check these SCIM references:

- http://www.simplecloud.info
- https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7644

Create automatic assignments in Gong:
1. In Gong, go to Admin center > Settings > PEOPLE > Team Member Provisioning.
2. Create an assignment to assign data capture, workspace, and permission settings:
  1. In the Assign settings area, click ADD ASSIGNMENT.
  2. Give the assignment a name.
  3. In the custom SCIM source groups area, select the group you want to define the settings for.
  4. Select the Gong seats you want team members in this group to have assigned to them. NoteEnsure you assign the Gong seats required for the permissions and other settings included in the assignment.
  5. In the Workspaces and permissions area, set the permissions profile for each workspace in your organization.
  6. In the Data capture area, select which data should be captured and imported to Gong. For details see About managing team members.
  7. In the Update settings area, define how settings can be managed for this assignment:
    - Select Manual editing to manage data capture and permission settings for users in this assignment in Gong. After you create the assignment: if you make changes to group settings in Okta, they will not be pushed to Gong. However, you can edit the group settings manually in Gong.
    - Select Automatic updates to give Okta governance over data capture and permission settings in Gong. Define data capture and permission settings in Gong only when creating an assignment. Thereafter, other changes will only be applied to users in groups with this assignment when pushed from Okta.
  8. Click ADD ASSIGNMENT.
3. Click SAVE.

Bottom-up forecasting for the whole org:
Once you've set up your forecast methodology as a top-down motion, Gong Forecast also supports you bottom-up, allowing reps to update their forecast number and add notes across all forecasting categories used by your business. In turn, leaders can see their reps' forecasts in one place, and update their own, eradicating the need for labor-intensive and misaligned processes, steering away from opinion-based forecasts.

- Roll up reps and sales leaders' forecasts in one place
- Get timely reminders and forecast update status
- Forecast with greater confidence and accuracy

chunks.title: Recipe: Coach reps for maximum deal performance

chunks.text:
- Does the rep have a timely next step set for every open opportunity?
- Are they responding promptly to customer emails?
- Are they engaging enough contacts on each account to create broad influence and reduce risk?
- Do they consistently bring in the right titles for the deal size, stage, and segment, and do they keep them engaged throughout the process?
- How have they handled the most recent email sequence or call? Would you have handled it differently?

Step 3: If you’re focused on a particular development area for your team or an individual rep, pay more attention to activities related to that area. For example, if you want to reinforce the use of upfront contracts, check how the rep is setting the agenda and purpose of next steps.

TipCalls shown on the Account console include a list of topics discussed, allowing you to jump straight to the topic of interest.

Step 4: Tag the rep in comments on the account to provide immediate tactical guidance. For coaching on broader behaviors, collect a few examples to discuss in your next 1:1. Use comments to add reminders of what you want to cover in the discussion. Make the comments visible only to the rep if the topic is sensitive, or private if you’d rather address the issue face-to-face. Ask the rep to come to the 1:1 prepared to reflect on and discuss the focus area. In addition, encourage them to choose their own focus area to bring to the meeting. Have them share the real customer examples they’d like to work through by tagging you in comments, so that you can prepare ahead of time.

Who can use this: Any team memberAvailable on: Gong ForecastIdeal for: Sales manager

Outcome: This recipe helps you quickly achieve high confidence that your forecast to management contains only deals that are on track to close

Frequency: Weekly or monthly, depending on your forecasting cadence
chunks.title: Recipe: Cross check your team's forecast

chunks.text:
Your steps:
Step 1: Ensure your team has updated their opportunity stages and forecast status with enough time for you to cross check before sending your forecast rollup. Go to the Gong deal board and filter to see the deals for everyone in your team for the relevant time period (e.g. deals closing this quarter, or this month). You can declutter the view by showing only open deals. The deal count and total amount at the top of the page should stack up with your expectations.

Step 2: Sort the opportunity list by account name, amount, or stage to home in on the deals that will make or break your forecast. You’ll likely apply more scrutiny to the opportunities being forecast by more junior or less tenured reps, so use the filter to view an individual rep’s pipeline.

Tip: If you need to make a last minute check while on-the-go, you can review your Deal Board on the Gong mobile app.

Step 3: For deals in your committed or upside forecast, look for evidence that they are on track to close:

- Is there enough bi-directional activity—not just rep outreach—to indicate healthy engagement?
- Are next calls scheduled soon enough to maintain deal velocity?
- Are there any Gong deal warnings?

Step 4: Go deeper on key deals. Click into the deal to see a detailed view of the communication back-and-forth on the the Account page:

- Open the engagement map from the account timeline. Is there a healthy level of multi-threading?
- Do you have the right titles engaged to close the deal? Are they active in conversations, rather than passive?
- Review the latest emails and calls exchanged with key contacts. Is the back-and-forth consistent with a deal that’s on track or one that’s going to push?

Step 2 - Take a pulse check:
In this step, review these key data points on all deals in your deal board to identify where you need to explore.

- Check activity: activity is a good sign of deal health. Sort the list by activity. Look for bidirectional activity, not just rep outreach.
- Check activity for stage: Sort the list by stage to check the level of activity looks right for the deal stage.
- Check next calls: Check whether a next call is scheduled, and if so, whether it's soon enough to maintain deal velocity.
- Check warnings: Check what Gong-AI warnings are showing you about the deals

Tip:If you're subscribed to the board, check your inbox for a weekly deal digest email to get an understanding of what's happening in your pipeline.

Step 3 - Drill into particular deals:
Once you’ve short-listed deals to look at, take a more detailed approach.

1. Click the deal activity area on the board, and in the deal panel Activity tab, check whether there's evidence of multi-threading.
2. Review the latest emails and calls with key contacts. Verify that the back-and-forth is consistent with a deal that’s on track.
3. In the Contacts tab, check whether the right titles are engaged, given the deal stage, and whether those people are active in conversations

The more critical the deal, the deeper you’ll likely go in investigating the deal.

Where to go: Revenue > Analytics

Follow this recipe to learn how to investigate 'blips' in your pipeline and forecast by simply looking in Gong. This recipe has 3 steps.
chunks.title: Recipe: Investigate pipeline and forecast fluctuations

chunks.text:
1. In the Analytics > Trends report, look for large blips which indicate something going awry. For example, here we can see that we doubled the amount of deals in Commit around January/February, which then disappear in the middle of February: In other words, there were a lot of deals in pipeline that didn't get booked. The pipeline size doubled by $200K, and then it disappeared. You'll want to investigate those deals that slipped.
2. Go to the Analytics > Changes report, and filter the time range to look at the same 'blip' here. In our example, we can see that indeed there were a lot of deals (over $1M) that were pushed out:
3. Triage the deals that caused the 'blip'.
  1. Filter the Changes report to just Commit deals in order to focus on the most critical deals at that time. In our example, we can see that 4 deals were pushed out of Commit.
  2. Scroll down to look at those 4 deals at a high-level. In our example, we can see: So, you'll want to take a closer look at the Aventine and Indis deals.
    - All 4 deals had changes to their close date, explaining the change
    - The Aventine deal has a warning on it, and not a lot of activity
    - The Indis deal is the biggest ($80k) but is still in Validation
  3. Click the deal name to review the deal from within the Changes report. Use "Ask anything" to answer your questions about the deals and review each deal's activity in order to reach a decision on how to best handle those deals.
    - Do you want to stop wasting time and kill one or both of those deals?
    - Or do you want to let those deals ride out because they are legit? Should you rethink the strategy on them?

chunks.title: Record and drop voicemail messages

chunks.text:
Record a voicemail message:
Record voicemail messages in the My settings page. Each recording is saved to your personal list and can be selected when leaving a voicemail during a call.

To record a voicemail message:

1. In the top toolbar, click the quick access settings (your initials) icon and select My settings.
2. Under Gong Connect, click Manage your voicemails.
3. Click + Record new voicemail.
4. Enter a name for the voicemail message and click Record a voicemail.
5. Once you’ve finished recording, click Play to review the recording.
6. Click Save if you are happy with the voicemail, or Delete to start again.

The voicemail message is added to your list of saved recordings.

chunks.text:
Manage voicemail messages:
You can update, remove, or reorganize saved voicemail messages from Manage Voicemail Recordings.

To manage a voicemail message:

1. In the top toolbar, click the quick access settings (your initials) icon and select My settings.
2. Under Gong Connect, click Manage your voicemails.
3. Choose what you want to do:
  - Edit a voicemail message: Click Edit , to update the recording, and save your changes.
  - Delete a voicemail message: Click Delete to remove the recording.
  - Reorder voicemail messages: Move the recording to a new position in the list. Note: The order of voicemail messages determines the order in which they appear when selecting a voicemail message during a call.

chunks.text:
Drop a voicemail message during a call:
When a call reaches voicemail, you can leave a saved voicemail message instead of recording the message live.

Note: Wait until you hear the voicemail tone or beep before dropping a voicemail message.

To drop a voicemail message:

1. Place a call using the Gong Dialer.
2. If there’s no answer, wait for the voicemail tone or beep.
3. Select Voicemail drop icon to see the list of recorded voicemail messages.
4. Select the voicemail message you want to leave.

The selected voicemail message is played to the recipient's voicemail.

chunks.title: Record meetings on mobile

chunks.text:
Record scheduled meetings:
To record scheduled meetings using the Gong app, make sure:

- Your phone's native calendar app (not the Google or Outlook calendar app) grants full access to the Gong app.
- Your phone's native calendar app is synced with the Google or Outlook calendar that you use with Gong.

If you've met these prerequisites, you're good to go. Here's how:

1. Open the Gong app and tap at the top right. You'll see a calendar icon with the name of scheduled meetings within the next 2 hours.
2. Tap RECORD to associate the recording with a specific meeting. (You can also tap SKIP, in which case you'll record, but the recording won't be associated with the meeting.)
3. Tap to start recording, to pause it, and to resume recording.
4. When you're finished, tap to stop the recording. Give the recording a name and then tap Save. The recording is uploaded to Gong, analyzed and transcribed.

Gong offers two data redaction features to automatically permanently remove certain sensitive data from both call recordings processed by Gong and the resulting transcripts, specifically: (1) numeric redaction and (2) PHI redaction.

When redaction is enabled, Gong replaces certain text within a transcript with (REDACTED) and mutes the corresponding section in the audio. Once enabled, redaction applies to new calls and their transcripts. To apply it retroactively, contact Gong Support.

ImportantGong needs to process your call recording in order to redact the audio and resulting transcript. Redacted data is not stored in Gong and can’t be recovered, not even by Gong. Once set, redaction applies to new calls.

chunks.text:
Numeric redaction:
Numeric redaction removes single digits and sequences of digits from your calls and their related transcripts.

Numeric redaction:

- Can be turned on and off by your company Gong admin.
- Doesn’t redact the spoken words “thousand”, “million”, or “billion”.
- Your admin can select the number of digits in a sequence to be targeted for redaction. When enabled, numbers that meet or exceed that threshold are redacted. For example, if you set the threshold to 4 digits:

- The number 156 will not be redacted (3 digits, so below the threshold)
- The number 1564 will be redacted (4 digits, so meets the threshold)

See more numeric redaction examples

The tables below show how calls will be transcribed and what the audio will sound like when data redaction has been configured to sequences of 1, 2, 3 or 4 digits.

No redaction

| Said in the call | Written in the transcript | Heard in the recording |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "one two three four” | "one two three four" | "one two three four" |
| “one five” | “one five” | "one five" |
| “fifteen” | “fifteen” | "fifteen" |
| “fifteen hundred” | “fifteen hundred” | "fifteen hundred" |
| “fifteen thousand” | “fifteen thousand” | "fifteen thousand" |
| “one thousand five hundred” | “one thousand five hundred” | "one thousand five hundred" |
| “fifteen million” | “fifteen million” | "fifteen million" |

Redaction set to 1 digit or more

chunks.text:
PHI redaction:
PHI redaction removes personal identifiers such as names, dates, email addresses, professions, and street addresses from calls and their transcripts. It’s designed for organizations in regulated industries such as healthcare services.

PHI redaction:

- Can only be enabled by Gong, upon request.
- Applies to recorded calls process by Gong and the resulting transcripts
- Currently, only available for English-language calls.

Potential impact of redaction on AI insights:Turning on PHI redaction, may affect AI-generated insights like briefs, summaries, and tracker detections. Because PHI redaction removes parts of the audio and transcript, this may affect your use of certain Gong features that rely on those transcripts, such as call summaries, call briefs, call tracker detections, and other analytics provided by Gong.

chunks.text:
Step 1: Create a Limited User in Redshift:
1. Connect to Redshift using the SQL client.
2. Execute the following query to create a user to write the data.

```
CREATE USER <username> PASSWORD DISABLE;
```

1. Grant user CREATE and TEMPORARY privileges on the database. CREATE allows the service to create new schemas and TEMPORARY allows the service to create temporary tables.

```
GRANT CREATE, TEMPORARY ON DATABASE <database> TO <username>;
```

📘 The schema will be created during the first sync The schema name supplied as part of Step 4 will be created during the first connection. It does not need to be created manually in the destination ahead of time.

📘 If the schema already exists By default, the service creates a new schema based on the destination configuration. If you prefer to create the schema yourself before connecting the destination, you must ensure that the writer user has the proper permissions on the schema, using: GRANT ALL ON schema <schema> TO <username>;` Once you've provided the GRANT ALL permission on the schema, you can safely remove the CREATE permission on the database (but you must retain the TEMPORARY permission on the database).

How filters affect Gong Assistant responses:
On the Search page, Gong Assistant uses the conversations included in the current search results.

Each response is tied to the filters that were active when you asked the question.

If you change the filters:

- New questions use the updated search results.
- Earlier responses remain tied to the previous search results.

This allows you to compare different sets of conversations without losing earlier analyses.

July 2026:
The following changes were released and may require changes to your Admin center settings:

Improved sync settings for Microsoft Dynamics

Changing MS Dynamics CRM settings, such as importing a new field is now done via asynchronous backfill. New data continues to be synced in real time and isn’t affected by changes to the CRM settings.

New scorecard permission

A new View all answered scorecards permission has been added to the permission profiles. Team members with this permission will be able to view answered scorecards regardless of the scorecards Visibility on call page setting. By default, this setting is off for existing permission profiles. This can be useful for teams who assess the effectiveness of a scorecard, or use scorecards to assess and improve performance. Learn more

New settings in activity association

You can now set CRM fields to be used for associating contacts and leads with Gong activities. Learn more

New metrics in the Utilization report

The utilization report now includes metrics on Gong Assistant and meeting prep usage. Learn more

Gong for Salesforce creates topic and tracker records in the context of each Gong Conversation in Salesforce. Reduce Gong for Salesforce's data storage consumption by deleting empty tracker and topic records, i.e. those that contain either no duration (topics) or no occurrences (trackers).

There are two ways to remove the records: through Salesforce Developer Console, or using Salesforce Data Loader (or similar tools).
chunks.body:
Gong for Salesforce creates topic and tracker records in the context of each Gong Conversation in Salesforce. Reduce Gong for Salesforce's data storage consumption by deleting empty tracker and topic records, i.e. those that contain either no duration (topics) or no occurrences (trackers).

There are two ways to remove the records: through Salesforce Developer Console, or using Salesforce Data Loader (or similar tools).
chunks.title: Remove empty tracker and topic records

chunks.text:
Remove empty tracker and topic records via Salesforce Developer Console:
1. Go to the Salesforce Developer Console > Query tab.
2. To identify all the topic records that have the Topic Duration (Sec.) equal 0, type: SELECT Id FROM Gong__Topic__c WHERE Gong__Topic_Duration_Sec__c = 0
3. Press RETURN.
4. Select all the IDs and click Delete Row.
5. To identify all the tracker records where Tracker Occurrences equal 0, type: SELECT Id FROM Gong__Tracker__c WHERE Gong__Tracker_Occurrences__c=0
6. Press RETURN.
7. Select all the IDs and click Delete Row.

chunks.title: Remove empty tracker and topic records

chunks.text:
Remove empty tracker and topic records via Salesforce Data Loader:
1. Login to Dataloader and click Export.
2. Select the Topic object: Topic (Gong_Topic_c)
3. Set the generated query fields to: Select Id FROM Gong__Topic__c WHERE Gong__Topic_Duration_Sec__c = 0
4. Click Finish. A .csv file is created containing all the record IDs of empty topics that can be deleted.
5. Click Delete.
6. Select the Topic object and the .csv file you just created.
7. Click Next and then OK in the field mapping step.
8. Click Create or Edit a Map, and select Auto-Match Fields to Columns to match the ID column with the Id field.
9. Click OK.
10. Click Next and then click Finish.
11. Click Yes to confirm the deletion.
12. Repeat these steps for empty trackers using the following query: Select Id FROM Gong__Tracker__c WHERE Gong__Tracker_Occurrences__c = 0

chunks.text:
How to build it:
1. Build 6 KPI widgets:
  1. Booking attainment:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - Bookings ($), measured against its target - Bookings.
    2. Set the date (close date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Filter deals by record type - New business or Upsell.
  2. Coverage:
    1. Base the widget on side-by-side metrics: Coverage (#) and Open Pipeline ($).
    2. Set the date and team member to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Filter deals by record type - New business.
  3. Gap to target:
    1. Base the widget on a single formula metric - Gap to target ($).
    2. Set the date and team member to be taken from the dashboard.
    3. Filter deals by record type - New business or Upsell.
  4. Pipeline created
    1. Base the widget on side-by-side metrics: Pipeline created ($) and Pipeline created - AE ($).
    2. Set the date (close date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
  5. Win rate
    1. Based the widget on side-by-side metrics: Win rate ($) and Win rate (#).
    2. Set the date and team member to be taken from the dashboard.
  6. ASP:
    1. Base the widget on a single metric - ASP ($).
    2. Set the date (close date) and team member (owner) to be taken from the dashboard.
2. Build 5 custom charts:
  1. Booking performance over time:
    1. Base the widget on Booking ($).
    2. Filter deals by period - last 4 fiscal Qs and the current fiscal Q, and by record type - New business or Upsell.
    3. Break down the data by created date (fiscal quarters).
  2. Pipeline created performance over time:
    1. Base the widget on Pipeline created - AE ($).
    2. Filter deals by period - last 4 fiscal Qs and the current fiscal Q, and by record type - New business or Upsell.
    3. Break down the data by Created date (fiscal Qs) and by Deal status.
  3. Win rate performance over time
    1. Base the widget on Win rate ($).
    2. Filter deals by period - last 4 fiscal Qs and the current fiscal Q, and by record type - New business or Upsell.
    3. Break down the data by Created date (fiscal Qs).
  4. Average sales price performance over time
    1. Base the widget on ASP ($).
    2. Filter deals by period - last 4 fiscal Qs and the current fiscal Q.
    3. Break down the data by Created date (fiscal quarters).
  5. Lost deals by reason

If you're getting notifications on comments in Slack, you can reply to them directly in Slack, and they'll be synced into Gong.

What you need to know:

- Learn how to turn Slack notifications on and off
- Learn about notifications

What you can do in Slack:

- Reply to comment notifications in thread
  - Do: Enter a text comment, include links, tag Gong users, use your Gong hashtags* * When using hashtags, Slack offers you a list of Slack channels. Use the full Gong hashtag for it to be picked up in Gong when your comment is synced.
  - Don't:
    - Reply with gifs, images, or files - we can't show them in Gong
    - Put an emoji on the comment - we can't show that in Gong
- Edit your reply
- Delete your reply

Your replies, edits, and deletes are immediately synced to Gong, and vice versa.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

Where to find Gong reports > Out-of-the-box reports::
- $ pipeline impacted by Economic Pulse: Shows the total dollar value of opportunities where Gong’s Economic Pulse tracker comes up in conversations
- $ pipeline impacted by competitive Opps: Shows the total dollar value of open opportunities where competitors were mentioned in conversations
- $ value of won Opps with competition: Shows the total dollar value of won opportunities where competitors were mentioned
- Closing Opps w/o their VP participation: Lists Opportunities due to close this quarter where no VP from the prospect’s side participated in a call
- Closing Opps with your VP participation: Lists Opportunities due to close this quarter where a VP on your side participated in a call
- Competitive Opps closing this Q: Lists Opportunities due to close this quarter where prospects mentioned competitors during a call
- Early-stage Opps where pricing mentioned: Lists Early-stage opportunities where pricing was mentioned
- Economic Pulse - Impacted Account Types: Shows which account types are most affected when Gong’s Economic Pulse tracker identifies economic factors, such as inflation or cost increases, in customer conversations.
- Economic Pulse - Impacted Industries: Shows which industries are most affected when Gong’s Economic Pulse tracker identifies economic factors, such as inflation or cost increases, in customer conversations.
- Economic Pulse - Impacted Opportunities: Shows which opportunities are most affected when Gong’s Economic Pulse tracker identifies economic factors, such as inflation or cost increases, in customer conversations.
- Economic Pulse rate in Conversations: Shows the percentage of conversations where terms identified by Gong’s Economic Pulse tracker were discussed.
- Email Activity per Contacts in Account: Shows the number of emails each contact in an account received over the last 30 days. Included in the Gong Email Activity dashboard.
- Email Activity per Opportunity Size: Shows whether email activity aligns with opportunity size by listing emails sent for opportunities closing at the end of the following month. Included in the Gong Email Activity dashboard.
- Email Activity per Rep: Shows the number of emails sent by each rep. Included in the Gong Email Activity dashboard.
- Giving scores: Shows how many times people scored other people
- Got Scored: Shows how many times people got scored
- Late-stage Opps without pricing: Lists Late-stage opportunities where pricing wasn't mentioned
- Managers avg. scores over time: Lists average scores manager gave in a specific month
- Most Emailed Contacts - Top 20: Shows the 20 contacts who received the highest number of emails, sorted from highest to lowest. Included in the Gong Email Activity dashboard.
- No. of open Opps per Q per competitor: Shows the number of open opportunities with competition, grouped by competitor
- Number of Opportunities Rep Engaged In: Shows the number of opportunities each rep was involved in, in the last 30 days. Included in the Gong Email Activity dashboard.
- Opportunities without Email Activities: Shows opportunities where no email was sent in the last 30 days. Included in the Gong Email Activity dashboard.
- Overall win rate per quarter: Shows the percentage of opportunities that were won in that quarter. Allows you to see trends in your win-rate.
- Reps avg. scores over time: Lists average scores the rep recieved in a specific month
- Scorecards given over time: Shows number of scorecards given per month
- Scores by scorecard names: Shows the scores given for each scorecard
- Scoring done per month by manager: Shows how many times a manager scored someone in a specific month
- Users average overall score: Shows the average score given to team members per month
- Percentage of competitive won Opps per Q: The quarterly trend of the percentage of opportunities won when there was competition
- Win rate per Q for competitive Opps: The quarterly trend of how often you won opportunities when there was competition
- Win Rate - Economic pulse impacted opps: Shows which opportunities were won even though Gong’s Economic Pulse tracker identifies economic factors, such as inflation or cost increases, in customer conversations.
