In order to display all data you want to export to Salesforce, you need to create additional fields in the task or contact object and add them to the layout for that object. You can let Gong do this automatically by installing the Gong for Salesforce app, or you can set the fields up manually in Salesforce.

To set up the configuration for your custom fields:

1. In Gong, go to Admin center > Settings > CRM > CRM settings.
2. In the Salesforce integration page, go to the Export tab and scroll down to Custom fields for Gong activities. The custom fields you need to create are grouped by the feature they support.
3. Select whether you want automatic or manual setup for the custom fields.
  1. For automatic configuration Install Gong for Salesforce.
  2. For manual configuration, create the custom fields in the relevant Salesforce objects and then add them to the object layout.
4. A green success icon next to the feature name indicates that all custom fields for that feature have been created. A yellow icon with a number next to the feature shows how many custom fields haven’t been created. Note:It takes up to an hour for new fields to be populated in Salesforce and for the alert on missing fields to disappear.

chunks.text:
Prerequisites:
We ask for the following information:

- Identity Provider Metadata URL or Identity Provider Metadata XML file The URL must be a public URL, meaning that it's publicly accessible, and it should generate a valid SAML Metadata response. The XML response or the Metadata XML file must include two SSO bindings with a valid URL: An example of the SAML response Gong receives:
  - HTTP-POST
  - HTTP-REDIRECT
- The URL you want to redirect people to after they log out of Gong
- In your provider, set the SAML name identifier property to emailAddress
- In your provider, make sure that Signed Authentication Request is turned off

chunks.text:
Microsoft Entra ID SAML SSO setup:
To set up authentication via Microsoft Entra ID:

1. Log into Microsoft Entra ID with admin credentials and select Enterprise applications.
2. Click +New application > Create your own application.
3. Give the application a name such as Gong SSO, keep the default settings and click Create.
4. In the application, select Set up single sign on.
5. Select SAML.
6. Edit the Basic SAML Configurations and enter the following values:
  1. Identifier (Entity ID): https://app.gong.io
  2. Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL): https://app.gong.io/welcome/okta/saml/login
7. Click Save.
8. Edit the Attributes & Claims section as follows: Note:If you plan to provision team members via Microsoft Entra ID make sure you configure the permissions listed in Microsoft Entra ID provisioning setup.
  1. Name identifier format: Email address
  2. Source: set to Attribute
  3. Source attribute: user.mail
  4. Delete any Additional claims
9. In the Users and Groups section, add the users or groups you want to have SSO login to Gong.
10. In the Single sign-on section, copy the App Federation Metadata URL.

Once you have set up Microsoft Entra ID for SSO authentication in Gong:

1. In Gong, go to Admin center > Settings > Company > Authentication.
2. In the Identity provider metadata URL, enter the App Federation Metadata URL you copied from Microsoft Entra ID.
3. In After logout, redirect to, enter https://myapps.microsoft.com or a URL that displayes the applications the user has access to.
4. Click Update. Logout and login via Entra ID to test the SSO authentication.

You can set up the integration with Zoom in the following ways:

- Record with native Zoom recording.
- Record with the Gong bot.

In addition, with both types of recording, you can choose whether to record company-wide, that is to connect all your employees automatically, or user-by-user by defining specific users in your organization who can use the integration. Each user then has to request to connect Gong to Zoom.

You need to be a Zoom admin with the necessary Zoom role permissions to set up the connection.

NoteThe integration will disconnect if the person who sets up the integration stops being a Zoom admin later.You can only set up the Gong Zoom integration once per connecting user. If you have 2 Gong instances, you can Connect additional Gong instances to a Zoom account.

chunks.title: Set up the Zoom integration

chunks.text:
Setting up the integration:
1. In the Web conferrencing page, in the Zoom row, click the Recording toggle to enable recording Zoom conversations with the Gong bot.
2. Click SETTINGS on the Zoom row.
3. If you want to connect everyone in your organization to Zoom, click Connect account. Note:The Gong app for Zoom can only be installed if the Zoom integration is set up company-wide.
  1. Sign in to your Zoom account, and authorize access to Zoom. This installs a Gong integration app instance in your Zoom account and connects your Gong instance to Zoom. Once connected the Native Recording section shows that it is Enabled together with additional validation settings.
  2. In the Set up & validate Zoom connection step:
    1. Select your Zoom plan.
    2. Click TEST ZOOM SET UP. Gong checks the settings for users and meetings in both Gong and Zoom to make sure Zoom recording can be enabled successfully. The test can take a few minutes to run.
  3. When the test is complete, click View test results:
    - Green indicates the test passed.
    - Yellow indicates that some team members may still continue to be recorded with the Gong bot.
    - Red indicates there was a problem. Click How to fix to find out how to resolve the issue and run the test again. Note:If you have a Zoom Business or Enterprise account, but the test suggests that you do not, check the following:In your Zoom account settings, make sure Cloud Recording is turned on and check whether the Audio Transcript setting appears. If you can't see it, contact Zoom and ask them to enable it for your organization. Zoom's audio transcripts speaker timeline is used by Gong in native Zoom recording.
  4. Click ENABLE ZOOM RECORDING to use Zoom to record calls in Zoom. When native recording can’t be used, such as, if the user doesn’t have a Zoom license, the Gong bot joins the call. Enable the Gong audio prompt in the consent profile for cases when the Gong bot joins the call.
  5. Click Edit settings and toggle Delete recordings from Zoom once they are retrieved by Gong and Delete recordings initiated by Gong but not retrieved to ON (recommended). These settings can help reduce your Zoom storage and uphold data retention policies. See Delete recordings in Zoom to learn more.
  6. Toggle Enable live-streaming from Zoom to the Gong app in order to enable the live-stream transcript while using the Gong for Zoom app.
  7. Send an email to all recorded users that their Gong calls can now be recorded in Zoom.
4. If you want to limit the people in your organization who can connect to Zoom, click Set up user-by-user connection. Note:The Gong app for Zoom requires a company-wide set up.
  1. In Zoom, set up the list of people approved to have their Zoom conversations imported to Gong.
  2. Select Pre-approve now, if you want to automatically approve team members connecting to Zoom. Otherwise you’ll have to approve each request separately.
  3. By default, Native recording is switched on.
  4. Check Delete recordings from Zoom once they are retrieved by Gong and Delete recordings initiated by Gong but not retrieved (recommended). These settings can help reduce your Zoom storage and uphold data retention policies. See Delete recordings in Zoom to learn more.
  5. Choose whether to email your team members about the integration.
  6. Click Activate connection.
  7. Once you have activated the connection, you’ll see:
    - The number of people successfully connected
    - The number of people who are connected but who’s settings need to be changed
    - The number of people who were unable to connect
    - The number of people who haven’t yet tried to connect
5. Once connected, you can use the Gong consent page with dynamic links when recording calls.
6. Read Detailed Zoom settings for native Zoom recording to learn about settings we recommend you set in Zoom.

What happens when you switch between dialers:
If you switch from the Gong Dialer to an external dialer like Zoom Phone, your Gong business phone numbers are retained for 10 days. If you switch back to the Gong Dialer within that window, the numbers are still available. If you switch to the external dialer again during that period, the 10-day window starts over.

Certain features are only available while using the Gong Dialer and are not available while Zoom Phone or another external dialer is active:

- Dialer recording settings configured for mobile
- Trust Hub profile and trusted calling configuration
- Business phone numbers (except personal numbers for mobile)
- Regulatory documentation for the Gong Dialer
- Email notifications about submitted documentation
- Call notes

Engage users should use only one dialer. Even after switching to Zoom Phone, you can still import calls from the Gong Dialer and other telephony systems through the Telephony Systems page for other parts of your organization that continue to use them.

Conditional filters are rules applied to data that specify certain conditions for displaying or processing information. They help customize the data to meet specific criteria.

Gong provides conditional filters (And, Or and Not) when creating your deal and forecast boards. These allow for the flexibility of using CRM fields to target specific deals for inclusion or exclusion, resulting in more precise pipeline and forecast scenarios.

This article will guide you through the best way to use conditional filters and give some typical examples of deal board filters you might want to create. We recommend reading all the examples so that you’re familiar with how And, Or and Not filters work specifically within Gong.

Conditional filters are rules applied to data that specify certain conditions for displaying or processing information. They help customize the data to meet specific criteria.

Gong provides conditional filters (And, Or and Not) when creating your deal and forecast boards. These allow for the flexibility of using CRM fields to target specific deals for inclusion or exclusion, resulting in more precise pipeline and forecast scenarios.

This article will guide you through the best way to use conditional filters and give some typical examples of deal board filters you might want to create. We recommend reading all the examples so that you’re familiar with how And, Or and Not filters work specifically within Gong.
chunks.title: Apply conditional filters

chunks.text:
Principles for conditional filters in Gong:
When using conditional filters in Gong, it's important to understand these basic facts:

Their core meaning:

- When combining filters, they are grouped and handled in a specific order: Not functions are applied first, followed by And. Finally Or functions take place.
- Whether you add a filter from a group or subgroup level will affect how the groups are nested.
- You can add an unlimited amount of filters, however you can only add up to 3 nested levels.

Remember these points specifically about using Not filters:

- Using a Not group means that the deals you’ll see in your deal or forecast board are the opposite to the fields included in that group.
- You can’t add a Not subgroup to a Not group (this is considered a double negative).
- Add And subgroups to show deals that don’t match ALL fields. If a deal matches one of those fields only, it will still appear.
- Add an Or subgroup to show deals that don’t match ANY fields.

Note:Using zero filters. Even if you don’t add any filters, you'll automatically be offered an Or condition. For example:The tab criteria includes all deals that have Score type=High, Score type=Fair or Score type=Low. This means that deals of all 3 types are included.
chunks.body:
When using conditional filters in Gong, it's important to understand these basic facts:

Their core meaning:

- When combining filters, they are grouped and handled in a specific order: Not functions are applied first, followed by And. Finally Or functions take place.
- Whether you add a filter from a group or subgroup level will affect how the groups are nested.
- You can add an unlimited amount of filters, however you can only add up to 3 nested levels.

Remember these points specifically about using Not filters:

- Using a Not group means that the deals you’ll see in your deal or forecast board are the opposite to the fields included in that group.
- You can’t add a Not subgroup to a Not group (this is considered a double negative).
- Add And subgroups to show deals that don’t match ALL fields. If a deal matches one of those fields only, it will still appear.
- Add an Or subgroup to show deals that don’t match ANY fields.

Note:Using zero filters. Even if you don’t add any filters, you'll automatically be offered an Or condition. For example:The tab criteria includes all deals that have Score type=High, Score type=Fair or Score type=Low. This means that deals of all 3 types are included.
chunks.headingPath: Principles for conditional filters in Gong

Business phone numbers can appear as spam when calling new prospects, which reduces the chance they will answer. Trusted calling lets you register your business numbers so that service providers can identify your calls as legitimate. This increases the likelihood that calls go through and are shown as verified rather than unknown or spam.

Trusted calling is only available for companies with US-based addresses. It can be set up as soon as you have provisioned business numbers.

Setting up trusted calling involves two steps: creating a business profile and then activating the relevant protocols for your numbers.

Setting up trusted calling involves two steps: creating a business profile and then activating the relevant protocols for your numbers.
chunks.title: Set up trusted calling

chunks.text:
What trusted calling includes:
- SHAKEN/STIR protocols: Adds a digital certificate to your phone numbers so that service providers can verify your identity. This is a suite of protocols implemented in the US and Canada to combat robocalls.
- Voice Integrity: Registers your numbers directly with call providers to help prevent them from marking your numbers as spam.

Once your profile is submitted and verified, all current business numbers and any future numbers you provision are automatically marked as trusted.

chunks.text:
Set up trusted calling:
You can start this process immediately after getting business numbers, or at any time from the Trust Hub tab in Dialer setup.

To set up trusted calling:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click Dialer setup under Gong Engage.
3. Click the Trust Hub tab.
4. Click Create profile. (If you have just provisioned numbers, you may be prompted to do this as part of the number confirmation flow.)
5. Enter your business details:
  - Legal Business Name
  - Business type
  - Business industry
  - Business Registration ID Type and Number
  - Business Regions of Operations
  - Website URL
  - Social Media Profile URL
6. Click Next.
7. Enter your company's main business address. Providing a US address is recommended, as some trusted calling features require it. If you register with a non-US address, some features may not be available.
8. Click Next.
9. In Business address, enter your business address and click Next.
10. In People to contact, enter the contact details of the people service providers should reach to verify your business. Add additional contacts as needed and click Next.
11. Accept the terms and conditions and click Next.
12. Accept the terms for adding SHAKEN/STIR protocols and click Next.
13. Choose whether to set up Voice Integrity and click Submit.

Your details are submitted for verification. Once approved, your business numbers are marked as trusted.

chunks.text:
Arrange your deal board view:
Where to go: Revenue > Deals

Any Gong user can view a deal board, where you’ll see key deal information at a glance, including columns for:

- Deal likelihood score: A score for each open deal to show how likely it is to close within its expected period compared to others in the pipeline.
- Warnings: Hover over the number to see exactly what warning has been flagged on that deal.
- Contacts: Hover over the number of contacts to see who was recently active.
- Activity timeline: Shows recent customer and rep interactions.
- Playbooks: View completed elements of your company’s playbook methodology at a glance.
- Trackers: Hover over the tracker column to see when the phrases were mentioned.
- Amount: Displays your selected CRM amount field. Click to view shared attribution details.

Refer to the screenshot for some ways you can customize your view:

1. Switch between different boards.
2. Choose whose deals you're viewing and date ranges.
3. Click +Add filter to filter the board using CRM or Gong AI fields such as Warnings.
4. Select a tab across the top for different deal groupings, with rollup totals at the top.
5. Use the Groups panel on the left, to group deals ad-hoc by CRM or Gong fields.
6. Toggle between Deals and Team to view pipeline by individual deals or team member rollups.
7. Click the arrows next to a column title to sort the board by that column.
8. Search accounts using the search icon in the account name column.

Each forecast board includes a set of columns that show the current state of key business metrics—such as bookings, targets, or a combination of both. Teams or individuals appear in the rows, with each cell displaying their relevant metrics.

You can see your team aggregated roll-up number in the blue bar.

Some columns are set to retrieve submissions - either manually or automatically. Submission cells appear with a square around the submission number.

chunks.text:
How to submit your forecast numbers:
When it's time to submit your forecast, you’ll see this reminder on your Gong homepage, which disappears once it's done:

1. Select your team, the forecast board, and the period for which you’re forecasting.
2. Click a Submission cell, for example: Commit. A panel opens on the right.
3. Enter your forecast number. If your admin has set this column to auto-submit, numbers are submitted automatically on your behalf. You see the last submitted number and when it was submitted.
4. Below your submission number, you can:
  - Add a note for your manager.
  - Click Submission changes to see how your submissions are trending and what has changed over time.
  - Drill into the deals in the cell (if set by your admin). They open on a deal board, where you can move into each deal’s panel for specific details.
  - See your forecast numbers broken into months if you’re forecasting for the quarter.
  - Click Progress to target to see how you progress toward your target (if set by your admin).
5. Click Next submission to move to the next submission cell or click Save.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Where to go: Admin center > Settings > Data capture > Web conferencing

Important:You must ensure the Record to computer files settings are toggled to on (in Zoom - Settings - Recording). Your Zoom admin can enable this for all users. We won’t be able to record calls if this isn’t configured correctly.

Team members can record Zoom calls by adding the Gong bot as a participant to their meetings. The Gong bot is displayed the same as any other participant in the call and is an alternative for recording calls when native Zoom recording isn’t used.

Native Zoom recording can’t be used in calls where:

- The call host doesn’t have a Gong seat or permissions to record calls
- The team member doesn’t have the correct settings to allow native Zoom recording
- Someone outside your company hosts the meeting

We therefore recommend setting up both Zoom native recording and recording with the Gong bot.

To set the Zoom integration to record with the Gong bot:

- In Admin center > Settings > Data capture > Web conferencing, toggle the Zoom integration to on.

chunks.text:
How reps experience recording with the Gong bot:
Once this is set, Zoom calls are recorded with the Gong bot as follows:

- The bot is added to the Zoom call from the waiting room and recording must be approved by the call host.
- Zoom plays an audio prompt informing participants the call is being recorded.
- The Zoom consent page to record is displayed to all participants when the bot is added to the call.
- For calls hosted by a third party, the host must approve recording the call.
- If the host is absent from the call, the call will not be recorded.
- The recording icon is displayed in calls that are recorded.

chunks.text:
How to improve the recording experience:
Reps who regularly host calls may prefer to automatically enable recording with the Gong bot and not expressly give permission at the start of each call. In addition, they may want calls recorded even if the host does not join the call.

We’ve set up the Zoom Meetings - Recording Bot app so that when the call host is in your organization:

- Recording is automatically initiated by the bot when it joins the call and does not need to first be approved by the host.
- When a waiting room is used, the host must allow the Gong bot to join the meeting before recording can start. To pause the recording, the host moves the Bot to the waiting room and brings it back to start recording again.
- The host no longer needs to be on the call in order for the bot to record the call.
- We recommend setting this up as well as setting up native Zoom recording, as in the following cases the Gong bot will record conversations even if you have native Zoom recording set up:

In addition:

- The audio prompt and consent page are displayed to notify participants the call is being recorded.
- Calls hosted by a third party still need the host to approve the call recording.

Note that automatic approval to record calls only applies to calls set up by people in your organization.

chunks.text:
Configure Zoom settings:
The following settings should be set by your organization’s Zoom admin for all Gong users.

1. In Zoom, go to Settings > Recordings.
2. Make sure Record to computer files is toggled On.
3. Make sure Hosts can give meeting participants permission to record on their computer is toggled On.
4. If you have installed the Zoom Meetings - recording bot app, the Only users in your account can request to record to computer files can be toggled On or Off. If you have not installed the app, this setting must be toggled Off for Gong to record calls with the bot.

Add the following custom fields:

chunks.title: Setting up HubSpot custom fields

chunks.text:
Engage flow fields:
| Field lable name | Description | Object to add field to | Field API name | Data type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gong flow ID | The ID of the flow the contact is in. Empty when not associated with a flow | Contact | gong_current_flow_id__c | Text (30) |
| Gong step attempt ID | The ID of the action that represents the step in the flow the task is associated with. For example, if a rep makes a phone call as part of a step in a flow, and they had to call 5 times before the person answered, this ID represents one of the times the rep tried to call. | Contact | gong_flow_execution_id__c | Text (50) |
| Gong flow name | The name of the flow the contact is in | Contact | gong_current_flow_name__c | Text (100) |
| Gong flow status | The status of the flow the contact is in | Contact | gong_current_flow_status__c | Picklist. See possible flow statuses in your CRM |
| Gong step number | The step in the flow the contact is in | Contact | gong_current_flow_step_number__c | Text (10) |
| Gong step type | The type of step the contact is in | Contact | gong_current_flow_step_type__c | Text (80) |
| Gong step due date | The date the current task is due to be completed. For example, if the step is to make a phone call, this field shows the date the call should be made. | Contact | gong_current_flow_task_due_date__c | Date |
| Gong added to flow by | The name of the Gong user who assigned the contact to a flow | Contact | gong_current_flow_user_name__c | Text (80) |
| Gong currently in a flow | Indicates whether the contact is currently in an Engage flow | Contact | gong_actively_being_in_a_flow__c | Checkbox |
| Date Added to Engage Flow | The date the contact was added to the flow | Contact | gong_added_to_flow_date__c | Date |
| Currently in Engage Flow | Indicates whether the contact is currently in an Engage flow | Contact | gong_actively_being_in_a_flow__c | Checkbox |

chunks.text:
Share a call:
1. Click Share icon at the top right of the call page.
  1. Choose Share internally to share with people at your company who use Gong.
  2. Click Share with customers to share with customers, prospects, or people at your company who don’t use Gong.
  3. Embed call gives you an embeddable link that can be viewed by people at your company who use Gong. Note:You can share calls while they are still processing. Schedule an email that will be sent when the call is ready, or send a link that gives access to the call when it’s ready.

chunks.text:
Share internally:
Share calls via email or Slack with people at your company who use Gong, and they’ll get a link to the call that is accessible in Gong. If the call is shared in Slack, recipients see an AI-generated call brief in the Slack message.

- Share via email: Enter the person's name or email address. Sharing by email gives recipients access to the call if they didn’t already have it.
- Share via Slack: Choose a channel. To share via Slack, your Gong account needs to be connected to Slack. To share in a private channel, Gong must be invited to that channel.
- Share via Microsoft Teams: Select and team and channel to share the call in. Only available if your company set up the Microsoft Teams - Notifications app.

chunks.title: Share a call

chunks.text:
Share with customers > Share via link:
Share a call by generating a customer-facing link that you can copy and send through email, chat, CRM records, or other communication channels.

1. Select the Get link tab.
2. Update share settings as needed.
3. Enter the names or email addresses of the people you want to share the call with.
4. (Optional) Select Also allow anyone from these company domains to access. Anyone with an email address from the same company domains as the recipients can access the call after verifying their email address. Note:Personal email domains such as Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook, Hotmail, iCloud, and AOL are not included in domain-based access. Recipients using these email providers can still access the call if they were added directly as recipients.
5. Click Copy link and share the link with your customers.

When you share calls this way, recipients get a link to a dedicated call page that includes:

- The call recording
- Call details
- Gong AI summaries (optional)

Recipients using these email providers can still access the call if they were added directly as recipients.

chunks.text:
About call views:
- Views for each share, via email or link, are tracked separately. If you share the same call multiple times, each share has its own view record.
- If you share a call via email and don't require the viewer to identify themselves, every time that link is used it is logged as if the email recipient viewed the call, even if they forwarded it to someone else.
- If a link or embed link is shared, we tell you that the link was generated and how many times it was used. If access requires viewers to identify themselves, we’ll tell you who accessed the link.

chunks.text:
FAQs:
How are call views tracked?

Each time you share a call, views are tracked separately. So if you share a call today using a shareable link and via email, views for each of those shares are tracked separately. If you share the call again tomorrow via email, views for that share are tracked separately, too.

How do I know who has viewed a call?

If you share a call via email and require the viewer to identify themselves, you’ll know who is viewing the call. every time that link is used, the person using it must log in. This gives you data about who is viewing the call.

How do I restrict who can view the call?

To restrict who views a call, click edit on the call sharing screen and select: Only specific users will be able to access.

I don’t know who viewed my call. Why not?

If you share a call using a shareable link and set access to Anyone with the link can access the call, we can only tell you that the link was generated and how many times it was used. We can't tell you who used it. If you want to know who viewed a call, either require users to identify themselves when they access the call, or allow only specific users to access the call.

How do I cancel access to a call after it's been shared?

If you've shared a call with customers, that call is accessible until the link expires. To cancel access before the link expires, go to the call page, and click the Shares & Views icon along the right panel. From here you can cancel access to the shared call.

What’s the difference between Embed call on the Share call menu, and the Copy embed link in the Share with customers dialog?

If you choose Embed call from the Share call menu, you get an internal link to the call that can only be accessed by people at your company using Gong. If you choose the Copy embed link option from the Share call with customers dialog, the link is accessible to customers, prospects, and people at your company who don’t use Gong.

Can the prospect I shared the call with forward it to other stakeholders in their organization?

Yes. If you want additional stakeholders from the same organization to be able to access the call when it's forwarded, make sure:

- The call privacy setting is set to Only specific people can access.
- Also allow anyone from these company domains to access this option must be selected when sharing the call.

With these settings enabled, other people from the same approved company domain can access the call after verifying their email address, without you needing to grant access to each person individually.

Dialer calls:
The following table lists dialer call skip codes and explains why a call may not have been recorded.

| Skip code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| AUTO_RECORDING_EXCLUDED | Your company has restricted automatic recording within this country or area code, and the user didn't manually start the recording |
| BUSY_LINE | The prospect's line was busy |
| CALL_DECLINED | Either the call was declined by the recipient or the person was unavailable |
| CARRIER_BLOCKED | Unable to make calls from this number since it was marked as spam by the provider |
| DESTINATION_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE | The destination number is temporarily unavailable |
| HIGH_RISK | Phone number is in high risk |
| INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER | The call was made to an invalid phone number |
| MANUAL_RECORDING_EXCLUDED | Your company has set this country or area code to manual recording, and the user didn't manually start the recording |
| RECORDING_DELETED_BY_USER | The recording was deleted by the user |
| RECORDING_RESTRICTED | Recording in this specific country or area code was prohibited by your company |

Web conference calls:

chunks.body: The following table lists web conferences call skip codes and explains why it may not have been recorded.
chunks.title: Skip codes for unrecorded calls and meetings

chunks.text:
Web conference calls:
| Skip code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| BAD_SCHEDULE | The meeting didn’t start at the planned time so the Gong bot was unable to join. This may happen when a meeting is moved close to the planned start time (after the Gong bot was dispatched). |
| CALL_BLOCKLISTED | The meeting was blocklisted because it contains a blocked email, domain, or phrase. |
| CALL_PROVIDER_DISABLED_FOR_COMPANY | The meeting was scheduled with a web conferencing or telephony provider that was disabled for your company before the meeting started. |
| CAN_NOT_LISTEN_IN | The meeting didn't have VoIP set up so the Gong recorder couldn't record it |
| CANCELED_BY_OWNER | The host cancelled the recording using the Stop recording action on the Gong homepage. |
| CANCELLED | The calendar event was moved or updated, for example, cancelled via the calendar, or deleted or rejected by the organizer. |
| CANNOT_CONNECT_ERROR | The Gong bot was unable to get into the meeting for a technical reason. For example, because the Zoom meeting required a version upgrade, or the Webex meeting had a redirect URL. |
| CAPTCHA_VERIFICATION_BLOCKED_BOT | For Microsoft Teams calls only.The Gong recorder couldn't join the meeting because it couldn't pass a human-verification challenge (CAPTCHA) |
| COMPLIANCE_AUDIO_ANNOUNCEMENT | The call wasn't recorded because the bot couldn't play the audio announcement that the call is being recorded |
| COMPLIANCE_ENFORCING | The meeting didn't comply with the recording consent settings so the call wasn’t recorded.For example, this can happen when the consent page was changed to be enforced after the meeting was scheduled, and the meeting doesn’t use the consent page link. |
| COMPLIANCE_SYSTEM_DECISION | Compliance with the consent settings is enabled, but we were unable to verify that the meeting complied with the settings, and therefore didn’t record the meeting. |
| COMPLIANCE_USER_REQUEST | A participant did not consent for the call to be recorded. They clicked the Join but don't record option when joining the meeting. |
| CONNECTOR_WAS_NOT_APPROVED | The Gong bot was not admitted to the meeting. |
| DENIED_ENTRY | The Gong bot was actively denied entrance to the meeting. |
| DID_NOT_START | Gong logged a "waiting for the meeting to start" notification, but the meeting never started. |
| DUPLICATE | Two meetings were scheduled to start at the same time, and Gong recorded the second meeting. For example, this can happen when:There are overlapping meetings when using a personal meeting link with native Zoom recordingThere are overlapping meetings when using dynamic links and/or the Gong bot |
| ENDED | The meeting ended before or when the Gong bot joined. |
| HAS_DO_NOT_RECORD_USERS | One of the participants is set to "never record". |
| HOST_DENIED_LOCAL_RECORDING | The host denied the request to allow recording |
| HOST_NEVER_SHOWED | Gong logged a "waiting for the host to start the meeting" notification but the meeting never started. |
| HOST_NOT_ANSWERED | The meeting’s host did not respond to multiple recording authorization requests. |

Who can use this: Any team memberRequired permissions: Manage AI Trackers

What are smart trackers?

Smart trackers are AI models that identify and surface specific concepts by taking into account diverse words, sentence structure, intent, and context. For example, create a smart tracker that asks the question “Are customers asking for discounts?” and you’ll surface instances such as “Can we get a better price?” and “What’s your best offer?”

Who can build smart trackers?

Only a Gong admin can build a smart tracker.

What’s the difference between keyword trackers and smart trackers?

Keyword trackers are based on specific words, terms, or phrases that are mentioned in conversations. Smart trackers are AI models trained to identify and find concepts, even when they are said using different words and in unexpected ways.

How do I choose whether to build a keyword tracker and a smart tracker?

Use a keyword tracker when you want to track exact terms, like a competitor’s name or a campaign. Keyword trackers are unlimited in number. Choose a smart tracker when you want to capture intent, even if it’s expressed in different ways.

What's the difference between the question builder and free-text options?

The difference is in how you create the question. The question builder is the default option, and lets you construct a question by choosing from predefined phrases across three sections. The free-text option allows you to ask your own question using natural language.

Does the concept always need to be worded as a question?

chunks.title: Smart tracker FAQs

chunks.text:
The question builder is the default option, and lets you construct a question by choosing from predefined phrases across three sections. The free-text option allows you to ask your own question using natural language. Does the concept always need to be worded as a question?

When using the question builder, the concept will always be phrased as a question. With the free-text option, it doesn’t have to be a question, but we recommend writing it as one. This makes the concept clearer, and you’ll still have space to add more details and context in the next step.

What’s a good smart tracker concept?

A good concept is specific rather than broad. For example, “Is the prospect asking for a discount?” works well, while “pricing” is too general. Customers may express the same idea in very different ways—like “Is that the best you can do?” or “That price is too high. Can you go lower?” Because the wording varies, keyword trackers can miss these instances, but smart trackers can surface them.

Why should I use smart trackers?

People don’t always say things the way we expect them to, and smart trackers take that into account. With smart trackers, you can discover new and unexpected ways in which people say things, so you can identify market needs, even if you can’t anticipate how they will be expressed.

How many smart trackers can I build?

You can create and publish as many question-based smart trackers as needed.

Question-based smart trackers consume Gong credits based on the amount of call and email data analyzed. Smart tracker configuration, including filters and analysis scope, can affect overall credit consumption.

chunks.title: Smart tracker FAQs

chunks.text:
Smart tracker configuration, including filters and analysis scope, can affect overall credit consumption.

To optimize smart tracker usage, apply filters and regularly review active smart trackers.

Where can I see smart trackers?

You can see smart trackers throughout Gong: on the Search page, individual call pages, Team Stats, Streams, Initiatives boards, Deals, and more.

I just activated a smart tracker, why do I only the only place I see it is on the Search page. Why?

If you’ve activated a tracker and applied it to calls that happened in the past, it can take some time to process those calls. The tracker will be available on the Search page right away, but it may not appear in other areas yet because we show aggregated data there, and don’t want to show incomplete data as it could be misleading.

How long does it take to set up a smart tracker?

With the question-based smart tracker builder, setting up a smart tracker takes just a few minutes.

Which languages support smart trackers?

All Gong languages support smart trackers.

Do I need a minimum number of calls to build a smart tracker?

No. Smart trackers are available with no minimum call volume.

What happens to past results when I update a tracker?

Updating a tracker doesn’t overwrite or delete past results. Conversations already processed keep the old tracker data, while the updated tracker applies only to new conversations and to historical conversations within the backfill window you select (14 or 30 days). This means you may see old and new results side by side, depending on the time period.

Who can use this: Tech admin, Business adminAvailable on: Gong EngageIdeal for: Sales manager, Manager of managers. Quota-carrying manager

As a manager, part of your daily routine might involve keeping things moving while reps are away, especially during holidays or vacation periods when multiple team members are away at the same time. To prevent tasks from piling up and becoming overdue, you can set up timeframes for your teams or individual reps where their flow to-dos will be snoozed.

Managers, tech admins, business admins, and global admins automatically have permission to set up snooze time for other team members. To give anyone else in your company the ability to snooze flow to-dos and auto emails for other users, ensure they have the necessary permissions in their permission profile.

What gets snoozed during snooze time?

During snooze time, the due dates and expiration dates for any flow to-dos and auto emails will be automatically adjusted according to your selected snooze time. Any flow to-do with a due date on or later than the first day of the snooze period will be moved forward by the number of business days in the snooze period. When you delete snooze time, the due date and expiration date are moved back by the number of business days in the snooze period.

What doesn’t get snoozed during snooze time?

- One-off to-dos (to-dos created by the rep)
- Gong-recommended to-dos
- Email reply
- Meeting booked
- Email bounced

To set up snooze time for your teams or reps:

1. Go to Engage > To-dos
2. At the top right, click Snooze
3. Click Set snooze time
4. Set the date range
5. Select the teams or team members whose flow to-dos should be snoozed during the selected date range
6. Click Save

When you delete snooze time, the due date and expiration date are moved back by the number of business days in the snooze period.

What doesn’t get snoozed during snooze time?

- One-off to-dos (to-dos created by the rep)
- Gong-recommended to-dos
- Email reply
- Meeting booked
- Email bounced

To set up snooze time for your teams or reps:

1. Go to Engage > To-dos
2. At the top right, click Snooze
3. Click Set snooze time
4. Set the date range
5. Select the teams or team members whose flow to-dos should be snoozed during the selected date range
6. Click Save

chunks.text:
What updates appear in Business pulse:
The mobile feed includes several types of updates for your followed and suggested accounts:

- New customer calls: Surfaces risks, highlights, and next steps from recent customer conversations.
- CRM changes: Includes stage moves, closed won/lost deals, financial developments, and close date changes, including context on what may have driven them.
- Weekly account recaps: Comprehensive summaries for all accounts that had activity in the last week.
- Red flag emails: Highlights potential risks identified in customer email communications. Emails labeled as Red flag are surfaced as feed updates to help managers quickly spot and act on critical risk signals.
- Customer objections: Flags significant customer objections detected by smart trackers in recent calls. A dedicated feed update helps teams quickly spot deal risks and blockers.

chunks.text:
Quota carriers: Submit your own forecast:
If you're a quota-carrier, you'll get a reminder an hour before it's time to submit your forecast for a specific line of business. For example, if you're set to submit your "New business" forecast every week, you'll get a weekly reminder similar to this one:

To submit your forecast:

1. Tap the reminder or go to Deals > Forecast.
2. If you tap the reminder, the board and timeframe are preselected for you. If you enter manually through Deals > Forecast, you'll need to select them. Until you submit your forecast, you'll see whether the forecast is due or overdue:
3. Select the forecast category you want to update and tap its card.
4. Update your forecast for the selected category. Leave notes for your manager to add context.
5. Tap Update. When you complete all categories in a selected line of business, you'll be notified. Your manager will be notified 2 hours after the due time.
6. Repeat the above steps for every line of business.

chunks.text:
Security certifications and compliance reports:
- ISO 27701: ISO 27701 is a globally recognized, privacy-based certification that builds upon security requirements outlined in ISO 27001 with emphasis on an organization's Privacy Information Management System (PIMS).
- ISO 27001: ISO 27001 is a globally recognized, standards-based approach to security that outlines requirements for an organization's Information Security Management System (ISMS).
- ISO 27017: This standard provides guidelines on how we implement information security controls for the provision and use of cloud services.
- ISO 27018: This standard protects personally identifiable information (PII) in public clouds that act as PII processors. This further extends our ability to safeguard the personal and customer data we collect, process, and manage on your behalf.
- EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF): Gong is certified with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (EU-U.S. DPF) and, as applicable, the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF, and/or the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (Swiss-U.S. DPF). See our public DPF profile.
- CSA STAR: Learn about Gong's cloud security controls, as documented in the Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) STAR Registry.
- SOC 2 Type II + HIPAA: Gong maintains our own SOC 2 Type II report with scope that spans Gong operations. The independent assessment affirms our commitment to customer data security, availability, confidentiality, and privacy. Gong's report also includes a mapping to Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) security requirements.
- PCI DSS: Gong has created the mechanisms that ingest and process calls from external telephony systems in a way that is PCI-DSS compliant. Gong maintains a specific scope for PCI DSS that analyzes the calls, identifies the PCI-related data, and redacts digits set forth by customer business rules. For full scope details and customer responsibilities, see Gong PCI DSS scope and responsibilities.
- Penetration testing: Gong obtains independent validation security with third-party penetration testing.

Data security:
- Data encryption: Customer data is encrypted in transit using at least TLS 1.2 and at rest using AES-256.
- Key management: Gong leverages the cloud provider's native key management service.Customers can encrypt their own data using bring your own key (BYOK). Learn more about setting up data encryption in Gong.
- Data segregation: Customer data is logically separated within Gong's multi-tenant environment, consistent with common SaaS practices.
- Data retention: Data retention is determined by the customer and can be configured at any time. Learn more about managing data retention in Gong.
- Information redaction: Gong offers optional numerical and PHI redaction capabilities to help protect sensitive information in call recordings and transcripts. Numeric redaction replaces digit sequences that meet a customer-defined threshold with (REDACTED), while PHI redaction removes supported personal identifiers. Redacted transcript content is replaced with (REDACTED) and the corresponding audio is muted. PHI redaction is currently available for English-language calls. Learn more about redacting sensitive information in Gong.
- Data deletion: Gong provides multiple ways of deleting data from the tenant environment and provides tools for the customer to meet DSAR requests. Learn more about deleting personal data from Gong.

chunks.text:
Identity and access management:
- Provisioning: Gong supports a system for single or cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) provisioning systems.
- Single sign-on: Gong supports authentication through common Identity Providers, such as Google, Microsoft (Entra ID Active Directory and Office 365), and Salesforce. Gong also supports SAML 2.0-based SSO, OAuth 2.0 authorization, and OpenID Connect, including Okta, OneLogin, Rippling, and custom providers.
- Password policy: Our preference is for our customers to use their Single Sign On (SSO) to inherit the rules associated with their password policy. For non-SSO users, Gong supports authentication, which enforces the following password requirements: minimum of eight characters, at least one number, at least one special character, cannot contain part of the username, cannot reuse the last four passwords.
- Session management: Gong supports session management for inactivity. For username/password and SAML authentication, the default timeout is 30 minutes (configurable for SAML). For identity providers such as Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, or Okta OpenID Connect, the identity provider controls the session timeout policy.
- API authentication: There are two ways to retrieve credentials to the Gong Public API: Basic Authorization, which requires manually obtaining an Access Key and Access Key Secret; OAuth, which generates a Bearer Token.
- Workspaces: You can set up workspaces in Gong to segment your Gong instance to match your business needs. This feature helps enforce principles of least privilege within your business users. This is useful if you have separate business units or geographic regions (such as offices in the United States and in EMEA), where you may want to apply different business settings, permissioning, or retention policies. Creating separate workspaces allows you to easily manage different settings between distinct business groups.
- User roles: Gong provides four out-of-the-box user roles that can be configured for granular permissioning: Collaborator, Standard user, Business administrator, and Technical administrator.
- Role-based access control: In addition to standard user roles, Gong supports granular permission profiles. Create granular permission profiles to restrict access and actions related to: calls, emails, call libraries, deals, coaching and stats pages, forecast, CRM, and exporting. Access can be restricted on an individual, team, or custom basis. Note: This is separate from consent profiles.
- Call access controls: Gong provides multiple options to manage access to calls. Through granular permission profiles, a technical admin can restrict access to calls, such as: determining whether users can download call media, restricting whether calls can be shared with customers, allowing users to set calls as private, letting users delete calls, and restricting whether users can export reports on calls.
- Access to customer data: Gong restricts and limits access to customer data to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis. Access of customer data by Gong personnel through the Gong platform can be audited in the Audit API.

Data backup and recovery:
- Cloud hosting: Gong is a SaaS application hosted in cloud infrastructure.
- Backups and recovery: Gong conducts regular daily backups of customer data. The backups are applied to keep the Gong environment resilient to outages or cases where we needed to recover customer data. Gong's Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) are each 24 hours.

chunks.text:
Privacy and compliance:
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA): Gong's DPA sets out the terms that apply with regard to the Processing of Personal Data by Gong on behalf of Customers, in the course of providing the Gong Service to Customers under the Agreement. See our Data Processing Addendum.
- Privacy policy: You can find our privacy policy at gong.io/legal/privacy-policy.
- Sub-processors: You can find our list of sub-processors at gong.io/legal/sub-processors. We recommend subscribing to stay up to date on any changes that may occur.
- Right to be forgotten: Gong provides mechanisms within the platform interface and Gong API to delete personal data upon request to observe DSAR requests.
- Consent profiles: You can create different consent profiles for different teams. Consent profiles are separate from permission profiles, and enable you to enforce multiple streams of consent based on different geographic or state privacy regulations.
- Voice identification: Voice identification can be enabled to identify licensed Gong users in mono telephony calls. This function is disabled by default. Technical administrators can enable this function for licensed Gong users, who must also consent to the function.

- via API
- via Salesforce
- Other - set up yourself, or with help from either Gong or the telephony provider

The following sections list the telephony systems supported by Gong for each integration type. We constantly add new providers, so if you have any needs, suggestions or questions, get in touch with Gong Support.

chunks.body:
Who can use this: Tech admin, Business adminAvailable on: Gong Foundation, Gong Engage

If your company currently uses Zoom Phone as its dialer in Gong Engage, you can switch to the Gong Dialer at any time. Before switching, there are a few things to know about phone numbers, downtime, and dialer usage.
chunks.title: Switch from Zoom Phone to the Gong Dialer

chunks.text:
Phone numbers:
The Gong Dialer uses Twilio-provided business phone numbers. These are different from your Zoom Phone numbers. When you switch, you will need to provision new business numbers through Gong.

If keeping your existing Zoom Phone numbers is important, you can port them to Twilio. Number porting can take several weeks to months and is a paid service that requires a statement of work. Contact your PS Consultant to begin.
chunks.body:

If keeping your existing Zoom Phone numbers is important, you can port them to Twilio. Number porting can take several weeks to months and is a paid service that requires a statement of work. Contact your PS Consultant to begin.
chunks.title: Switch from Zoom Phone to the Gong Dialer

chunks.text:
Downtime during the switch:
Plan the transition during a designated window. Your team may experience downtime while the Gong Dialer is being set up.
chunks.body: Plan the transition during a designated window. Your team may experience downtime while the Gong Dialer is being set up.
chunks.title: Switch from Zoom Phone to the Gong Dialer

chunks.text:
Engage users should use only one dialer:
After switching, Engage users should use only the Gong Dialer. You can still import Zoom Phone calls from other parts of your company through the Telephony Systems page, but Engage users should not be calling from both dialers.
chunks.body: After switching, Engage users should use only the Gong Dialer. You can still import Zoom Phone calls from other parts of your company through the Telephony Systems page, but Engage users should not be calling from both dialers.
chunks.headingPath: Engage users should use only one dialer
chunks.title: Switch from Zoom Phone to the Gong Dialer

chunks.text:
Switch to the Gong Dialer:
To switch from Zoom Phone to the Gong Dialer:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click Dialer setup under Gong Engage.
3. Use the dropdown at the top to select Gong Dialer and de-select Zoom Phone.
4. Follow the setup instructions to enable and configure the Gong Dialer.

The Gong Dialer is now your active dialer. Complete the setup steps below to get your team calling.

chunks.title: Switch from Zoom Phone to the Gong Dialer

chunks.text:
After switching: recommended next steps:
After switching to the Gong Dialer, complete the following setup steps:

- Get business numbers for your team
- Enable mobile access for the Gong Dialer
- Configure dialer recording methods
- Set up call outcomes
- Set up trusted calling (US only)
- Review dialer network connectivity requirements

chunks.title: Switch from Zoom Phone to the Gong Dialer

chunks.text:
Switching back to an external dialer:
If you switch from the Gong Dialer back to an external dialer such as Zoom Phone, your Gong Dialer business numbers are retained for 10 days. If you switch back to the Gong Dialer within those 10 days, your numbers are still available. If you switch to the external dialer again during that period, the 10-day retention window starts over.

The following are not available while using an external dialer:

- Dialer recording settings configured for mobile
- Your Trust Hub profile and trusted calling configuration
- Business phone numbers (except personal numbers for mobile)
- Regulations submitted for the Gong Dialer
- Email notifications about submitted regulatory documentation
- Call notes

Gong’s AI-driven sales engagement solution that helps sales teams prioritize, personalize, and automate outreach activities to accelerate their pipelines. Access to features depends on your company’s plan and your assigned seat.

chunks.text:
Who can use this: Any team memberAvailable on: Any Gong plan

Where to go: Conversations > Search

Save time by taking bulk actions on calls. Actions you can take include sharing multiple calls, setting calls as private, moving calls to another workspace, and more. Your ability to take some of these actions depends on your permission profile. Some of the actions are only available to call owners and admins.

chunks.title: Take bulk actions on calls

chunks.text:
Select multiple calls:
1. Go to Conversations > Search and filter for the calls you want to take action on.
2. Hover over the left side of the calls to show selection boxes beside each call.
3. Select at least one call to show a floating bar at the bottom of the page. From this bar, you can:
  - Share > Share internally to share calls with colleagues using Gong. Learn more
  - Share > Share with customers to share the calls externally, or with people at your company who don’t use Gong. Learn more
  - > Set as private to set calls that you own to private. Learn more
  - > Move from workspace to move calls to a different workspace. Learn more
  - > Delete to remove calls altogether from Gong. Learn more
4. Select up to 10 calls per page, or choose Select all from the floating action bar to select all of the calls at once.

chunks.text:
Select multiple calls > Considerations:
Share

- Share up to 100 calls at one time. When sharing multiple calls with customers, the customer gets a single email with links to the calls.

Set as private

- Set up to 100 calls as private at one time.
- If you select multiple calls to set as private but don’t have permission to set them all as private because you are not the call owner for all of them, you’ll be able to set the ones you own as private. The rest of the calls will remain public.

Delete

- Only company tech admins can delete multiple calls at one time.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

With Gong recording your calls, you can focus on the conversation without having to take notes. For example, Gong automatically picks up points of interest in a call so you see what questions were raised. Trackers automatically detect concepts and phrases that you may have missed in the original conversation.

That said, if you want to take notes in real-time, you can do this with the in-app notepad. If the call is pushed as a Task to Salesforce, these notes will be pushed with the call.

chunks.text:
How to take notes:
1. While on a call that’s being recorded, go to the homepage and locate the live call in the Conversations widget.
2. Click Take notes. The notepad opens to the right of your screen.
3. Click Post Note when you've finished. Your note is timestamped and appears in the comments section of the call. Anyone how has access to the call will be able to see the note.

Tip: If your company is using the native Zoom recorder, use the Gong app for Zoom to take notes, collaborate with colleagues during the call, and more.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

chunks.text:
What’s a target attainment widget:
With target attainment widgets, you can track key performance metrics against targets over time. To simplify the view and allow viewers to see whether people are on the right track at a glance, you may assign different colors to value ranges in table view. Viewers can also toggle between team and individual views.

Target attainment widgets support Fiscal date pickers only and don’t support Rolling range date pickers.

chunks.title: Target attainment widget

chunks.text:
Building a target attainment widget:
1. Select your dashboard, click +New widget, and select Target attainment from the gallery.
2. In the dashboard header, click the edit icon to rename your widget and, optionally, + Add description.
3. Under Metric, select the metric to include in the widget. You can rename it by clicking and then Rename metric. Click + New metric to create a new metric, and then pull it to your Target attainment widget. Click to edit an existing metric and click Save.
4. Check Measure against target to show the attainment value (metric/target percentage value) for each team or period.
5. To assign display color to value ranges:
  1. In the Preview pane, change the display to Table.
  2. Color code the metric’s values, and apply green, yellow, and red indications to different ranges. Note:If Measure against target is selected, the ranges reflect the attainment value, rather than the metric’s value.
6. Select your Drilldown view: The view that opens up when viewers click to inspect the deals/accounts included in the widget.
7. You may add any filter (+Add filter) that defines which deals/accounts qualify to be included in the widger. For example, deals in which Sales qualified is true and Deal stage is neither Closed-won nor Closed-lost.
8. Below your metric, under Select team and period, you’ll notice the team member and date fields are set to be dynamic and respond to whatever is selected in your dashboard. You can change them to fixed values. Note:If you select fixed values for the team member and period, the widget would no longer respond to selections made on the dashboard level. The team selection will be applied to the selected metrics’ team member field, and the period selection will be applied to the selected metrics’ date field.
9. Select breakdown options: Breakdown by period and/or Breakdown by team. Note:To break down by both period and individuals, switch to table view.
10. Play with the Preview options on the right to validate your settings. When you’re happy with the results, click Save.

chunks.text:
Best practices:
To get the most out of target attainment widgets, we recommend:

Using color coding sensibly

The color coding should make sense for all teams/periods if the dashboard widget is set to work with dynamic teams and periods.

Therefore, use color coding only for metrics that have a standard definition of good across different teams and periods (such as win rate, ASP, attainment) and not metrics like Bookings or Pipeline created that can vary between teams and periods.

Using different ways to compare

To compare two periods’ target attainment, you can:

- Place two target attainment widgets side-by-side
- Place one target attainment widget at the top of the dashboard and a few KPI widgets, one for each metric included in the performance widget, underneath it.

Team hierarchy defines which team members report to which managers. It enables you to see stats and deal data per team, filter calls by teams, make sure feedback requests go to the right person, and more. By default, every company starts with a single hierarchy. A single rep is assigned a single manager, who may be assigned their own manager, rolling upwards.

When team hierarchy is set up correctly you can:

- See stats and deal data per team
- Filter calls by specific teams
- Ensure that feedback requests on calls go to the correct manager (appears in the Activity queue)
- Do bulk actions on teams such as change data capture settings and assign permission profiles.

When updating hierarchy in the team members page, it can take from a few minutes up to a couple of hours to update across Gong, for example in the call filters and Activity page.

You can create hierarchy automatically through automatic provisioning or manually on the Team members page.

chunks.text:
About multiple hierarchies:
Note:This capability is in limited availability. For details on setting it up, contact your Gong rep.

Large organizations may have more than one hierarchy to support their sales departments. For example, a rep may have one manager based on what they sell and another manager based on where they sell. Multiple hierarchies enable you to assign more than one manager to a single rep. Multiple managers can then coach that rep, view stats, and more, according to the hierarchy they choose.

Setting up an additional hierarchy:
1. Contact your Gong rep to make sure you’re in the beta.
2. Go to Admin center > Settings > Hierarchies.
3. Click + Add hierarchy.
4. Give the hierarchy a name and add a description.

Once you’ve created a new hierarchy, you’ll be able to assign team members to managers under that hierarchy. This can be done in bulk or manually.

Note:We use email addresses as the unique identifier for Gong users. To assign an alternative manager to a team member, both the manager and the team member must be Gong users.

Filter according to new hierarchies:
Once you’ve assigned managers in the additional hierarchy to team members, you can use the hierarchy selector in the Team Members page to view a hierarchy’s full organization tree.

In Gong, team members can choose which hierarchy they want to view in the following pages:

- Conversations > Search: Filter call participants according to a specific team
- Coaching: Managers can filter according to reps on their teams
- Insights: Data can be filtered according to any hierarchy
- Home: Managers choose which hierarchy they want to view
- Revenue > Deals: Filter deals according to any hierarchy

chunks.text:
FAQs:
Can managers see all of their reports from all hierarchy types at the same time?

No, managers can select a single hierarchy at once, and see their reports in that hierarchy.

Where can I set new hierarchies for team members?

Once a hierarchy has been added, you can set team member hierarchy on their settings page.

Where in the platform are additional hierarchies visible?

Additional hierarchies can be seen in the following areas:

- Conversations > Search: Filter call participants according to a specific team
- Coaching: Managers can filter according to reps on their teams
- Insights: Data can be filtered according to any hierarchy
- Home: Managers choose which hierarchy they want to view
- Revenue > Deals: Filter deals according to any hierarchy

Is there a limit to the number of hierarchies we can create?

This depends on your plan:

- Coaching and Professional plans: 3
- Enterprise plan: 25

Reach out to your Revenue Architect (RA) if you need more hierarchies.

Can a single manager belong to more than one hierarchy?

Yes, managers can belong to multiple hierarchies.

How do I download reports according to a specific hierarchy?

Once you select a hierarchy in the company settings page, any report you download will be aligned with that hierarchy.

Can I delete a hierarchy?

You can delete any hierarchy except for the default one. To delete a hierarchy, go to Company Settings > Hierarchies and click the trash can beside the hierarchy name. This removes any team members from the hierarchy and can’t be undone.

chunks.text:
To-dos created by you:
These include one-off to-dos you can create for yourself. Use them to set yourself reminders, to plan your day, or to break down your next step for a deal or an account into smaller action items. You do not need to be the contact or lead owner to create an associated one-off to-do.

When creating a one-off to-do, you can choose the to-do type: email, call, or task.

Depending on which task type you choose, the to-do appears in the To-dos page under its respective column. The to-do type is set to Email by default.

For a one-off to-do where you've selected email or call as to-do type, selecting the person you want to email or call is required. For leads, no account will be shown. For contacts, the connected account will be shown automatically.

For a one-off to-do where you've selected task as to-do type, selecting a person is optional. If you select a lead from the list, the account field is disabled. You can also leave the Person field blank and just choose an account.

Adding a specific time to the due date is optional. Click Show time to add a time.

You can also assign a priority level. Priority levels include Low, Medium, High, and Critical. All to-dos default to Medium unless updated.

To associate a one-off to-do with a deal, you need to be a deal owner.

You can create a one-off to-do and assign it to another team member. This helps clarify priorities and next steps across your team and keeps work visible in the right context.

Who can use this: Any team memberAvailable on: Gong EngageIdeal for: Sales rep

Why does a to-do appear when I've already sent a follow-up mail?

Gong monitors your email, and we mark to-dos as done when we identify that you sent a follow-up mail. Sometimes, typically if you sent a follow-up email during or just after the call, we might miss it and miss marking the to-do done.

Does writing an email directly from a to-do require a new permission?

Yes, it does. The first time you click WRITE EMAIL, Gong asks you for permission to write emails. Giving Gong this permission means the emails you compose in Gong are integrated with your email client (Gmail or Office365) and sent directly from them. This means:

- Emails you send appear in your client Sent folder.
- Emails you compose but don't send appear in your email client Drafts folder.
- If the to-do was triggered from an existing email thread (for example, an Out of Office reply), the email is included in the existing thread in your email client.

Are the emails that I send directly from to-dos tracked?

Yes, they are! Emails sent from Gong are tracked for "Email open" events and "Email links clicked" events, and are displayed as events in the deal activity timeline.

Are there any admin permissions that relate to sending emails from to-dos?

If you’re a tech admin, you can opt out of this capability for your entire account. To do this, go to Company Settings and in the Data Capture section, select the email provider that you integrate with Gong (Gmail or Office 365). Under Connection Import Settings, deselect the Allow team members to send emails via Gong toggle.

chunks.text:
Under Connection Import Settings, deselect the Allow team members to send emails via Gong toggle.

Why is the link to the call recording set to expire in a certain amount of days?

The access period for shared call is defined in your company settings. Contact your Gong admin to change the default.

Why does a to-do say it will be removed tonight

AI-generated to-dos are removed after 7 days in order to keep your to-dos current and relevant.

Where do the action items come from?

Gong picks up action items that were mentioned on the call by you or other attendees, and surfaces them in the to-do to make sure you don't miss anything in your follow-up.

Do all the calls that I host trigger to-dos?

No. Calls that are less than 10 minutes long, or only include participants from your company, do not trigger a to-do to follow-up.

I'm not seeing Gong-recommended to-dos. Why not?

To-dos will show for organizations with a CRM integration and with emails imported to Gong. If you think you should be seeing to-dos, talk to your Gong admin.

What happens to to-dos when a contact or lead is deleted in the CRM?

When a contact or lead is deleted in the CRM, their flow is stopped, and any associated flow to-dos are deleted from Gong. Any associated non-flow to-dos created manually by you or other team members will not be deleted.

Which to-dos are supported in languages besides English?

Fully supported in languages besides English: call/meeting follow up, meeting confirmation, intro, no next meeting

Why is the link to the call recording set to expire in a certain amount of days?

The access period for shared call is defined in your company settings. Contact your Gong admin to change the default.

Why does a to-do say it will be removed tonight

AI-generated to-dos are removed after 7 days in order to keep your to-dos current and relevant.

Where do the action items come from?

Gong picks up action items that were mentioned on the call by you or other attendees, and surfaces them in the to-do to make sure you don't miss anything in your follow-up.

Do all the calls that I host trigger to-dos?

No. Calls that are less than 10 minutes long, or only include participants from your company, do not trigger a to-do to follow-up.

I'm not seeing Gong-recommended to-dos. Why not?

To-dos will show for organizations with a CRM integration and with emails imported to Gong. If you think you should be seeing to-dos, talk to your Gong admin.

What happens to to-dos when a contact or lead is deleted in the CRM?

When a contact or lead is deleted in the CRM, their flow is stopped, and any associated flow to-dos are deleted from Gong. Any associated non-flow to-dos created manually by you or other team members will not be deleted.

Which to-dos are supported in languages besides English?

Fully supported in languages besides English: call/meeting follow up, meeting confirmation, intro, no next meeting
chunks.title: To-dos FAQs

chunks.text:
Partially supported in languages besides English: nudge, response, back from OOO

For AI-generated follow-up emails, they are generated in the same language as the call.

Why is my auto email appearing as a manual email in my to-do list?

Auto emails will only appear in your to-do list if they fail to send, in which case they become manual emails. Auto emails can fail to send if:

- There are missing variables
- The thread is missing
- The recipient email address is missing
- Your email account was disconnected
- Your email provider hit its rate limit

To find out why your auto email didn't send and send it manually, go to the To-dos page and hover over the to-do to.

What happens if an email address is marked as invalid?

If the contact or lead has an email address that's marked as invalid before the email gets sent, we convert that auto email to a manual email that appears on the rep's To-dos page. The rep can then replace the email address and resend the email.

Note: If no email is currently queued to send and you mark the top email address on a contact or lead record as invalid, Gong moves that address to the bottom of that person’s saved email address list.

What happens if an email bounces?

If an email bounces, we:

- Automatically mark the email address as invalid
- Automatically pause the person's flow
- Generate a to-do for the rep to replace the email address and send again
- Automatically save that new email address for the contact or lead to prevent the next email from bouncing

If your auto emails are still being sent to email addresses that are marked as invalid in Gong, contact support.

chunks.text:
Get analytics on your slides:
Sales decks are a valuable business resource and marketers invest a lot of time designing new ones. Using slide analytics, you can check how individuals and teams are adopting the latest sales deck.

To get analytics on your slides, filter calls based on slide titles that were presented, and the amount of time they were shown. Here’s how:

1. Go to Conversations > Search.
2. Click Add filters.
3. Click Screen share and select Words or phrases in slide title.
4. Now add the words or phrases from the slide title you need, for example ‘Customer success testimonial.’
5. Use the slider to select a time range for how long the slide is shown.
6. Remember to refine your selection using the additional filters.

You’ll now see a library of the calls where that slide was shown. View the chart at the top of the page to see trends for slide usage.

Tip:Want to watch the part of the call where they show the slide? Open the call page, click Points of interest, and select Slides. Click on the slide you’re interested in to go straight to the right place.

chunks.text:
Create customized smart trackers:
As a marketer, you’re constantly creating valuable new messaging for the sales team, who are the frontline to the customer. But how often is your new material being referenced in calls?

Smart trackers let you train Gong to locate very specific themes, regardless of the wording, so Gong can leverage AI to identify them in past and new calls. You can then easily find relevant calls, create statistics relating to these concepts, and also use trackers in initiative boards to measure how these talk tracks relate to deal success.

Note:To customize your own smart trackers, you’ll need a database of at least 500 calls. You should also have at least 200 occurrences of the topic in your team's conversations. If you don’t have that many calls yet, try building a keyword tracker.

Here’s how to customize your own smart tracker:

1. Go to Admin center > Agent studio.
2. Click Settings on the AI Tracker card.
3. Click Create tracker and select Smart tracker.
4. Choose a name, description, and how you want to filter the calls.
5. Provide at least 5 sentences that reflect the concept you want to track.
6. Gong will now create a set of sentences from your existing calls. Tag the sentences with YES, NO, or NOT SURE so the model learns which ones match your concept and which ones don’t.
7. In Review model, you’ll be able to evaluate the results. Click Activate and your new smart tracker is ready to use.

Creating customized smart trackers has several stages so we suggest you read this article or consult with your company’s Gong admin for a more guided approach.

chunks.text:
Use initiative boards to measure success*:
Now that you’ve created trackers for the key messaging you want the sales team to use, an initiative board will provide data and trends on which teams and individuals are adopting your initiatives. By choosing to view results by deals, you can also get valuable data on whether the new initiative’s messaging is having a positive impact on the business.

Once your initiative board is ready, you can compare and view adoption trends over time. You can also drill-down into the deal percentage to see tracker data in the context of deal wins and losses, allowing you to promote the benefits of your project, or assess the need to adjust your messaging or training.

Follow these steps to create a new initiative board:

1. Go to Insights > Initiatives > Create new board.
2. Choose a name, description, and that you want to view results by deals–which shows the percentage of deals in which tracker terms were mentioned during the deal. You can also view the results by calls to see the percentage of calls in which tracker terms were mentioned.
3. Add your smart tracker or keyword tracker. Set the percentages below and above which you want initiative adoption to be measured. You can add as many trackers as you like but we suggest no more than 6.
4. Optional: Choose filters and/or a call category so that you can focus on specific types of calls, opportunities, and accounts.

See these articles for more support creating initiative boards and using them to track adoption of your initiatives.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.
