Troubleshooting:
Why can't I see Activity?

Contact your business admin to make sure your permission profile allows you to see Activity.

The current time indicator seems wrong

The red line shows you the current time so you can see what's happening right now. Check your time zone settings in your profile if you think the current time is incorrect.

Someone's schedule is empty

Someone's schedule may appear empty for several reasons:

- They haven't connected their calendar to Gong
- Their calendar sync is experiencing issues
- They're not part of the team hierarchy

Check with the team member first. If everything seems configured correctly, contact your technical admin for assistance.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

A team member who manages a team of sales reps.

A leader who oversees multiple sales managers.

chunks.text:
How to view deal drivers for a particular team:
Where to go: Revenue > Analytics > Drivers

Set up your deal driver metrics by selecting the right filters. Here's how:

1. Team. Search for and select the manager whose team you want to view.
2. Show risk for. Use trends to see whether coaching has helped to improve an individual's scores. Select a time period to view trends over:
  1. Now – a snapshot of the current state.
  2. Last 30 days - data from the last month.
  3. Last 90 days – data from the last quarter.
3. Based on deal board. Select the deal board usually used to see the team's pipeline.

A set of metrics for the selected team will be displayed, with the number of deals they had open (for at least 1 day in the selected time range), and the percentage of deals that had a warning for at least one day during the selected time period.

Note:No next call indicates no scheduled calls in the next 12 weeks.

- The warnings and their threshold settings make up the table columns.
- In each column, the 3 scores with the highest percentage will be highlighted yellow, and show where more attention is needed. For example, if a large proportion of an individual's deals only have one contact engaged on the prospect side, it's probably a good time for some reinforcement on approaches for multi-threading.
- The highest percentage will appear in the brightest yellow, and means that warning was triggered on more deals for that individual.
- If more than 3 individuals have a high percentage, it suggests that the entire team needs training on that factor.
- Click in a cell to see the deals where the warning was flagged. Then click VIEW DEAL to go to the account page.
- The scores are specific to all deals on the selected deal board, its relevant warnings and their set thresholds. To change the metrics shown for the selected deal board, either edit it or create a new deal board with the warnings and filters you want to see. For example, to focus your coaching efforts on how reps are handling late stage deals.

How activities appear in Salesforce > One task per Gong activity:
When this option is enabled, Gong creates a single Salesforce task for each Gong activity.

The task includes all related context in custom fields, such as:

- All activity participants
- All associated accounts
- All associated opportunities

This option keeps the Salesforce activity timeline concise and avoids duplicate tasks. Reps review the full context by opening the task and checking the populated Gong fields.

This option is commonly used by teams that prefer a single source of truth for each activity.

We know that not every meeting gets recorded, for example, face-to-face meetings, customer-scheduled calls, or when a web-conference URL is not included in the invite.

However, it's important to track every customer interaction so you can gain important visibility into deal progress and insights into buying signals by viewing meetings that take place but are not scheduled for recording.

No matter what your role is, this helps you to:

- Learn if deal activity cadence is on course

- Review the invitees to make sure the right people are on the call

- Review the meeting description to understand the purpose of the meeting.

We pull meetings associated with CRM contacts into Gong when they appear in your calendar, regardless of whether or not they are accepted, and regardless of whether or not they are recorded, with the exception of private calls. They appear alongside your recorded meetings and other events in your activity timeline, which is available via the Deals page tabs, in the Account console, and the Activity page.

Meetings without scheduled recordings are shown with theicon. They are marked as Not recorded if they already took place, and Will not be recorded if they're in the future.

Some things to note about meetings without scheduled recording:

- They do count as activity when we calculate deal warnings.
- They can be deleted from Gong by the host or any participant in the Activity page

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Gong data is sent via APIs to Salesforce. Each API call has a standard batch size and the amount of data sent in each API request is based on this batch size. In certain situations, such as when there is a lot of data to update or where your Salesforce instance is processing data from other applications, it might be necessary to adjust the batch size to avoid throttling in Salesforce.

Gong checks the status of your Salesforce instance to assess whether the batch size of the API calls should be adjusted or not, and when necessary, automatically changes the batch size.

You can see the current batch size in the Salesforce integration page.

chunks.title: Viewing the funnel widget

chunks.text:
Dive into your funnel > Funnel-level supportive metrics:
The following metrics are displayed at the top of the view:

- Deals total: The total value of all deals that entered the funnel, alongside the total count of individual deals.

Note:A deal is included in the report as long as it passed through at least one stage (not including closed-won). If it were ingested into the pipeline at a later stage rather than the first one, we consider it as though it had passed through the early stages, but exclude the time it spent in each stage from the calculation to prevent misinformation and maintain pipeline hygiene.

- Funnel win rate: The percentage of won deals out of the total deal count.

Note:If you see discrepancies between the deal board and the funnel widget data, it's because the funnel’s “won” category includes all potential “win” stages, even those that aren’t part of your deal board.

- Avg time to convert: The average time it took for a deal to move from the first stage in the funnel to the last one (closed-won).
- Avg deal size: The average monetary value of closed-won deals.

The table below the bar chart show stage-level metrics:

- Deals total: The total value of all deals in the stage.

- Top-of-funnel conversion: The percentage of deals that made it to the current stage out of the funnel’s initial deal count.
- Stage win rate: The percentage of deals that made it to the last stage in the funnel out of the stage’s total deal count.
- Avg days in stage: The average monetary value of each deal, calculated by dividing deals total by the deal count.

chunks.text:
Set up in Vonage:
Make sure you complete the following steps in Vonage Contact Center (formerly NewVoiceMedia) before enabling the integration:

1. Log into Vonage with an admin user that has permissions to create API credentials.
2. In the VCC portal click API Credentials. If this option isn’t available, ask your Vonage CSM / support team to enable it for you.
3. Create API credentials with read access to the interaction content and user admin API endpoints. The user can also have write access, but this is not required for the integration. Contact your Vonage CSM or Vonage support if the user you logged in with doesn’t have read access to the API endpoints and can’t create the API credentials.
4. Make a note of the Vonage Client ID, Client secret, and Region. You’ll need this when setting up the integration in Gong.
5. Make sure calls are set to be recorded in Vonage.

You can now proceed with the integration in Gong.

chunks.text:
How meetings are recorded:
Meetings are recorded in one of the following ways:

- Gong bot. A virtual participant, responsible for recording the call, is added to the meeting. Available for all web conferencing integrations.
- Native recording. Recording is via the provider’s native recording functionality, with no additional participant added to the call. Native recording is only available with Zoom.

If a meeting isn’t set to record automatically, hosts can add the Gong bot to the meeting by including the Gong assistant in the list of meeting participants. These meetings are recorded either with the Gong bot or natively in Zoom, depending on your settings.

Note:If a meeting is recorded with the Gong bot and has a waiting room enabled, the host must admit the bot to start the recording. With native Zoom recording, clicking the record button starts the recording, even when a waiting room is in use.

With native Zoom recording, Zoom records the call directly, no Gong bot is added. This results in better audio quality and more accurate speaker identification. Team members can also install the Gong app for Zoom to take notes, collaborate, and receive real-time insights on their speaking time during calls.

You can set up your system for both native Zoom recording and recording with the Gong bot.

To set up native Zoom recording, see Zoom integration overview.

chunks.title: Webex integration

chunks.text:
Required permissions and scopes > Manage meetings:
- Permission (scopes): Create, manage, or cancel meetings of any Webex user in your organization
- What it does: Allows Gong to create, update, and delete meetings in Webex on behalf of your team members.

When a user schedules a meeting using the Gong add-on, Gong creates a corresponding Webex meeting so the recording consent link is mapped to the correct Webex meeting link. If a meeting is rescheduled or canceled in Gong, the update is automatically reflected in Webex.

chunks.title: What is a Revenue Architect (RA)?

chunks.text:
What your Revenue Architect can help with:
Your Revenue Architect focuses on activating your go-to-market strategy through Gong, driving feature adoption across your organization, and helping you reach your revenue outcome goals.

They can help you:

- Recommend what Gong features to activate to best achieve your business goals: Accelerate to outcomes like improving forecast accuracy, growing new business, or reducing churn, by setting up the relevant Gong workflows, behaviors, and metrics.
- Deepen how Gong fits into your company operations: Consult on how you can embed Gong into deal reviews, forecasting processes, rep and manager coaching, product feedback mechanisms, business insights, quarterly planning and more so it becomes part of the fabric of how you run your revenue organization.
- Drive adoption among team members: Clarify who should use what, when, and how (by role or team), and agree on what success looks like over time.
- Review results and plan next steps: Help you assess what’s working ahead of key milestones (like renewals or new rollouts), what’s blocked, and what to prioritize achieving next with Gong.
- Get best‑practice, outcome‑focused guidance: Ask “What’s the best way to use Gong to achieve this goal?” rather than “Where is this setting?”. Your Revenue Architect is there to guide your strategic use of Gong’s platform.

In addition to having access to a Revenue Architect, you also have resources such as Gong's Help Center, the Gong Academy, and our Visioneers Community, as well as the Gong Assistant which can answer many questions instantly.

Note:Your Revenue Architect doesn’t handle: Implementation or configuration projects Technical troubleshooting: Our Technical Support Team are always on hand to assist with this. Pricing, contracts, and commercial negotiations: Your Account Executive or Renewal Manager will be happy to assist with this.

Data capture is the term used for how Gong identifies and imports interactions with your customers. Gong captures and imports your activities, such as telephony calls, emails, and web conference meetings. We then analyze your activities and apply AI capabilities to provide insights as to how you can improve your organization, teams and deals, and suggest next steps for your sales managers and account executives.

Depending on your setup, Gong can capture the following:

- Voice based customer activities, such as telephony calls, web conference calls
- Text based customer activities, such as emails and text messages
- Digital interactions, such as customers signing documents or viewing your website

Setting up an integration with your CRM will enable us to enrich your activities by adding business context information together with your activities.

chunks.title: What is Data capture?

chunks.text:
What data is imported?:
Data imported for telephony calls:

- The audio recording, recorded by the external provider (such as, RingCentral, 8x8, ZoomPhone)
- Call metadata, captured by the external provider
- Call attempts and calls without recordings

Data imported for web conference calls:

- Audio and video files: These can be recorded either by adding the Gong bot to the call, or if your provider is Zoom, set up the native Zoom integration so that calls can be recorded and ingested into Gong by Zoom.
- Web conference metadata: details about the call are imported regardless of whether the call was recorded.

Data imported for emails:

- Email subject and body, timestamps, recipients, and metadata

Data imported for text messages:

- SMS participants, SMS body text

Data imported for digital interactions: Gong integrates with a variety of platforms to provide a comprehensive view of the customer’s digital footprint. Those platforms include:

- Content Management System (CMS) digital interactions
- Video Management System (VMS) digital interactions
- Gifting Platforms digital interactions
- Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ) digital interactions
- Buyer Intent digital interactions
chunks.body:
Data imported for telephony calls:

- The audio recording, recorded by the external provider (such as, RingCentral, 8x8, ZoomPhone)
- Call metadata, captured by the external provider
- Call attempts and calls without recordings

Data imported for web conference calls:

- Audio and video files: These can be recorded either by adding the Gong bot to the call, or if your provider is Zoom, set up the native Zoom integration so that calls can be recorded and ingested into Gong by Zoom.
- Web conference metadata: details about the call are imported regardless of whether the call was recorded.

Data imported for emails:

- Email subject and body, timestamps, recipients, and metadata

Data imported for text messages:

- SMS participants, SMS body text

Data imported for digital interactions: Gong integrates with a variety of platforms to provide a comprehensive view of the customer’s digital footprint. Those platforms include:

- Content Management System (CMS) digital interactions
- Video Management System (VMS) digital interactions
- Gifting Platforms digital interactions
- Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ) digital interactions
- Buyer Intent digital interactions
chunks.title: What is Data capture?

chunks.text:
How is the data used?:
Data captured by Gong is spread across the platform, for example, calls can be seen and listened to in the Home page, Conversations and Deals. Emails are displayed in the activity timeline for deal boards. Captured data is also used in Engage for advanced features like AI-generated follow-up emails and AI-generated call outcomes. Deal likelihood, deal warnings, the Win/Loss analysis, insights and coaching depend on captured data to provide analysis on your deal health and team productivity.

Gong supports more than 70 languages, making it easier for global teams to capture, understand, and share what happens in every conversation. Frequently asked questions:
What’s the difference between AI Translator and languages spoken during calls?

Languages spoken during calls help Gong identify the language used on your calls for transcription. AI Translator controls the language of translated and AI-generated content you see in Gong. AI Translator does not change the language Gong uses to transcribe calls. Spoken languages and AI Translator are separate settings. AI Translator changes the language of translated transcripts and AI-generated content in Gong.

What languages are available in the Gong Help Center?

Currently, the Gong Help Center is only available in English.

Does changing my UI display language affect transcription or AI translation?

No. These are separate settings. Transcription language is determined by the language spoken on the call. AI translation is configured separately in your profile or by your admin.

Does changing my UI display language translate CRM content in Gong?

No. UI display language only affects the Gong interface. CRM data appears in whatever language it was entered in your CRM.

What language does the Gong Assistant use to answer my questions?

The Gong Assistant responds in the language used in the question. If you ask a question in German, Gong Assistant responds in German.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

chunks.text:
The Gong API is available to all partners and customers and enables them to:

- Send a call recorded by other systems. This is the audio of the call and should include the channel the company's representative spoke on.
- Retrieve analyzed call data from Gong, such as internal and external participants, topics, trackers, public comments, scorecards, and call transcripts.
- Retrieve all team members who used Gong and when.
- See daily user activity.
- See your users' interaction statistics.
- Upload call data to Gong from any telephony system or recorder. This enables the calls to be fully transcribed and analyzed.
- Upload your CRM data to Gong so that your CRM data is displayed together with your activities such as conversations. In addition, you can see all your customer interactions, see trends in your pipeline, get warnings on deals that are at risk, and assess your forecast based on real data.

See the API documentation here.

When you import Gong data into your systems, you access the wealth of information Gong extracts about your team members and their calls. Build custom reporting and custom workflows around this data to yield end-to-end insights and create end-to-end optimized processes.

For example:

- Keep track of calls made to customers. Create custom objects to import call data to your CRM (not required for Salesforce).
- Correlate between user stats in Gong to external data. For example, does listening to calls in Gong increase deal success metrics?
- Import Gong calls, transcripts, scorecards, and stats data into your BI solution, e.g. Tableau, to understand what’s happening in your salesforce.

Rate limits:
API rate limits are:

- 3 API calls per second, and 10,000 API calls per day.
- When the rate of API calls exceeds these limits an HTTP status code 429 is returned and the Retry-After header indicates how many seconds to wait before making a new request.

*The features available to you depend on your company’s plan and your assigned seats.

chunks.text:
Permissions required by Gong:
Gong requires the following access for the following MS Graph API permission scopes:

| Permissions |  |
| --- | --- |
| Mail.Read | Required for importing Office 365 emails. Used when import emails is enabled. |
| Calendars.ReadCalendars.Read.Shared | Required for importing Office 365 calendars and calendar events. Used when calendar import is enabled. |
| User.Read.AllUser.Read | Required for retrieving Office 365 user IDs to use in user-specific API calls when importing emails, calendars, and photos. |
| Group.Read.All | Required for retrieving Office 365 group information for troubleshooting only. |
| OpenID Connect: openid | Required for user-by-user connections, so that Gong can view user profile data |
| OpenID Connect: email | Required for user-by-user connections, so that Gong can read the user’s primary email address |
| OpenID Connect: profile | Required for user-by-user connections, so that Gong can see user’s basic profile such as name, picture, user name, email address |
| OpenID Connect: offline_access | Required for user-by-user connections. Enables Gong to view and update the data you’ve granted access to, even when you’re not actively using Office 365. This does not provide any additional permissions. |

chunks.title: When calls are on air

chunks.text:
When calls are recorded natively by Zoom:
ON AIR typically shows about 15 minutes before the meeting is scheduled to start. If the meeting is started before the scheduled time, it shows when the meeting starts.

If you have back-to-back meetings and are using your personal room link, ON AIR shows at least 5 minutes before the scheduled start time.

ON AIR stops showing at the scheduled end time if the meeting has ended in Zoom. If the meeting continues, ON AIR will continue to show until the meeting ends, up to a maximum of 6 hours after the scheduled end time.

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

See credit usage:
View your credit balance and usage details in Gong.

To view your company’s credit usage:

1. From the left sidebar, click Admin center.
2. In the Settings tab, click Gong credits under Reports.

The Gong credits page shows:

- Credits: Your credit balance shown as a progress bar, including the number of credits used out of your total and the next annual reset date
- Credits used: The percentage of credits consumed and the number of credits used out of your total
- Credits will run out in: The estimated number of days until your credits are exhausted, based on usage over the last 30 days
- Average daily usage: The average number of credits consumed per day, based on usage over the last 30 days

chunks.text:
What to use instead: AI Theme Spotter:
AI Theme Spotter is an AI agent that helps you analyze the voice of the customer at scale by automatically detecting recurring patterns across large sets of calls. Instead of defining topics manually, AI Theme Spotter uses AI Tracker detections to surface insights that are difficult to identify on your own.

With AI Theme Spotter, you can:

- Identify recurring customer themes across up to 20,000 calls per analysis
- Analyze conversations in all supported languages
- Focus on business questions like customer pain, objections, pricing reactions, and decision criteria
- Explore and share out results to inform strategy

This makes it easier to move from individual conversations to meaningful, company-wide insights.

A common use case: Understanding buyer decisions at scale:
If you previously used Whisper for Topics to analyze customer conversations, AI Theme Spotter is the improved way to do this today.

Example:You want to understand the most common factors influencing buyer decisions mentioned in recent calls.

With AI Theme Spotter, you can:

1. Go to Insights > AI Theme Spotter and create a new analysis
2. Choose a business question from the drop-down list related to buyer decisions
3. Narrow the scope using call filters like date range, deal stage, or account attributes
4. Let Gong analyze the calls and surface recurring themes

The result is a clear view of what customers are consistently talking about—without manual topic setup.

Refer to this screenshot to understand the analysis.

1. The question asked in the analysis
2. Filters that were applied to the analysis, and the period covered by it
3. The number of themes identified while answering the question, and the number of calls and accounts in which these themes were mentioned
4. A breakdown of each theme according to the percentage of analyzed calls it appeared in, how many deals and accounts these calls reflect, and the revenue associated with these deals
5. Each theme, clearly named, and a short summary
6. Click View details to see a drill-down into the theme and its subthemes

chunks.title: Troubleshooting: Why can't I see some deals?

chunks.text:
Find out why deals are missing:
Where to go: Revenue > Deals

1. If your tab or entire board is empty, you can either:
  1. Click Find out why.
  2. From the deal board menu, click Missing some deals?
2. Go to your CRM and open a deal you think should be showing.
3. From the deal’s URL, copy the ID: For example if the deal url is: https://gong.salesforce.com/0012v00002HlkT0AA The ID is: 0012v00002HlkT0AA Note:CRM platforms may vary in the url structure. Make sure you copy a valid ID. Avoid copying entire URLs, account names, or deal names.
4. Paste the ID back into Gong and click Submit. We’ll tell you why the deal isn’t showing.

chunks.headingPath: Find out why deals are missing
chunks.title: Troubleshooting: Why can't I see some deals?

chunks.text:
Possible reasons that your deal isn’t showing:
If a deal isn’t showing, it may be due to the following reasons:

The deal isn’t synced with Gong yet

Try refreshing the page. In a few minutes, if you still can’t see the deal, contact your admin.

The deal is being filtered out by the board or tab settings

Check the filters in the board settings.

If you think it belongs in this board, or if you don’t have access to the board settings, contact your admin.

The deal is being filtered out by your custom filters or groups

Try adjusting your filters to show the deal.

The deal is on a different tab

Search for the deal to find out which tab, as explained above. If you think the deal belongs in the currently selected tab, contact your admin.

The team member isn’t a member of the selected team

At the top left corner of the board, select a team that includes the team member associated with the deal (for example, the deal’s owner).

The close date is outside the selected period

For example, the deal’s close date is Aug 18, 2024, while the currently selected period is Q4, FY 2025.

At the top left corner of the board, try selecting a period that includes the date associated with the deal.

Everything matches, but the deal is still not showing

It may be because:

- You don’t have permission to view it
- It’s not associated with an account
- The user associated with the account isn’t a provisioned Gong user
- The user associated with the deal is set as hidden

For further help, contact your Gong admin or open a support ticket.

Filters can be combined in different ways to refine search results. Understanding how filters work can help you build more accurate searches and find the conversations you need.
chunks.title: Work with filters

chunks.text:
Filter calls that match any specified value:
Many filters allow you to select multiple values.

When multiple values are selected in the same text area or drop down, conversations that match any of the selected values are returned.

For example, if you select Adam Smith and John Browner in the Participants filter, the results include calls that contain Adam, John, or both participants.

The same behavior applies to other filters that allow multiple values to be selected.
chunks.body:

The same behavior applies to other filters that allow multiple values to be selected.
chunks.headingPath: Filter calls that match any specified value
chunks.title: Work with filters

chunks.text:
Filter calls that that match all specified values:
Some filters include an Add icon that let you add another instance of the same filter.

When multiple instances of the same filter are added, calls must match all filter criteria.

For example, if one participant filter contains Adam Smith and a second participant filter contains John Browner, the results only include conversations that contain both Sarah and John.

This can be useful when you want to find conversations involving specific combinations of participants, terms, or other filter values.

Use free-text filters:
Some filters allow you to enter your own search terms instead of selecting values from a predefined list. These filters include:

- Words or phrases
- Call title
- Words or phrases in slide title
- Text in comment on call

Free-text filters support search operators that help you find more specific results.

For example:"price" + "discount"

chunks.title: Work with filters

chunks.text:
Use free-text filters > Exclude terms from the results:
Use a minus sign (-) to exclude terms from the results.

For example:"price" + (-"competitor")

Returns conversations containing price but not competitor.

You can exclude multiple terms by adding an exclusion for each term.

For example:"price" + (-"competitor") + (-"budget")

Returns conversations containing price but not competitor or budget.

chunks.title: Work with filters

chunks.text:
Use free-text filters > Include or exclude results:
Some filters include options that let you control whether matching results are included or excluded.

For example, you can search for conversations that contain the term competitor to find conversations where competitors were discussed. Alternatively, you can search for conversations that don't contain the term competitor to find conversations where competitors were not mentioned.

Similarly, tracker filters can be configured to return conversations that contain or don't contain a specific tracker.

Using these options can help you find conversations where something was discussed, or identify conversations where a term, phrase, or tracker was not mentioned.

chunks.title: Work with filters

chunks.text:
Examples for filtering search results:
Here are some ideas on how you can use the filters to find exactly the calls you’re looking for. If you are looking for:

A call that you owned?

In the Participants filter, select your own name and select the Hosted filter.

A call that someone on your team attended?

In the Participants filter, search by the team’s manager and choose “Anyone on <manager’s name> team’. This will give you calls that anyone on that team attended, including the manager.

A call that you and your teammate attended?

In the Participants filter, select your own name and then click the Add icon to open another Participant filter. Enter your colleague’s name. Now, the search results only include calls that both of you attended.

Calls in which a top performer successfully handled a specific objection?

You may want to find calls in which a top performer dealt with a specific type of objection that lead to a closed-won deal. In the Participants filter, enter their name, in the Trackers filter, select the tracker that identifies the specific objection.

A call in which you remember a few words or phrases?

In the Words or phrases filter, enter the words or phrases you remember saying or hearing. Use quotation marks if you remember the exact phrase. If you remember who said the words or phrases, select the party in the Mentioned by drop down.

A call that took place some time last quarter?

In the Date filter, select the date, month, week, or quarter when the call took place. You can also enter a custom date range. For example, if you know the call took place just around the New Year, enter the relevant months.

chunks.text:
Ask questions in Gong Assistant:
Ask Gong Assistant to answer a question about a call, an account, a set of search results, or a broader workspace.

To ask a question:

1. Open Gong Assistant from a call page, Search, the Account Console, or the Gong Assistant page. Note: The information Gong Assistant uses depends on where you start. For example, if you open it from the Account Console, responses are scoped to the account you're viewing.
2. Enter your question, or choose a suggested prompt if one is available.
3. Review the response. On a call, responses can include citations to the source material.

chunks.text:
Focus Gong Assistant on specific information:
Gong Assistant can often determine which information to analyze based on how you phrase your question. For example, it can understand references to timeframes, accounts, and people when you include them directly in your question.

When you need more precise control over the information Gong Assistant uses, add context. Adding context lets you explicitly choose the calls, folders, streams, or files Gong Assistant should use when answering questions or creating content.

To focus Gong Assistant on specific information:

1. From the left sidebar, click Assistant and select Add context.
2. Select the data you want Gong Assistant to use:
  - Calls: Set up a filter so that Gong Assistant uses the relevant calls to answer questions or create content. You can also word your question in a way that filters the calls that are analyzed. See Refine questions with natural language or filters to see when you can filter with natural language and when it’s better to set a filter.
  - Folders and streams: Select a folder or stream which contains the calls the Assistant should use to answer questions or create content
3. Ask your question.

Adding context helps Gong Assistant focus on the information most relevant to your question.

chunks.text:
Upload files to Gong Assistant:
Upload files when you want Gong Assistant to work with information that does not originate from Gong conversations, or when you want it to follow a specific template or example. Uploaded files can be used alongside Gong data when answering questions, analyzing information, or generating content.

To upload files:

1. From the left sidebar, click Assistant.
2. Select Add context and then select Upload files.
3. Upload the files you want Gong Assistant to use.
4. Ask your question or request. Gong Assistant uses the uploaded files together with the available Gong context.

PDF, MD, TXT, and CSV files are supported. A maximum of 10 files of up to 20 MB per file can be uploaded per message.

chunks.text:
Create documents and Gong assets:
Gong Assistant can create documents and Gong assets based on the conversations and other information it has access to. Create documents when you want Gong Assistant to generate content such as training materials, battlecards, FAQs, and talk tracks. Build Gong assets such as scorecards, when you want it to create reusable items.

Note:You can ask Gong Assistant to create a document or asset from the call page and the search page. The document or asset is opened in the main Gong Assistant page.

To create a document or Gong asset:

1. From the left sidebar, click Assistant.
2. Click Create to create a document based on the relevant data.
3. Click Build to create a Gong asset such as a scorecard and enter the details of what you want to create. Tip:You can also describe what you want to create directly in your request. Gong Assistant can create the appropriate document or asset even if you do not manually select Create or Build first.
4. Click the document or asset you created to open it in the right panel.
5. Review the generated output.
6. Ask Gong Assistant to make changes if you want a revised version.
7. Click the drop down at the top of the right panel to swap between different documents.
8. Once you are happy with the document, you can copy or download a markdown file for documents. For Gong assets such as a scorecard, click Create scorecard. The scorecard is created but not published. You can view, edit, and publish the scorecard in the Scorecards page.

chunks.text:
How to set up opportunity teams:
Where to go: Revenue > Deals

Where to go: Revenue > Forecast

1. You can set up opportunity teams in either a deal board or forecast board:
  1. In a deal board, click Edit board or + Create board.
  2. In your chosen forecast board, click Forecast settings.
2. In the Basics section, under Show deals where team members are in, choose one of the following options:
  1. Team member attribute or opportunity team. Included deals are those handled by team members that appear either in the selected Team member attribute field or in the deal’s opportunity team.
  2. Opportunity team only. Included deals are those handled by team members who are part of the deal’s opportunity team.
3. Select Team member attribute as usual. This can be any role defined in your CRM, for example – Owner, Sales engineer, CSM. The board will then show deals handled by people in those roles.

| --- | --- |
| Team member attribute or opportunity team | Deals where team members appear either in the selected team member attribute field or in the deal’s opportunity team. |
| Opportunity team only | Deals where team members are part of the deal’s opportunity team. |

chunks.text:
How compliance policies work:
Compliance policies:

- Surface visual indicators in Engage
- Restrict or block certain outreach actions
- Automatically adjust behavior in flows

Compliance policies are set up by your admin. Depending on your company’s setup, policies may use:

- A global opt-out model, which gives you the option to mark someone as “do not contact”, or
- A granular opt-out model, which gives you separate options for marking someone as “do not call” and/or “do not email”

chunks.text:
Types of flows:
- Your flows: These are the flows that reps can create for themselves. If reps duplicate any company flows and save them with changes, they'll appear in this section. You can define which team members can create and manage personal templates through the available permission settings in their permission profile.
- Company flows: These flows are available to everyone in your org. They can only be edited by people who are authorized to do so through their permission profile, but anyone can duplicate them and save them as their own flows.
  - Starter flows: These flows are available to everyone in your org. They're pre-built by Gong to help team members speed up onboarding and reach out to prospects faster.

To get started with flows, you can choose a starter flow or a company flow and duplicate it, or create a new personal flow from scratch.

Where to go: Assets > Flows

chunks.title: Working with flows

chunks.text:
How to create a personal flow:
1. Open the Personal flows section and select the folder where you want the new company flow to live, or create a new folder.
2. Click to create a new flow.
3. Click at the top to give your flow a descriptive name.
4. Click Add description to give a meaningful description for the flow.
5. Add steps to the flow: To learn more about how each step type works, see Understanding flow steps. Available step types are:
  1. Manual email: Craft an email or generate one using AI.
  2. Auto email: Set up an email that sends automatically. The sender/to-do assignee is the person who adds the contact/lead to the flow. If flow automations are set up, the to-do assignee and sender can be specified by an automation. Learn more about auto email scheduling.
  3. Call: Schedule a call step.
  4. LinkedIn connect: Plan a LinkedIn connection request.
  5. LinkedIn message: Plan a LinkedIn message.
  6. Task: Any actions that aren't necessarily call, email, or LinkedIn-related, like sending a gift, prepping for an upcoming meeting, or researching a company.
6. Set time delays between steps: After adding each step, define the delay before the next step occurs.
7. Review step order and rearrange as needed.
8. Define the flow's visibility: Publish or unpublish the flow at the top left corner.
  1. For personal flows: Published means only you can start this flow for contacts and leads. Other team members won't see it in the "Add to flow" menu. If you unpublish a published flow, any flows already in progress will continue. Unpublished means no one can start this flow. It does not appear in the "Add to flow" menu.
  2. For company flows: Published means anyone can start this flow for contacts and leads. It appears in the "Add to flow" menu for all team members. If you unpublish a published flow, any flows already in progress will continue. Unpublished means no one can start this flow. It does not appear in the "Add to flow" menu.
9. Select the flow's ruleset: If your company allows contacts and leads to be active in multiple flows at once, you have the option to set the flow as exclusive. To learn more about rulesets, see Understanding rulesets.
  1. Go to the Settings tab.
  2. Click Change ruleset to select a different ruleset.
10. Save the flow.

chunks.text:
Set priority levels for flow steps:
When building or editing a flow, you can assign a priority level to each step. Any to-do created from that step automatically inherits the selected priority. Every to-do generated from the step uses the selected priority. Priority levels include Low, Medium, High, and Critical. All to-dos default to Medium unless updated. This helps teams focus on the most important items first when working through their to-dos.

chunks.text:
How to add attachments to a flow step:
Where to go: Assets > Flows

Open the flow you want to work on, then add attachments to flow steps by clicking . The email body size can be up to 3 MB. Body size does not include attachments, but it does include in-line images and GIFs. The total size of an email including attachments can be up to 20 MB.

When adding an attachment to a step in a flow that hasn't been saved yet, you'll be prompted to save the flow first in order to add the attachment. If you add an attachment to the flow step and then add a template that has attachments, any attachments you previously added will be removed or replaced with the template's attachments.

chunks.text:
How to edit a flow:
Where to go: Assets > Flows

You can edit a flow at any time. What you can change depends on whether the flow has contacts. To prevent you from accidentally overwriting another team member's work or losing your own, Gong detects when a flow has been updated by someone else while you're viewing or editing it. Gong also detects when new contacts were added to the flow while you were viewing or editing it. When a potential conflict is detected, you'll get a notification with options to safely manage your changes.

Learn more about editing flows with active contacts and leads.

chunks.text:
Validate contact details before adding people to flows:
Before the flow starts, Gong automatically checks whether the contact or lead has the required details to complete the steps in that flow. This helps you catch missing or invalid information in advance and improve delivery success.

If the flow contains:

- An email step, Gong checks that each contact or lead has at least one valid email address
- A call step, Gong checks that each contact or lead has at least one valid phone number If any contacts are missing required information, a validation window appears before the flow starts, giving you options to:
  - Proceed without an email address or phone number
  - Select a different flow

When adding people to flows in bulk, you can also:

- View the list of people in a new tab in the People page
  - If your list includes both contacts and leads, two tabs open automatically, one for leads and one for contacts
- Click Refresh list to recheck for missing information after making updates in Gong or your CRM
- Remove people with missing email addresses or phone numbers from the selection

If you choose to skip steps and later update a contact with valid details, Gong will automatically include them in the relevant steps when the flow runs.

Personalize flow steps when adding people to flows > Delay when a flow starts:
Choose how many days to wait before a flow begins instead of starting it immediately to better pace outreach and prevent daily task overload. Add the person to the flow as you normally would, and then choose the number of business days you want to delay the flow start by.

Say a contact is added to a flow on Wednesday with Delay first step set to "3 business days". Thursday is the first skipped day, Friday is the second skipped day, then Saturday and Sunday are weekend days, so Monday would be the flow's start day (3 business days later).

chunks.text:
How automatic pausing works when someone is in multiple flows:
For flow to-dos: Bounced email, Email response, and Meeting booked

If you receive any of these to-dos, only the relevant flow is automatically paused. You can choose to pause all flows for that person or all flows for the entire account. Emails already scheduled to go out from another flow to that bounced address will still send to that address unless action is taken prior to the scheduled send time

If you start drafting a new message via another flow to the email address that bounced, that bounce will have marked that address as invalid. You'll see that it's invalid in the "To" field when when writing the draft.

For Out of Office response

If you receive an out of office message, the current to-do for all flows the person is in will be snoozed until the person's return date (the flows are not paused). This ensures that follow-ups resume only after the contact is expected to be back. If Gong can't detect a date of return, flow steps proceed as originally scheduled, even if the only replies are repeated automated out of office messages.

For a missed call back

Only the flow from which the call originated will be paused.

chunks.text:
What happens when a contact or lead in a flow is deleted from your CRM?:
When a contact or lead is deleted in your CRM, Gong helps keep your flows running smoothly by automatically replacing the deleted person in the flow with a matching duplicate. Gong checks for another contact or lead in your CRM with the same email address.

If exactly one match is found, Gong will replace the deleted person with the matching contact or lead and automatically continue the flow without interruption.

If there are multiple matches or no matches, Gong will stop the flow.

This automation helps avoid unnecessary flow interruptions when contacts or leads are merged in your CRM, reducing manual cleanup.

Rulesets are groups of rules applied to flows that allow you to manage flow behavior. Instead of configuring individual flow settings, your admin can set the behavior once and then apply it across multiple flows at scale.

Permissions

Whether or not you can create and manage rulesets depends on your permission profile. If you have permission to edit a flow, you can change its ruleset. All flows, including company flows and personal flows, have a ruleset. Each flow can only have one ruleset applied at a time.

Default ruleset

There is always one default ruleset. Whichever ruleset is set as the default is automatically applied to new flows. The ruleset for individual flows can be changed later by anyone who has permission to edit the flow.

Rulesets vs. automations

Every flow has a ruleset, which is a group of flow settings that define flow behavior, such as what happens when someone replies or reaches the end of a flow. Automations on the other hand can only be applied to company flows, not personal flows. Flow automations are actions triggered automatically when certain conditions are met, such as adding someone to a flow.

Rulesets override call outcome automations for matching outcomes. For calls in a flow, the ruleset settings run instead of any automation configured by your admin for that outcome.

chunks.text:
How to change a flow’s ruleset:
Where to go: Assets > Flows > Select flow > Settings

1. Click Change ruleset
2. Select the ruleset you want to use and click Select

Once applied, you can always change a flow’s ruleset as many times as needed. You cannot edit the ruleset directly from the flow, you can only change which ruleset is applied. Whether or not you can edit rulesets from the Rulesets page depends on your permission profile.

Which ruleset you apply to a flow determines the flow’s behavior, including:

- Response handling. Controls what happens when someone replies, books a meeting, calls back, or their email bounces.
  - Customizable rules:
    - Set what happens when someone replies via email
    - Set what happens when someone books a meeting
  - Non-customizable rules:
    - When someone returns a call (answered or missed), pause the flow
    - When a recipient replies with an Out of Office message, snooze the flow step
      - One of the rules Gong provides automatically as part of every ruleset delays the next flow step when someone replies with an OOO email. The step is delayed until the person’s return date (the flow is not paused), ensuring follow-ups resume only after the contact is expected to be back. If Gong can't detect a date of return, flow steps proceed as originally scheduled, even if the only replies are repeated automated out of office messages.
    - When an email bounces, pause the flow and create an email bounced to-do

Any team member can access this feature if they have the required permissions.

chunks.text:
Types of templates in Gong Engage:
- Your personal templates: These are the templates created by individual team members. If you duplicate a company template and save it with changes, it’ll be here too. Your admin can provide you with the Create and manage their own templates permission. Admins can view all personal content of team members in their organization, while managers can view personal content of users reporting directly to them. However, admins and managers cannot edit other team members’ content.
- Company templates: These templates are available to everyone in your org. They can only be edited by people with the Manage company templates permission, but anyone can duplicate them and save them as their own personal templates.
- Influencer templates: Get inspiration from the best in the business with these ready-to-use templates from industry experts. Use them as is or edit them to your preferences. They're available in your templates library. Duplicate them to create personal templates out of them. Modify an influencer template once you’ve saved it to Your templates, or once you selected it while writing an email. The metrics for each influencer template are calculated based on your whole company's usage, not personal usage.
- Shared with you: These templates have been shared with you by other team members. You can’t edit content shared with you unless you duplicate it and save it as your own. Depending on your permissions, you can archive or restore shared templates to manage visibility in your library. Shared templates can be used when drafting emails or building flow email steps.
- Archive: Archive templates to remove them from your active list. However, archived templates are not available for use when drafting emails or building flow email steps. You can restore archived templates from this folder if needed

How to use templates or prompts:
- Within the email composer: Click Write email from a to-do to open the email composer. At the bottom, click Templates. Select a template to populate the email, or select a prompt to have Gong generate the email subject and body. You can review and edit before sending.
- When creating or editing a flow: When configuring a manual or automated email step, choose one of the following:
  - Use a saved template or prompt: Select an existing template or prompt from the library.
  - Write a prompt directly in the flow step: Enter prompt instructions that are used only for that step and aren't saved for reuse. Prompts are supported for manual and automated email steps, but not for reply email steps.
- When sending call follow-up emails: From a call page, click Generate follow-up email. Generate the email with AI, or select a template enabled for call follow-up emails. To find relevant templates faster, select Only show templates enabled for follow-up emails. Gong uses the selected template together with the call transcript to generate a follow-up email that you can review and edit before sending.
- From the Chrome Extension: When selecting a template to use, note that field placeholders in Gong are grouped the same way they're grouped in your CRM. To avoid errors, use templates with recipient field placeholders that align with the entity you're contacting. Recipient field placeholders are auto-populated with information about a recipient, like their name, company name, or job title, when the message is sent. For example, if you're emailing a lead, use the "Lead First Name" field placeholder instead of the "Contact First Name" field placeholder.

- Within the email composer: Click Write email from a to-do to open the email composer. At the bottom, click Templates. Select a template to populate the email, or select a prompt to have Gong generate the email subject and body. You can review and edit before sending.
- When creating or editing a flow: When configuring a manual or automated email step, choose one of the following:
  - Use a saved template or prompt: Select an existing template or prompt from the library.
  - Write a prompt directly in the flow step: Enter prompt instructions that are used only for that step and aren't saved for reuse. Prompts are supported for manual and automated email steps, but not for reply email steps.
- When sending call follow-up emails: From a call page, click Generate follow-up email. Generate the email with AI, or select a template enabled for call follow-up emails. To find relevant templates faster, select Only show templates enabled for follow-up emails. Gong uses the selected template together with the call transcript to generate a follow-up email that you can review and edit before sending.
- From the Chrome Extension: When selecting a template to use, note that field placeholders in Gong are grouped the same way they're grouped in your CRM. To avoid errors, use templates with recipient field placeholders that align with the entity you're contacting. Recipient field placeholders are auto-populated with information about a recipient, like their name, company name, or job title, when the message is sent. For example, if you're emailing a lead, use the "Lead First Name" field placeholder instead of the "Contact First Name" field placeholder.

Where to go: To-dos

The to-dos you see in Engage are a combination of tasks and reminders that help you stay on top of your daily work. It brings together tasks and reminders related to emails, calls, LinkedIn messages, connection requests, and custom tasks.

To-dos can be generated in several ways:

- Flow to-dos. These to-dos are generated by flow steps. They let you know when a flow step is due, and when flow events happen involving contacts or leads you’re assigned to.
- To-dos created by you. One-off to-dos that you create for yourself also appear on your to-do list. You can link them to contacts, leads, accounts, and deals.
- Gong-recommended to-dos. Gong identifies potential actions you might want to take with prospects and customers. With Gong letting you know about these actions, there’s less of a chance that something will slip through the cracks. Some of these to-dos are generated using AI. Calls that are less than 10 minutes long, or only include participants from your company, do not trigger a to-do to follow up.

See your to-dos:

Set up your to-do list > Sort your to-do list:
Sort your to-do list by:

- Priority. Group to-dos to focus on the most important work first. Priority levels include Low, Medium, High, and Critical. For flow to-dos, priority level for that flow step is set by the person who created the flow. For one-off to-dos, click on the priority level to change it at any time.
- Due date. Due date of the to-do. Can be changed by clicking on it.
- Local time. Linked contact/lead local time. The way local time is generated depends on what your admin has set up for your company
- Flow step number. To-dos are grouped by step numbers, so you’ll see all step 1 to-dos first, then step 2 to-dos, etc. The secondary sorter is flow name
- Recent digital interactions. Associated contacts or leads that had the most recent email opens and clicks. The engagement count for each contact is shown with a blue lightning bolt next to the contact name, showing you how many email opens and clicks that person had.
- Digital interaction count. Number of email opens and clicks over the last 30 days. The number of opens and clicks is counted at the contact/lead level.

Set up your to-do list > Group your to-dos:
Group your to-do list to better organize your daily work and prioritize important tasks.

Group by:

- Flow and step number: When you group by flow name, to-dos are organized by flow and step number. This can help you see your progress through each flow, prioritize which steps to complete next, and keep related tasks together instead of switching contexts
- Account name: Organize your to-dos by account name to see everything related to the same prospect or customer in one place. This view is ideal when you're managing multiple deals or outreach efforts within the same account.
- Prospect local time: Identify who's available now and time your outreach accordingly.

To-dos that aren't tied to a flow (like Gong-recommended or one-off to-dos) are grouped by to-do type.

You can apply a variety of filters to help you prioritize your to-dos. For example, you may want to focus on certain to-dos based on which flow or step they’re related to, or focus on tasks related to people showing specific signs of interest using recent digital interactions. You may want to handle a bunch of calls due today, send out a bunch of LinkedIn messages in a row, or catch up on emails for the next hour. You can move between the tabs at the top left of To-dos to show all tasks, or tasks of a specific type.

Click Add filter to apply filters to your to-do list.

| Due date | Filter by tasks that are due today, tomorrow, this week, or overdue |

| Prospect local time | Filter by morning hours, business hours, or set a specific time range. This filter only applies to to-dos that are linked to a contact or lead and have a local time available. If you don't see the local time filter or sorting option, ask your admin to configure your company's time zone settings in Engage |

chunks.text:
How to take action on your to-dos > Handle to-dos in bulk:
Work more efficiently using bulk actions instead of actioning your to-dos one by one. Start by selecting at least one to-do, which triggers the floating bulk actions menu bar to appear.

Bulk actions are only available when viewing your own to-dos. If you are viewing someone else’s to-dos, bulk actions are not available.

The bulk action bar includes the following actions:

- Start. opens selected to-dos in a queue (not available for the All tab)
- Mark as complete. marks selected to-dos as complete. When completing flow to-dos, the next step is generated automatically
- Update due date. updates due date for selected to-dos
- Dismiss. dismisses non-flow to-dos (available when only non-flow to-dos are selected)
- Skip step. skips flow step (available when only flow to-dos are selected). The next step is generated automatically
- Skip step/dismiss. skips flow step to-dos and dismisses non-flow to-dos (available when a mix of flow and non-flow to-dos is selected)
- Remove from flow. removes people from flows (available when only flow to-dos are selected)
- Pause flow. pauses flows (available when only flow to-dos are selected)

chunks.text:
How to take action on your to-dos > Handle to-dos consecutively:
To help you work faster and stay focused, you may want to handle a number of to-dos in a row. This is available from all tabs, so you can move through different types of to-dos all in one sequence.

Sort them in a way that’s convenient for you, whether you want to sort by flow name, which groups to-dos by which flow they’re in and orders them by step number, or by associated account, which groups to-dos by account name and orders them according to deal name. As you work through your list, the next to-do on your list is opened for you as soon as you complete your current one.

You can also select the specific to-dos you want to work on and click Start in the bulk actions menu.

Don’t want to work on a particular to-do right now? Click Next to open the next one on the list. Click Previous to get back to the previous to-do.

Once a to-do is completed, dismissed, or skipped, it’s no longer part of the queue.

To work on a single to-do, either select it and click Start, or close the window when you're done.

chunks.text:
How to take action on your to-dos > Send an email:
Any to-do that prompts you to write an email with opens the email composer. The first time you write an email, Gong asks you for permission to write emails. Giving Gong this permission means the emails you compose in Gong are integrated with your email client (Gmail or Office365) and sent directly from them. This means:

- Emails you send appear in your client Sent folder.
- Emails you compose but don't send appear in your email client Drafts folder.
- If the to-do was triggered from an existing email thread (for example, an Out of Office reply), the email is included in the existing thread in your email client.

Emails sent from Gong can be tracked for email open and link click events depending on your company’s setup.

To make writing emails even quicker, take advantage of templates, inspiration from your teammates, the AI rephraser, and other tools available directly within the email composer.

If you send an email from your email client instead of sending it through the Gong email composer, the to-do is not marked as complete automatically.

To update CRM information while you're writing an email, go to the CRM tab inside the email composer. From here, you can efficiently update account and deal fields while handling your task.

How to take action on your to-dos > Edit or send an auto email:
When the step before an auto email in a flow is completed, an auto email to-do is created. Auto email to-dos can be found under the All and Flow categories. Hover over an auto email to-do and click Edit auto email to open the email composer, where you can edit the email body or change the scheduled send time. Save your changes or click Send now to send the auto email immediately instead of at its scheduled time.

Manage the to-do by skipping it or marking it as complete.

If an auto email has values missing for field placeholders or the contact has no email address, the to-do for that auto email appears under the Flow errors category on your to-do list.

Any to-do that prompts you to make a call with opens the Gong dialer, so you can call people directly from Gong. These calls can be recorded, giving you the same analytics and insights as all recorded calls in Gong. While working on a call to-do, you can make call attempts without marking the to-do as complete, and then return to the open to-do later on.

To use the dialer, your admin must enable it for you, and must set business numbers that are available either to you specifically (assigned numbers) or to your entire team.

You can use templates for call scripts to make things easy when it comes time to dial someone.

To update CRM information while you're making a call, go to the CRM tab inside the dialer. From here, you can efficiently update account and deal fields while handling your task.

chunks.text:
How to take action on your to-dos > Send LinkedIn connection requests and messages:
To send LinkedIn connection requests and messages from Gong, your admin must integrate LinkedIn Sales Navigator and Gong, and you must have a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus license. If you don’t have a Sales Navigator license but want to move the contact along in the flow, simply mark the step as complete.

While writing your message, use the tabs on the right side to get context about the person or account you're engaging with. LinkedIn messages don’t auto-populate inside the LinkedIn section of the window. Instead, copy and paste the message from the Script section of the window into the LinkedIn message box.

You need to add a message to send the connection request. If the message box is blank, the connection request won't be sent.

When opening a LinkedIn to-do, you may notice that the wrong LinkedIn profile has been marked as a match in Gong, either by you or someone else on your team. If so, that person will continue to appear as a match until marked as "Not the right person". To do this, click on the user icon at the top right of the LinkedIn window and click Not the right person.

While both LinkedIn messages and LinkedIn connection request to-dos can be synced to your CRM, the option to Log this conversation to CRM is only available for messages and not for connection requests, and depends on which Sales Navigator plan you have. Gong only supports the Sales Navigator Advanced Plus license, where you have the option for full CRM integration, including "Log to CRM" for tracking interactions.

chunks.text:
Describe the task:
Clearly explain what you want the agent to do.

The prompt should focus on a specific task or outcome rather than a general request.

Examples include:

- Summarize the main customer concerns discussed in the calls.
- Identify implementation risks mentioned by the customer.
- Draft a follow-up email based on the conversation.

Specific instructions help the agent understand the goal of the analysis.

The first time you click WRITE EMAIL, whether it's directly from a to-do or elsewhere, we'll ask you for permission to write emails.

Be sure to allow all permissions when prompted. If only some permissions are allowed, you won’t be able to connect your email provider and write emails through Engage.

If your email write permission is disconnected or expires later, Gong displays a banner with a link to reconnect your email account. Without email write permission, you won't be able to send emails from Gong, including auto-emails in flows.

Giving us this permission means the emails you compose in Gong are integrated with your email client (Gmail or Office365) and sent directly from them. This means:

- Emails you send appear in your email client Sent folder.
- If the to-do was triggered from an existing email thread (for example, an Out of Office reply), the email is included in the existing thread in your email client.

When you click WRITE EMAIL, the email is pre-populated with key info such as contacts and key steps, as relevant, and includes suggested text that you can edit freely. You can also add emojis, links and attachments.

chunks.text:
What's in the Gong email composer:
- Deal info: Click Deal info in the right-side menu of the email composer to get all relevant deal context at your fingertips. See contacts sorted by activity level, past events related to the deal, and view and edit CRM fields on the go (amount, close date, and stage).
- Call info/last email: Depending on the type of activity leading up to the email you're writing, the next section labeled Call info or Last email may appear. This section shows you the last call's details including next steps, or lets you view the last email thread right next to the one you're currently writing.
- Templates: The Templates section gives you handy templates you can easily reuse to speed up your writing process. Templates often contain variables, which let you quickly personalize your message. Under each template, you'll see open rate stats to help you choose the ones that are most effective.
- Variables: Variables serve as a great way to easily personalize your messaging. If you try to send an email with a missing variable, or placeholder text between double brackets that we can't find a value for, we'll warn you before sending. The same applies for auto-emails send via flows; if there are any missing variables, we'll let you know by presenting the email as a manual email in the To-dos. Learn more about using variables in Gong. Note that variables, which populate automatically based on the recipient or account information, are different from placeholders. A placeholder can be any text between curly brackets, intended for the person sending the email to replace it with the relevant information before it goes out. Like with variables, we'll let you know before the email gets sent if there are any placeholders still left in the email.
- AI-generated email drafts: For certain Gong-generated to-dos, Engage provides you with an AI-generated email draft using the context of your last interactions. You get a personalized suggested draft that you can quickly rephrase to adjust the tone of the message. You can get AI-generated email drafts in flows, too. chunks.text:
What's in the Gong email composer > For Outlook users: How to use Calibri and Aptos fonts in the Gong email composer:
1. Make sure you’re using a chromium-based browser (Google Chrome or MS Edge)
2. Make sure your browser is updated
3. Check whether the font you need is installed on your computer:
  1. On Mac:
    1. Open the Font Book app (you can search for it via Spotlight).
    2. Search for the font by name. Make sure it’s an exact match, like “Aptos” or “Calibri”. Something like "Calibri Regular", for example, will not work.
    3. If it’s not listed, download and install the font, then restart your browser.
  2. On Windows:
    1. Open the Control Panel > Appearance and Personalization > Fonts.
    2. Search for the font by name. Make sure it’s an exact match, like “Aptos” or “Calibri”. Something like "Calibri Regular", for example, will not work.
    3. If it’s not listed, download and install the font, then restart your browser.
4. Make sure the “Fonts” setting is switched on in your browser
5. Quit and relaunch your browser. Just closing a tab or window isn’t enough, the browser must be fully quit and relaunched.
6. Once reopened, check if the font appears in the Gong email composer.

chunks.text:
Which email address are my emails being sent from?:
Gong can only import email and calendar information for a single mailbox. The email address listed in My profile, which is the one that’s connected to your email provider, is the address we ingest emails from and the address your emails come from when sent from Gong.

If the email address you connect to in My settings under Emails is different from the email connected to your email provider, your emails will be sent from that address, but not ingested into Gong. It’s not recommended to connect a different email address through My settings from the one you have listed in My profile.

Depending on your organization’s setup, the email listed in My profile might be assigned by your admin or provisioning system.

Any email addresses listed in Additional email addresses under My profile are used to identify you on emails, calendar meetings, web conferencing calls, telephony calls, and CRM mappings. Gong does not support sending emails from an email alias.

chunks.text:
Save time writing emails with AI:
The Gong email composer uses AI to give you ready-to-send, personalized messaging in a click. You can use this time-saving tool when:

- Actioning Gong-recommended to-dos: When working through your to-do list, click Write email next to one of the following Gong-recommended to-dos to get an AI-generated email draft:
  - Meeting follow-up: Draft is generated based on the transcript of the call or meeting
  - Back from OOO: Draft is generated based on the original email that was sent to the person and the Out of Office reply that was received
  - Nudge: Draft is generated based on the previous email you sent to the person
  - Meeting confirmation: Draft is generated based on the subject, date and time of the meeting
- Creating flows: When creating a flow step that involves sending an email, choose Generate an email so that each time someone reaches that step in the flow, Gong will generate a personalized email draft for you. You can choose which type of email you want Gong to generate:
  - Nudge email: Gently remind someone to get back to you with a message that references your last email
  - Cold email: Start a conversation with a new prospect. When a prospect reaches this step in the flow, Gong will prompt you for a few quick pieces of information about the prospect, company, and industry in order to generate a highly personalized email. Once the email is generated, either send it off right away, or click Edit to adjust your answers and regenerate the email draft
- Reviewing a call: While watching a call back, easily generate a follow-up email. From the call page, click Generate follow-up email in the top right corner to open an AI-generated email draft summarizing the call.

chunks.text:
Schedule emails to be sent later:
Stay one step ahead by choosing the date and time you want your email to land in your recipient’s mailbox. To schedule an email, click on the arrow next to the send button. You have a few quick options to choose from, but you can also click Choose custom time to set a specific date and time. If there’s only one recipient, you can also see what that time will be for your recipient based on their time zone.

What happens once I’ve scheduled an email?

Once you've scheduled an email to be sent later, the email shows up in the activity timeline on the corresponding account page with a note stating when it's scheduled to be sent. From here, you can edit the email draft or cancel and delete it so that it will no longer be sent.

Before the scheduled email goes out, you can edit the email from within Gong. Your email will still get sent out at the right time including the changes you made.

If you start composing a new email but you already have another draft that’s been scheduled to go to that same recipient, we’ll let you know with a note at the top of the email composer. The note tells you when the scheduled draft is set to go out. From here, you can view the scheduled email right next to the one you’re working on and decide whether to keep the scheduled draft or the new one you’ve started.

Is there a limit to the number of emails that can be sent at once?

Set up and edit your email signature:
Where to go: Top nav bar > Click your name > My Settings

1. Go to the Emails section and click Edit signature
2. Set up your signature by creating a new one here, or use the same one you use with your email provider. You can change the text, add and embed links, and add images.
  1. For Gmail users: If you’ve set up an email signature in Gmail, turn on Import Gmail signature to import it directly into Gong. Your signature will look exactly the same in Gong as it does in Gmail, including formatting.

3. Set whether your email signature should be included in replies and forwards using the checkbox.
4. When you're ready, click Done.

We automatically check for signature updates every 24 hours. For example, if your signature was last imported two days ago, we’ll fetch the latest version when you open the email composer to ensure it’s up to date.

There is no need to perform any special set up, although you may be asked to sign into your Gong account via Zapier when creating a rule.

Additional details are available on our Zapier integration page.

Create a rule using Gong data

About the integration:
1. (Recommended) In Gong, save a search with the type of calls you want to trigger a Zap:
  - Go to Conversations > Search, create a filter to set up and save a search to find the required types of calls.
2. Go to zapier.com, and log in to your Zapier account.
3. Click Create Zap.
4. Create the trigger:
  1. Select Gong from the list of apps.
  2. Select New Call as the trigger event. We will soon change this to the saved search created in step 1.
  3. Click Continue.
  4. If asked, sign into your Gong account, and allow Zapier access. Engagement Events from Zapier asks for access Gong's public API in order to retrieve a list of all workspaces and send user engagement data events to Gong.
  5. If relevant, select the Gong workspace.
  6. Select the saved search created in step 1. NoteIf you don't select a saved search, data for all calls are sent from Gong to the selected app.
  7. Click Continue and test the trigger as instructed. When the process is complete, review the data collected.
  8. If you're satisfied, click Continue.
5. Create the action:
  1. Select the destination app from the list of apps.
  2. Select the action event.
  3. Click Continue.
  4. If asked, sign into your account in the third party app, and allow Zapier access.
  5. Set up the action (the exact fields depend on the selected app and action event).
  6. Test the action.
6. Give your Zap a name, and turn it on when ready. NoteZaps that pull data from Gong are shown in the Gong Rule Manager (Settings > Data Access > Automation Rules). Whenever a call is found that fits the criteria, the Zap rule is triggered and the data sent to your selected application. The following animated GIF shows the full process.

chunks.text:
About the integration:
Where do I create a Zapier rule (Zap)?

You can only create a Zap in Zapier. Any rule you create in Zapier is displayed in Gong's automation rules page and can be enabled or disabled. To edit or delete the rule, you must go back to Zapier.

Why should I use Zapier?

Zapier offers an easy way to transfer data from Gong to thousands of Zapier-supported applications, such as HubSpot. It also enables you to pick and choose which data to forward.

Who can create a Zap?

Only a Gong business administrator can create Zaps.

What data is sent out from Gong?

Most of the call data is exported, including company name, user name, media type, user ID, opportunity name, opportunity stage, account name, snippet, call URL, opportunity amount, scope, snippet speaker and topics.

Which Gong searches do I see in Zapier?

You see your saved searches and any searches open to all Gong users.

Where can I push data to?

You can send the call data to any web app supported by Zapier (and there are thousands).

A team member who manages and configures the Gong platform and handles CRM integrations, user provisioning, permissions, and system settings. Find my Tech admin.

Access to this feature depends on your assigned seat.

chunks.text:
Recording options:
Choose one of the following methods to integrate Gong with Zoom:

- Native Zoom recording (recommended): Set up native zoom recording so that the call is recorded in Zoom and automatically pulled into Gong.
- Record calls using the Gong bot: The Gong bot is added to your meetings to record the call, and bring it into Gong. On such calls, your Gong users can listen in to the call live via Gong.

chunks.title: Zoom integration overview

chunks.text:
Advantages of connecting Gong to Zoom:
Whichever recording method you're using, connecting Gong to Zoom provides a number of advantages:

- More accurate meeting attribution and speaker and participant identification (including host identification when using Zoom Rooms)
- Switch Zoom user settings to VOIP automatically and make sure Gong records calls (bot recording)
- The ability to pause and resume the conversation when there may be sensitive information - Gong will stitch the recordings together, indicating that there was a pause
- Better recording quality
- Install Gong’s app for Zoom to take notes during meetings
- Leverage the Gong consent page to make sure you have participant consent to record:
  - Dynamic links: The integration allows Gong to generate unique Zoom links for every meeting scheduled with the Gong add-in: Gong for Google calendar: domain-wide or per individual Gong for Outlook: domain-wide or per individual
  - Personal meeting (static) links: The integration allows Gong to associate personal meeting links with the team member's Gong consent page When you use the Gong consent page with Zoom, Gong automatically links the Zoom personal meeting room to each team member's consent page link.

Set up the integration:
1. In Gong, click Admin center > Settings > Data capture > Telephony systems.
2. Click + Add telephony system.
3. Select Zoom Phone.
4. Click CONNECT. You are redirected to Zoom Phone.
5. Enter your credentials, and approve. You are directed back to Gong. Zoom Phone provides a token that Gong captures in the background. You're now connected to the Zoom Phone API and calls will be captured. If this is the first time you've connected to Zoom Phone, Gong brings in the last three months worth of calls. If you're reconnecting to Zoom Phone, Gong brings in calls from the last sync date.
6. In Zoom phone, an admin should enable automatic recording.

chunks.title: Zoom Phone (SMS)

chunks.text:
Connect Zoom Phone (SMS):
Before you begin: Make sure for everyone you want to capture Zoom Phone text messages for, that Import telephony system calls is selected in their data capture settings.

1. In Gong, click Admin center > Settings tab > Data capture Telephony systems.
2. Click + Add telephony system.
3. Select Zoom Phone (SMS).
4. Click CONNECT. You are redirected to Zoom Phone.
5. Enter your credentials, and approve. You are directed back to Gong. Zoom Phone (SMS) provides a token that Gong captures in the background. You're now connected to the Zoom Phone API and sms will be captured. If this is the first time you've connected to Zoom Phone (SMS), Gong brings in the last three months worth of sms. If you're reconnecting to Zoom Phone (SMS), Gong brings in sms from the last sync date.
